Meanwhile a believer still owes justice and fairness to every human being, Muslim or non-Muslim. The unlawful friendship is alliance with non-Muslims at war with Islam. In God's eyes intention carries the issue. His scale catches every wrongdoer, and nothing human escapes His sight in public or in private. Yet sincere intention receives consideration, while God-conscious behaviour matters everywhere because account awaits everything.

Knowledge also consoles. Because nothing escapes Him, grief over calamity can soften. Succour and response approach, trials disappear, and assistance and protection are hastened. What finally matters is whether Islam lives in the heart. Faith means love for God springing from the heart's core. Such lovers merit His attention. A bond thus formed brings forgiveness for failings. Arrogance meets hardness, modesty meets gentleness.

### In short

- Concealed friendship and revealed hostility are equally known to Allah, who knows heaven and earth and can punish without delay.
- The heart's inward state is the ground of accountability, so no verbal denial can cover it.
- The same knowledge comforts the afflicted: assistance and protection are hastened by the One from whom nothing is hidden.

30.text:
The verse sets the meeting at which all of it appears: "˹Watch for˺ the Day when every soul will be presented with whatever good it has done. And it will wish that its misdeeds were far off. And Allah warns you about Himself. And Allah is Ever Gracious to ˹His˺ servants". Good deeds arrive as joy and evil deeds as grief, and the wish to be far from one's own sins is the human picture of that Day.

### Phrase by phrase

**"˹Watch for˺ the Day when every soul will be presented with whatever good it has done"**: Resurrection Day displays both good and evil actions before each servant. "On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forward, and what he left behind" (75:13). Registers contain the good without deficiency, present for its owner to see.

**"And it will wish that its misdeeds were far off"**: good deeds bring happiness and delight, but visible evil causes sadness and anger. A person would rather disown that work or place an immense interval (in one image, as long as sunrise-to-sunset) between himself and it so it could never reach him. Even his former devil-companion, who encouraged evil through life, receives the wish: "Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts, a horrible companion (indeed)!" (43:38).

**"And Allah warns you about Himself. And Allah is Ever Gracious to ˹His˺ servants"**: He warns you against His punishment, and the warning is repeated here for emphasis. Then He brings hope to His servants so they do not despair of His mercy or lose heart at His kindness. He is full of pity for the believers.

### Kindness inside the warning

Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī found kindness within the threat: Allah warns people against Himself precisely because He cares for them. Other readings stress mercy toward creation. He wants servants on the straight path and chosen religion, following His honoured Messenger, while repeated warning prevents despair by promising kindness after fear.

The sight of that Day will be dreadful. When the veil of the divine test is lifted, the world of the Hereafter appears and the fruits of a person's actions stand before him. The things of this world that had looked so pleasing become the very things he wants far away. Whoever is proved wrong on that scale cannot escape.

### Fear and hope by turns

The pairing teaches changing states. Servants move between fear and hope, contraction and expansion, harshness and generosity. "God warns you about Himself" first bewilders a person until selfhood loosens. Then clemency seats him in gentleness's ship and carries him from confoundedness's whirlpool toward intimacy's shore.

An elder of the religion wondered whether self's whirlpool could be escaped aboard deliverance, whether compassion's hand could catch his among wishing waves, whether unity's proof could draw dispersion's veil from his eyes, and whether his heart could rest inside the body. Avarice has emptied a hundred thousand merchants' purses of pure gold seeking just such an alchemy.

### In short

- On the Day of Resurrection every soul meets its good with delight and its evil with grief, wishing for an immense distance from its sins (75:13, 43:38).
- The repeated warning is itself kindness, meant to keep servants on the straight path and stop them despairing of mercy.
- Inwardly the verse alternates fear and hope until confoundedness gives way to intimacy.

31.text:
Here is the test for every claim of love: "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If you ˹sincerely˺ love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive your sins. For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”" Love is a secret with no yardstick of its own, so Allah sets the touchstone outside the claimant. Follow the Messenger, and the claim stands. Refuse, and it falls, whatever the words were.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If you ˹sincerely˺ love Allah, then follow me"**: say to mankind that whoever really loves Allah must follow Muhammad ﷺ, following what he brought on the inside and the outside. Love leaves traces and signs, and the educated guess about another's love is made from visible conditions and dealings. Here the visible test is exact: match the claim against where, how often and how well a person follows him.

**"Allah will love you and forgive your sins"**: what you earn is much more than what you sought in loving Him, because Allah will love you back, and by following the Messenger ﷺ you earn His love and forgiveness together, with the blessing of his mission. He will reward you and forgive your sins, the sins committed previously by the one who now follows, and He is Merciful to him.

**"For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”"**: Forgiving to whoever repents, and Merciful toward whoever dies in a state of repentance.

### A verse that judges claims

This honourable verse judges against everyone who claims to love Allah without following the way of Muhammad ﷺ. The claim stays unproven unless Muhammad's law and religion govern his speech, behaviour and circumstances. The Ṣaḥīḥ preserves the Messenger's ruling: "Whoever commits an act that does not conform with our matter (religion), then it will be rejected of him." Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and several scholars among the Salaf commented, "Some people claimed that they love Allah. So Allah tested them with this Ayah." The genuine and the false in a claim become visible in the same proportion as the following. The stronger the following, the truer the claim, and the weaker the following, the weaker the claim. The Prophet's own words sharpen it into an equation: "He who obeyed Muhammad ﷺ obeyed Allah and he who disobeyed Muhammad ﷺ disobeyed Allah."

### The disputes that surrounded the command

Several settings frame the command. Idol-worshippers said their worship sought closeness to God through love, prompting the answer. Jews also claimed divine sonship and beloved status. After revelation, ʿAbdullāh Ibn Ubayy accused Muhammad ﷺ of demanding Christian-style love for Jesus from Muslims. Jews echoed that Islam wanted him taken as a compassionate Lord like Jesus. The next verse (3:32) answers those objections. Claimed love here never means adoration of Muhammad ﷺ. It means heartfelt obedience, modelled perfectly by a Prophet whose own obedience God attested. A believer nominal in sentiment but disobedient in life aligns with denial, because nobody loves a beloved while embracing the beloved's enemy.

### Intellect as watchman, not as leader

At reality's level, fervour hears another summons: step into the Prophet's tracks, because the task is already prepared in his footsteps. Intellect should watch the gate, not hold the reins. It can carry rulings' saddle-cloth, but religion's magnificence exceeds intellectual scales and categories of substance and accident. Seek the object through prophethood, not autonomous reason.

This faith is shared with the 124,000 prophets and messengers. Scripture says: "He has set down for you as the religion that with which He counseled Noah" (42:13). Only two supports uphold it: "God said" and "God's Messenger said." Remove the theologians' substances, accidents, distinctions and intellectual determinations from creation entirely, and neither religion's threshold nor the Sunnah's gate would suffer an iota. Folk of the Sunnah heard perfection announced: "Today I have perfected your religion for..." (5:3). Kalām's route is shadowy, its shadows among the worst. Follow instead the Hadith people's road, where Muṣṭafā's imamate suffices. Confusion is discarded in the simple religion of servants and old women.

### A covenant made before the world

Before Adam's dust and the world itself existed, created spirits gathered and the prophets' spirits covenanted: "Say: If you love God, follow me." Serving the empire's chieftain and centre of fortune required a tightened belt and willing assistance. The divine retelling says: "They said, 'We assent.' He said, 'So bear witness'" (3:81). Spirits then vanished into nonexistence's concealment. Across breaths in the field of power and decree, entrances into the world came singly. Adam, Ibrāhīm (Abraham), Mūsā (Moses) and ʿĪsā (Jesus) passed through and entered dust, as did thousands of prophets. Eventually the field emptied and Muḥammad was called to his moment.

His single imperial step toppled fourteen battlements from Caesar's castle. All 360 Kaabah idols fell face down. Truth's arrival and falsehood's departure sounded across the world's four corners: "The truth has come, and falsehood has..." (17:81). Prophethood's pearl rested upon exaltation's carpet while messengerhood's pavilion stretched ropes east to west. Noble traits spread like gems as beauty's mask lifted, matching his saying: "I was sent out with the all-comprehensive words to complete the noble character traits." Eyes that saw his sanctified spirit let spirit detach from heart. One shell opened in love's ocean and pearls filled the water. In the language of the Folk of the Ṭarīqah, "You love God" names dispersion, whereas "God will love you" names togetherness.

### In short

- The truth of loving Allah is measured by following the Messenger in statement, action and condition, and the reward is greater than the claim: Allah's love and forgiveness.
- Occasions of the verse include idol-worship for closeness, Jewish claims of sonship, and Ibn Ubayy's charge that Muslims were being made to love Muhammad ﷺ as Christians loved Jesus.
- Read inwardly, intellect serves as watchman while prophethood leads, and the command echoes a covenant taken from the prophets before the world (42:13, 5:3, 3:81, 17:81).

32.text:
The sequence closes with a blunt order: "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Obey Allah and His Messenger.” If they still turn away, then truly Allah does not like the disbelievers". The obedience asked for is the belief in the Oneness of Allah that the Messenger enjoins, together with what Allah obligated and the Messenger practised. Turning away after that is named by its final name.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Obey Allah and His Messenger.”"**: obey Allah, who has obligated His commands, and His Messenger in his practices and instructions. Fulfilling His instructions and avoiding His prohibitions, following His sacred law and the Messenger's commands, is what obedience means here.

**"If they still turn away, then truly Allah does not like the disbelievers"**: if they object to obedience and turn their backs, Allah will chastise them. The shift to the open noun, "the disbelievers", in place of the pronoun "they", makes the judgement explicit. For the Jews and hypocrites addressed, turning away from obeying them became the disbelief named here.

### Why refusal is called disbelief

Defying the Messenger's path is kufr. Claiming to love Allah or draw near to Him does not change its status until the claimant follows the unlettered Prophet, the final messenger to humans and jinn. Earlier prophets and mighty messengers, had they lived in his era, could only follow, obey and remain under his law. The prophets' covenant verse will make that explicit (3:81).

Belief in prophethood and the necessity of following the Messenger stand here beside the Oneness of Allah, and rejecting either is counted the same kind of act. The psychological fact behind it is plain. A person cannot truly love someone and love that person's enemy, and when the beloved is the Creator and Sustainer, love for Him necessarily awakens the desire to obey Him in all matters. Sentiment that produces no obedience is false. The example of total obedience has been testified by God Himself in His Prophet, and the authentic model of a life of God-worship is the one his messenger handed down.

### A mercy hidden in the naming

He commanded obedience, then said, "But if they turn their backs." He did not say, then Allah loves not the disobedient, ʿāṣūn. He said the disbelievers, kāfirūn. The address therefore indicates that He loves the believers even when they are disobedient. The threat of this verse lands on rejection, not on sin inside faith. Obedience remains commanded, and the previous verse remains the proof of love, but the person who believes and falls short is still inside the circle of those He loves.

### In short

- Obeying Allah and His Messenger in belief, command and prohibition is the form love must take, and refusal is named disbelief.
- Every earlier prophet, had he lived in Muhammad's time, would have followed him (3:81).
- The verse calls the turners-away disbelievers rather than disobedient, which indicates that Allah loves believers even when they disobey.

33.text:
The story of Maryam and her son begins with election: "Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of ’Imrân above all people ˹of their time˺". Four names and households are placed above the nations, and the last of them is the family into which Maryam will be born. The Prophet ﷺ is being comforted with predecessors, because disbelievers had doubted his prophethood, and the names prepare the reader for ʿĪsā, who follows immediately in the narrative.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of ’Imrân above all people ˹of their time˺"**: Allah preferred these households over the people of the earth, and over all the people of their own times. He preferred their very selves by making prophethood reside in them and in their progeny.

### What the choosing involved in each case

Allah chose Adam by creating him with His Hand and breathing life into him, commanding the angels to prostrate before him, teaching him the names of everything and letting him dwell in Paradise before sending him down from it out of His wisdom. He honoured Adam by that prostration of the angels.

He chose Nūḥ (Noah) as earth's first messenger, sent when idols were worshipped and partners were associated with Allah. Nūḥ preached day and night, publicly and privately, across an immense period, but distance only grew. His supplication followed, the flood drowned his people, and survival belonged solely to his followers.

He chose the household of Ibrāhīm (Abraham) by placing prophethood in his children, and the household includes the master of all mankind and the Final Prophet, Muhammad ﷺ. He chose the household of ʿImrān, the father of Maryam, mother of ʿĪsā, and the choice is also a choice of Jesus through his mother. ʿĪsā is from the offspring of Ibrāhīm, as will be shown in Surah Al-An'am.

When the Jews heard this, they said, "We follow the religion of Adam, we are Muslims", and the answer named choice after choice in Islam: Adam preferred with Islam, Nūḥ with Islam, the children of Ibrāhīm with Islam, and the family of ʿImrān, that is Moses and Aaron, with Islam, outranking contemporaries. Another view denies that this ʿImrān was father to Moses and Aaron.

The brief reference serves the Prophet ﷺ directly. Since disbelievers would not obey him because they doubted his prophethood, names of past prophets were cited to remove the doubt. ʿĪsā is singled out for fuller identification because he will come again to this world and work with the followers of the Prophet ﷺ, so Muslims need to know who he is.

### In short

- Adam, Nūḥ, the family of Ibrāhīm and the family of ʿImrān were chosen above the people of their times.
- The honour includes creation, prostration, first messengership, prophethood in Abraham's children, and Maryam's line.
- The names console the Prophet ﷺ and prepare for the story of ʿĪsā.

34.text:
The next verse ties the households together: "They are descendants of one another. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing." The chosen are not scattered favourites. They form one line of descent and one pattern of religion, and Allah hears both the claims made about them and the truth of those who actually follow them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"They are descendants of one another"**: the seed of one is offspring from another. Some follow the religion of the others, and the offspring of some are the descendants of others. These prophets and their followers were one family in declaring Allah's Oneness and doing good, and they passed noble character and virtues to one another.

**"And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing"**: statements from servants reach His hearing and their deeds fall under His knowledge, so selection remains His. Applied to Jewish claims of being Allah's children, beloved people and followers of His religion, He also knows their punishment and recognises genuine followers.

### Chosen is given, not inherited by blood alone

Adam and his seed are made of the same substance, yet the characteristic of being chosen, iṣṭifāʾ, comes from Allah and not from lineage or relation. The family connection is real, but it is not the cause of election. These houses are singled out because Allah set prophethood in their progeny and sustained Oneness and virtue through them. Descent explains how one messenger can be offspring of another. It does not explain why one is chosen, and the verse joins the genealogy directly to hearing and knowing so that the cause stays with Allah's choice rather than with human pedigree.

### In short

- The prophets and their followers are one continuous family in descent, in the declaration of Oneness and in inherited virtue.
- Allah Hears the claims people make about these families and Knows who actually follows their religion.
- Election itself, iṣṭifāʾ, is a gift from Allah, not a product of lineage.

35.text:
A vow opens Maryam's story: "˹Remember˺ when the wife of ’Imrân said, “My Lord! I dedicate what is in my womb entirely to Your service, so accept it from me. You ˹alone˺ are truly the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.”" The woman was Hannah, the mother of Maryam, and she made the vow before she knew whether the child was male or female. The dedication expected a servant of the sanctuary, and the prayer asks only for acceptance.

### Phrase by phrase

**"˹Remember˺ when the wife of ’Imrân said"**: remember, O Muhammad, when Hannah, the mother of Mary, spoke. She is introduced by her husband's name, while the coming verses show that the vow, the naming and the prayer of refuge are hers.

**"My Lord! I dedicate what is in my womb entirely to Your service"**: my unborn child is vowed as a consecrated offering, to serve Jerusalem's Sanctuary. Earlier prophetic codes allowed one child to be released from worldly work and assigned wholly to Allah, worshipping Him and attending His House without worldly chores. The newborn was expected to serve Bayt Al-Maqdis, Jerusalem's mosque, in God's way.

**"so accept it from me. You ˹alone˺ are truly the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.”"**: You hear my supplication and You know my intention. He is the Hearer of prayers and the Knower of the answer and of what lies in the womb. She did not know then whether she would bear a male or a female.

### How Hannah came to make the vow

Muḥammad bin Ishaq says childlessness preceded the vow. Hannah watched a bird feeding its chick, longed for offspring and begged Allah for a child. Her supplication was accepted, intercourse with her husband followed, and pregnancy began. A second narration makes her elderly before the longing, prayer and first awareness of conception. ʿImrān died while she was still pregnant.

When she became aware of her pregnancy, she made the child over to worship and service of Bayt Al-Maqdis. Her motherly authority is itself noted here. A mother holds a measure of guardianship over her child in education and training. She would never have vowed if she had no right of guardianship, and the naming in the next verse proves that a mother also has the right to give her child a name.

### In short

- Hannah, long childless, prayed for offspring and vowed the unborn child entirely to the service of Bayt Al-Maqdis.
- She expected to dedicate a servant of the sanctuary without knowing the child's sex, while ʿImrān died during the pregnancy.
- The vow implies a mother's guardianship in training and makes her the one who seeks acceptance directly from Allah.

36.text:
Birth confounds the vow's expectation: "When she delivered, she said, “My Lord! I have given birth to a girl,”—and Allah fully knew what she had delivered—“and the male is not like the female. I have named her Mary, and I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan, the accursed.”" Hannah had hoped for a boy because only males were consecrated for service. She apologised for a girl, and Allah accepted this very girl and made her distinct from every other girl in the world.

### Phrase by phrase

**"When she delivered, she said, “My Lord! I have given birth to a girl,”"**: when she was delivered of what was in her womb, it was a baby girl. She had been hoping for a boy, because only males were consecrated to the service of God.

**"and Allah fully knew what she had delivered"**: what she bore was already perfectly known to God. A variant reading makes the words Hannah's confession: "God knows very well what I have given birth to."

**"and the male is not like the female"**: the male she asked for is not as the female bestowed on her. He was designed for the service of God, while she might seem unsuitable in strength and in the commitment to worship Allah and serve the mosque in Jerusalem, because of lesser physical ability, her private parts and the effects of menstruation. In the simpler phrasing, the male is not like the female in service and in weakness.

**"I have named her Mary"**: she gave her the name Maryam. A mother has the right to name her child, and the ayat testifies that a newborn may be named on the day of birth, as part of the law of those before us.

**"and I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan, the accursed”"**: I crave Your protection and safety for her and for her seed, her children, from the outcast and accursed Satan. The offspring meant is ʿĪsā.

### Naming a child on the day of birth

The Prophet's Sunnah confirms the practice. He announced, "This night, a son was born for me and I called him by my father's name, Ibrahim." Both al-Bukhārī and Muslim preserve it. Anas bin Malik's newborn brother likewise received a date chewed by the Prophet ﷺ placed in his mouth and was named ʿAbdullāh, and other infants were named on their birth day.

Naming belongs with another rite. Through Qatādah and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Samurah bin Jundub reports: "Every new born boy held in security by his 'Aqiqah, until his seventh day, a sacrifice is offered on his behalf, he is given a name, and the hair on his head is shaved." Aḥmad and the Sunan collectors preserve the hadith, and at-Tirmidhī graded it Ṣaḥīḥ. A second wording, "and blood is offered on his behalf", is described as more famous and established, and Allah knows best.

### The one child Satan could not touch

Allah accepted Hannah's supplication for refuge. ʿAbd ar-Razzāq recorded that Abū Hurayrah said the Messenger of Allah ﷺ declared, "Every newly born baby is touched by Shaytan when it is born, and the baby starts crying because of this touch, except Maryam and her son." Abū Hurayrah then said, "Read if you will: 'And I seek refuge with You for her and for her offspring from Shaytan, the outcast.'" The same statement is reported by the two Shaykhs, al-Bukhārī and Muslim: "Every new-born is touched by Satan and begins life by crying except for Mary and her son."

### Consecrated means free of every other master

A consecrated person, muḥarrar, owes bondage to no creature. God's prior decree frees such a one from preoccupation with anything besides the Real across every state. Hannah felt shame when the promised consecration produced a girl apparently unable to serve. Yet God's knowledge of the child exposed the comparison: maleness and femaleness differ outwardly, but acceptance caused miracles to flow from Maryam. Her plea succeeded in both daughter and son. Their story saved one company and destroyed another through trial, fitna. Even her prayer for refuge has an inward edge: protection was sought from God against any Satanic element hiding in her own speech.

Acceptance left visible effects in Maryam and her son. Through the pair, one company found salvation while another met destruction and trial, fitna. Even the refuge clause turns inward: she asked God to guard her speech itself from anything Satanic.

### In short

- Hannah apologised for a girl, expecting only boys to serve, yet Allah accepted Maryam and set her apart from every other girl.
- Maryam was named at birth, a practice the Prophet ﷺ confirmed, and naming is joined to the ʿaqīqah, its sacrifice and the shaving of the head on the seventh day.
- The prayer for refuge was answered visibly: Maryam and her son are the exception to Satan's touch at birth.

37.text:
The acceptance becomes visible at once: "So her Lord accepted her graciously and blessed her with a pleasant upbringing—entrusting her to the care of Zachariah. Whenever Zachariah visited her in the sanctuary, he found her supplied with provisions. He exclaimed, “O Mary! Where did this come from?” She replied, “It is from Allah. Surely Allah provides for whoever He wills without limit.”" Maryam grows under a prophet's care, in a room in the sanctuary, with food that does not follow the seasons.

### Phrase by phrase

**"So her Lord accepted her graciously and blessed her with a pleasant upbringing"**: He received Maryam from her mother with goodly acceptance as a result of the vow. He made her grow in a good manner, making her conduct becoming and her mannerism delightful, and He made her well liked among people. She would grow in a day by as much as a newborn grew during a year. She accompanied the righteous so she could learn righteousness, knowledge and religion.

**"entrusting her to the care of Zachariah"**: Allah made Zakariyya her sponsor and guardian for her benefit, so she could learn from his tremendous knowledge and righteous conduct. A variant reading makes the direction explicit: kaffalahā, "He gave Zakariyya charge of her", with God as the subject of the verb.

**"Whenever Zachariah visited her in the sanctuary, he found her supplied with provisions"**: every time he entered the miḥrāb, the sanctuary, the room and most noble seat in the temple where she worshipped, he found sustenance already with her.

**"He exclaimed, “O Mary! Where did this come from?” She replied, “It is from Allah. Surely Allah provides for whoever He wills without limit.”"**: she said, still very young, "From God. He sends it to me from Paradise." God provides abundantly, without reckoning and without consequence, for whomever He wills, in season or out of it.

### How Zakariyya became her guardian

To fulfil the vow, Maryam's mother brought her to Bayt Al-Maqdis and addressed its caretakers and worshippers, including Zakariyya. The dedicated child could not remain at home, so she asked them to receive her. Before the priests who kept Jerusalem's Holy House she declared, "This here before you is the dedication I offered." 

Guardianship became a contest because the imam's daughter had arrived. ʿImrān, the mosque's imam, had died during the pregnancy, although fatherhood and office would have made him the natural guardian. Zakariyya argued kinship: his wife was Maryam's maternal aunt and nearest female relative after mother. The others rejected automatic preference. Twenty-nine men went to the River Jordan and cast quills, stipulating that the one that stayed fast and surfaced would win. Zakariyya's quill did exactly that.

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Jarir call Zakariyya the husband of Maryam's maternal aunt. Another description makes him her brother-in-law, supported by the Ṣaḥīḥ phrase, "I saw John and 'Isa, who are maternal cousins." Ibn Ishaq's version is judged plausible, meaning an aunt raised Maryam. Two Sahihs show the same principle in the Prophet's decision that ʿAmārah bint Ḥamzah live with her maternal aunt, Jaʿfar bin Abi Talib's wife: "The maternal aunt is just like the mother." 

Zakariyya built a ladder-accessed gallery room inside the temple, visited by nobody else. Reports disagree on nursing: one uses a wet-nurse, another says Maryam needed no suckling and soon sat and walked. Her dwelling stood beside the mosque in a good house. Zakariyya locked it when leaving and unlocked it upon returning, while supplying food, drink and oil.

### Fruit out of season

One repeated observation about provisions assigns seasons in reverse. As-Suddī, ʿAtiyyah al-ʿAwfī, ar-Rabīʿ bin Anas, Qatādah, ad-Daḥḥāk, Ibrāhīm an-Nakhaʿī, Abū ash-Shaʿthāʾ, Saʿīd bin Jubayr, ʿIkrimah and Mujāhid all describe summer fruits appearing in winter and winter fruits in summer. Corn culms and out-of-season grapes illustrate the inversion. Another telling credits Gabriel with bringing them. God gives continuously, in abundant measure and without inconvenience to whomever He chooses.

### What gracious acceptance looked like

Maryam received more than her mother had even wished. Gracious acceptance, qabūl ḥasan, may mean a singular obedience entrusted to her as God entrusts His friends, awliyāʾ. Contemporaries marvelled that so excellent a trust, ḥusn, belonged to a girl. Alternatively, graciousness lay in perfect care despite advance knowledge of slander that would touch God's name because of her. Enemy shaming does not concern Him. Passion can even savour blame when it occasions mention of the Beloved, careless of whoever speaks.

Acceptance also protected her from sin and error, ʿiṣma, until her later declaration, "Lo! I seek refuge in the Compassionate One from you! If you fear God" (19:18). Growth became straight obedience, constant preference for His pleasure, and eventually a fruit named ʿĪsā. A prophet's guardianship formed part of the gift, since Zakariyya supervised and protected her affairs. A revelation to Dāwūd (David) says: "If you see someone seeking Me, become a servant to him," in Arabic, in raʾayta lī Ṭāliban fa-kun lahu khādiman. Another sign is location: Maryam could only be found in the sanctuary, the miḥrāb. Servants who remain where worship occurs are rare and precious.

### In short

- Maryam was accepted, grew beautifully among the righteous, and was placed with Zakariyya, her maternal aunt's husband, after twenty-nine keepers cast quills in the Jordan.
- In her sanctuary room he found summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer, and she answered that it was from Allah, who provides without limit.
- Her gracious acceptance meant unique obedience, preservation, a prophet's guardianship, and a life found only in the miḥrāb.

38.text:
Seeing Maryam's provisions moved her guardian to pray for the impossible: "Then and there Zachariah prayed to his Lord, saying, “My Lord! Grant me—by your grace—righteous offspring. You are certainly the Hearer of ˹all˺ prayers.”" Zakariyya was an old man with feeble bones and a head full of gray hair, and his wife was old and barren. Until he watched fruit arrive out of season, he had not had the courage to extend the hand of prayer for a child.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Then and there Zachariah prayed to his Lord"**: at that point, upon entering the sanctuary to pray in the middle of the night, he called on his Lord in secret. Seeing provision outside its season taught him that natural timing does not bind the One who governs it. An old man could receive a child even after his family line had died out.

**"saying, “My Lord! Grant me—by your grace—righteous offspring"**: grant me from You, from Ladunka, a good offspring, meaning a righteous child.

**"You are certainly the Hearer of ˹all˺ prayers.”"**: You are the All-Hearer of invocation, the One who hears the prayer of the one who prays and knows his condition, and answers prayers.

### What gave him courage to ask

Zakariyya firmly believed Allah could change the usual course of things and bless him at an advanced age. What he lacked was a witnessed instance. When he saw unusual and out-of-season food provided for Maryam, he was persuaded: Allah who gives a servant fruit out of season can also give an old man offspring in late age. He saw the special gift, karāma, shown to her and grew increasingly certain and hopeful, so he asked for a son in spite of his age, and the granting of such a request is a rupture of ordinary reality, naqḍ al-ʿāda.

His request also had its aim. It is said that he asked for a son to help him in obedience and to be an heir from his progeny in prophethood, upholding God's right, ḥaqq Allāh. Requests belonging to the Real, ḥaqq al-ḥaqq, rather than the lower self's worldly share, ḥaẓẓ al-nafs, are not refused. Zakariyya wanted the old-age son to be a sign, āya, and a miracle, muʿjiza.

### Praying for children is the practice of prophets

This verse also teaches that asking Allah for children is a blessed practice of the prophets and the righteous. Allah said, "And We sent messengers before you and provided them with wives and children" (13:38), making children among the blessings bestowed on the Prophet ﷺ and on other prophets. Whoever tries to stop the birth of children rebels against nature and deprives himself of harmony with the common practice of prophets. The Prophet of Islam ﷺ gave marriage and children such importance that he allowed no capable person to avoid married life and remain counted among his followers:

1. "Marriage is my sunnah (way)."
2. "So, whoever turns away from my sunnah, he is not from me."
3. "Therefore, marry a woman who is loving and fertile, for I shall compete with other communities on the basis of your numbers."

Allah praises those who pray for family righteousness: "And those who say: 'O our Lord, bless us with such among our wives and our children as be the delight of our eyes'" (25:74). Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī explained "delight of the eyes", qurrata aʿyun, as seeing one's wife and children devoted in obedience to Allah. Umm Sulaym asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for his attendant Anas, and he prayed, "O Allah, increase his wealth and his children and make him prosper in what You have bestowed on him." Anas ended with about a hundred children and ample wealth, as the outcome of that prayer.

### In short

- Maryam's out-of-season provision persuaded old, childless Zakariyya to ask for a righteous son, trusting the Hearer of prayers.
- Praying for children belongs to the prophets' practice, and marriage with a loving and fertile spouse is praised, not shunned (13:38, 25:74).
- His request sought an heir in obedience and prophethood, a matter of God's right rather than the lower self's share.

39.text:
The answer came while prayer was still in progress: "So the angels called out to him while he stood praying in the sanctuary, “Allah gives you good news of ˹the birth of˺ John who will confirm the Word of Allah and will be a great leader, chaste, and a prophet among the righteous.”" The angels spoke to him directly as he stood secluded at his place of worship. The child promised has a name, a mission and three qualities, and the promise of prophethood is better news than the promise of birth.

### Phrase by phrase

**"So the angels called out to him while he stood praying in the sanctuary"**: the angels, that is Gabriel, called to him as he stood praying in the miḥrāb, the sanctuary in the temple, in the mosque, at worship. A variant reading makes the call a direct statement, "God gives you good tidings", read yubashshiruka or yubshiruka.

**"Allah gives you good news of ˹the birth of˺ John"**: glad tidings of a child from your offspring, and his name is Yaḥyā. Qatādah and other scholars said he was called Yaḥyā, literally "he lives", because Allah filled his life with faith.

**"who will confirm the Word of Allah"**: he believes in the Word sent from Allah, namely ʿĪsā, son of Maryam. The attribution runs widely: ad-Daḥḥāk, ar-Rabīʿ bin Anas, as-Suddī, Abū ash-Shaʿthāʾ, Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah, Qatādah, al-Ḥasan and several others join Ibn ʿAbbās through al-ʿAwfī. ʿĪsā is called God's Word because creation came through kun, "Be", and God's Spirit denotes his fatherless origin.

**"and will be a great leader, chaste"**: Sayyid and Ḥaṣūr. The Sayyid is explained in many ways. Abū al-ʿĀliyah, ar-Rabīʿ bin Anas, Qatādah and Saʿīd bin Jubayr said he is a wise man. Ibn ʿAbbās, ath-Thawrī and ad-Daḥḥāk said the noble, wise and pious man. Saʿīd bin Al-Musayyib said the Sayyid is the scholar and jurist, the faqih. ʿAtiyah said the man noble in behaviour and piety. ʿIkrimah said a person not overcome by anger. Ibn Zayd said the noble man. Mujāhid said one honoured by Allah. He will be a leader of his people through his knowledge and worship.

**"and a prophet among the righteous.”"**: this is further good news, sending Yaḥyā as a prophet after announcing his birth. Allah said the same thing in a harder case, to the mother of Mūsā (Moses): "Verily, We shall bring him back to you, and shall make him one of the Messengers" (28:7).

### What "chaste" means for Yaḥyā

Ḥaṣūr does not mean that Yaḥyā would refrain from lawful relations with women. It means he is immune from illegal sexual relations. It does not follow that he would not marry and have lawful relations, since Zakariyya prayed for a good offspring, a son who would himself have offspring, and Allah knows best. In another telling he is chaste as having no desire for women, forbidden from women, and it is said he never sinned and never intended to.

Abstinence is the wider gloss: he was particular about shielding himself from temptations and habitual enjoyments, even from permitted things such as good food, fine dress and marital life. Because this quality is praised here, abstinence appears to be the better way, yet sound reports prove the higher merit of marriage. The considered opinion is that both stand, for different people. One who is so absorbed in the life to come that he feels no need of a wife and has neither time nor frame of mind to fulfil the rights of wife and children does better to abstain, as Yaḥyā did. One who can marry and is capable of fulfilling his wife's due rights should marry, for that is better for him. Otherwise he is not advised to marry.

### The inward portrait of Yaḥyā

Petitioners should stay at the door. Anyone seeking something from kings remains there until an answer arrives, so Allah gives requests to people who embrace His service, khidma, while turning away from obedience sinks a person into estrangement's lowliness.

Three etymologies explain Yaḥyā. His heart's life, ḥayāt, through God may supply it. His mother's barrenness may have been revived, ḥayy, through him. Or believers' hearts quicken to life through him. Confirming God's word can mean confirming Allah's own word used in worship, or existing because God's word brought him into being.

A Sayyid, lord, is captive to no created thing. Freedom, taḥarrara, from whims and creatures defines him. He may embody actualised servanthood, ʿubūdiyya, outrank his contemporaries, as Yaḥyā did, or seek no rank and assign himself no worth. Humility before God then raises him over the group as its lord. Chastity frees him from passions and human carnal traits, guards the lower self through exaltation and nearness, and follows realities uprooting worldly preferences. Prophethood among the righteous confirms his worthiness for their rank.

### In short

- Yaḥyā's name, his confirmation of ʿĪsā the Word, his wise and noble leadership, his chastity and his prophethood are all announced before his birth.
- Chastity, ḥaṣūr, is immunity from unlawful relations and freedom from desire's grip, and it suits one absorbed in the next life, while marriage remains better for the capable.
- Inwardly Yaḥyā is a lord because he is no creature's captive, and a servant because his servanthood, ʿubūdiyya, is complete.

40.text:
Zakariyya's question sounds like doubt and is not: "Zachariah exclaimed, “My Lord! How can I have a son when I am very old and my wife is barren?” He replied, “So will it be. Allah does what He wills.”" He had prayed believing in Allah's absolute power and had seen its signs repeatedly. What he wanted to know was the state in which the promise would happen.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Zachariah exclaimed, “My Lord! How can I have a son when I am very old and my wife is barren?”"**: how can a boy arrive now that old age has overtaken me? Ages in the reports reach extremes: 120 years old for him and 98 for his wife. He addressed the words to Gabriel as "O master!", asking how a son could come when he was aged and his wife could not conceive.

**"He replied, “So will it be. Allah does what He wills.”"**: the matter remains exactly as announced, and God will create a boy from the two of you. John's creation, in spite of old age and barrenness, is in that respect like the creation of anything Allah wishes to create, even though ordinary custom says otherwise. His power extends over everything, and He does whatever He wills in His wisdom and knowledge.

### State, not possibility, is what he asked about

The reply settles the manner. They would remain at the same age, and they would have offspring in that very state. So the question was not unbelief. It asked whether present extreme old age would stay unchanged or be altered first. He was even inspired to ask it so that this great power would be manifested in the answer, and his soul longed for the swift fulfilment of what had been announced.

Inward alternatives widen the question. A long pause between prayer and answer may have prompted it. "By what right would a response come if not by Your favour?" suggests another meaning, and means could be meant as well: adoption or procreation. Perhaps another woman, even a slave concubine, was being contemplated because his wife was advanced too. The response closes those routes. Shared loneliness makes the son good news for both spouses.

### In short

- "How can I have a son?" asks about the state of fulfilment, not about Allah's power, and the answer is that the elderly couple would remain as they were.
- His age is given as 120 and his wife's as 98, so the birth is creation outside the ordinary by a will that nothing can prevent.
- Possible means, adoption, procreation or another woman, are inwardly narrowed to one: the son is for both of them together.

41.text:
A sign is requested for gratitude, not for proof: "Zachariah said, “My Lord! Grant me a sign.” He said, “Your sign is that you will not ˹be able to˺ speak to people for three days except through gestures. Remember your Lord often and glorify ˹Him˺ morning and evening.”" The sign is fitted to its purpose, because a man who cannot speak to people can do little else with his tongue but thank and remember.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Zachariah said, “My Lord! Grant me a sign.”"**: appoint for me a sign, an indication of my wife's pregnancy and a mark that alerts me that the child will come. His purpose was to rejoice at the prospect and show gratitude all along, even before the child's actual birth.

**"He said, “Your sign is that you will not ˹be able to˺ speak to people for three days except through gestures"**: for three days and nights he would refrain from speaking to men, but not from remembrance of God, save by tokens and gestures. He would not be able to speak except with signals, although he was not mute. The days are also given as nights: "For three nights, though having no bodily defect" (19:10). Gestures could use lips, eyebrows, eyes and hands, or writing on the ground.

**"Remember your Lord often and glorify ˹Him˺ morning and evening.”"**: remember Him with tongue and heart much, in all circumstances, and glorify Him by performing prayer at the end of the day and its beginning, in the early hours of night and morning, praying in the morning and at night as you used to do.

### Gesture as speech, and the gratitude the sign produces

The sign was remarkably suited to its purpose. His request came from a wish to show gratefulness. The sign leaves him incapable of anything but that, and a hundred other signs would not have done what this one did. The last phrase also establishes that where speech is impossible for a valid reason, gesture counts as its substitute. It appears in a hadith that the Prophet ﷺ asked a maid-servant, "Where is Allah?" She pointed toward the sky. He said, "This maid-servant is a Muslim." Al-Qurtubi transmitted that report.

### Three days of speech given to one Speaker

The sign redirects his audience. His tongue would be stopped from the people for three days, so secret whispering would belong to God and speech would speak of Him. By allusion, the promised child would be severed from world and creatures and have the face of his heart turned toward God. His qiblah would be the divine Presence and his ease would lie in conversing with Him. Name, image and passion become all that appear in speech, heart and eyes.

Zakariyya's command extends to the faithful: "And remember your Lord often" (8:45). Days are to be carried out in obedience and service, belonging totally to Him, calling on Him while knowing Him through all states and works. Ease should rest in His remembrance and message, joy in His name and mark. Do not pass God's house like a stranger without knocking on its door. If you talk, talk only of Him, and if you drink, drink only in remembrance of Him.

### The three degrees of remembrance

Remembrance of Allah has three degrees. The first is outward remembrance, with the tongue, in laudation and supplication: "And remember thy Lord often." The second is concealed remembrance in the heart: "Or with more intense remembrance" (2:200). The Prophet ﷺ said, "The best remembrance is the concealed and the best provision the sufficient." The third is true remembrance, which is witnessing God's remembrance of you: "And remember thy Lord when thou forgettest" (18:24).

### In short

- The sign of pregnancy is three days without speech to people, speech surviving only in gestures, writing and the remembrance of God (19:10).
- The sign fits its purpose perfectly, since a silenced tongue can do little besides show gratitude, and al-Qurtubi's hadith makes gesture a lawful substitute for speech.
- Remembrance itself climbs three degrees, from the tongue to the heart, to witnessing God's remembrance of you (8:45, 2:200, 18:24).

42.text:
The angels turn from the guardian to the ward: "And ˹remember˺ when the angels said, “O Mary! Surely Allah has selected you, purified you, and chosen you over all women of the world". Maryam is chosen twice in one sentence, and the hadiths that follow measure what that means: in her own time she had no equal among women, and in perfection she stands with one other woman in all history.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And ˹remember˺ when the angels said, “O Mary! Surely Allah has selected you"**: the angels spoke to Maryam by His command. The speaker is also given as Gabriel. Allah chose her because of her service to Him, her modesty, honour, innocence and conviction, and with Islam and worship.

**"purified you"**: He made her pure of the touch of men, pure from disbelief, from associating partners with Allah and from blemishes. It is also said this means He saved her from being killed.

**"and chosen you over all women of the world"**: He preferred her above the women of the nations, the inhabitants of her time, by the birth of Jesus. She is chosen because of her praiseworthy qualities and purified from all defects, over all the other women of her time.

### What the hadiths say about her rank

At-Tirmidhī recorded that ʿAlī bin Abi Talib said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, 'The best woman (in her time) was Maryam, daughter of 'Imran, and the best woman (of the Prophet's time) is Khadijah (his wife), daughter of Khuwaylid.'" The Two Sahihs recorded this hadith.

Ibn Jarir recorded Abū Mūsā Al-Ash'ari's report that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Many men achieved perfection, but among women, only Maryam the daughter of 'Imran and Asiah, the wife of Fir'awn, achieved perfection." The Six, apart from Abu Dawud, recorded it. Al-Bukhari's wording says:

> "Many men reached the level of perfection, but no woman reached such a level except Asiah, the wife of Fir'awn, and Maryam, the daughter of 'Imran. The superiority of 'A'ishah (his wife) to other women, is like the superiority of Tharid (meat and bread dish) to other meals."

The chains and wordings of this hadith are treated in the story of ʿĪsā, son of Maryam.

The phrase "women of all the worlds" is referred to all women in that period of time. On that basis the statement in hadith that Fāṭimah is the foremost among the women of Paradise does not contradict it.

### Why the choice is stated twice

This may begin a message elevating Maryam's state, whether she saw the angels or heard only a voice. Preference singled her out from her peers and kind. Purity removed indecency and sin with beautiful immunity and kept her from men's physical contact. Preference placed her over the women of her time. Repetition divides the honour. First come special gifts, position and exaltation. Then comes fatherless bearing of Jesus, unmatched by any woman until Resurrection Day. Hence "above all women of the worlds".

### In short

- Allah selected Maryam for her service, modesty, honour and conviction, purified her from defect and the touch of men, and chose her over the women of her time.
- At-Tirmidhī and the Two Sahihs rank her the best woman of her time, and Ibn Jarir's report gives perfection to her and Asiah alone among women.
- The doubled choosing ends in the unmatched second gift: bearing Jesus without a father.

43.text:
Election is answered with worship: "O Mary! Be devout to your Lord, prostrate yourself ˹in prayer˺ and bow along with those who bow down.” The angels told Maryam to multiply worship, humility, submission, prostration and bowing. Those acts prepared her for God's decree, and the test itself elevated her rank in this world and the hereafter.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O Mary! Be devout to your Lord"**: submit yourself with obedience, Aqnuti, to your Lord. Qunut means to submit with humbleness. It is read as prolonged prayer offered as a token of gratitude to Him, standing for long periods in prayer. Allah uses the same word for universal submission: "Nay, to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and on earth, and all surrender with obedience (Qanitun) to Him" (2:116).

**"prostrate yourself ˹in prayer˺"**: prostrate to your Lord. Prostration is commanded first and without qualification.

**"and bow along with those who bow down.”"**: bow down along with ar-Rākiʿīn, those who bow in worship, the people of worship, praying with those who pray, with His righteous servants who bow to Him, compliant before God.

### Prostration plain, bowing qualified

It is noticed that the command to bow carries a qualification that the command to prostrate does not: with those who bow. This seems to hint that people generally show less concern in their rukūʿ, bowing. They bend a little and then resume standing, as if in a hurry, and that kind of bowing is closer to standing, qiyām, than to bowing. By attaching "those who bow" to the command, Allah gives a model to follow, so that one's own bowing becomes like the bowing of those who bow fully and perfectly, as is due.

### Perseverance on the carpet of worship

Inward instruction matches rank. Stay on worship's carpet and keep practising obedience, never falling short in service, khidma. Singled out by station, she was to surpass her contemporaries in worship. Growth in devotion also prepared the demonstration of divine power: a son formed within her with no male intervention.

### In short

- Maryam is commanded to qunut, humble and prolonged devotion, then prostration, then bowing with the bowers (2:116).
- Bowing alone is qualified with a model, because hurried bowing slides back toward standing and must be learned from those who bow fully.
- Continuous service is both gratitude for election and preparation for the miracle decreed for her.

44.text:
The narrative closes by pointing at its own source: "This is news of the unseen that We reveal to you ˹O Prophet˺. You were not with them when they cast lots to decide who would be Mary’s guardian, nor were you there when they argued ˹about it˺". Muhammad ﷺ was not present when a guardian was chosen by lot in Jerusalem centuries earlier. The detail of the quarrel and the pens is itself offered as proof that the account came by revelation.

### Phrase by phrase

**"This is news of the unseen that We reveal to you ˹O Prophet˺"**: this is part of the news of the Ghayb, the Unseen, which We reveal and narrate to you, O Muhammad ﷺ. It was unknown to you. Gabriel is sent with it.

**"You were not with them when they cast lots to decide who would be Mary’s guardian"**: you were not present when they cast lots with their pens to decide which of them should be charged with her care and bring her up. You cannot narrate what happened as an eyewitness.

**"nor were you there when they argued ˹about it˺"**: you were not with them when custodianship became a dispute and every claimant argued his superiority. Allah disclosed events as if you had witnessed them.

### How the lots were cast, in the fuller report

Ibn Jarir records ʿIkrimah's account of Maryam's mother carrying the infant, wrapped in cloth, to rabbis descended from Aaron, brother of Musa. They administered Bayt Al-Maqdis then, as others administered the Kaʿbah. She offered the vowed child to them, declaring her free because a menstruating daughter should not enter the Masjid and would not be taken home. Their response turned on paternity: she was their Imam's daughter, and ʿImrān had led prayer and managed sacrificial rituals. Zakariyya replied that her maternal aunt was his wife. Because their hearts could not yield the Imam's daughter so readily, they used the pens with which they wrote the Tawrah for a lottery, and Zakariyya won her care. He was also master, chief, scholar, imam and prophet among them.

ʿIkrimah, as-Suddī, Qatādah, ar-Rabīʿ bin Anas and several others describe the mechanism in the river. The rabbis went into the Jordan and threw their pens in, deciding that the pen which remained afloat and idle would mark the man who would take care of Maryam. The water took all the pens under except Zakariyya's, which stayed afloat in its place. Another description of the prior agreement is that the owner of the pen which flows against the current would be the winner. They had argued first about custody before agreeing on the draw.

### Why the detail itself is the argument

These events belong to a remote past. The Prophet ﷺ had no likely way to see, hear or read them through ordinary channels available to him. The verse says he missed both the reed pens cast by agreement and the preceding quarrel over custody. Revelation therefore supplied the particulars as part of his message, and the account itself testifies to his prophethood. Being told these stories and their meanings in divine speech can be rarer and more perfect than personal witnessing.

### The law of drawing lots

The rule governing qurʿah, drawing lots, follows from the example. In the view of the Hanafi jurists, a lot cannot decide rights that are already known and fixed in Islamic law. Using it there counts as qimār, gambling. If several people jointly own something and a lot is drawn so that one takes the whole thing, that is not allowed. If a child's parentage is disputed, a lot cannot make one man the father. Where rights depend on opinion, lots are permissible. Portions of a joint property can be allotted by lot, A taking the eastern portion and B the western, because that could equally be done by mutual agreement or by a judge's decree. In short, where everyone's rights are equal and the lot only allocates equal portions and decides which portion belongs to whom, the draw is permissible.

### In short

- The Prophet ﷺ was absent from the quarrel and the casting of pens over Maryam's guardianship, so its details reach him only by revelation (ghayb).
- The reports put Zakariyya's pen afloat in the Jordan while the others sank, after the rabbis of Ārūn's line had argued over their imam's daughter.
- Lots may allocate equal shares, but they may not decide fixed legal rights or a child's parentage.

45.text:
The announcement interrupted by verse 44 now resumes: "˹Remember˺ when the angels proclaimed, “O Mary! Allah gives you good news of a Word from Him, his name will be the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary; honoured in this world and the Hereafter, and he will be one of those nearest ˹to Allah˺"". Maryam (Mary) receives a son who exists by a word, carries three names at once, and holds rank in both worlds. The account prepares the ground for the birth, mission and miracles of ʿĪsā.

### Phrase by phrase

**"˹Remember˺ when the angels proclaimed, “O Mary! Allah gives you good news of a Word from Him"**: Gabriel announces a son brought into being through Allah's word "Be". Most scholars connect him with Yaḥyā's promised belief in "the Word from Allah" (3:39). Maryam hears of no worldly portion or future fortune for herself, only a tremendous sign, a prophet and confirmation of a miracle.

**"his name will be the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary"**: Al-Masīḥ, ʿĪsā, son of Maryam, known by this name in this life especially among the believers. He was called Al-Masīḥ because when he touched, mash, those afflicted with illness, they were healed by Allah's leave. The Messiah is also said to mean one who travels from country to country, or a king. He is attributed to his mother because he had no father, against the custom of attributing a child to its father, so that his fatherless birth is announced in his very name.

**"honoured in this world and the Hereafter, and he will be one of those nearest ˹to Allah˺"**: he will be a leader honoured by Allah in this life through the law revealed to him, the Scripture sent down to him and other bounties, illustrious among people with standing and position. In the Hereafter he has standing and position with Allah, high stations, and will intercede, by His leave, on behalf of some people, as his brethren the mighty messengers do. He is one of those brought near to Allah in the Garden of Eden.

### The caress inside the announcement

The universe's God, who enacts the world's folk, assigns provisions and bestows bounty, lovingly caresses His friends. Here He separates Maryam from other women and honours her. His first gift is address: "O Mary." How exalted that vocative and call are. Prophets and friends by the thousands have passed away either resting in its discovery or lingering in remorseful hope.

The asymmetry of address is then turned into a teaching. O spirit of the world, if you call on Him a thousand times saying "My Lord, my Lord", that is not like His calling on you once: "My servant, My servant." Your accepting Him in lordhood gains you nothing, because His lordhood is inseparable from you in any case. What does the work is His accepting you for servanthood, once. Abū Yazīd BasṬāmī said that God stood him before Him in a thousand standing places, presenting the empire to him, and he kept saying, "I do not desire it." In the last standing place He asked, "O Abū Yazīd, what do you desire?" He said, "I desire not to desire", meaning I desire what You desire. Then He said, "You are My servant in truth."

Those unable to address God with Abū Yazīd's boldness can still bring needs, burning and hope. "O Lord, a name and mark is enough for me! You have come from Your threshold to place a name on me. Whatever name You want, let it be." At a bazaar, a would-be slave buyer selected a man and asked his name. The answer was, "First buy me so that I may belong to you. Then call me by whatever name you want." 

Her heart was strengthened by hearing her son's future in step-by-step detail. Divine power's overwhelming force, qudra, brings a person before His ruling, ḥukm, and miracles beyond anyone's experience follow. Maryam's reputation for chastity was excellent, but circumstances made her appear blameworthy to confused observers. Foolish eyes missed jaryān al-taqdīr, the decree flowing beneath appearances.

### In short

- The son promised exists by Allah's word "Be", is named Al-Masīḥ, ʿĪsā, son of Maryam, and holds honour and nearness in both worlds.
- "Son of Maryam" itself proclaims the miracle: he is attributed to his mother because he had no father.
- The announcement is read as divine caress: being called "My servant" once outweighs a thousand calls of "My Lord", as Abū Yazīd's thousand standings show.

46.text:
The promise adds speech at both ends of life: "And he will speak to people in ˹his˺ infancy and adulthood and will be one of the righteous.”" In the cradle he will call people to worship Allah alone, as a miracle. In manhood he will speak by Allah's revelation. Between those two speeches stands the charge against his mother, which the first of them was sent to answer.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And he will speak to people in ˹his˺ infancy"**: he will speak while still in the cradle, in the lap of his mother, saying, "I am the servant of Allah and His Messiah." Speaking in infancy was certainly a sign and a miracle. When people chided Maryam after the birth on a false accusation, the newborn ʿĪsā spoke up: "I am a servant of Allah."

**"and adulthood"**: and in his manhood, after he reaches thirty years old, saying that he is a prophet. Adult speech sounds ordinary, so its inclusion demands explanation, taken up below.

**"and will be one of the righteous.”"**: of the righteous in his statements and actions, one of the messengers, possessing pure knowledge and righteous works, telling people what is best for them in their religious and worldly affairs.

### The infants who spoke in the cradle

Two hadith reports narrow the cradle-speakers. Muḥammad bin Ishaq recorded that Abū Hurayrah said the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stated, "No infant spoke in the cradle except 'Isa and the companion of Jurayj." Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded that Abū Hurayrah said the Prophet ﷺ declared, "No infant spoke in the cradle except three, 'Isa, the boy during the time of Jurayj, and another boy."

### Why mention speech in manhood at all?

Speaking to people during middle age is something everyone does, Muslim or non-Muslim, learned or illiterate, so why list it as a distinction? One answer is that its purpose is to sharpen the infant speech. The reference to middle age tells us the childhood speech would not be baby-talk. It would be rational, learned and eloquent, the speech of a man in advanced years.

History supplies another answer. Reports on his ascension put ʿĪsā at roughly thirty to thirty-five, still in youth's prime. Kahl, middle age, therefore never occurred during his earthly life before ascension. Middle-aged speech must await a renewed presence here, making it miraculous like infancy speech. Inwardly, "his manhood" is likewise interpreted as after his descent from heaven.

Fortification was a nearer purpose. Details about her son, including enemies' ineffective deception, were disclosed sequentially. Maryam would remain silent concerning her innocence after childbirth, while God made Jesus speak from childhood. His speech would prove sincerity and exalted honour for her.

### In short

- ʿĪsā will speak in the cradle as a miracle, declaring himself Allah's servant, and in manhood by revelation, righteous in word and action.
- Only Jesus, the companion of Jurayj and one more boy are said to have spoken as infants.
- Speech in middle age is named because he left this world at about thirty to thirty-five, so such speech awaits his descent, and because his infant words would already be learned and eloquent.

47.text:
The mother answers with a question about means: "Mary wondered, “My Lord! How can I have a child when no man has ever touched me?” An angel replied, “So will it be. Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He simply tells it, ‘Be!’ And it is"". She had not married, did not intend to marry, and was not an indecent woman. The answer removes the need for any of those routes.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Mary wondered, “My Lord! How can I have a child when no man has ever touched me?”"**: speaking to Gabriel as "O master!", Maryam asks how a child can exist when no mortal approached her either lawfully or unlawfully, conjugally or otherwise. Is God performing a miracle, or will marriage be requested?

**"An angel replied, “So will it be. Allah creates what He wills"**: Gabriel conveyed Allah's answer: so it will be, as I have told you. God will create from you a child without a father. The word "create" is used here rather than "does", as in the account of Zakariyya (3:40), precisely to eradicate any evil thought concerning ʿĪsā.

**"When He decrees a matter, He simply tells it, ‘Be!’ And it is"**: when He has decreed a thing, willing its creation, He says to it only "Be", and it is. What Allah wills comes into existence instantly and without delay. "And Our commandment is but one as the twinkling of an eye" (54:50), meaning the command is issued once and existence follows as fast as, and faster than, a blink.

His will alone can originate anything, without medium or cause. Originating and producing things impose no difficulty. When He desires a ruling, ḥukm, it only needs "Be".

### The same break with ordinary reality she had already seen

Inwardly, her sanctuary had prepared the pattern. Provisions there already broke ordinary reality's rules, and a son created without a man's touch would do the same. Blame after birth triggered a further break: one-day-old Jesus spoke, saying, "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord" (3:49).

### In short

- Maryam asks about means, not possibility: she neither married nor intended marriage, and the answer leaves no human route in place.
- Allah "creates" rather than "does" here, cutting off evil suspicion, and His decree is a single "Be", faster than the twinkling of an eye (54:50).
- The fatherless birth repeats a pattern she had already witnessed in provisions that broke ordinary reality.

48.text:
The education of the promised son is announced with the birth: "And Allah will teach him writing and wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel". He will be taught the Book, al-Ḥikmah, the Tawrah given to Mūsā (Moses), and the Injīl given to himself, and he memorised both books. The teaching is part of the good news, because the miracles that follow stand on it.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And Allah will teach him writing"**: the Book here appears to refer to writing, or to the Scriptures of past prophets. A variant reading changes the voice: nuʿallimuhu, "We will teach him", or yuʿallimuhu, "He will teach him". He will be taught to say and do things correctly.

**"and wisdom"**: al-Ḥikmah is the lawful and the prohibited, or the wisdom of the prophets who preceded him.

**"the Torah and the Gospel"**: Mūsā, son of ʿImrān, received the Tawrah from Allah. ʿĪsā, son of Maryam, received the Injīl, and memorised the two books. An odd division places Torah learning in his mother's womb and Gospel learning after emergence. Direct learning from Allah is the august virtue at work.

### Cradle speech against two future slanders

Foreknowledge shaped the cradle speech. Christians would later exaggerate Jesus, so his infancy words answer them in advance: "Surely I am the servant of God" (19:30). He means that God created him and remains his Lord. Critics of his mother receive a parallel rebuke in "O sister of Aaron! Your father was..." (19:28). Divine innocence was declared for her, and infant speech brightened her eyes with vindication.

Pain and joy are paired deliberately. Jesus would brighten Mary's eyes and gladden her heart in both worlds, so birth burden belonged at the start: "And the birth pangs took her to..." (19:23). Suffering made a due incumbent for her, and blessings with ease arrived as its counterpart.

MuṣṬafā's mother presents the inverse. God knew she would possess no portion of him here or hereafter, so birth imposed no comparable burden and created no due. The pattern reaches Noah's and Muṣṭafā's communities: Nūḥ was told, "Do not let yourself suffer for the..." (11:36), then prayed, "My Lord, leave no disbeliever dwelling on..." (71:26), and God acted.

MuṣṬafā's state with his mother was the opposite. In God's knowledge his mother would have no portion of him in this world or the next, so He did not place the burden of Muṣṭafā upon her, and no suffering reached her at his birth, lest a rightful due become incumbent for her. The same pattern is set out in the stories of Noah and Muṣṭafā and their communities. It was said to Nūḥ (Noah), "Do not let yourself suffer for the..." (11:36), and in keeping with that address he supplicated, "My Lord, leave no disbeliever dwelling on..." (71:26), and God did that.

A transfer of trust lies behind the education. Jews had borne divine guidance, following God's path and communicating it, until later corruption made them unworthy. God removed that trust to Abraham's other branch, Banū Ismāʿīl. Before enforcement, their untrustworthiness had to be demonstrated. Jesus's extraordinary birth and miracles were sent to convince Jews that God had commissioned him and that his speech came from God.

### In short

- ʿĪsā will be taught writing, wisdom, the Torah of Mūsā and his own Gospel, and he memorised both.
- His infant speech was given in advance against Christian exaggeration and against his mother's critics (19:30, 19:28).
- Mary's birth pangs created a due that blessings answered, the opposite of the burden-free birth of Muṣṭafā.

49.text:
The mission begins with a speech of signs: "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord". A clay bird will live, the blind and leper will be healed, the dead will rise, and hidden stores will be disclosed, each by Allah's Will. Four miracles are enumerated, and each returns its power to Allah's leave, so that the performer cannot be turned into a god.

### Phrase by phrase

**"and ˹make him˺ a messenger to the Children of Israel ˹to proclaim,˺ ‘I have come to you with a sign from your Lord"**: Allah sends ʿĪsā to Israel in tender years or after puberty with evidence of truthfulness. Gabriel had breathed into the opening of her garment, she became pregnant, and Surah Maryam tells later events. His opening self-announcement is, "I am God's Messenger to you." 

**"I will make for you a bird from clay, breathe into it, and it will become a ˹real˺ bird—by Allah’s Will"**: clay is shaped into a bird's likeness, breathed into as a sleeper breathes, and rises flying by Allah's command. The miracle testifies that He sent him.

**"I will heal the blind and the leper and raise the dead to life—by Allah’s Will"**: I heal the akmah, the one born blind, which perfects the miracle and makes the challenge more daring. The leper has a known disease. Both afflictions leave a person completely helpless, so they are singled out. Raising the dead is repeated "by Allah's leave" to preclude false attributions of divinity to him.

**"And I will prophesize what you eat and store in your houses"**: unseen meals and stores become reportable. He tells one person what was eaten recently and what is kept for tomorrow, across morning and night and from lunch to dinner to next day's lunch, without ever seeing it.

**"Surely in this is a sign for you if you ˹truly˺ believe"**: in all this is a sign testifying to the truth of what he was sent with, for those who believe, who wish to have faith and accept the proof.

### What happened when the signs were shown

His clay creation was a bat, the bird described as most perfectly formed. Spectators watched flight until distance hid it, at which point death followed. That boundary distinguishes Jesus's creaturely making from divine creation and points perfection solely to God. Life in clay still prompted cries of sorcery and demands for more signs.

Through supplication he healed fifty thousand in one day, conditioned on each becoming a believer. Raised dead include his friend ʿĀzar, an old woman's son and a tithe-collector's daughter, all living onward and producing offspring. Shem, Nūḥ's son, rose only to die immediately. Reports of eaten and future food completed what audiences had not seen.

### Miracles fitted to their age

Many commentators match prophetic miracles to historical circumstances. Magic dominated Mūsā's age and elevated magicians. Moses received a sign that captured eyes and bewildered professionals. Recognising the Almighty source, magicians believed and became pious. Jesus arrived amid advances in medicine and physics and performed what no physician can: animating clay, curing blindness and leprosy, and recalling the entombed. Muhammad ﷺ confronted eloquent poets with God's Book. Humans and jinn, even collectively, cannot imitate ten chapters or one, because Qur'anic speech is Allah's Word rather than creaturely language.

The signs were outward and dazzling, overpowering proofs: life to the dead, healing of the blind and the leper, disclosure of what people did secretly, and other miracles. But the proof only works on a willing reader. Extraordinary signs and astonishing speech cannot force a person whose prestige blocks the truth. The unbelievers of his time had become insensitive and insolent, and although the proofs were very clear they refused to believe in him. The sign makes sense to one who wants to believe, can come out of himself and ponder its veracity without letting personal prestige obstruct acceptance.

Astonishing speech reinforced signs. Effective, persuasive and logical expression had no equal in his era. As Luke records, "all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers" (Luke 2:47). Fatherless birth might have invited abuse, but his miraculous personality and speech forestalled it. His teaching stood in the same line: he was taught the Torah and the Gospel and confirmed earlier law in the Qur'an's account, while abrogating part and establishing part.

### A ruling drawn from the clay bird

Forming a bird amounted to making an image. That sharīʿah allowed it for Banū Isra'il, while our sharīʿah later abrogated the permission.

### In short

- As messenger to the Children of Israel, ʿĪsā makes a clay bird live, heals the born-blind and the leper, raises the dead and reports hidden food, always by Allah's leave.
- A bat that falls dead out of sight separates creaturely work from the Creator's, and fifty thousand cures in a day are tied to belief.
- Each prophet's miracle fits his age: magic for Mūsā's, medicine for ʿĪsā's, and inimitable speech for Muhammad's ﷺ.

50.text:
The new messenger places himself inside the older law before he changes any of it: "And I will confirm the Torah revealed before me and legalize some of what had been forbidden to you. I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so be mindful of Allah and obey me". Confirmation and abrogation stand together. What he confirms gives him the standing from which some prohibitions can be lifted.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And I will confirm the Torah revealed before me"**: I have come confirming and upholding the Tawrah. In the fuller phrasing he confirms Allah's divine Oneness in the religion, and the Torah and all other Scriptures that came before him.

**"and legalize some of what had been forbidden to you"**: part of earlier prohibition becomes lawful. Camel meat, bovine and sheep fat and the Sabbath illustrate release. Another account permits fish and birds lacking spikes. A further view makes everything lawful and reads baʿd, "some", as kull, "all".

**"I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so be mindful of Allah and obey me"**: he repeats that he has come with a proof from their Lord, containing affirmation and evidence of the truth of what he conveys. So have taqwa of Allah, fear Him in what He commanded and repent to Him, and obey me in what I command you about affirming God's Oneness and being obedient to Him. He makes things easy for them, and they are to follow what he calls them to.

### What abrogation by a new prophet means

The unlawfulness of some things in the earlier code stands abrogated by the new one brought by ʿĪsā, and his station of prophethood is itself the conclusive argument for the claim. The proof of his truth was the signs from their Lord. He also came to make clear some of the points in which people differed: "And in order to make clear to you some of the (points) in which you differ" (43:63). At the same time, the statement affirms the Tawrah and upholds it. Confirmation is not flattery of the old law, and abrogation is not contempt for it. One prophet verifies the book before him and then, on the authority of the same Lord, releases part of its burden.

### In short

- ʿĪsā confirms the Torah and, on the same authority, legalises part of what it forbade, such as camel meat, bovine and sheep fat and the Sabbath.
- Some reports expand the release to everything, reading "some" as "all", and the abrogation rests on his proven prophethood.
- The sign is repeated so that taqwa and obedience follow from evidence, not from novelty.

51.text:
The speech ends where it must: "Surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord. So worship Him ˹alone˺. This is the Straight Path.’”" After miracles, law and confirmation, the messenger names the one doctrine that organises them. He and his audience stand in the same servitude, and the straight path is that shared submission.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord"**: Messenger and hearers share one servitude, submission and humility before Him. That is the ultimate in belief: Allah is my Lord and your Lord.

**"So worship Him ˹alone˺"**: declare His divine Oneness. Worship Him alone, mindful of Him as the only One who deserves to be followed and feared, fulfilling His instructions and avoiding His prohibitions.

**"This is the Straight Path.’”"**: divine Oneness is a straight path, an established religion, Islam, with which He is pleased, with no crookedness. That which I enjoin on you is this path. But they rejected him and did not believe in him.

### Belief and deed joined

Verse 51 states the destination of everything before it. Once his prophethood is established, ʿĪsā asks them to beware of any contravention of divine commandments, to fear Allah, and to follow his teachings in matters of religion. In a nutshell they are that Allah is my Lord and your Lord, which is the ultimate in belief, and worship Him, which is the ultimate in deeds.
