The combination of right belief and right action is the straight path that leads to salvation and communion with Allah.

### In short

- ʿĪsā places himself and Israel under one Lord, so worship belongs to Allah alone.
- The straight path joins the ultimate belief, one Lord for messenger and audience, to the ultimate deed, worshipping Him alone.
- They rejected him anyway, which is why this closing sentence also becomes the charge against them.

52.text:
Rejection hardens into a plot, and a small company steps forward: "When Jesus sensed disbelief from his people, he asked, “Who will stand up with me for Allah?” The disciples replied, “We will stand up for Allah. We believe in Allah, so bear witness that we have submitted.”" ʿĪsā had presented his call to Banī Isra'il with miracles proving his prophethood. They remained adamant, rejected him, and moved toward physical hostility, yet a first group of followers declared its creed before its prophet.

### Phrase by phrase

**"When Jesus sensed disbelief from his people"**: persistence in disbelief and misguidance had become clear. He knew their unbelief, saw murder being intended, and repeatedly heard rejection.

**"he asked, “Who will stand up with me for Allah?”"**: who will be my helpers in Allah's cause, against His enemies? Mujāhid commented, "Who would follow me to Allah?" It appears more likely that he was asking who would help him convey the message of Allah.

**"The disciples replied, “We will stand up for Allah. We believe in Allah, so bear witness that we have submitted.”"**: the Ḥawāriyyūn said, "We are the helpers of Allah." They were his closest disciples and intimates, the first to believe in him, twelve in number.

### Helpers before the Hijrah, and a hawārī for every prophet

The Prophet's life supplies a later match. Before the Hijrah, during Hajj season, he asked, "Who will give me asylum so that I can convey the Speech of my Lord, for the Quraysh have prevented me from conveying the Speech of my Lord." The search ended with the Anṣār, who sheltered him, received his migration, comforted him and guarded him from enemies. Jesus likewise found Israelites who believed, supported him and followed the light sent with him.

Ḥawārī in Arabic means "support". A report in the Two Sahihs describes Az-Zubayr stepping forward twice when fighters were sought at Al-Ahzab, after which the Prophet ﷺ said:

> "Every Prophet has a Hawari, and Az-Zubayr is my Hawari."

A hadith cited through al-Qurtubi gives the wider gloss: every prophet has a ḥawāriyy, a sincere companion, and Zubayr is mine.

The name itself is explained from whiteness. Ḥawāriyy, singular of al-Ḥawāriyyūn, derives from ḥawar, whiteness. The title was given to the sincere disciples of ʿĪsā because of their sincerity, the purity of their hearts, or their white dress. They were twelve men of pure white complexion, though some say they were called ḥawāriyyūn because they were bleachers of clothes, qaṣṣārūn.

An important note follows from the timing. ʿĪsā looked for helpers in Allah's way only when he sensed hostility from disbelievers, not at the first stage of his call. He rose to the task alone, obeying his Lord's command without first setting up a party. When the need came, he found a group around him. Every worthy mission is said to demand that determination and courage.

### What it costs to stand with a rejected caller

The religious leaders of the Israelites had refused to believe. In any society, leading lights control resources and hold the religious seats, becoming the representatives of religion in people's eyes. If such people reject someone, he is deprived of life's resources and, even after losing everything for truth, remains a heretic to the crowd. Supporting a preacher of truth in that atmosphere is the hardest of tasks. It testifies to his veracity amid suspicion and opposition and sides with truth while it stands alone and unsupported.

Truth in its purity unsettles lives built on untruth, particularly those decorated with truth's label to secure public honour. Such leaders suppress the call, turn crowds against its bearer through misconstructions, and eventually reach for power against both call and caller. God's succour nevertheless remains with the preacher, allowing his mission to finish. Blocking Paradise-bound people from its path is treated as their greatest evil.

Inwardly, the disciples' answer is sharpened further. When the message reached them and people differed, some believing and most calling him a liar, Jesus learned that prophethood spares no one from affliction and enemy oppression. He separated his heart from them and held to his goal, qaṣd. His question then asks who will help him in exclusive devotion to God's true reality and sincere dedication to His goal. Those touched by the effects of providence, āthār al-ʿināya, and chosen through the effects of selection, āthār al-takhṣīṣ, answered that he should bear witness to them in truth and let nothing from them cast doubt on him.

### In short

- Sensing hardened disbelief, ʿĪsā asked for helpers to convey Allah's message, and twelve disciples answered as helpers of Allah.
- The Prophet ﷺ made the same request before the Hijrah and found the Anṣār, and he named Az-Zubayr his ḥawārī at Al-Ahzab in the Two Sahihs.
- Standing with a rejected caller means testifying to truth while it is alone, which is why obstructing Paradise's path is counted the worst opposition.

53.text:
The disciples repeat their declaration as prayer: "˹They prayed to Allah,˺ “Our Lord! We believe in Your revelations and follow the messenger, so count us among those who bear witness.”" What they said to their prophet in the previous verse, they now say to their Lord. The creed does not change when the audience does.

### Phrase by phrase

**"˹They prayed to Allah,˺ “Our Lord! We believe in Your revelations"**: we believe in what You have revealed, in the Scripture, that is the Gospel. Their faith is in Allah and in what He sent down.

**"and follow the messenger"**: we follow him whom You sent, the religion of the Messenger Jesus, the messenger sent to them.

**"so count us among those who bear witness.”"**: enrol us with witnesses to Your Oneness and Your Messenger's truthfulness, people who attest truth and believe in You and Your messengers. Another gloss asks for enrollment among earlier forerunners who witnessed before them.

### Among the community of Muhammad

Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded that Ibn ʿAbbās explained "write us down among those who bear witness" as "among the Ummah of Muhammad." This hadith has a good chain of narration. The same meaning is reached from the other direction in the simpler gloss, which can mean "make us of the community of Muhammad ﷺ." A small company in Israel therefore prays to be enrolled with witnesses who had not yet come, and the phrase opens their local stand into the wider community of faith.

These were people with no material expectations from their children and no envy at goodness in others. Their happiness rested on dedication and devotion to God's cause, on children kept safe from Satan and enrolled among believers. Through their good influence their children controlled their selves and joined those who truly remembered God, choosing the right way and abandoning the path that leads astray. Such people are provided for out of God's special mercy.

### The fate closing around the prayer

The rest intensified dissension and enmity and turned to plotting. Their scheming rebounded when God made them taste its evil. Crucifixion and killing Jesus existed in imagination, born from ignorance and confusion, while God had raised His prophet, nabī, and friend, walī. His enemies earned banishment and cursing instead. That was God's scheming with them.

### In short

- The disciples ask to be written with the witnesses to Oneness and to their messenger's truthfulness.
- Ibn ʿAbbās, in a report with a good chain, reads the witnesses as the community of Muhammad ﷺ.
- Around the prayer the majority plots and imagines a crucifixion, while God raises His prophet and friend.

54.text:
Two plans meet: "And the disbelievers made a plan ˹against Jesus˺, but Allah also planned—and Allah is the best of planners". The Jews planned arrest and crucifixion. Allah's counter-plan saved His prophet, turned the plot back on the plotters, and left them certain they had succeeded. The verse's key word, makr, needs care, because Allah is called the best of those who practise it.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And the disbelievers made a plan ˹against Jesus˺"**: Israel's disbelievers conspired around defamation and crucifixion in an attempt to kill ʿĪsā. One description assigns an assassin to carry out the murder. Their aim was simply to kill Jesus.

**"but Allah also planned"**: against them, Allah placed Jesus's likeness on the would-be killer and raised Jesus heavenward while the substitute died. On the attempted murder's occasion they were left inside misguidance. He also wished death for their man Tatianos.

**"and Allah is the best of planners"**: no schemer is stronger in will, none knows Jesus more completely, and no plot against enemies can be more severe than His.

### How the plot unfolded, and how it was answered

The Jews complained about ʿĪsā to a king who was a disbeliever. They claimed he misguided people, discouraged obedience to the king, caused division, and separated a man from his own son, adding other lies they will carry on their necks, including calling him an illegitimate son. The king grew furious and sent men to capture ʿĪsā, torture him and crucify him.

His home was surrounded, leaving capture apparently certain. God rescued him by raising him from the house into heaven and transferring his image to a man inside. In darkness the unjust intruders mistook that man for ʿĪsā, seized and humiliated him, crucified him and crowned him with thorns. Deception thus turned on the deceivers. The Prophet was saved and raised, while the plotters remained disordered inside transgression's darkness, convinced of success. Hard, truth-defiant hearts and enduring disgrace followed them until Resurrection Day.

The machinery is filled in a little more in the next verse and in the reports around it. They sent one of their own to arrest him, and Allah changed that man's face to resemble ʿĪsā while ʿĪsā was raised to the heavens. The person was crucified under mistaken identity. The Jews had convinced the ruler that ʿĪsā was a heretic bent on changing the Torah and making apostates of everybody, and the ruler ordered the arrest. The subtle and secret move made by Allah countered their evil plans more effectively than open force would have done.

### Makr: a subtle and secret move

Arabic makr is a move made subtly and secretly. Purpose determines its moral quality: good if good, bad if bad. Hence the restriction in "And evil plan besets none but its perpetrator" (35:43). Everyday Urdu usage limits makr to conspiracy, evil plans and strategy, so that idiom must not govern the Arabic. Allah can therefore be Khair al-Mākirīn, the best of those who make moves.

Another account explains divine deception through blessings. Ibn ʿAbbās said God increased blessings as unbelief and sin increased, drawing people into total recklessness. Immense unbelief followed as heads turned toward rebellion and misguidance. Only then were they taken gradually from an unknown direction.

A tradition adds the paradox of a harmful blessing. Someone tormented Abū Dardā, and Abū Dardā prayed, "Lord God, bestow upon him a healthy body, long life, and great wealth!" An intelligent man who ponders those words will know that this is the worst of supplications. Given these gifts, recklessness and heedlessness can make a person heedless of the next world until he is destroyed.

### What the ascension claim protects

The miraculous ascension of ʿĪsā, his life in the heavens and his later descent form the Muslim community's shared belief. Some sects, contrary to that belief, are said to deny all three and to exploit these verses' words and meanings in opening distortion's doors. The defence rests on the plain sequence: an arresting party entered, a likeness was taken, and the prophet was raised. Allah's plan leaves the plotters holding a body that is not his.

### In short

- The plot was a complaint to a disbelieving king, a house surrounded at night and a crucifixion performed on the wrong man.
- Makr is a secret move, good or bad by its purpose, and Allah's move saved ʿĪsā, cast his likeness on the assassin and hardened the plotters in disgrace (35:43).
- Ibn ʿAbbās reads divine deception as increased blessings drawing the wicked into recklessness until they are taken unawares.

55.text:
After the plot, Allah speaks directly to the intended victim: "˹Remember˺ when Allah said, “O Jesus! I will take you and raise you up to Myself. I will deliver you from those who disbelieve, and elevate your followers above the disbelievers until the Day of Judgment. Then to Me you will ˹all˺ return, and I will settle all your disputes”". Five promises are packed into one address. He will take ʿĪsā, raise him, cleanse him from the disbelievers, set his followers above them until the Resurrection, and judge their disputes at the return.

### Phrase by phrase

**"˹Remember˺ when Allah said, “O Jesus! I will take you"**: I will take you in full, mutawaffīka, and raise you to Myself while you are asleep. The taking is elsewhere used of sleep: "It is He Who takes your souls by night (when you are asleep)" (6:60), and "It is Allah Who takes away the souls at the time of their death, and those that die not during their sleep" (39:42). When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would awaken he used to say, "All the thanks are due to Allah Who brought us back to life after He had caused us to die (sleep), and the Return is to Him." Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded that al-Ḥasan said the taking here refers to sleep, because Allah raised ʿĪsā while he was asleep.

**"and raise you up to Myself"**: I will gather you, seize you and raise you to Me away from the world without death, taking your body and soul alive and ridding you of the filth of those who disbelieved you.

**"I will deliver you from those who disbelieve"**: I will purify and save you from those who disbelieve, by raising you to heaven, cleansing you and removing you far away from them.

**"and elevate your followers above the disbelievers until the Day of Judgment"**: Your followers will be placed over the disbelievers until Resurrection Day, prevailing by decisive proof and sword, by help, by force and by evidence.

**"Then to Me you will ˹all˺ return, and I will settle all your disputes”"**: then to Me shall be your return after death, and I will judge between you concerning the matters of religion in which you used to differ and argue.

### What "I will take you" means

The word mutawaffī takes tawaffī as its verbal noun from the root wafy, which lexically means "to take in full". Its derivations wafā, īfāʾ and istīfāʾ convey the same sense. Because a person completes his appointed time at death and the soul given by Allah is taken back fully and conclusively, the word is also used figuratively for death, and the same word covers daily sleep in the verse "Allah takes away lives of the living at the time of their death and of those that do not die, in their sleep" (39:42).

Ibn Taimiyyah says in al-Jawāb al-Ṣaḥīḥ that al-tawaffī in Arabic means to exact fully or take in full. Three forms are distinguished: taking during sleep, taking in death, and taking soul and body together. Kulliyāt Abū al-Baqāʾ describes common usage as putting to death and exacting the soul, but classical usage as taking in full and exacting due right. Most scholars therefore render mutawaffīka "taking in full": ʿĪsā would not be left in Jewish hands, but taken away into the heavens.

Some authentic explainers read the word as "giving death", but never death at enemy hands. On their account Allah comforted Jesus with two things while the Jews were bent on killing him. His death would be natural, not a killing, and to rescue him from their designs Allah would first raise him toward Himself. That is the explanation reported from Ibn ʿAbbās through al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthur, on the authority of several narrators. It depends on precedence in wording: "I shall raise you" happens first, and "I shall give you death" later. The order itself hints at what is coming. The raising will not last forever. It will be temporary, and he will return to the mortal world, prevail over his enemies, and only then meet a natural death. His return and death after victory become a consummation of honour, and a refutation in advance of Christian divinity, since a Jesus who will die cannot be the Living and Eternal.

A second gloss makes the return smaller and inward: death will follow your descent, or alternatively, love of worldly life will die inside your heart.

Raising, rafʿ, can be figurative, as rank: "And raised some of you in ranks over others" (6:165), and "and Allah will raise up in rank those of you who believe and those who have been given knowledge" (58:11). In this verse the word ilā, "towards", removes that figure. Rafiʿuka ilayya, "I shall raise you towards Me", cannot mean rank alone. Sūrat Al-Nisāʾ settles it further: the Jews certainly did not kill Jesus. Rather, Allah raised him towards Himself (4:158), an expression used only for raising the spirit and the body alive. In his Tafsīr, Imām al-Rāzī, in al-Tafsīr al-Kabīr, observed that precedence of a later event over an earlier one is frequent in the Qur'an for exactly such expedient reasons.

### Why this prophet's emigration went to heaven

Prophets opposed to the end usually end in one of two ways. Either their people are annihilated, as with ʿĀd and Thamūd and the peoples of Lūṭ (Lot) and Ṣāliḥ, or the prophet is told to migrate and later achieves power and victory elsewhere. Ibrāhīm (Abraham) migrated from Iraq and took refuge in Syria. Mūsā (Moses) migrated from Egypt and came to Madyan. Muhammad ﷺ migrated from Makkah and came to Madinah, and from there finally attacked Makkah and conquered it. The raising of Jesus to the heavens was an emigration of its own kind, after which he would return to the world and gain total victory over the Jews.

Why should his emigration alone have heaven as destination? His case is like Adam's. Adam's birth differed from normal birth, without father and mother, and the birth of Jesus took a miraculous form different from normal human birth, without a father. His death too will take a unique and unmatched form, materialising after hundreds of years following his return to the world. His emigration fittingly follows a unique pattern. The marvels led ignorant Christians to declare him God, while reflection on those same marvels proves his servitude as a human being, his obedience to the divine will and his human traits. The Qur'an therefore refutes the godhood of Jesus at all such points. Because a raising to heaven would have strengthened that doubt, the word mutawaffīka comes first and eliminates it. The verse negates the Jewish plan, since they were set to crucify and kill Jesus and Allah made their plans come to nothing, and the precedence of the words also refutes the Christians, because Jesus is no God who never dies.

### Five promises and their fulfilment

1. **His death would not come by Jewish killing.** It will be natural, at its appointed time near the Day of Doom, when ʿĪsā descends from the heavens to earth, as detailed in sound hadith transmitted through unbroken chains.

2. **He would be raised toward the heavens in that situation.** This was fulfilled at once, reported in Surah al-Nisa: "the Jews certainly did not kill him; rather, Allah raised him towards Himself" (4:158). The wider passage runs: "And because of their disbelief and allegations against Maryam and because of their saying 'We killed Al-Masih 'Isa, son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah', but they killed him not, nor crucified him, but it appeared that way to them... For surely they killed him not. But Allah raised him up unto Himself. And Allah is Ever All-Powerful, All-Wise. And there is none of the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) but must believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection, he ['Isa] will be a witness against them" (4:156-159). "Before his death" refers to ʿĪsā. The People of the Book will believe in him before he dies, when he returns before the Day of Resurrection, annuls the jizyah and accepts only Islam from people.

3. **He would be cleansed of false accusations.** This was fulfilled when the last of the prophets came and refuted them. The Jews slandered his parentage because he was born without a father. The Qur'an answers that this was Allah's power and will, and that Adam, born without both father and mother, is more surprising still. They also accused ʿĪsā of claiming to be God. Many verses report him publicly confessing instead that he is human, a servant and bondsman of Allah.

4. **His followers would stand above the disbelievers.** Once Allah raised ʿĪsā, his followers split into sects. One company accepted his actual commission: Allah's servant, His Messenger, and son of His female servant. Others reached extremes by calling him God's son, God Himself, or a Trinity member. False creeds are named and refuted in the Qur'an. Christians persisted until the third century CE, when a Greek king, Constantine, became Christian in order, the narrative says, to destroy Christianity. Whether philosopher or simply ignorant, Constantine inserted and deleted material, created rituals and the so-called Great Trust (really the Great Treachery), permitted swine, turned prayer eastward, founded churches and added ten fast days to compensate for an alleged personal sin. Christianity became Constantinian, with more than twelve thousand churches, temples and monasteries and Constantinople bearing his name. Christians then dominated Jews for a time, helped because they stood closer to truth than Jews did, though both are described as disbelievers.

Following here means belief in and confession of the prophethood of ʿĪsā. Practising all the injunctions ascribed to him is not a precondition for the worldly dominance promised. Christians and Muslims both fall in this category, since both believe in his prophethood and messengership. Salvation in the Hereafter is another matter. It depends on believing all the injunctions ʿĪsā brought, including the instruction to believe in the last of the prophets who would come after Jesus departed. Christians did not follow that instruction in faith, so they deprived themselves of salvation, while Muslims acted on it and became deserving of it. But dominance over the Jews depended on the prophethood of ʿĪsā alone, and from the time of the promise to now, Christians and Muslims have dominated the Jews, and so it shall be through the Day of Judgment. Their empires have covered the world.

5. **Their disputes would be judged at the return.** "Then, to Me is your return, whereupon I shall judge between you" (3:55). This fifth promise will be fulfilled at its appointed time.

### What happened after Muhammad ﷺ was sent

Muhammad's followers changed the map. Belief in Allah, angels, Books and messengers took its correct form, making them true followers of every earth-sent prophet. They embraced the unlettered final Prophet and master of mankind, summoning humanity to the entire truth. Hence they deserved every prophet more than nations that claim his path while altering his religion. Muhammad's Law abrogated earlier laws and will remain unchanged, dominant and victorious until the Last Hour.

Under that promise, Muslims conquered the world's east and west and earthly kingdoms. Countries submitted. Kisrā of Persia fell, the Czar was destroyed, and their treasures were taken and spent for Allah, exactly as promised: "Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous good deeds, that He will certainly grant them succession in the land, as He granted it to those before them, and that He will grant them the authority to practice their religion which He has chosen for them. And He will surely give them in exchange a safe security after their fear (provided) they worship Me and do not associate anything with Me" (24:55).

So Muslims became the true believers in ʿĪsā. They acquired Ash-Sham from the Christians, who evacuated to Asia Minor and their fortified city of Constantinople. Muslims will remain above them until the Day of Resurrection, and the truthful one who received the true news has told them they will conquer Constantinople in the future and seize its treasures.

### The objection of a Jewish state in the present age

The present state of Israel is treated as no counter-evidence. In the argument given, that state is a manifestation of the military might of Russia and Christians of Euro-American origin, established and maintained against Muslims. Withdraw that patronage and the state would collapse and disappear from the map, so it is not a manifestation of Jewish domination at all. Even allowing it as a Jewish state for argument's sake, Christians and Muslims together remain wielders of far greater influence, and Jews remain much subjugated with fear. A temporary Jewish domination near the Day of Judgment is itself reported in authentic hadith of the Prophet ﷺ, so even such an episode would not contradict the promise, and a short-lived occupation cannot be named a state or government, especially one said to rest on a conspiracy of Christians and communists.

### Life, death and return: the consensus described

The Jews alone say that ʿĪsā was crucified, killed and buried and never returned to life. The Christians say he was indeed killed on the cross, then brought back to life and raised into the heavens. Both are refuted by mistaken identity: "And they did not kill him and they did not crucify him, but they were deluded by resemblance" (4:157). Jews rejoiced after killing their own man. Christians made the same mistake by believing it was Jesus who died on the cross. The Islamic belief stated here and in several other verses is that Allah raised him alive onto the heavens to rescue him from the Jews. He was not killed and not crucified. He is alive in heaven, will descend close to the Day of Judgment, lead Muslims to victory over the Jews, and finally die a natural death.

Consensus of the entire Muslim community is claimed for this belief. Ḥāfiẓ ibn Ḥajr reported the consensus in Talkhīṣ al-Ḥabīr. It is said to stand on several Qur'anic verses and on mutawātir hadith transmitted through unbroken chains of reporting. On Surah Al-Zukhruf, a classical explanation adds that uninterrupted hadith transmission presents ʿĪsā as a just leader arriving before Judgment Day (43:61).

Special works on the question are named. ʿAqīdat al-Islām fī Ḥayāti ʿĪsā, by Maulānā Sayyid Muḥammad Anwar Shāh al-Kashmīrī, Ḥayāt-e-ʿĪsā in Urdu by Ḥaḍrat Maulānā Badr ʿĀlam Muhājir Madanī, and Ḥayāt-e-Masīḥ in Urdu by Maulānā Sayyid Muḥammad Idrīs are given among hundreds of published books and essays. A student executing al-Kashmīrī's orders gathered over one hundred mutawātir hadith on the raising and future descent. His al-Taṣrīḥ bimā Tawātara fī Nuzūl al-Masīḥ appeared lately in Beirut, annotated by ʿAllāma ʿAbd al-Fattāḥ Abū Ghuddah of Aleppo, Syria.

### Why so much detail is given about him

In the eleventh section of this surah, Adam, Nūḥ (Noah), Āl-Ibrāhīm and Āl-ʿImrān are covered briefly in one verse. Nearly three sections and twenty-two verses then treat ʿĪsā and his family in meticulous detail. His grandmother's pledge, his mother's birth, name and upbringing, his conception and birth, what his mother ate and drank after childbirth, her return to her family with the newborn, their blame and curses, the newborn's gift of eloquence, his growing up and call, the opposition and the disciples' help, the Jewish attempts to trap and kill him, his raising alive into the heavens, and after that his additional traits, looks, physique and dress. No prophet receives this much detail in the whole spectrum of Qur'an and hadith.

The wisdom given is identification. The final Prophet, with no apostle after him, guided his community about what it would face until the Day of Judgment. He identified by name those it should follow and marked the astray who endangered its faith. Of later mischief-makers, Dajjāl, the false Messiah, is the most notorious, so the Prophet ﷺ detailed his profile and distinguishing traits. Among later reformers and elders, ʿĪsā is the most distinguished, blessed with prophethood, kept alive in heaven to rescue the Muslim community in Dajjāl's wicked period, and appointed to kill Dajjāl near the Day of Judgment. Clear indications of his person and qualities prevent doubt when he comes a second time.

Secondly, he will not come then designated as Prophet in function. He will lead the Muslim community as its Khalīfa, vice-regent, while his personal station of prophethood remains unremoved, like a provincial governor visiting another province whose office at home is not thereby taken away. Rejecting his prophethood is infidelity still. A community already professing faith in it must not fall into the grievous error of rejection by failing to recognise him.

Thirdly, because the event falls in the world's later years, ambiguity in his marks could let another person claim to be the Messiah. In pre-partition India, Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian claimed precisely that. Scholars of the Muslim community refuted his claim using these very indicators. The detailed description therefore indicates his reappearance close to the Day of Judgment, and an Urdu treatise, Masīḥ Mawʿūd kī Pahchān, "Identifying the Promised Messiah", is offered for the full details.

### The inward gathering

The allusion inside the address runs: I will gather you away from yourself and raise you above mortal human qualities, purifying your own desire, irāda, so completely that you act as Our agent, muṣarrif, through and for Us. Free choice, ikhtiyār, will belong to you in nothing. Divine governorship, tawallī, will descend instead and stand for you. Through that quality dead people came alive by Jesus's hands, which is possible only through divine deliberative power.

His heart was purified from turning toward others, aghyār, or seeing simulacra and traces, al-amthāl wa-l-āthār, across states and phases, al-aḥwāl wa-l-aṭwār. Unchanged followers of his religion, dīn, and creed, ʿaqīda, within tawḥīd are believers, muʾminūn, right and helped until Resurrection Day. Divine judgment then assigns disbelievers to hellfire, ammā l-kuffār fa-fī l-jaḥīm, and believers to felicity, wa-ammā l-muʾminūn fa-fī l-naʿīm.

### In short

- "I will take you" means taken in full, in sleep, and raised body and soul to heaven, not killed by the Jews (4:158, 6:60, 39:42).
- Five promises follow: natural death deferred, raising fulfilled, slanders refuted, followers dominant through Christians and Muslims, and disputes judged at the return.
- Raised alive, ʿĪsā will descend near the Day of Judgment, and the unmatched detail of his story lets the community identify him and reject false claimants.

56.text:
The judgement announced to Jesus begins with its first half: "As for those who disbelieve, I will subject them to a severe punishment in this life and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers". The previous verse said that Allah will be the final judge in what they used to differ about. This verse describes the decision for one side, and its form raises a question about timing, because punishment in this world is named from the standpoint of a decision delivered at the end.

### Phrase by phrase

**"As for those who disbelieve"**: unbelief in Allah and His messengers, Muhammad and Jesus, is meant. The statement recounts God's response to Jews who rejected ʿĪsā and Christians who exceeded all bounds over him.

**"I will subject them to a severe punishment in this life and the Hereafter"**: heavy chastisement here takes the form of sword and capitation tax, jizyah, while the Hereafter throws them into Fire. Historically they were killed, captured, taxed and stripped of wealth and kingdoms, but later torment is worse and more severe.

**"and they will have no helpers"**: no helper can save them from Allah's punishment in either world, and no Waq, defender or protector, stands against Allah: "And they have no Waq (defender or protector) against Allah" (13:34).

### A judge's sentence counts from its award

The difficulty is resolved by an analogy. A judge says to a culprit, "Right now I am sending you to jail for a year. If you misbehave there, I shall make it two years." The two years are counted from the day the punishment is awarded. Given the misconduct, the whole sentence regulates itself and one more year becomes effective as an add-on. Here, punishment in the world has already been given. The punishment of the Hereafter will now be added, and the total will be executed on the Last Day. Worldly punishment will not serve as expiation for the punishment of the Hereafter.

Believers stand in the opposite condition. Struck by suffering in mortal life, they have their sins forgiven and their due punishment in the Hereafter lightened or warded off. The hint is given in the next verse, "Allah does not like the wrongdoers": believers are dear because of belief, and the beloved are treated with that mercy. Disbelievers are detested because of disbelief, and the detested do not receive such treatment.

The Jewish community's worldly decree is framed in a second way: the Jews made a false case against Jesus and took him to the Roman court in Palestine, which decreed crucifixion, but God saved him and Roman soldiers crucified another person who resembled Christ. As punishment for that crime, believers in Jesus Christ would forever, until Doomsday, hold dominion over the Jewish people. That was God's decree for this world. The Hereafter is another matter.

### In short

- Disbelievers in Muhammad and in Jesus are punished severely in this world by sword, capture and jizyah, and in the Hereafter by the Fire, with no protector (13:34).
- Worldly punishment does not expiate for them, as a judge's added year runs from sentencing. It is added to the punishment of the next world.
- For believers, worldly suffering works in reverse, forgiving sins and lightening what comes after.

57.text:
The other half of the decision balances the first: "And as for those who believe and do good, they will be rewarded in full. And Allah does not like the wrongdoers.”" Belief and righteous action meet complete payment in both worlds, and the closing statement returns the contrast to God's own attitude: wrongdoing is not loved, and wrongdoers will be chastised.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And as for those who believe and do good"**: faith covers Allah, Scripture and messengers Muhammad and Jesus. Good works are done sincerely between servants and their Lord. Prayer, charity, fasting and family ties exemplify them.

**"they will be rewarded in full"**: their wages are paid completely, read as yuwaffīhim, "He will pay them in full", or nuwaffīhim, "We will pay them in full". Victory and domination reward them now. Paradise and elevated grades reward them later. On Judgment Day Allah completes payment.

**"And Allah does not like the wrongdoers.”"**: Allah loves not the evildoers, meaning He will chastise them. The wrongdoers are the idolaters, with their transgressions and association of partners with Allah. The greatest wrong is to ascribe partners to Allah and disbelieve His messengers.

### The ascension pictured, and the descent in hadith

A report about the raising itself says that God sent Jesus a cloud which raised him up while his mother clutched at him in tears. He said to her, "Verily, the Resurrection shall bring us together again." This took place on Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Ordainment, in Jerusalem's Holy House, when he was thirty-three. Six further years of life remained for his mother.

Bukhārī and Muslim, the two Shaykhs, report a descent close to the Hour, with rule conducted by our Prophet Muhammad's Law. The cross will be broken, the swine slain, the false messiah killed and jizya imposed. In Muslim's hadith he will remain seven years. According to Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī, he will remain forty years, then die and have prayers performed over him. Forty may instead total all his earthly years, before ascension and after return.

The believers here are glossed as Messiah's followers prior to Prophet Muhammad's coming, whose arrival the Messiah himself confirmed. Faith in his truth led them to good actions, and their reward comes without reduction.

### In short

- Believers in Allah, Scripture, Muhammad and Jesus who do good are paid in full, here with victory and hereafter with Paradise.
- Allah does not love wrongdoers, whose greatest wrong is associating partners with Him and disbelieving His messengers.
- Reports put his raising on Laylat al-Qadr at age thirty-three, and his descent before the Hour with a rule by Muhammad's law.

58.text:
The story of Jesus closes with its seal: "We recite ˹all˺ this to you ˹O Prophet˺ as one of the signs and ˹as˺ a wise reminder". What has been narrated about ʿĪsā, his birth and his life is presented as recitation from Allah, not reconstruction, and its function is dual: signs that prove, and a reminder that instructs.

### Phrase by phrase

**"We recite ˹all˺ this to you ˹O Prophet˺"**: what We narrate to Muhammad ﷺ conveys commands and prohibitions and comes through Gabriel. This account of Jesus clearly signals the truth of revelation, a perfect and falsehood-free message for God-conscious people.

**"as one of the signs"**: of the verses, the revelations of the Qur'an. Allah conveyed and revealed this to you from the Preserved Tablet, Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz, leaving it free of doubt. In the wording, "of verses" is a circumstantial element: min al-āyāt qualifies what is recited, its force carried by the demonstrative "This".

**"and ˹as˺ a wise reminder"**: a wise, clear remembrance, namely the Qur'an, enjoining what is lawful and what is unlawful. It is also said that it corroborates the Torah and the Gospel, and that it confirms what is in the Guarded Tablet.

### Knowledge not reached by effort

To Muhammad ﷺ the point is sharpened. This We recite to you in order to inform you of the meanings of what We have revealed. No exertion to attain knowledge, no parable-derived learning and no reasoning-based deduction delivered these meanings to you.

Surah Maryam seals the same account: "Such is 'Isa, son of Maryam. (It is) a statement of truth, about which they doubt (or dispute)." It then denies that Allah begets a son and repeats that decreeing a thing requires only "Be!" The account was not assembled by the Prophet. Allah conveyed the story of Jesus from the Preserved Tablet, untouched by doubt.

### In short

- The Jesus narrative ends as revelation recited to Muhammad ﷺ, not history he reconstructed.
- It is both sign and wise reminder: proof of the revelation's truth, and instruction about lawful and unlawful.
- The Preserved Tablet, Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz, is its source, leaving it untouched by doubt.

59.text:
The comparison that ends the argument is short: "Indeed, the example of Jesus in the sight of Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, “Be!” And he was". ʿĪsā was created without a father. Adam was created without father or mother. If fatherless creation made a son of God, Adam would have the stronger claim, and since that claim is obviously false for Adam, it is even more false for ʿĪsā.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, the example of Jesus in the sight of Allah is like that of Adam"**: regarding Allah's ability, the likeness of ʿĪsā is the likeness of Adam. His remarkable case in God's sight is as Adam's case. The comparison sets one remarkable thing beside another more remarkable, so that it convinces the disputer and settles in the mind more effectively.

**"He created him from dust"**: He created Adam, his form, of dust, without father or mother.

**"then said to him, “Be!” And he was"**: He said to Adam, "Be", a human being, and he was. Similarly He said to Jesus, "Be", without a father, and he was. Jesus became as Allah willed: "Become a man. And he became."

### The question that drew this answer

The delegation from Najran asked the Prophet ﷺ for proof from the Qur'an that Jesus was not the son of Allah. In one setting, they accused him directly: "Why do you insult Jesus?" He asked what he had said. They answered, "You say that he is a servant." He said, "Indeed, he is the servant and messenger of Allah, as well as His word which He cast into the Virgin Mary." They grew angry: "Have you ever seen a human being born without a father? If you are truthful, show us such a person." Then Allah revealed this verse.

In another report, two monks from Najran came and were invited to surrender to Allah. One claimed that surrender had preceded the Prophet. The answer named three preventions: worship of the cross, eating pork, and claiming Allah has a son. When they asked for Jesus's father, the Prophet ﷺ did not answer hastily. He waited for Allah, and revelation supplied this verse.

Adam supplies common ground for Christians too. Everyone believes he was the first man, brought directly into existence by God's command rather than born from a father and a mother. If that mode of arrival leaves Adam human and not Allah's son, fatherlessness cannot by itself make Jesus Allah's son.

### The delegation and its three claims about ʿĪsā

The reason for the surah's opening sequence is this Najran delegation. It came to Al-Madinah to argue about ʿĪsā, claiming he was divine and the son of Allah, and Allah sent down the beginning of this surah to refute them, as Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar and other scholars stated.

Ibn Ishaq's famous Sīrah counts sixty horsemen, including fourteen chiefs who made decisions. Their leading three were Al-ʿAqib, also known as ʿAbdul-Masih, their leader and reference for advice and decision. As-Sayyid, also known as Al-Ayham, was their scholar and leader in journeys and gatherings. Abu Harithah bin ʿAlqamah, of Bakr bin Waʾil, their patriarch, priest and religious leader. The others were named Uways bin Al-Harith, Zayd, Qays, Yazid, Nabih, Khuwaylid, ʿAmr, Khalid, ʿAbdullah and Yuhannas. Abu Harithah was an Arab who, on embracing Christianity, was honoured by the Romans and their kings, who built churches for him or in his honour, supported him financially and gave him servants because of his firm faith. He knew the description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from earlier divine Books. His position and honour kept him Christian, all the same.

They entered the Prophet's mosque after ʿAsr prayer wearing robes and garments, accompanying a caravan of camels led by Banū al-Ḥārith bin Kaʿb. Companions who saw them said they had never seen a delegation like them. Abu Harithah and Al-ʿAqib spoke, as Christians of the king's community, but they disagreed about ʿĪsā among themselves. Some said, "He is Allah." Others said, "He is the son of Allah." Others said, "He is one of a trinity." Resurrection of the dead, healing of blindness, leprosy and illness, foretelling the future, and shaping birds and breathing life into them feed the first claim. Every miracle happened by Allah's leave so that ʿĪsā would be a sign for people.

The Qur'an refutes all three. As for ability, its pattern is now complete: Adam made without male or female, Eve from a male without a female, ʿĪsā from a mother without a father, and the rest of creation from male and female. In Surah Maryam the conclusion stands: "And We made him a sign for mankind" (19:21).

### Two creations, one mortality

Inwardly, the two are paired through the spirit, rūḥ. He chose to purify the spirit in them from transmigration, tanāsukh, passing through loins. Adam is singled out as the first of men, while Jesus is singled out for the distinction of the spirit breathed into him in the most exalted way. Yet both were weighty beings for whom being in time and being mortal were unavoidable: "He created him of dust then He said to him Be and he was" (3:59).

### In short

- Fatherless creation cannot make Jesus God's son, because Adam had neither father nor mother and nobody calls him God's son.
- The Najran delegation's own cases, miracles, fatherlessness and the plural "We", are answered by Allah's leave, by Adam, and by the one command "Be" (19:21).
- Both Adam and Jesus carry the mark of mortality, which separates them from God.

60.text:
After the comparison, the matter is closed in one line: "This is the truth from your Lord, so do not be one of those who doubt". What lies beyond truth, the argument asks, except falsehood? The truth about ʿĪsā is the only true story about him, and doubt is treated not as humility but as wavering away from what has been laid out.

### Phrase by phrase

**"This is the truth from your Lord"**: al-ḥaqqu min rabbik. The implied subject is "the matter concerning ʿĪsā", whose affair comes from your Lord. Jesus is established as neither Allah, His son nor His partner. Revelation from your Lord leaves the truth about him undoubtable.

**"so do not be one of those who doubt"**: be not of those who waver, who are uncertain about it and doubt what has been set out concerning the creation of Jesus without a father. Instead, be firm on the truth you have.

### One giver of existence

No associates or partners stand beside Him in the power of existence-giving. He needs and requires no one in it, and no one besides Him has the power of existence-giving and devising. One of the elders, the pīrs, of the Ṭarīqah whispered:

> "O Lord, the one who does the work is the one who can, and the one who bestows is the one who has. What do I have and what can I do? Who has ability like Your ability? In praising You who has a tongue? Without Your love, who has the joy of spirit?"

> Without the breeze of the heart-taker's love, the garden has no ease. Without the radiance of that rose-coloured face, there's no light or fire.

### In short

- The matter of ʿĪsā is settled as truth from the Lord: he is not God, son or partner.
- Doubt after the exposition is wavering, not caution.
- Existence is given by God alone, which leaves no partner to share the act of "Be".

61.text:
Argument gives way to a solemn ordeal: "Now, whoever disputes with you ˹O Prophet˺ concerning Jesus after full knowledge has come to you, say, “Come! Let us gather our children and your children, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves—then let us sincerely invoke Allah’s curse upon the liars.”" This is the Mubāhalah. Najran was invited to stake families on the dispute. Najran declined, and made peace instead.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Now, whoever disputes with you ˹O Prophet˺ concerning Jesus after full knowledge has come to you"**: whoever from among the Christians disputes with you concerning Jesus, claiming he was not Allah's servant, after the exposition and correct knowledge of his affair has come to you.

**"say, “Come! Let us gather our children and your children, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves"**: both camps bring sons, women and selves together. Prayer is made humbly to our Lord with utmost effort.

**"then let us sincerely invoke Allah’s curse upon the liars.”"**: together they ask Allah to curse whoever lies about Him concerning Jesus: "Lord, curse the one that tells lies concerning the affair of Jesus." Both sides supplicate against the liars between them.

### What Mubāhalah is

Mubāhalah literally means mutual prayer. In the terminology of Islamic sharīʿah it is a particular form of resolving religious disputes. When argument from both sides fails to resolve a religious issue, the parties jointly pray for Allah to cast His curse on whichever party is false. A curse means moving someone far away from divine mercy. Moving far from mercy is being close to divine wrath, so its essence is: wrath be on the liar. The liar then faces the evil consequences, and the truth becomes evident even to the disbelievers.

Originally only the disputants are needed. They simply get together and pray. Assembling all the family members is not required, but it makes a Mubāhalah more effective, which is why the Prophet ﷺ was instructed to invite the families of both sides.

"Sons" carries its general sense and includes grandsons, not only sons of the loins, in common usage. So Ḥasan and Ḥusayn, the Prophet's grandsons, fall inside "our sons", and ʿAlī, his son-in-law, is included too. ʿAlī has another reason for inclusion: he grew up under the Prophet's patronage, treated like his own son. Some have claimed that because ʿAlī was not the Prophet's son he must belong instead to "ourselves", making him the Prophet's immediate successor. The answer given is that this argument fails once "sons" is read in its normal breadth.

### The day Najran declined

An ultimatum frames the meeting: accept Islam, pay jizya (the levy imposed on free non-Muslims living under Muslim rule), or prepare for war. The shorter delegation named Shurahbil, ʿAbdullah ibn Shurahbil and Jabbar ibn Fayd. Debate escalated around proving Jesus's godhood until the ordeal was announced. The Prophet ﷺ came with Fāṭimah, ʿAlī, Ḥasan and Ḥusayn. Shurahbil warned his companions that Mubāhalah against a prophet meant certain death and destruction and advised the Prophet's proposed truce. Agreement produced peace through an accepted levy.

Najran, a great Christian centre some 150 miles north of Sanaa toward Yemen, sent a deputation in the tenth Hijra year. Arguments were presented, including the contrast between God, who never dies, and Jesus, who would eventually meet death. They remained unmoved. The following day the Prophet emerged with grandsons Hasan and Husayn, daughter Fāṭimah and son-in-law ʿAlī. Consultation turned on the promised prophet among the Ishmaelites: if Muhammad was he, mutual imprecation would destroy the people and reach later generations. "By God," one scholar said, "I am seeing such faces as could move mountains with their prayers." Peace treaties and departure looked better.

The fuller account ends the same way, with a judge requested in place of the ordeal. Verses judged between the Prophet ﷺ and People of the Book and commanded the call if truth continued to be refused. Najran asked for time to decide and consulted Al-ʿAqib, who warned:

> "By Allah, O Christian fellows! You know that Muhammad is a Messenger and that he brought you the final word regarding your fellow ('Isa). You also know that no Prophet conducted Mubahalah with any people without destruction falling on them. Indeed, it will be the end of you if you do it. If you have decided to remain in your religion and your creed regarding your fellow ('Isa), then conduct a treaty with the man (Muhammad) and go back to your land."

They told Abu Al-Qasim that dual adherence should continue, each community remaining on its religion, and requested a trusted Companion to judge their monetary disputes, a role they found acceptable in him.

Al-Bukhari's report from Hudhayfah has Al-ʿAqib and As-Sayyid come seeking imprecation. One warned the other against proceeding: if Muhammad was truly a Prophet, invoking curses would ruin them and their offspring forever. They asked for "a trusted man, just a trusted man" to go with them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ promised a truly trustworthy man, and every Companion hoped to be chosen. He called Abu ʿUbaydah bin Al-Jarrah to stand and said, "This is the trustee of this Ummah." Al-Bukhari also records Anas's version of the saying: "Every Ummah has a trustee, and the trustee of this Ummah is Abu 'Ubaydah bin Al-Jarrah." 

When Najran met the Prophet ﷺ already accompanied by al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, Fāṭima and ʿAlī, he instructed them, "When I supplicate you say 'Amen'." No imprecation followed. Peace was exchanged for jizya, as Abū Nuʿaym reports. Ibn ʿAbbās adds the Prophet's warning that going through with it would mean returning home to neither possessions nor family. Another version has fire consuming those who set out with that intention.

A report from Ibn ʿAbbās in Ahmad's collection first recalls Abu Jahl's threat to step on Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying beside the Ka'bah. The Prophet ﷺ responded:

> "Had he tried to do it, the angels would have taken him publicly. Had the Jews wished for death, they would have perished and would have seen their seats in the Fire. Had those who sought Mubahalah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, went ahead with it, they would not have found estates or families when they returned home."

The same hadith appears in al-Bukhari and An-Nasa'i as well. At-Tirmidhi graded it Hasan Sahih.

The same hadith appears in al-Bukhari and An-Nasa'i as well. At-Tirmidhi graded it Hasan Sahih.

In the account of the two monks, the ending is compressed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ brought al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, Fāṭimah and all his family and children. When the two Christians left, one said to the other, "Consent to pay the Jizyah and do not agree to summon Allah's curse on the liar." They went back and said, "We agree to pay the Jizyah and abstain from summoning Allah's curse on the liar."

### Why the curse was never spoken

Inward explanation gives the respite a purpose. Once truth imparted to the heart has been sincerely proclaimed, challenge should not be withheld. Force, qahr, and help, nuṣra, protect the challenger within nearness's wing. Had Najran pursued the cursing, fire would have rained down on the valley. Respite was granted because future believers would come from their progeny. The verse also evokes people no longer counted among the sincere, ṣiddīqūn: when the sincere lights appear, their remnants fade completely.

### In short

- Mubāhalah stakes both families on a curse against the liar, and families are included to make it more effective, with "sons" covering grandsons.
- Najran declined after its own leaders warned that no people survives a prophet's imprecation, paid jizya instead, and asked for a trustee-judge, receiving Abu ʿUbaydah bin Al-Jarrah.
- Abu Nuʿaym and Ibn ʿAbbās describe the road not taken: had they gone out, they would have found neither possessions nor family at home.

62.text:
The seal comes after the standoff: "Certainly, this is the true narrative, and there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Allah. And indeed, Allah ˹alone˺ is the Almighty, All-Wise". What was narrated about ʿĪsā is declared the plain truth that cannot be avoided. Its truth rests not on the agreement of the disputants, who never signed it, but on the One who is Mighty and Wise.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Certainly, this is the true narrative"**: the account of Jesus and Najran has the character of a report free from doubt. It establishes a single point: Jesus was neither Allah, His son nor His partner.

**"and there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Allah"**: none has the right to be worshipped but Allah, without a son or partner.

**"And indeed, Allah ˹alone˺ is the Almighty, All-Wise"**: His kingdom is mighty, His vengeance reaches unbelievers, and His actions are wise. Worship has been commanded for Him alone. An alternative explanation of “Wise” says He decreed the imprecation outing, but Najran refused because they knew their own falsehood and recognised a true Prophet and emissary whose traits their own Scripture described.

### No dust over the witnessing of unity

The true story leaves confusion powerless. Its dust has no authority over divine unity's witnessings. Created delusion cannot reach the secret of His ruling, ḥukm, because nothing existing can approximate it and imagination cannot conceive His decree, taqdīr.

### In short

- The account of Jesus is declared the true narrative with no doubt in it, and Allah alone deserves worship.
- The delegation's refusal is read as private knowledge: they knew Muhammad ﷺ was a true prophet from their own Scripture.
- Confusion has no authority over the witnessing of unity.

63.text:
One line disposes of those who walked away: "If they turn away, then surely Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of the corruptors". They rejected faith after knowledge had come to them. The verse replaces the pronoun with the open name, the agents of corruption, and leaves their requital to the One who knows them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"If they turn away"**: they turn their backs, abandon truth, reject faith and refuse joining the Prophet ﷺ in invoking Allah's curse on liars concerning Jesus.

**"then surely Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of the corruptors"**: Allah knows completely those who commit mischief, here the Najran Christians. Abandoning truth for falsehood is mischief, and full knowledge leads to requital and the worst punishment. The overt noun al-mufsidūn replaces "they". He controls everything.

### Being left to one's conjecture

Inward timing governs judgement. When backs turn, false talkers' confusion cannot resist the rays of Muhammad's light. Allah knows corruption's agents and may either sweep them away immediately or delay while conjectures set firmly. Sudden seizure then leaves them helpless.

### In short

- Turning away after knowledge is named corruption, and its requital belongs to Allah.
- The corruptors meant are the Najran Christians who refused both the truth and the ordeal.
- Judgement may sweep at once or wait until false conjecture hardens, then seize suddenly.

64.text:
After the ordeal was refused, a fairer door is opened: "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O People of the Book! Let us come to common terms: that we will worship none but Allah, associate none with Him, nor take one another as lords instead of Allah.” But if they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that we have submitted ˹to Allah alone˺.”" The call begins at the one point both sides already profess: the Oneness of God. Jews and Christians are addressed, and those who follow their ways, and the invitation is repeated in the Prophet's letter to the Roman emperor.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O People of the Book! Let us come to common terms"**: "Word" here is a complete sentence, although Allah calls it one word. It is described as a word that is the same between us and you, mustawin amruhā, a matter upright and fair to both parties. Jews and Christians are invited to unite on this fair word in which all are equal.

**"that we will worship none but Allah, associate none with Him"**: we worship neither a statue, cross, idol, Taghut, false god, fire or anything else. Rather, we worship Allah alone without partners. This is the message of all Allah's messengers: "And We did not send any Messenger before you but We revealed to him (saying): 'None has the right to be worshipped but I (Allah), so worship Me (Alone and none else)'" (21:25), and "And verily, We have sent among every Ummah a Messenger (proclaiming): 'Worship Allah (Alone), and avoid (or keep away from) Taghut (all false deities)'" (16:36).

**"nor take one another as lords instead of Allah.”"**: Ibn Jurayj commented, "We do not obey each other in disobedience to Allah." Nobody is to obey another person in what involves a transgression against Allah, and nobody is to take rabbis and monks as lords, to be worshipped and followed besides Allah, no matter the person's rank or status.

**"But if they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that we have submitted ˹to Allah alone˺.”"**: if they abandon this fair call and reject God's Oneness, say to them, "Bear witness that we are Muslims", that we have surrendered to Allah and are of those who affirm His Oneness and obey Him. You will remain in Islam as Allah legislated for you.

### The letter to Heraclius and a problem of dates

The Prophet ﷺ wrote the same invitation to the Byzantine ruler. In al-Bukhari's version it runs:

> "I begin with the name of Allah who is All-Merciful, Very-Merciful. From Muhammad, servant of Allah, and His messenger: To Heraclius, the Byzantine emperor. Peace be on him who takes the right path. After that, I invite you to the call of Islam. Embrace Islam and be in peace. Allah will bestow upon you a twofold reward, but should you turn away, then, on you shall be the sin of your subjects."

Then the verse itself is quoted. In the other version the sender is "Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah", the greeting is "peace be upon those who follow the true guidance", the promise is that Allah will grant you a double reward, and the warning is that you will carry the burden of the peasants.

This raises a difficulty. Muhammad bin Ishaq and other scholars said the beginning of Surah Āl-ʿImrān, and more than eighty verses after it, were revealed concerning the Najran delegation. Az-Zuhri placed Najran first among peoples paying Jizyah, the tax paid to the Muslim state. Yet the Jizyah verse (9:29) belongs after Makkah's conquest, later than Najran's arrival in Al-Madinah. How could 3:64 enter a letter to Heraclius before the victory at Makkah, and how are these statements harmonised?

The proposed solution dates Najran before Al-Hudaybiyyah and treats its payment as Mubahalah's substitute rather than Jizyah. Later revelation supported what had occurred with Najran. Law can confirm prior practice: ʿAbdullah bin Jahsh divided raid booty into one fifth for the Prophet ﷺ and four-fifths for fighters before Badr, and later verses upheld the division. The Prophet ﷺ may therefore have written "Say, 'O People of the Scripture...'" before the Qur'anic verse descended, with revelation then matching his words exactly. Revelation also agreed with ʿUmar on Badr's prisoners, the Hijab, not praying for hypocrites, and his statements at (2:125) and (66:5).

### A principle of calling, and the close of an argument

Tabligh, preaching, and Daʿwah, calling to Islam, have a method. A person carrying his call to a group holding different beliefs should induce that group to unite only on what both can agree to. When the Prophet ﷺ called Heraclius he picked the one agreed point, the Oneness of Allah Almighty. And the closing words of the verse teach a second lesson. If someone refuses the truth after it has been proved clearly, the proper course is to restate your own belief and conclude the conversation. Further debate and verbal altercation are not appropriate.

Judged by this criterion, monotheism is not only a basic teaching of the Prophet Muhammad. It stands enshrined even in the interpolated versions of the Torah and the Bible. Monotheism implies belief in one God, worship of Him alone, no associates, and no human being accorded the place that is the sole prerogative of the Lord of the Universe. That concept is preserved in pure form in Islam in the Qur'an. Other religions, while accepting monotheism ideologically, adopted almost everything that ran counter to it: believing in God as Sustainer, in practice they accorded that status to their saints.

### The inward form of the common word

Realisation turns the address toward people of tawḥīd seeking ultimate reality. Tomorrow's dwellers in the seat of truthfulness (54:55) should guard today's walkway from customs' debris, clear mortal nature's opacities from the present moment's carpet and purify aspiration's drinking place from others' dust. Singleness of heart, desire and aspiration is prescribed: "When someone comes to have one concern, God will suffice him against the concerns of this world and the next."

"Some of us do not take others of us as lords apart from God" also forbids settling in every street with a scattered heart. Refuse obedience to the commanding soul. Do not make blameworthy caprice an object of worship: "take not two gods; surely He is but One God" (16:51). As long as some defiled fellow's talk grabs you, you serve your own fancy, not God.

### In short

- The common word is worship of Allah alone, no partners, and no human lords, the message of every messenger (21:25, 16:36).
- The same words went to Heraclius, and their presence before the Jizyah verse is explained by Najran's payment being in lieu of Mubahalah (9:29).
- When the fair call is refused, the method is to witness to your own submission and end the argument.

65.text:
The dispute now runs backward in time and collapses on its own chronology: "O People of the Book! Why do you argue about Abraham, while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until long after him? Do you not understand". Jews and Christians each claimed Ibrāhīm (Abraham) as one of their own. Neither Judaism nor Christianity existed when he lived, because both came after the books that founded them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O People of the Book! Why do you argue about Abraham"**: Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar reports through Ibn ʿAbbās that Najran Christians and Jewish rabbis disputed before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. "Ibrahim was certainly Jewish," said the rabbis. "Certainly, Ibrahim was Christian," said the Christians. This verse answered them. They also claimed surrender and adherence to Abraham's religion from the Torah.

**"while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until long after him?"**: how can you, Jews, claim Ibrāhīm was a Jew, when he lived before Allah sent down the Tawrah to Mūsā (Moses)? How can you, Christians, claim he was a Christian, when Christianity came after his time? The Torah was not revealed, and neither was the Gospel, until a very long time after him. Only after those two were revealed did Jewry and Christianity come into being. Neither book says that Abraham was Jew or Christian.

**"Do you not understand"**: have you then no sense? Do you not comprehend the falsehood of what you say?

### A cloak over the friend of God

Inwardly, possessiveness was cloaked with a niqāb and jealousy with a ḥijāb over His friend. After their accusation, his connection to every later claimant was severed and confused arguments decisively contradicted. No later religion can retroactively own Abraham.

### In short

- Ibrāhīm lived before the Torah and the Gospel, so he cannot have belonged to Judaism or Christianity.
- Both claims were made face to face before the Prophet ﷺ by Najran Christians and Jewish rabbis, and refuted by chronology.
- The friend of God is veiled from later claimants, not delivered to them.

66.text:
The rebuke sharpens from chronology to method: "Here you are! You disputed about what you have ˹little˺ knowledge of, but why do you now argue about what you have no knowledge of? Allah knows and you do not know". Disputing inside one's own scripture is one thing. Disputing about a man who predates it is another, and the verse orders unknown matters to be referred to the One who knows the seen and the unseen.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Here you are! You disputed about what you have ˹little˺ knowledge of"**: hā! You disputed concerning what you know: the affairs of Moses and Jesus, your claimed adherence to their religions, and the Law legislated for you until Muhammad ﷺ. Scripture itself had clear evidence, bayān, that could be proof, burhān: Muhammad is a prophet sent by Allah, and Abraham was neither Jew nor Christian. You rejected it.

**"but why do you now argue about what you have no knowledge of?"**: Abraham's circumstances are absent from your book and were not discussed by your prophets. Without definitive evidence, dalīl, and no way of knowing, maʿrifa, judgment and comprehension cannot be claimed.

**"Allah knows and you do not know"**: God knows his circumstances, and you know not that he was Jew or Christian, because he was neither. Allah knows the true reality of all things.

### Arguing without knowledge

This verse criticises everyone who argues and disputes without knowledge, as the Jews and Christians did over Ibrāhīm. Had they confined themselves to disputing about their religions, which they had knowledge of, it would have been better for them. Instead they argued about what they had no knowledge of, and Allah commanded them to refer such matters to Him Who knows the seen and unseen matters. Advocates in every age use the names of prophets and saints to justify additions and inventions, and with time people stop distinguishing the original religion from its later version, until the later version is taken as the real one. When the call to return to the true and pure religion is issued, opponents discredit it as an attack on what their saints handed down, although their yardstick is a body of later alterations, not the saints' own religion. This is how a veil of falsehood is drawn over the truth, through pronouncements invalid in religion and logic that the public cannot analyse.

### In short

- Dispute inside known revelation is bad enough, while dispute about Abraham, outside both books, has no evidence at all.
- Scripture itself contained the proof rejected: Muhammad's prophethood and Abraham's freedom from both labels.
- Unknown things must be referred to Allah, who knows reality, rather than claimed by inheritance.

67.text:
The answer is stated plainly: "Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian; he submitted in all uprightness and was not a polytheist". Ibrāhīm (Abraham) was a Ḥanīf and a Muslim, shunning shirk and living in īmān, faith. The Makkan polytheists made the same false claim in the other direction, calling their religion the faith of Abraham.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian"**: God dissociated Abraham from their claims. No, in truth he was not a Jew following the religion of the Jews, nor a Christian following the religion of the Christians. He was not a Jew or Christian in belief.

**"he submitted in all uprightness"**: he was a true Muslim Ḥanīfa, professing God's Oneness and leaving all other religions for the upright one. Treading monotheism's straight path, he opposed false religions and obeyed Allah alone.

**"and was not a polytheist"**: he was not of the Mushrikīn, and not one of those who ascribe partners to Allah. This cuts against the idolaters of the Arabs, who claimed to follow his belief while practising the opposite.

### What a Ḥanīf is

The Ḥanīf stands straight, mustaqīm, in truth. An aḥnaf may stand straight with curved legs, leaning on a twisted foot, so calling him mustaqīm is optimistic language. Abraham did not bend from truth, swerve from law or stumble after personal gain. He surrendered wealth, self and son, everything altogether, to God's decree, standing ready for His command.

Jews and Christians bracketed their religious history with Abraham's, and the Makkan polytheists did the same. In every age people use the names of prophets and saints to justify additions and inventions, until the later version passes for the original religion. Secondary features can be so emphasised by interpretation that they appear to be the main focus, while the fundamentals lose their significance. People stray from monotheism's thoroughfare into byways of unimportant issues. A Ḥanīf is the one who does not stray.

### The same answer in Surah Al-Baqarah

This verse is paired with the answer given in Surah Al-Baqarah: "And they say, 'Be Jews or Christians, then you will be guided...'" (2:135). The alternatives offered there are the same two labels claimed here, and both are answered by the Ḥanīf who precedes them.

### In short

- Ibrāhīm was a Muslim and a Ḥanīf, inclined away from every false religion toward the upright one, and no polytheist.
- Arab idolaters who claimed his faith are refuted by the same sentence that refutes Jews and Christians.
- A Ḥanīf stands straight in truth and surrenders wealth, self and son to God's decree.

68.text:
The right to Abraham is awarded: "Indeed, those who have the best claim to Abraham are his followers, this Prophet, and the believers." And "Allah is the Guardian of those who believe". Claims to Abraham are weighed by practice rather than argument volume. His own era's followers, Muhammad ﷺ, and those who believe in him carry the right.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, those who have the best claim to Abraham are his followers"**: the strongest right to follow Ibrahim belongs to those who followed his religion during his time. They, rather than you, deserve to say, "We follow his religion." 

**"this Prophet, and the believers"**: and this Prophet, Muhammad ﷺ, and his Companions from the Muhājirīn, the Anṣār and those who followed their lead. Muhammad follows Abraham's religion and accords with him in most of the rulings of his Law, and those who believe in Muhammad and in the Qur'an follow Abraham's religion too.

**"And Allah is the Guardian of those who believe"**: Allah is the Walī, the Protector and Helper of the believers, their Helper and Preserver. He is the Protector of all those who believe in His messengers.

### The occasion, and every prophet's guardian among prophets

Ibn ʿAbbās said the leaders of the Jews declared, "By Allah, O Muhammad, you know that we have the better claim to Abraham's religion than you or anybody else, and you know that he was a Jew. You are only resentfully envious!" Then Allah revealed this verse.

Saʿīd bin Mansur recorded that Ibn Masʿud said the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Every Prophet had a Wali (supporter, best friend) from among the Prophets. My Wali among them is my father Ibrahim, the Khalil (intimate friend) of my Lord, the Exalted and Most Honored." The Prophet ﷺ then recited this verse.

The community is identified in the same terms: the closest people to Ibrāhīm now are the Prophet of Islam, Muhammad al-Mustafa ﷺ, and the believers in him and in past prophets. These believers are Muhammad's community, guarded by Allah, who rewards their belief.

### One party across the ages

Whims, ahwāʾ, and blameworthy innovations, bidaʿ, break a group into factions, each ending in error. The people of truth, ahl al-ḥaqq, in every era, time and moment, hold to the best proof and form a single party. Abraham, truth's companion, ṣāḥib al-ḥaqq, gives that party its claim over others. Professing his religion, in the manner of our Messenger ﷺ and his community, places a person inside Abraham's religion, whose core is declaring God's unity, tawḥīd.

### A second report behind the claim

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm reported the same saying from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with a longer setting also mentioned by Muhammad ibn Ishaq bin Yasar. After Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib and his companions migrated to Abyssinia and settled there, and after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ migrated to Madinah and the Battle of Badr followed, the Quraysh met in Dar al-Nadwah. They resolved to exact revenge for their dead at Badr from Muhammad's Companions who were with the Negus. Money and gifts, including tanned skins, were collected for the Negus, and two men of good judgement were selected for the mission: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and ʿUmārah ibn Abi Muʿayt. They sailed across the sea to Abyssinia, prostrated themselves before the Negus and greeted him, and warned him that the emigrants represented a liar who had emerged among them claiming to be Allah's Messenger, followed only by fools. They claimed the Quraysh had made life very hard on them, driven them to the canyons, cut off all access, and left them destroyed by hunger and thirst. The report as it stands breaks off at that appeal.

### In short

- The best claim to Abraham belongs to his followers in his own time, to Muhammad ﷺ, and to the believers, not to late argument.
- The Prophet ﷺ named his own Walī among the prophets as his father Ibrahim, the Khalil of his Lord.
- Allah guards the believers with aid, help, selection and nearness, in every age one party holding the best proof.

69.text:
A wish is exposed and turned back on those who held it: "Some of the People of the Book wish to mislead you ˹believers˺. They mislead none but themselves, yet they fail to perceive it". The Jews envy the faithful and want them misguided, as they had been misguided themselves. The punishment of the attempt falls on the attempters, while they remain unaware of it.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Some of the People of the Book wish to mislead you ˹believers˺"**: a party from Scripture's people longs to push you away from Islam. Jewish and Christian scholars want believers diverted from Allah-guided truth.

**"They mislead none but themselves, yet they fail to perceive it"**: straying's burden lands on guides whose audience will not follow them. Attempts deepen their own misguidance and carry consequences they cannot see. A second possibility is that Allah's informing His Prophet escapes their perception.

### The invitation after Uhud

The occasion was an invitation to named Companions. After the Battle of Uhud, Kaʿb al-Ashraf invited ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, Muʿādh ibn Jabal and Hudhayfa ibn al-Yamān to join Judaism and leave Islam. The verse was revealed about ʿAmmār, Muʿādh and Hudhayfa when the Jews called them to embrace their religion. The signs at stake sat in the Torah and Injil themselves.

Misery tries to reproduce itself inwardly. People ruined by discord, tribulation and temptation wish their condition on everyone. Believers were their target, but God would perfect His light and return the evil effects to the actors.

### In short

- Envious scholars wish the believers misguided and only deepen their own misguidance, unaware.
- The named targets were Muʿādh, Hudhayfa and ʿAmmār, invited to Judaism after Uhud.
- Discord wishes its own condition on everyone, but Allah perfects His light instead.

70.text:
The accusation moves from wish to contradiction: "O People of the Book! Why do you reject the signs of Allah while you bear witness ˹to their truth˺". They know for certain that Allah's verses are true and authentic, and they bear witness to them. Their disbelief targets what their own books confirm.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O People of the Book! Why do you reject the signs of Allah"**: why disbelieve in the revelations of Allah, Muhammad and the Qur'an, and in the verses in Torah and Injīl proving Muhammad's prophethood? To deny his prophethood is to declare those verses false, which is infidelity.

**"while you bear witness ˹to their truth˺"**: Scripture itself teaches you that Muhammad is a prophet sent by Allah. His prophecy's authenticity had your witness before the mission, and confirmation of these signs comes from you.

### Knowledge aggravates, but never licenses

The witness and knowledge named in these two verses do not mean that disbelief would be acceptable without them. Kufr, disbelief, is intrinsically abominable to practise and is prohibited under all conditions. Attestation and knowledge are mentioned to increase the impact of reproach. You disavow what you know, and the reproach lands because the knowledge is there.

### In short

- The signs rejected include their own Torah and Injīl verses proving Muhammad's prophethood.
- Witnessing the truth beforehand makes denial a disavowal of knowledge, not an error of ignorance.
- Disbelief is forbidden in every condition, and knowledge only deepens the rebuke.

71.text:
The second reproach names the method: "O People of the Book! Why do you mix the truth with falsehood and hide the truth knowingly". Truth and falsehood are first blended, by distortion and false explanation, and then the truth left clear, such as the description of the Prophet in their books, is hidden by people who know exactly what they are doing.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O People of the Book! Why do you mix the truth with falsehood"**: why do you confound, mix, truth with falsehood by distorting and falsifying Scripture?
