The real statement, the prophecy of Muhammad's prophethood, is confused with the fictitious, interpolated statements and false exegesis. Muhammad's traits are confounded with those assigned to the anti-Christ.

**"and hide the truth knowingly"**: conceal Muhammad's description and traits as found in Scripture, despite knowing your conduct, knowing the truth, and knowing what is false.

### Forsaking as a judgement, and the double life

Regarding Muḥammad's affair, concealment persists despite knowledge that he is a truthful Prophet. Nothing explains it inwardly except divine forsaking, ḥukm al-khidhlān, and deprivation's decision, qaḍiyyat al-ḥirmān, descending on concealers.

Hypocrites are also exposed among them. They wanted to forestall trouble with the Muslims while avoiding conflict with their brothers among the disbelievers. So they conspired to pretend agreement publicly with the Messenger ﷺ and the Muslims while secretly remaining true among themselves to their corrupt beliefs.

### In short

- Mixing is done by interpolation and false explanation, while hiding is done by concealing the Prophet's description, knowingly.
- The traits of the anti-Christ are even confounded with Muhammad's traits to complete the confusion.
- Concealment is read as divine forsaking, and its social form is a public agreement that hides private corruption.

72.text:
A staged conversion is described from the inside: "A group among the People of the Book said ˹to one another˺, “Believe in what has been revealed to the believers in the morning and reject it in the evening, so they may abandon their faith". The plan was cooked up to manufacture doubt. A learned group would enter Islam at dawn and leave it by night, hoping weak believers would conclude that the learned had found a defect.

### Phrase by phrase

**"A group among the People of the Book said ˹to one another˺, “Believe in what has been revealed to the believers in the morning"**: a party from Scripture's people told some among them to believe in the Qur'an, revealed to believers, at dawn prayer's opening.

**"and reject it in the evening"**: and disbelieve in it at the end of the day, at the end thereof, at the Ẓuhr prayer in the qiblah version.

**"so they may abandon their faith"**: so that they, the believers, may turn back from Muhammad's religion. The ignorant would say, "They reverted to their old religion because they uncovered some shortcomings in the Islamic religion." Or: "These Jews are knowledgeable, and they could only have turned away after accepting it because they know it to be false." Or, in the plotters' own summary, "These people know better about Allah's Book and they have turned back."

### Twelve rabbis and a script

Al-Ḥasan and as-Suddī give the conspiracy a cast: twelve rabbis from Khaybar's Jews and the town of Uraynah. Morning would bring pretended entry into Muhammad's religion. Evening would bring declared disbelief. Their alternative line announced scriptural research and scholarly consultation proving Muhammad not genuine, clearly a lying falsehood. Doubt among his Companions would follow, because People of the Book seemed more knowledgeable. Revelation warned the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and believers.

According to Ibn Abī Najīḥ, Mujāhid pictured Jews at dawn prayer beside the Prophet ﷺ, then unbelieving by day's end. Brief adherence was meant to look like investigation that uncovered defects in a briefly followed religion.

### The qiblah version of the same trick

Mujāhid, Muqātil and al-Kalbī connect revelation with the qiblah's change toward the Kaʿbah. Resistance to being opposed led Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and companions to tell lowly people to accept Muhammad's Kaʿbah revelation and pray toward it in the morning, then disbelieve in the Kaʿbah and restore the former qiblah that night. Observers might declare that People of the Book knew better and return to their qiblah and religion.

The plan had a rule of sincerity kept for its own side. The feigned declaration of belief in Islam was reserved to hoodwink Muslims only. True belief would be affirmed before none but those who follow their own creed: sincerity with the latter, expediency with the former.

By exposing it, God showed that their hypocrisy benefited them in neither world. In this world Allah informed His Prophet and the believers of it. In the hereafter it deprived them of sincere devotion toward God.

### In short

- Twelve rabbis of Khaybar and Uraynah scripted a dawn conversion and an evening apostasy to make Muslims suspect a discovered defect.
- The same staged trick is reported around the change of qiblah toward the Kaʿbah, driven by Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf.
- Exposure cancels the trick in this world, and the absence of sincere devotion cancels it in the next.

73.text:
The plotters' private instruction follows: "And only believe those who follow your religion.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Surely, ˹the only˺ true guidance is Allah’s guidance.” ˹They also said,˺ “Do not believe that someone will receive ˹revealed˺ knowledge similar to yours or argue against you before your Lord.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Indeed, all bounty is in the Hands of Allah—He grants it to whoever He wills. And Allah is All-Bountiful, All-Knowing.”" Knowledge is to be hoarded inside the community and denied to outsiders, because outsiders given the like of it would become equals, or better.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And only believe those who follow your religion.”"**: secret knowledge should be trusted only to followers of your religion. Belief or acceptance was limited to a Jew following Judaism and its Jerusalem qiblah. Muslims were to be denied exposure that might create faith or furnish proof. Li-man's lām is extra, yielding "follow and accord with your religion".

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Surely, ˹the only˺ true guidance is Allah’s guidance.”"**: God's guidance is Islam. All else is error. Its parenthetical placement does not reduce its force. Islam is Allah's religion, and the Kaʿbah is His qiblah.

**"˹They also said,˺ “Do not believe that someone will receive ˹revealed˺ knowledge similar to yours or argue against you before your Lord.”"**: the Book, wisdom and virtues they received should be admitted as given to nobody unless religion is followed. Ahad, "anyone", precedes the exception, producing exclusion before identification. Another construal guards against believers disputing and prevailing before their Lord on Resurrection Day from a supposedly sounder religion. A rebuking hamza in a variant demands denial that another could receive its like and be affirmed.

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Indeed, all bounty is in the Hands of Allah—He grants it to whoever He wills. And Allah is All-Bountiful, All-Knowing.”"**: bounty lies in Allah's Hand and goes to whomever He wills. He suffices His creatures' needs, embraces bounty amply, and knows recipients and deserving people. Prophethood, Islam and Abraham's Qiblah are Muhammad and his Companions' portion.

### Why the secret had to be kept

Their rationale is superiority lost. If Muslims learn the secret, equality follows. Indeed, belief could make them better still, or proof could be used against their teachers before the Lord in this life and the Hereafter. Allah nevertheless guides faithful hearts to perfect faith through clear verses, plain proofs and unequivocal evidence sent down to His servant and Messenger Muhammad ﷺ. This happens even though the description of Muhammad ﷺ is hidden, the unlettered Prophet already present in the Books received from earlier prophets. Giving and taking belong to His control. He gives faith, knowledge and sound comprehension to whomever He wills, and He misguides whomever He wills by blinding sight and mind, sealing his heart and hearing and stamping his eyes closed, with perfect wisdom and unequivocal proofs.

Their motive is envy, envy that Muslims were given the Scripture, or envy of their supremacy in religious argument. The tricks fail for the same reason. Guidance is in Allah's control, so He can make whoever He will steadfast on it, and no trick, plan or enticement can wean such a person away.

### A second address: the caress of the believers

Some explainers take part of this address as God's speech to the Muslims, caressing the folk of recognition and faith and reminding them of His favour in the religion of submission. It then has two paths: one toward the common faithful of this community, and one toward the recognisers and the elect among the folk of the Ṭarīqah. In the first respect it runs: "O assembly of submitters! Do not suppose or hold firm that anyone has been given what has been given to you." Submission is unmatched as religion, the Qur'an as book and Muḥammad as prophet, each given to you. Ramadan is unmatched as a month and Friday as a day, and both belong to you. Shari'ahs fall before your shariah and compacts before your compact. Covenant holds perfection of religion and Shariah, together with beauty of Tariqah and Haqiqah: "Today I have perfected your religion for..." (5:3).

Gratitude is then commanded, and with it a boundary: "Do not have faith in any but those who follow your religion." Friendship belongs only to sharers of religion, brotherhood only to the faithful, and distance must be kept from the irreligious and the estranged. This is what He says here too: "Do not lean upon those who do..." (11:113).

### In short

- Secret knowledge is to be kept from outsiders lest they equal or surpass its owners and use it as proof before the Lord.
- True guidance is Allah's guidance alone, Islam, and bounty is in His hand to give without asking any community's permission.
- Some explainers also hear the verse caressing the believers: no religion, book, prophet, month or day like theirs was given to anyone (5:3, 11:113).

74.text:
The answer ends with selection: "He chooses whoever He wills to receive His mercy. And Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty". Guidance, prophethood and favour are not a community's inheritance to guard. They are gifts distributed by a bounty that singles out whom it wills, and envy misunderstands the nature, timing and wisdom of grace.

### Phrase by phrase

**"He chooses whoever He wills to receive His mercy"**: Muhammad and his Companions are singled out for His religion and mercy. Selection from creation brings guidance, prophethood and numerous favours to whomever He wishes.

**"And Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty"**: Allah is of bounty abounding. He is generous toward Muhammad by bestowing on him prophethood and Islam. He has endowed you, O believers, with tremendous virtue, honouring your Prophet Muhammad ﷺ over all other prophets and directing you to the best Shari'ah there is.

### Mercy distributed in kinds

Blessings are singled out by kind. Provisions go to one group. Another receives character traits, another worship, and another desire. Outward success belongs elsewhere, while secret cores are realised by some and encountered by others. Still others receive outer skins as a gift. God says, and His words are truth: "If you count God's blessings, you will..." (14:34).

The recipients remain grouped obscurely, with nobody specified, so hope can grow in the hopeful and fear not harden in the fearful. No servant states surpass hope and fear in worship and obedience, and the Lord of the Worlds praises servants in these states: "They hope for His mercy and fear..." (17:57).

Utmost striving changes nothing at the final step. After complete obedience and every condition of servanthood, deliverance still comes by God's mercy. A prophetic narration says:

> "No one will enter the Garden by his deeds." It was said to him, "Not even you, O Messenger of God!" He said, "Not even I, unless God envelops me with His mercy." 

### In short

- Allah selects Muhammad and his Companions, and whomever He wills, for His mercy, and His bounty has no limit.
- Mercy is distributed in many kinds, material, moral, inward and secret, beyond counting (14:34).
- Being left unspecified feeds hope and fear together, and even perfect obedience is finally delivered by mercy, not by deeds.

75.text:
Trust in money divides the People of the Book into two kinds: "There are some among the People of the Book who, if entrusted with a stack of gold, will readily return it. Yet there are others who, if entrusted with a single coin, will not repay it unless you constantly demand it. This is because they say, “We are not accountable for ˹exploiting˺ the Gentiles.” And ˹so˺ they attribute lies to Allah knowingly". After breach of faith in belief, breach of trust in property is named, and the verse refuses to paint a whole community with one brush.

### Phrase by phrase

**"There are some among the People of the Book who, if entrusted with a stack of gold, will readily return it"**: Scripture's people include a man who repays a Qintar, a great amount of wealth, without problem, hardship or temptation to declare it lawful. Smaller sums obviously follow. ʿAbdullāh Ibn Salām and his companions are the named example: a man entrusted ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām with 1200 plates of gold, and they were returned.

**"Yet there are others who, if entrusted with a single coin, will not repay it unless you constantly demand it"**: another man keeps even a dinar, one silver coin, unless the owner stands over him without leaving for a minute. Departure invites denial. More than a dinar is still less safe. Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf denied a Quraysh man's entrusted dinar.

**"This is because they say, “We are not accountable for ˹exploiting˺ the Gentiles.”"**: their stated doctrine excuses betrayal and seizure of illiterate people's property, the Arabs. Religion supposedly suffers no harm when unlettered property is eaten, because Allah allegedly permitted it. Injustice toward anyone of another religion became lawful in their conviction, and God was made its source.

**"And ˹so˺ they attribute lies to Allah knowingly"**: they tell a lie against Allah while they know it, a lie and word of misguidance they invented. Unless they had a right to it, Allah would not have allowed them this money.

### A test case: chickens and sheep taken in battle

ʿAbd ar-Razzāq records Saʿsaʿah bin Yazid's question to Ibn ʿAbbās about battlefield capture of Ahl Adh-Dhimmah property, such as chickens and sheep. The captors regarded confiscation as sinless. Ibn ʿAbbās answered that they were repeating the People of the Book's claim about illiterates. Once Jizyah is paid, their property is forbidden except what they willingly surrender.

From "unless you keep standing over him", Imam Abu Hanifah derived a lender's right to pursue the borrower until receiving his due, as al-Qurtubi noted.

### Can a disbeliever's good deed be praised?

Some in this verse are praised for trustworthiness. If the trustworthy are those among the People of the Book who had embraced Islam, the praise poses no problem. But if they are People of the Book in the absolute sense, including non-Muslims, a question arises: when no act of a kāfir, a disbeliever, is acceptable, why praise it?

The answer separates acceptability from praise. An action's acceptance with Allah is one question, whether observers praise it is another. Praise does not produce acceptance. Good in a disbeliever still counts as good to a degree: reputation in the mortal world and reduced punishment in the Hereafter benefit him. Prejudice and short-sightedness are rejected, and an adversary's excellence receives open-hearted appreciation.

The inward reading agrees that moral quality varies beneath a shared religious failure. Trust of religion, amāna of dīn, may be broken while proper human interactions are respected. Sincere dealing earns no reward for a disbeliever but can lessen punishment, since detailed laws hold disbelievers accountable. Lesser sin means less suffering than the worst offenders, though punishment remains perpetual. Judgment is not theirs, and the words about Gentiles settle nothing.

The positive picture is completed by a description of chosen servants. Being chosen to represent God's religion is not based on belonging to a certain community. The recipient is one selected for spiritual virtues, attached to God and fearing Him until He becomes his Keeper and Lord in the true sense. One who enters a covenant with his Creator cannot go back. Those who fulfil trusts and keep promises are showered with blessings, while the careless in trusts and promises are of no value in God's eyes.

### In short

- A Qintar returned by ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and a dinar denied by Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf mark the two kinds of trustee.
- "No accountability toward the Gentiles" is a lie invented against Allah, and it does not cover even a dhimmī's chickens once jizyah is paid.
- A disbeliever's honesty can be praised without being accepted, earning reputation here and lighter punishment there.

76.text:
The short verse answers with the opposite portrait: "Absolutely! Those who honour their trusts and shun evil—surely Allah loves those who are mindful ˹of Him˺". Yes, there is duty toward the Gentiles. And yes, covenant-keeping, not community membership, is what Allah loves.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Absolutely! Those who honour their trusts"**: Nay, duty in this regard is incumbent. A covenant made personally, or God's covenant itself, is fulfilled by restoring trusts and other obligations. Allah's chosen keeper honours pledges made with his Lord as well as pledges made with people.

**"and shun evil"**: God-fearing protects pledges from treachery and reversal. Disobedience is refrained from, obedience performed, and Allah's promise to believe in Him and His Messenger is kept alongside promises to honour human trusts. Instructions are fulfilled and prohibitions avoided.

**"surely Allah loves those who are mindful ˹of Him˺"**: Allah loves the Muttaqin, the pious. "He loves them" means He will reward them. The overt noun al-muttaqīn, the God-fearing, replaces the pronoun.

### The covenant meant, and the Sunnah's constant stress

Fulfilment here first targets the covenant Allah took from the People of the Book to believe in Muhammad ﷺ when he was sent, a covenant also taken from all prophets and their nations. Avoiding prohibitions, obeying Him and adhering to the Shari'ah sent with the Final Messenger ﷺ, master of all mankind, fulfil it. Qur'an and Sunnah stress fulfilled commitments again and again.

### Who is loved, and who is shamed

Those who hold to the covenant deserve to be united in friendship, honour and the garden. Those who are in error deserve aversion, ignominy and shame. The loved person is chosen for spiritual virtues. A servant attached to God and fearing Him can have Him as Keeper and Lord in the fullest sense of those words. God's chosen servants fulfil their trusts and do not break their promises, and people such as these are showered with God's blessings.

### In short

- Yes: covenant-keeping and God-fearing are the loved qualities, against the claim of no duty.
- The pledge chiefly meant is the covenant to believe in Muhammad ﷺ, alongside every trust between people.
- Covenant-keepers win friendship, honour and the garden, while promise-breakers earn aversion and shame.

77.text:
The warning against covenant-breaking is total: "Indeed, those who trade Allah’s covenant and their oaths for a fleeting gain will have no share in the Hereafter. Allah will neither speak to them, nor look at them, nor purify them on the Day of Judgment. And they will suffer a painful punishment". Whoever prefers the small things of a short life to fulfilling what he promised Allah sells the Hereafter at the cheapest price in the passage.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, those who trade Allah’s covenant and their oaths for a fleeting gain"**: a small worldly price is purchased at the cost of Allah's covenant and oaths. Distortion of the Prophet's descriptions and God's Torah covenant, together with false witness and false selling oaths, instantiate the trade. God's name is invoked mendaciously.

**"will have no share in the Hereafter"**: they shall have no portion in Paradise, no share or part in the Hereafter's rewards. Small gain in their living has consumed it.

**"Allah will neither speak to them, nor look at them, nor purify them on the Day of Judgment"**: no kind or nice speech, no merciful look, and no purification from sins and impurities await them. Jewish status brings no exoneration or peace of mind. Wrath is the mode in which He addresses them, and their order is toward Fire.

**"And they will suffer a painful punishment"**: painful doom awaits them, severe pain spreading into their hearts.

### The five warnings and the right of another servant

An ʿahd, pledge or covenant, is what is settled between parties after mutual discussion and binding on both. A waʿdah, promise, issues from one side only. So ʿahd is bilateral and waʿdah unilateral, and breaking a bilateral covenant draws the heavier charge.

Five warnings are counted against those who break their solemn pledge. They will have no share, no lot, in the blessings of heaven. Allah will not speak to them with glad tidings. Allah will not look at them mercifully on the Day of Doom. Their sins against a servant's right will not simply be forgiven: breach of trust wastes another human being's due, and God does not forgive what a human being owes to a human being. This is ḥaqq al-ʿabd, the right of a servant of Allah. A grievous punishment awaits them.

A hadith scales the point down: false-oath usurpation of a Muslim's right makes Hell compulsory even over an insignificant green tree bough. Muslim reports it.

### The hadiths gathered under this verse

Abu Dharr's report in Imam Ahmad says:

> "There are three persons whom Allah will not speak to, look at on the Day of Resurrection or purify, and they shall taste a painful torment. I said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Who are they, may they gain failure and loss?' He said, repeating this statement thrice, 'The Musbil (man whose clothes reach below the ankles), he who swears while lying so as to sell his merchandize and the one who gives charity and reminds people of it.'"

Muslim and collectors of the Sunan also record it.

ʿAdi bin ʿAmirah Al-Kindi tells of a land dispute in Ahmad involving Imru' Al-Qays bin ʿAbis of Kindah and a man from Hadramut. With no evidence from the Hadrami, an oath was required from Imru'. The Hadrami warned that swearing would lose his land by the Lord of the Ka'bah. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Whoever swears while lying to acquire the property of others, will meet Allah while He is angry with him." Raja' adds that the verse was then recited. Imru' asked what forfeiting gained. "Paradise" was the answer, so he witnessed that all the land was yielded. An-Nasa'i also records it. Accounts also attach the verse's revelation to ʿAbdan Ibn al-Ashuʿ and Imra' al-Qays and their dispute, as well as to the Jews.

ʿAbdullah reports another saying in Imam Ahmad: "Whoever takes a false oath to deprive a Muslim of his property will meet Allah while He is angry with him." Al-Ash'ath recognised his own land dispute with a Jewish man in it. He had no evidence. The Jew was asked to swear. He predicted an immediate false oath and lost property. Revelation followed. The Two Sahihs record the hadith. In a fuller report, al-Ashʿath ibn Qays heard Abu Abd al-Rahman relating this and said, "This verse was revealed about me." Bukhari narrates it from Abdan, from Abu Hamzah, from al-A'mash.

Abu Hurayrah reports in Imam Ahmad three more people Allah shall not speak to, look at, or purify on Resurrection Day, with painful torment: a man who withholds surplus water from a wayfarer, a man who swears falsely after ʿAsr prayer to complete a sale, and a man who pledges allegiance to an Imam and obeys only when given something. Abu Dawud and At-Tirmidhi record it too, and At-Tirmidhi graded it Hasan Sahih.

### A life that chooses the world at every fork

On embracing the faith, a person enters a covenant with God that he will obey Him and fulfil all the responsibilities God's law imposes, living among human beings under self-constraint. Such a life can be lived only by one who has risen above worldly interests. Whoever overlooks the divine pact whenever his self suffers or his interests are endangered barters the Hereafter at a paltry price. At every choice between world and Hereafter he prefers the world. How can one who values the Hereafter so little deserve God's mercies there?

Inwardly, caprice, hawāhum, wins over final outcome, ʿuqbāhum, and desires, munāhum, win over harmonious agreement with their Protector, mawlāhum. Present pleasure has cost both abodes and left them apart from the Real. Worldly pleasure, ḥaẓẓ, brought tribulations they fail to recognise, and their punishment is made to remain beyond time's count.

### In short

- Selling the covenant and oaths for a small gain forfeits any share in the Hereafter and draws silence, averted mercy, no purification and painful torment.
- False oaths over property stand at the centre of the hadiths, from Imru' al-Qays's land case to al-Ashʿath's disputed plot, and even a green bough counts.
- The habit beneath it is constant: at every fork the world is preferred, and caprice is chosen over the final outcome.

78.text:
Distortion is described as performance: "There are some among them who distort the Book with their tongues to make you think this ˹distortion˺ is from the Book—but it is not what the Book says. They say, “It is from Allah”—but it is not from Allah. And ˹so˺ they attribute lies to Allah knowingly". Words are twisted in recitation until invention sounds like revelation. The speaker knows the difference, and says it anyway.

### Phrase by phrase

**"There are some among them who distort the Book with their tongues to make you think this ˹distortion˺ is from the Book"**: Jewish distorters alter Allah's Words by tongue, move them from their proper places and change intended meanings, so the ignorant think Allah's Book contains them. Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf's party twisted tongues in recitation, especially with the Prophet's descriptions, and read anti-Christ traits into Scripture for lowly listeners.

**"but it is not what the Book says. They say, “It is from Allah”—but it is not from Allah"**: it is not from the Book, and not from Allah in the Torah. Instead, it is lies and fabrications against Allah. They attribute their own lies to Allah, knowing they have lied and invented falsehood.

**"And ˹so˺ they attribute lies to Allah knowingly"**: they speak a lie concerning Allah, fully aware that this is not in their Scripture. Mujāhid, ash-Shaʿbī, al-Ḥasan, Qatādah and Ar-Rabi' bin Anas explained the twisting of the Book by tongues simply as altering Allah's Words.

### Preserved books and tampered meanings

Al-Bukhari reports Ibn ʿAbbās as saying their activity is alteration and addition, because no created being can remove Allah's Words from His Books. Apparent meanings, rather, are altered and distorted.

Wahb bin Munabbih said:

> "The Tawrah and the Injil remain as Allah revealed them, and no letter in them was removed. However, the people misguide others by addition and false interpretation, relying on books that they wrote themselves. Then, 'they say: "This is from Allah," but it is not from Allah.' As for Allah's Books, they are still preserved and cannot be changed."

Ibn Abi Hatim recorded this statement.

Two qualifications follow. If Wahb meant the books currently in the hands of the People of the Book, alteration, distortion, addition and deletion are certain. Tremendous error and misinterpretation fill Arabic versions, and translators generally misunderstand them. If Wahb meant Allah's Books kept with Him, preservation without change is the meaning.

### A false claim on the path

Inward allusion targets false claimants on this path, Ṭarīqa. Their sayings are embellished and tongues loose concerning matters heart has neither information nor verification about. Foolish ordinary people and novices are deceived into imagining realisation. Deception's lords talk to the weak and expose the secrets of the people of realities, ahl al-ḥaqāʾiq, before them. Ruined hearts, qulūb, and veiled innermost selves, asrār, produce falsehood they know to be false.

During the Najran deputation, some Jews and Christians had asked: "O Muhammad, do you want us to worship you the way Christians worship Jesus, son of Mary?" He said: "I seek refuge with Allah that we worship someone other than Allah or call on others to do so. Allah Almighty has not sent us to do that." This verse followed, setting distortion in speech beside the refusal to be worshipped.

### In short

- Tongues twist the Book by altered recitation and interpretation so invention is mistaken for revelation, especially around the Prophet's description.
- Ibn ʿAbbās and Wahb hold the revealed Books preserved with God, while the copies in human hands are altered, added to and mistranslated.
- The same figure marks false teachers on the path, whose eloquent tongues speak from ruined hearts and veiled innermost selves.

79.text:
A prophet cannot become the object of worship: "It is not appropriate for someone who Allah has blessed with the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood to say to people, “Worship me instead of Allah.” Rather, he would say, “Be devoted to the worship of your Lord ˹alone˺”—in accordance with what these prophets read in the Scripture and what they taught". The verse was revealed when Najran Christians claimed Jesus had commanded them to take him as a divinity, and when some Muslims asked to be permitted to prostrate before the Prophet ﷺ rather than greet him with the salām.

### Phrase by phrase

**"It is not appropriate for someone who Allah has blessed with the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood to say to people, “Worship me instead of Allah.”"**: a human recipient of the Book, Al-Hukm (knowledge in the Law) and prophethood cannot proclaim worship for himself alongside Allah. A prophet or messenger lacks this right, so nobody else can possess it.

**"Rather, he would say, “Be devoted to the worship of your Lord ˹alone˺”"**: on the contrary, the messenger recommends that people be Rabbaniyyun, devoted to the worship of their Lord alone. Be faithful servants of the Lord, masters and scholars labouring, rabbāniyyūn, "those of the Lord", derived from rabb, "lord", with an extra alif and nūn as a superlative of rabbiyyūn. Ibn ʿAbbās, Abu Razin and several others said Rabbaniyyun means wise, learned, and forbearing.

**"in accordance with what these prophets read in the Scripture and what they taught"**: because you are teaching the Book, and you are studying it. It is also read "you teach" of the Book, and "in what you study", on account of the fact that you used to do this, so that its benefit is that you engage in action. Ad-Dahhak commented: "Whoever learns the Qur'an deserves to become a Faqih (learned)." Studying means preserving its words, and also knowledge of Scripture, reading from it, and putting what is learned into practice.

### Infallibility argued from appointment

The verse implies that a person invested by Allah with the Book, the Wisdom, the power of decisions and the station of prophethood remains faithful in communicating the message and calling people to be His servants. He cannot move them away from worship of one God and ask them to worship himself or other creatures. If he did, he would not deserve the designation.

A worldly government appointing someone to responsibility considers ability to understand and execute policy, and how far the appointee can be expected to execute directives and hold subjects in loyalty. No king or parliament knowingly appoints a representative suspected of anti-government activity or deviation. A human government may still misjudge ability or loyalty, but with Allah no such failure of knowledge exists. If He knows a man will not overstep loyalty and obedience even slightly, that man cannot later prove contrary to the assessment, unless divine knowledge were defective. From here the ʿiṣmah, the infallibility of the prophets, becomes clear. ʿIṣmah is a special protection given by Allah which makes a prophet refrain from sins. If the prophets are free of minor sins, the probability of shirk, associating others with Allah, or revolt against Allah cannot remain valid.

The refutation reaches three parties. Christians claimed that the Masīḥ asked them to believe in his sonship and godhead. Muslims who approached the Prophet ﷺ about prostrating before him rather than greeting him with salām were chastised. People of the Book who invested rabbis and monks with God's station were admonished.

### Messengers, custodians and cults

The messengers are emissaries between Allah and His creation, conveying His message and trust. They fulfilled their mission, gave sincere advice and conveyed the truth. The criticism here falls instead on ignorant rabbis, priests and teachers of misguidance. Sincere knowledgeable followers implement what they know and command what Allah commands through His messengers. A teaching can be tested by direction. The simplest testimony of truth is that it brings God's servants closer to their Lord and directs love and fear toward God. Any teaching producing a personal cult, or diverting finer feelings toward anything other than God, is based on falsehood even when couched in religious terms. Aspirants to worldly honour pervert teachings by altering wording or wilfully misinterpreting them for selfish interests. Rather than changing themselves, they change God's Book, seeking a religious aura for irreligious lives. Attributing to God what He did not say is the most heinous crime.

### The lordly ones

Before the universe existed and Adam was created, God knew in His eternal knowledge who among Adam's children would be worthy of prophethood and friendship, qualified for love and suited for messengerhood. "God knows better where to place His message" (6:124). The chosen MuṣṬafā and the caressed Jesus, after the honour of prophethood, confirmation of sinlessness and strength of messengerhood, could never step out of line and say, "Be servants of me instead of God!" By virtue of beginningless choice and eternal solicitude, the Lord of the Worlds answers on their behalf as deputy: "They do not say this. Rather they say, 'Be you lordly ones!'"

The lordly ones are singled out for God and described in His words: "When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears and his eyesight with which he sees." In the tasting of the folk of recognition, they become one for God with disengaged intention, sound trust and the breeze of intimacy. They step beyond the two worlds and seize the gentleness of the Patron's love. They say the prayer of the dead over their own attributes. They have souls undergoing annihilation and hearts full of thirst, burnt souls, secret cores lit by passion, and spirits hanging in hope: "I want a heart for choosing only You, a spirit for breathing the pain of Your passion, a body for desiring only Your love, an eye for seeing You and only You." Their aspiration goes beyond this world, their desire beyond Paradise, their repose beyond heaven and earth. They wait for the sun of love to rise, the moon of good fortune to come forth, the breeze of felicity to blow, and beginningless remembrance to bear fruit: "When will I throw off this cage and build a nest in the divine garden!?"

They are also those characterised by God's character traits. MuṣṬafā said, "Become characterized by the character traits of God!" and, "God has a number of character traits. Whoever becomes characterized by one of them will enter the Garden." The folk of knowledge have said that commentary on these traits is the meaning of the ninety-nine names of God, and that the servant must pass by way of these meanings in travelling to union. The Pir of Khurasan, Abu'l-Qāsim Kurragānī, warned that acquiring meanings and descriptions keeps a servant merely travelling. God's attraction has not yet arrived. Recognition can hold a seeker back from the Recognized, and seeking love can hide the Beloved. "Hurry to passion and don't sit in attachment, take a few steps beyond passion and being passionate!" A great man was asked when the servant reaches the Patron. He said, "When he reaches himself." Asked how, he said: "Seeking becomes lost in the Sought and recognition in the Recognized." Asked to explain more, he reduced the traveller to tongue in body, mark in heart, face-to-face vision in spirit. Hearing passes and the Heard remains, heart passes and the Shown remains.

### In short

- No recipient of Scripture, hukm and prophethood can call people to worship him, he calls them to be Rabbaniyyun, wise and devoted to the Lord.
- The impossibility of prophetic self-worship grounds ʿiṣmah, the protection of prophets from revolt against God and shirk.
- Teachings are tested by where they point: to God, or to a cult of personalities.

80.text:
The circle widens from one false claim to a system of false lordship: "And he would never ask you to take angels and prophets as lords. Would he ask you to disbelieve after you have submitted". A prophet commands worship of Allah alone. He cannot order the worship of sent messengers or angels, since whoever calls to worship other than Allah has called to kufr.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And he would never ask you to take angels and prophets as lords"**: taking angels and prophets as lords to be worshipped besides Allah cannot be ordered by him. A new clause reading, lā yaʾmurukum, yields "God would not order you", a supplementing reading produces "it does not belong to a mortal to order you". Cases are Sabaeans with angels, Jews with Ezra, ʿUzayr, and Christians with Jesus.

**"Would he ask you to disbelieve after you have submitted"**: how could he command you to follow disbelief after he commanded you to follow Islam, complete surrender to Allah? He would not do that.

### What every messenger actually commanded

The prophets only call to Iman, faith commanding worship of Allah Alone without partners: "And We did not send any Messenger before you (O Muhammad ﷺ) but We revealed to him (saying): 'None has the right to be worshipped but I, so worship Me'" (21:25). "And verily, We have sent among every Ummah a Messenger (proclaiming): 'Worship Allah (Alone), and avoid Taghut (all false deities)'" (16:36). "And ask those of Our Messengers whom We sent before you: 'Did We ever appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Gracious (Allah)?'" (43:45). Of the angels themselves: "And if any of them should say: 'Verily, I am a god besides Him (Allah),' such a one We should recompense with Hell. Thus We recompense the wrongdoers" (21:29).

One setting addresses Quraysh, Jews and Christians together: angels taken as daughters of Allah, and prophets made lords. How could Abraham command disbelief after commanding Islam? Allah says of Abraham's own charge: "Lo! Allah hath chosen for you the (true) Religion; therefore die not save as men who have surrendered" (2:132). No Messenger was sent without being commanded to follow Islam, not Judaism, Christianity or idol worship, as the unbelievers claim. It is also said the verse was revealed about Jewish claims that Muhammad commanded them to love him and worship him as the Christians worshipped Jesus. The Christians and idolaters made the same claim.

### No atom of establishment belongs to creatures

Do not attribute to angels and prophets so much as an atom in the establishment of good and evil, ithbāt al-khayr wa-l-sharr. The verse informs you of the boundary of human nature, ḥadd al-bashariyya, and the truth of lordship, ḥaqq al-rubūbiyya. Created things are to be respected, tawqīr, with regard to the command and the law, sharīʿa, but their worth is to be disdained, taḥqīr, in comparison to lordship, rubūbiyya. Would He order you to affirm, ithbāt, created things after bearing witness, shuhūd, to the Real? Would He order you to look to outward appearances, ashkāl, and attribute events to simulacra, amthāl, after the lights of unity, tawḥīd, have appeared in your innermost selves and the suns of singular devotion, tafrīd, have arisen in your hearts?

### In short

- A prophet cannot order worship of angels or prophets, every messenger commanded worship of Allah alone (21:25, 16:36, 43:45, 21:29).
- The lords named in practice are the Sabaeans' angels, Ezra for the Jews and Jesus for the Christians.
- Creatures are respected under the law but hold no atom of power to establish good and evil.

81.text:
A covenant older than any community binds every prophet to a successor: "˹Remember˺ when Allah made a covenant with the prophets, ˹saying,˺ “Now that I have given you the Book and wisdom, if there comes to you a messenger confirming what you have, you must believe in him and support him.” He added, “Do you affirm this covenant and accept this commitment?” They said, “Yes, we do.” Allah said, “Then bear witness, and I too am a Witness.”" From Adam to ʿĪsā, each prophet pledged belief and help before he knew the successor's generation.

### Phrase by phrase

**"˹Remember˺ when Allah made a covenant with the prophets, ˹saying,˺ “Now that I have given you the Book and wisdom"**: Allah took a pledge from every Prophet He sent, from Adam until ʿĪsā, that when He gives them the Book and the Ḥikmah, whatever high grades they deserve, the pledge applies. Scripture and knowledge contain details of the lawful and the unlawful. The word mā is read as introducing an oath, lamā, or as connected to "He took", limā, and the gift is read "I have given you", ātaytukum, or "We have given you", ātaynākum.

**"if there comes to you a messenger confirming what you have, you must believe in him and support him.”"**: a Messenger comes afterwards, confirming what is with you of Book and wisdom, and that is Muhammad ﷺ. You shall believe in him and help him if you reach his time and perceive him, and your communities of descendants follow you in what is incumbent on them. "Help him" includes help with the sword against his enemies and expounding his trait.

**"He added, “Do you affirm this covenant and accept this commitment?” They said, “Yes, we do.” Allah said, “Then bear witness, and I too am a Witness.”"**: Isri, ʾIṣrī, is read as "My covenant" by Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, ar-Rabīʿ, Qatādah and as-Suddī. Muhammad bin Ishaq gives the sense of a ratified pledge's responsibility. Witnessing occurs before their own souls and followers, with Allah among witnesses over both.

### How far the pledge reaches

ʿAli bin Abi Talib and his cousin ʿAbdullah bin ʿAbbās said:

> "Allah never sent a Prophet but after taking his pledge that if Muhammad ﷺ were sent in his lifetime, he would believe in and support him."

Each prophet was further commanded to pledge his nation to belief and support if Muhammad arrived in their era. Tawus, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Qatadah describe the covenant as prophets believing in one another, a statement compatible with ʿAli and Ibn ʿAbbās.

Traits, description and merit circulated mutually among prophets before nations were bound. God made prophets witnesses over one another while witnessing Himself. Every prophet then explained the pledge domestically and made his nation's members witnesses for each other, as each prophet bore witness to it.

Muhammad's finality until Resurrection follows. As greatest Imam, he merits obedience over every other Prophet in any era. Bayt Al-Maqdis prayer leadership during the Isra' night illustrates it, and Day of Gathering intercession completes it. At Al-Maqam Al-Mahmud, the praised station (17:79), mighty Prophets and Messengers decline a task Muhammad ﷺ carries.

### Two covenants, and a name joined to a name

No Qur'anic verse more completely explains the excellence of MuṣṬafā, to whom this verse is devoted without anyone else's association. God made two covenants with His creatures. One bound creatures to His Godhood and Enactorship: "When your Lord took from the children..." (7:172). The other bound angels and prophets to Muḥammad's prophethood and helping him. Through it his name became great beside God's name and his measure was lifted by God's measure.

Several thousand years before Muḥammad existed, Gabriel heard a command describing a friend named Muḥammad: praised and caressed, with his name placed next to God's name, his measure lifted up by bounty, obedience to him constituting obedience to God, his words forming revelation, and following him becoming friendship with God. Gabriel was told to covenant faith in him and help for him. He answered:

> "O Lord, I make a covenant that my hand will be one with his hand, I will help, and I will have faith in him."

God told him to keep the covenant and avoid opposition. Gabriel replied, "O Lord, who would have the gall to oppose You?!" Michael was then told to witness Gabriel's covenant. The same covenant was made with Michael, with Gabriel appointed as witness to Michael's covenant.

Discovering God means finding an eternal reality and travelling with the whole universe. Prejudice falls away, and truth is recognised in all situations, whether an Israelite prophet or an Ishmaelite prophet calls. Community-oriented thinking recognises truth only from its own member. An outside messenger's message therefore fails to lodge even when the heart witnesses its truth. Names will be deleted from the believers' list in the Hereafter, because truth was recognised in relation to their community rather than to God, and not acknowledging a message their own hearts testified to is the worst crime.

### In short

- Every prophet pledged to believe in and help a confirming messenger to come, and to bind his nation to the same pledge.
- ʿAli and Ibn ʿAbbās apply the pledge specifically to Muhammad ﷺ in any prophet's lifetime, matching his leadership of the prophets at Bayt Al-Maqdis and Al-Maqam Al-Mahmud (17:79).
- Beside the primordial covenant of lordship (7:172), this second covenant joins Muhammad's name to God's in measure and obedience.

82.text:
The covenant has an exit with a name on it: "Whoever turns back after this, they will be the rebellious". Turning away after promise, witness and divine witness is not change of opinion. It is leaving the religion of Allah and His obedience.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Whoever turns back after this"**: whoever turns his back in rejection after that covenant, from among the nations, whoever turns away from fulfilling this pledge and covenant.

**"they will be the rebellious"**: they are the wicked, the miscreants who have broken the covenant and are unbelievers. They are the ones who leave the religion of Allah and His obedience.

### Abandoning the path after the proof

The inward referent is anyone leaving the Prophet's Sunna or wandering from his Ṭarīqa once evidence and miracle have become clear. Corruption of condition follows. Denial breaks attachment to divine solicitude and earns wrath.

### In short

- Turning back after the witnessed covenant is rebellion and covenant-breaking, not reconsideration.
- Inwardly, leaving the Prophet's Sunna after clear evidence corrupts the condition and severs divine solicitude.

83.text:
Creation itself is summoned against a preference: "Do they desire a way other than Allah’s—knowing that all those in the heavens and the earth submit to His Will, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will ˹all˺ be returned". People who seek a religion other than Allah's are rebuked while every creature moves inside a submission it cannot leave.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Do they desire a way other than Allah’s"**: do the ones who turn away desire, yabghūna, also read tabghūna, "do you desire?", other than God's religion? The opening hamza in a-fa-ghayra denotes disavowal.

**"knowing that all those in the heavens and the earth submit to His Will, willingly or unwillingly"**: submission is made willingly without refusal, or unwillingly by the sword and by seeing what refusal results in. Angels in the heavens acknowledge Islam and Allah's divine Oneness, and believers do so on earth. The dwellers of the heavens submit willingly, the dwellers of the earth unwillingly. Or sincere believers acknowledge willingly while hypocrites submit unwillingly, or those born Muslim acknowledge willingly while those made to embrace Islam submit unwillingly.

**"and to Him they will ˹all˺ be returned"**: yurjaʿūna, also read turjaʿūna, "you shall be returned". They return after death, on the Day of Return, when He will reward or punish each person according to his deeds.

### Submission by nature and by covenant

"And unto Allah (Alone) falls in prostration whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly" (13:15). "Have they not observed things that Allah has created: (how) their shadows incline to the right and to the left, making prostration unto Allah, and they are lowly? And to Allah prostrate all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth, of the moving creatures and the angels, and they are not proud. They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded" (16:48-50).

Interior divides submission. Believers yield in both heart and body. Deniers yield only in the body, because irresistible power, control and kingship encompass them. Through Wakiʿ, Mujāhid hears even their confession that Allah created heaven and earth (39:38), and Ibn ʿAbbās hears the primordial moment "when He took the covenant from them".

The occasion is a judgment seat. Ibn Abbas said the people of the two Scriptures, Jews and Christians, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to settle a dispute regarding Abraham's religion, each claiming the best claim to it. The Prophet ﷺ said: "None of the parties has anything to do with the religion of Abraham." This angered both. They said: "By Allah, we do not accept your judgement nor are we going to follow your religion!" Then Allah revealed: "Seek they other than the religion of Allah".

Mirage imagery inwardly condemns attention paid to ghayr al-ḥaqīqa, anything unreal. Looking elsewhere for divinity, ilāhiyya, ends with dust, habāʾ, where water was imagined, māʾ. Supposition's errors cut people off, confuse them and leave them in a desolate wadi.

### In short

- Seeking another religion is disavowed while all creation prostrates, willingly or unwillingly (13:15, 16:48-50).
- Believers submit in heart and body, deniers submit only under irresistible power, and even they answer "Allah" when asked who created (39:38).
- The occasion is a rejected judgment: neither Jewish nor Christian party accepted having nothing to do with Abraham's religion.

84.text:
The believers answer with a single creed across all revelation: "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and his descendants; and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and other prophets from their Lord—we make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we ˹fully˺ submit.”" Faithful Muslims believe in every Prophet Allah sent and every Book He revealed, and never disbelieve in any of them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us"**: say to them, O Muhammad ﷺ: We believe in Allah alone without any partner, and in that which the Qur'an has revealed to us.

**"and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and his descendants"**: Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac and Jacob are believed in with their Scripture, as are the tribes. Jacob's twelve children originated the twelve tribes called the Asbat.

**"and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and other prophets from their Lord"**: we believe in Moses and his Scripture, the Tawrah, and Jesus and his Scripture, the Injīl, and in all the prophets and their scriptures. This encompasses all of Allah's Prophets.

**"we make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we ˹fully˺ submit.”"**: no division by believing some prophets and disbelieving others, and no prophet is disassociated from Allah in relation to prophethood and Islam. Sincere worship and acknowledgment of His Oneness are devoted to Him.

### Belief through God

A community can call refusal of outside truth a defence of faith, but the result is faith's destruction. Continuous divine inspiration nourishes the true believer. Self-worship and community-worship obstruct blessing's entry, and once inspiration is lost, faith loses its source of nurture.

Belief is itself mediated by God rather than lower selves. Strength, power, choice, effort and acquisition do not explain it. We believe through God in revelation and through God make no division among prophets. Without His teaching of who He is, knowledge would have been impossible.

### In short

- The creed believes in Allah, the Qur'an, and the revelations of Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Moses, Jesus and all prophets.
- No distinction is made between prophets, in belief or in prophethood.
- Belief itself is through God, not through the lower self's strength or acquisition.

85.text:
The argument closes at the gate: "Whoever seeks a way other than Islam, it will never be accepted from them, and in the Hereafter they will be among the losers". Whoever seeks other than what Allah has legislated will not have it accepted. This was revealed regarding those who apostatized and became disbelievers, and it ends them in the Fire made everlasting for them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Whoever seeks a way other than Islam"**: whoever desires and seeks a religion other than the Surrender to Allah, other than what Allah endorsed. The path is surrendering, Islam.

**"it will never be accepted from them"**: it will not be accepted from him by Allah. As the Prophet ﷺ said in an authentic Hadith: "Whoever commits an action that does not conform to our matter (religion) then it is rejected."

**"and in the Hereafter they will be among the losers"**: he will be one of the losers, among the duped, missing Paradise and all that is in it and dwelling in Hell with all that is in it, having lost his soul by entering the fire of Hell.

### Which Islam, in which age

The literal meaning of Islam is submission and obedience. As a term it stands for submission to the religion Allah sent through His prophets to guide human beings, because the fundamental principles are the same in all the prophets' codes. At times Islam is used in that general sense. At others it identifies exclusively the Last Shari'ah revealed to the Last of the Prophets. Past prophets called themselves Muslim and their communities the Muslim community. Concurrently the name is the particular name of the Last Prophet's community: "It was He who named you Muslims before, and in this (Qur'an)" (22:78).

The correct position is that either sense gives the same outcome here. The Islam of past prophets was for a limited group and a specified period. That was the Islam of that time. When a prophet departed and another replaced him, the earlier specific code ceased to be operative. The Islam of the time was what the new prophet presented. The fundamentals never differed, only subsidiary injunctions might. The Islam given through the last Prophet ﷺ remains unabrogable, a permanent code until the Day of Judgment. After he was sent, all previous religions stand abrogated. They are not Islam anymore. Islam is the name of the religion that has reached us through Muhammad al-Mustafa ﷺ. On belief in that alone depends the salvation, najat, of all human beings.

Authentic hadith support the conclusion. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Had Musa been living this day, following me would have been incumbent upon him too." He has also been reported to say that ʿĪsā, when he appears close to the Day of Resurrection, will follow no religious code except the Prophet of Islam's, despite holding the distinction and office of prophethood. Details of this were given at verse 3:19.

### The tree, its water and its lamp

Religion other than submission is false, and deeds detached from the Sunnah seed remorse. Submission is figured as a tree whose wellspring is the Sunnah, whose fruit is faith, and whose planter and nurturer is the Real. Divine solicitude replenishes that wellspring, withdrawal leaves it dry. A barren, ineffectual tree would verge on disappearance and destruction, as happened with apostates who turned away from submission.

When lordly solicitude replenishes the Sunnah, branches derive from the goodly word (14:24), fruit from pure belief grows, and heaven's guidance turns branches into ladders. Fruit remains constant and uncut in life and death (14:25). A second image makes submission a lamp. The Most Tremendous Light kindles it, while the Sunnah supplies visible material and nurture, echoing "Is he whose breast God has expanded..." (39:22). A breast lit in this way stays adorned only with assistance drawn from the same light. Without even a whiff of the Sunnah, no share in submission remains.

### In short

- A religion other than Islam, the surrender Allah endorsed, will not be accepted, and its seeker loses Paradise for Hell.
- Each age's Islam was its prophet's code, after Muhammad al-Mustafa ﷺ the permanent, unabrogated Islam is his.
- Submission is the tree and the Sunnah its water: without even a whiff of the Sunnah there is no portion of Islam (22:78, 14:24-25, 39:22).

86.text:
The question is asked of people who had everything needed to stay: "How will Allah guide a people who chose to disbelieve after they had believed, acknowledged the Messenger to be true, and received clear proofs? For Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people". Proofs and evidences were established, the truth was explained, and they reverted anyway into the darkness of polytheism. Guidance is withheld not from ignorance, but from a willing leap into blindness.

### Phrase by phrase

**"How will Allah guide a people who chose to disbelieve after they had believed"**: How shall Allah guide to His religion, or grant faith in Him and His messengers, to people who disbelieved after their belief, after having faith in Allah and witnessing that what the Prophet Muhammad brought was truth? He shall not guide them.

**"acknowledged the Messenger to be true, and received clear proofs?"**: and after they bore witness that the Messenger, Muhammad, is true, and after clear proofs of Allah's sovereignty had come to them, the exposition of the Truth and the Book. The proofs testified to the truth of what the Messenger was sent with.

**"For Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people"**: Allah guides not wrongdoing folk, the idolaters and those not fit for His religion, people who are wrongdoers and choose error instead of guidance.

### The Ansari who came back

Ibn Jarir records Ibn ʿAbbās on an Ansari who embraced Islam, reverted to the polytheists, regretted it, and asked his people to consult the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about repenting. Revelation descended from "How shall Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief" through "Verily, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful". Word reached him through his people, and Islam was re-embraced.

This is the wording recorded by An-Nasa'i, Al-Hakim and Ibn Hibban. Al-Hakim said, "Its chain is Sahih and they did not record it."

The man is named in another report. Al-Harith ibn Suwayd was a Muslim who had been with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He later renounced Islam and joined his own people. A man from among his people took these verses and read them to him. Al-Harith said, "By Allah, I know that you are truthful, and I know that the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, is more truthful than you, and Allah, exalted is He, is more truthful than all." He went back, declared his Islam and became a good Muslim. The same report came through Dawud ibn Abi Hind from ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbās: a certain man from the Helpers renounced Islam and joined idolatry, later regretted it and sent to ask whether his repentance would be accepted, and when the verses were sent he came back and became Muslim.

### A doubt removed: refusal, not impossibility

A superficial reading of "How shall Allah give guidance" raises the doubt that an apostate receives no guidance afterward, whereas many apostates do re-embrace faith and become recipients of guidance. The answer is that withholding here follows common usage. A punished criminal might say, "I have been given special treatment by the ruler with his own hands." The reply comes: "Why are we going to give special treatment to such a criminal?" That is, no special treatment is called for in this case. It does not mean the person cannot become deserving of special treatment if he behaves well. So the verses can both deny guidance to wrongdoers as they stand and open repentance to the one who returns.

Inwardly, the direction is stronger. Those rendered unsuitable in His prior decree for the communion of lovers cannot now expect nearness on service's carpet through favor. Remoteness decreed pre-eternally raises the same question about later sincerity in actions. God prevails over His affair.

### In short

- Guidance is denied to people who believed, witnessed the Messenger's truth, received clear proofs, and reverted willingly into blindness.
- An Ansari apostate, named as Al-Harith ibn Suwayd, heard these verses read to him, declared all three speakers truthful, and came back.
- "How shall Allah guide" refuses the claim of the obstinate, without making return impossible for the repentant.

87.text:
The sentence is stated by its three witnesses: "Their reward is that they will be condemned by Allah, the angels, and all of humanity". Their recompense is a curse that comes from every direction at once. Allah curses them, and His creation also curses them, and they are excluded and removed from His mercy.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Their reward is that they will be condemned by Allah"**: their requital is that there shall rest on them the curse of God, the punishment of Allah. The word "reward" carries the irony of the crime: this is what their choice earns.

**"the angels, and all of humanity"**: and of angels, the curse of the angels, and of men combined, the curse of the believers. Their condemnation is not a private decree. It is pronounced by Allah, the angels and humankind altogether.

### Rejection at the beginning, banishment at the end

End and beginning correspond in His decree. Fate's rejection, radd al-qisma, opens their affair. Being turned away from service, al-ṣaddu ʿan al-khidma, fills the middle. Banishment and abasement, al-Ṭard wa-l-madhalla, close the outcome.

### In short

- The apostates' requital is the curse of Allah, the angels and all humanity, and removal from mercy.
- Read inwardly, their arc runs from fate's rejection through being turned away from service to banishment and abasement.

88.text:
The curse is made permanent: "They will be in Hell forever. Their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be delayed ˹from it˺". They abide in the curse, or in the Fire implied by it, without lessening, postponement or respite. No hour of relief interrupts it, and no extra time is given to repent and ask forgiveness once it begins.

### Phrase by phrase

**"They will be in Hell forever"**: they will abide therein, in the curse, or in the Fire implied by the curse. These disbelievers will live eternally in the fire of Hell, never to leave.

**"Their punishment will not be lightened"**: neither will their torment be lightened. The chastisement shall not be lightened for them, not even for an hour, and not even for a moment.

**"nor will they be delayed ˹from it˺"**: nor will it be delayed or postponed. They shall not be reprieved, and they shall not be given any respite, nor more time to repent.

### No pause in the separation

Inside that abasement, no moment brings abatement: lā yaftur ʿanhum al-ʿadhāb laḥẓatan. Nor does an hour lighten separation: lā yukhaffafu dūnihim al-firāq sāʿatan. The two units of time are minimal on purpose. There is no smallest gap in which the punishment breathes.

### In short

- They abide in the curse and its Fire forever, with no lightening, no postponement and no respite.
- Even a moment's abatement and an hour's easing of separation are denied.

89.text:
The exception is opened in the same breath: "As for those who repent afterwards and mend their ways, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful". After apostasy, repentance and righteous deeds still meet forgiveness. This verse shows Allah's kindness, graciousness, compassion, mercy and favour on creatures who repent to Him.

### Phrase by phrase

**"As for those who repent afterwards and mend their ways"**: except those who afterward, after their apostasy, repent from disbelief and hypocrisy and do right. They make amends in their actions and sincerely declare Allah's divine Oneness.

**"then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful"**: God is Forgiving to them, Forgiving of those who repent among them, and Merciful toward those who die in a state of repentance.

### The mercy that identifies its people

Repentance identifies the people mercy reaches. They were not among the group distanced by the prior decree, although people imagined them to be part of it.

### In short

- Repentance after apostasy, joined to amended deeds, is met by Allah's forgiveness and mercy.
- The returning Ansari belongs to this verse, not to the group permanently distanced.

90.text:
The second apostasy passage is narrower and harder: "Indeed, those who disbelieve after having believed then increase in disbelief, their repentance will never be accepted. It is they who are astray." Allah threatens those who revert after believing and then insist on disbelief until death. In that terminal state, repentance is not accepted, because the time for acceptance has expired.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, those who disbelieve after having believed then increase in disbelief"**: those who disbelieve after their profession of belief and afterward grow violent in disbelief, who do not waver in their persistence. The Jews are specified in one explanation: those who disbelieve in Jesus after they have believed in Moses and then increase in unbelief in Muhammad ﷺ.

**"their repentance will never be accepted"**: their repentance shall not be accepted when they are drawing their last gasps of life, or when they have died as disbelievers, as long as they remain in that state. "And of no effect is the repentance of those who continue to do evil deeds until death faces one of them" (4:18).

**"It is they who are astray"**: they have lost their way from the straight path which leads to Allah, abandoning the path of truth for the path of wickedness.

### Repeated returns, and the reports that narrow the case

Al-Bazzar records Ibn ʿAbbās on people cycling through Islam, disbelief, Islam again, then disbelief. Their people inquired and asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This verse was revealed on that.

Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ata al-Khurasani apply revelation to Jews whose disbelief in Jesus and the Gospel grew by disbelief in Muhammad and the Qur'an. Abu'l-Aliyah widens it to Jews and Christians who rejected Muhammad, Allah bless him and give him peace, despite prior belief in his attributes and description, then added disbelief by remaining disbelievers.

### Apostasy from the path itself

This alludes to those who return to the states of the people of habit, ahl al-ʿāda, after having travelled the path of spiritual desire, Ṭarīq al-irāda. World preference and submission to whims replace seeking the Real. People of the path, ahl al-Ṭarīqa, are renounced, leaving greater solitude in inner darknesses. Trust, amāna, cannot be regained once treachery, khiyāna, has been displayed. Punishment arrives as day-by-day estrangement of the heart, without distress over lost felicity. Perseverance would have meant accepted repentance. Listless reversion to habitual states, aḥwāl al-ʿāda, without regret for vanished moments, nevertheless meets the Real's way, sunna. "And We shall confound their hearts and eyes; just as they did not believe in it the first time" (6:110).

An apostate from Islam makes a more powerful enemy to Muslims than an original disbeliever. Likewise, reverting from the path produces a stronger rejection and opposition against its people than lifelong alienation ever did.

### In short

- Repentance is refused only where disbelief is increased in and persisted in to the deathbed (4:18).
- Reports narrow the verse to repeated apostates, and to Jews and Christians who accepted the Prophet's description and then rejected him.
- Inwardly, the habit-bound revert after spiritual desire, whose hearts grow estranged without regretting what slipped away (6:110).

91.text:
No treasury can purchase an exit: "Indeed, if each of those who disbelieve then die as disbelievers were to offer a ransom of enough gold to fill the whole world, it would never be accepted from them. It is they who will suffer a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers". Dying in disbelief closes both doors at once: the ransom is refused, and there is no helper to take the punishment away.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, if each of those who disbelieve then die as disbelievers were to offer a ransom of enough gold to fill the whole world"**: those who disbelieved, and died while they were disbelievers, would not have the whole earth full of gold accepted from anyone of them if they offered it as ransom. If they gave the equivalent of the earth's weight in gold to ransom themselves, it would not be accepted. The earth's fill includes all of it: its mountains, hills, sand, dust, valleys, forests, land and sea. The fāʾ in fa-lan yuqbala, "it shall not be accepted", enters the predicate because the statement about "those who disbelieve" resembles a conditional.

**"it would never be accepted from them"**: no good deed shall ever be accepted from them, even if they spent the earth's fill of gold in what was perceived to be an act of obedience. "...nor shall compensation be accepted from him, nor shall intercession be of use to him" (2:123). A day comes "on which there will be neither mutual bargaining nor befriending" (14:31). "Verily, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth, and as much again therewith to ransom themselves thereby from the torment on the Day of Resurrection, it would never be accepted of them, and theirs would be a painful torment" (5:36).

**"It is they who will suffer a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers"**: for them is a painful torment, alīm, that is muʾlim, painful, which will extend to their hearts. They shall have no helpers to protect them, no one to save them from Allah's punishment or rescue them from His painful punishment on the Day of Judgement.

### Generosity without one sentence of faith

A question reached the Prophet ﷺ concerning ʿAbdullah bin Jud'an: would generosity to guests, help to the indebted and feeding the poor benefit him? The answer was: "No, for not even one day during his life did he pronounce, 'O my Lord! Forgive my sins on the Day of Judgment.'" 

The same exchange is pictured from the other side. Imam Ahmad recorded that Anas said the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

> "A man from among the people of Paradise will be brought and Allah will ask him, 'O son of Adam! How did you find your dwelling?' He will say, 'O Lord, it is the best dwelling.' Allah will say, 'Ask and wish.' The man will say, 'I only ask and wish that You send me back to the world so that I am killed ten times in Your cause,' because of the honor of martyrdom he would experience. A man from among the people of the Fire will be brought, and Allah will say to him, 'O son of Adam! How do you find your dwelling?' He will say, 'It is the worst dwelling, O Lord.' Allah will ask him, 'Would you ransom yourself from Me with the earth's fill of gold?' He will say, 'Yes, O Lord.' Allah will say, 'You have lied. I asked you to do what is less and easier than that, but you did not do it,' and he will be sent back to the Fire."

Ten hypocrites occasion verses 90 and 91: Tu'mah and his companions, who left Medina to Mecca as apostates from their religion, Islam. Some died as apostates, some were killed, and some later returned to the fold of Islam.

### A beautiful beginning that does not gather its owner

To die after becoming listless is the inward case. A beautiful beginning does not guarantee, in the hereafter, a gathering alongside the people of this story, ahl hādhi al-qiṣṣa, even if a thousand of those with deeper knowledge were to intercede for him. Perfection of the ruse casts his image onto someone else in the hereafter, so acquaintances among the people of deeper knowledge, ahl al-maʿrifa, mistake the image for him. No thought of interceding for him occurs to anyone.

### In short

- Dying in disbelief means no ransom is accepted, even earth's fill in gold, and no intercession or helper avails (2:123, 14:31, 5:36).
- ʿAbdullah bin Jud'an's generosity gained him nothing without a single day of asking forgiveness.
- The ten hypocrites around Tu'mah who left for Mecca are the occasion: some died, some were killed, some returned.

92.text:
Righteousness is reached through the wallet's dearest contents: "You will never achieve righteousness until you donate some of what you cherish. And whatever you give is certainly well known to Allah". After the refusal of a disbeliever's ransom, believers are taught acceptable charity. Its measure is not the size of the gift, but whether what is given is loved, needed and sincerely intended.

### Phrase by phrase

**"You will never achieve righteousness until you donate some of what you cherish"**: By no means shall you attain Al-Birr unless you spend of that which you love. Wakiʿ reported that ʿAmr bin Maymun said attaining Al-Birr means attaining Paradise. It is also glossed as the reward of piety, its honour and Paradise, or as reliance on Allah and God-fearingness. Voluntary alms are named in one reading as the road to piety's reward.

**"And whatever you give is certainly well known to Allah"**: whatever of good you spend, big or small, Allah knows it well, just as He is aware of your intentions, whether you intend His Countenance or other people's praise. He will requite it accordingly, and everyone will be rewarded accordingly.

### What birr means

The literal and real meaning of birr is the perfect fulfilment of someone's rights. It is also used for charity, performance of good deeds and nice conduct. Barr is a person who fulfils, fully and totally, all rights due on him. The Qur'an calls prophets good to parents in this sense: "good to my mother" (19:32), and "good to his father and mother" (19:14). The plural, abrār, the righteous, is frequent: "Surely the righteous shall drink of a cup the mixture of which is camphor" (76:5), "Surely the righteous shall be in bliss, upon furnished thrones gazing" (83:22), while the opposite pole is named: "And surely, the sinners shall be in hell ablaze" (82:14). The antonym of birr is fujūr, disobedience and sinfulness.

A report from Abu Bakr has the Prophet ﷺ say:

> "Stick to speaking the truth because truth is a companion of birr (righteousness) and both these are in Paradise; and abstain from lying because that is a companion of fujur (sin) and both these are in Hell."

It appears in al-Adab al-Mufrad of Imam al-Bukhari, in Ibn Majah and in the Musnad of Ahmad.

Verse 2:177 lists belief in Allah and the Last Day and a whole set of deeds and classes all of them as birr. Within that wide range, the most preferred form of righteousness named here is to spend the most cherished things in Allah's way. Perfect fulfilment of Allah's rights and total self-unburdening from them cannot come unless we spend what we hold dear. This has also been translated as perfect good, excellence in doing good, and the great merit. To sum up: entering the ranks of the abrār depends on sacrificing in Allah's way what one holds dear.

### Abu Talhah's garden, and the Companions who surveyed their hearts

The first addressees surveyed what they loved most and brought requests to spend it. Imam Ahmad reported that Anas bin Malik said Abu Talhah had more property than any other among the Ansar in Al-Madinah. The most beloved of his property was Bayruha' garden, in front of the Messenger's mosque. Sometimes Allah's Messenger ﷺ would go to the garden and drink its fresh water.

When these verses were revealed, Abu Talhah presented his intention:

> "O Allah's Messenger! Allah says, 'By no means shall you attain Al-Birr, unless you spend of that which you love.' No doubt, Bayruha' garden is the most beloved of all my property to me. So I want to give it in charity in Allah's cause, and I expect its reward and compensation from Allah. O Allah's Messenger! Spend it where Allah makes you think is feasible."

The Messenger ﷺ answered:

> "Well-done! It is profitable property, it is profitable property. I have heard what you have said, and I think it would be proper if you gave it to your kith and kin."

Abu Talhah accepted the suggestion and distributed that garden among his relatives and cousins. This hadith was recorded in the Two Sahihs. It teaches that charity is not restricted to the poor and needy: giving to family and relatives is equally charitable and meritorious.

Details of the place are preserved in the other direction. Abu Talhah was the richest person among the Ansar of Madinah, owner of a fruit farm across the mosque with a well called Bi'r Ha'. In place of the farm there is now, in front of Bab al-Majidi, a building known as Iṣṭifā Manzil where pilgrims to Madinah stay, in a corner north-east from it, Bi'r Ha' still exists by the same name. A translator notes that the building and well have now been demolished due to the extension of the Mosque. The Holy Prophet ﷺ used to visit this farm once in a while and drink water drawn from Bi'r Ha', and He liked the water from this well.

Sayyidna Zayd ibn Haritha brought a horse he loved above everything he owned, wishing to spend it in Allah's way. The Prophet ﷺ accepted it, then handed it to Zayd's son Sayyidna Usamah. Disappointment followed, because Zayd thought his own household had received the charity back. The Prophet ﷺ reassured him that Allah Almighty had accepted that charity of his (Ibn Jarir, and others).

Freedom also became a gift. Sayyidna ʿUmar freed the bond-maid he liked most for Allah's sake. Sayyidna ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar likewise freed a bond-maid he loved in Allah's name. The Two Sahihs also recorded that ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah! I never gained possession of a piece of property more precious to me than my share in Khaybar. Therefore, what do you command me to do with it?" The Prophet ﷺ said, "Retain the land to give its fruits in Allah's cause." 

### Rulings drawn from the verse

The word birr here is inclusive of all charity, obligatory or voluntary.

1. Some commentators take the spending to mean obligatory charity, zakah, while others take voluntary, Nafl, supererogatory charity. The consensus of respected researchers is that its sense is general and includes both. The recorded initiatives of the Companions cited above bear witness that their giving was voluntary. The outcome is that whatever has to be given, zakah or voluntary charity, attains perfect excellence only when what is liked and loved is given. Not the spare and worthless things picked out to get rid of the burden of charity as if it were a punitive tax.
