Another verse takes this up clearly: "O those who believe, spend of the good things you have earned and of what We have brought forth for you from the earth and do not opt for a bad thing spending only from there while you are not going to accept it at all unless you close your eyes to it..." (2:267). Picking out the bad and useless for charity is unacceptable, acceptable charity with full merit is what is spent out of dear belongings.

2. Moderation is hinted in the word "from", min, in "some of what you cherish". The purpose is not to spend away everything one likes and loves en masse in Allah's way. Spending from the good things, in the measure that has to be spent, brings the full reward of charity.

3. Sincerity counts, not price. Even a tiny beloved item can earn birr when given sincerely. Hasan al-Basri said that a single date-fruit alone, offered for Allah's pleasure, is enough for the promised merit.

4. Poor people are not excluded. On the outside, those with little to spend appear deprived of this great good. But birr can be achieved by other means as well: ʿIbādah, worship, Dhikr, remembrance, Tilawah of the Qur'an and abundance of nawafil, supererogatory prayers. The poor and needy can therefore also become recipients of this good, as Hadith narrations explain clearly.

5. "What you love" means what is working for you and needed by you, not what is spare and useless. The favoured servants feed others, in the words of (76:8), "the favoured servants of Allah feed the..." in spite of their love for the food. And they are further described: "They (the favoured servants of Allah) prefer others over their ownselves even though they themselves are in need" (59:9).

6. Spending the extra and spare is not devoid of merit. Entry into perfect good and the ranks of the righteous depends specially on spending cherished possessions. But no charity is devoid of merit, whether one spends the cherished or the extra. What is prohibited is the habit of always picking out the extra and the bad. A person who spends good things he likes in charity and also gives away extras, leftover food, used clothing, or defective utensils or articles in use, commits no sin thereby and definitely earns reward for those too. In addition, by spending the cherished, he achieves the great good and entry into the ranks of the righteous.

Allah is fully aware of the real quality of what a person spends. He knows whether it is dear to him, and whether he is spending it for Allah's good pleasure or for pretence and publicity. A verbal claim to be spending what one cherishes is not enough. The all-Knowing and all-Aware One keeps vigil, cognizant of the secrets of the heart, watching and knowing the true worth of the spending in His way.

### Some of what you love, or everything you love

The phrase is mimmā, min mā, "of what" you love, and min is the particle for dividing something into portions. Start from the greater desire. Wanting al-Bārr, the One who is All-Goodness, means expending everything loved. Wanting birr, piety and goodness, means expending some portion of what is loved. Worldly expenditure of the loved leads to what is sought from the Real. Attachment to lower-self fortunes, man kāna marbūṭan bi-ḥuẓūẓi nafsihi, blocks fortune in the Lord's nearness, lam yaḥẓu bi-qurbi rabbihi. If loved things have to be spent even for birr, preferring worldly fortunes above Him bars the road to al-Bārr.

Motives divide spenders. Contentment with His knowing motivates some. Others hope to defend themselves from affliction and tribulations, while still others seek reward and compensation. A lover's image has him deliberately walking weakly, hoping news of his suffering will bring her message. He trembles, through what seeking the sublime has taught, that one day she may mention his qualities before Salmā.

### In short

- Birr is the perfect fulfilment of rights, and its most preferred form in this verse is spending what you cherish, not what you discard (2:177, 2:267, 19:32, 19:14, 76:5, 83:22, 82:14).
- Abu Talhah gave Bayruha' to his kin, ʿUmar retained Khaybar's land for its fruits, and others freed the slaves they loved most.
- Quality is measured by sincerity and need, not price: one date given sincerely suffices, the poor can reach birr by worship and remembrance, and even spare goods carry reward when the cherished are also given.

93.text:
The refutation returns to dinner: "All food was lawful for the children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed. Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Bring the Torah and read it, if your claims are true.”" Jews objected that Muhammad ﷺ claimed Abraham's creed yet ate camel meat and drank its milk, which they held unlawful for Abraham. The verse answers that all food was lawful until Jacob forbade one thing to himself, and then dares them to produce their own book.

### Phrase by phrase

**"All food was lawful for the children of Israel"**: all food that is lawful for Muhammad and his community today was lawful for the Children of Israel, the sons of Jacob. Before the Torah was revealed, all types of food were allowed.

**"except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed"**: save what Israel, Jacob, forbade himself by way of vows, in days before the Torah was revealed to Moses. Jacob forbade himself the meat and milk of camels.

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Bring the Torah and read it, if your claims are true.”"**: Produce the Torah and read it unto us, where they are made forbidden, if you are truthful in your claim. Bring the Torah now and recite it, so that the truth of what you say may become clear. They failed to produce the Torah and knew they were liars, since there was nothing in the Torah to substantiate their claim. They were stupified and did not bring it.

### What Jacob forbade, and why

The Jews said to the Prophet: "You claim that you follow the creed of Abraham but Abraham did not eat camel's meat nor drink its milk." The response revealed that camel's meat was forbidden to Jacob himself when he was afflicted with sciatica, ʿirq al-nasā. He vowed that if he were cured, he would not eat of it again, and so it was forbidden him. The Torah was not revealed until long after Abraham, so camel was not unlawful in Abraham's time as they claimed.

Ibn ʿAbbās narrates in an authentic report that Jacob suffered from sciatica (Al-Hakim and al-Tirmidhi). He vowed to abandon what he liked most in what he ate if Allah Almighty cured him of the disease. Camel meat was what he liked most, so he abandoned it when cured. Then, it so happened that this prohibition which started because of a vow continued among the Bani Isra'il as a divine injunction. Their code recognized a vow as a cause of unlawfulness for something lawful, just as in our own Shari'ah a vow may make permissible acts obligatory. A vow that renders things unlawful is really an oath, in our Shari'ah it is not permissible to keep such an oath, and breaking it with Kaffarah becomes obligatory, in accordance with: "why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?" (66:1).

Abu Rawq and al-Kalbi said this was revealed when the Prophet ﷺ said, "We follow the religion of Abraham." The Jews responded: "How can this be so when you eat the meat of camels and drink their milk." He said: "That was lawful for Abraham and so we make it lawful too." The Jews said: "Everything that we take for unlawful today was unlawful to Noah and Abraham and so on and so forth until our time." To refute them, Allah revealed this verse. In the exchange as the Jews themselves retell it afterward, they claimed nothing was self-forbidden: whatever is forbidden for us today, such as camel meat, was already forbidden on all prophets from Adam to Moses, and only Muhammad makes such things lawful. And they claimed those things were also forbidden in the Torah. Hence the challenge.

For Allah's sake, Isra'il forbade himself the things he found most delightful. That practice was allowed under his period's law, making its placement after the previous verse apt. Our Law allows spending what we like and covet in obedience, not prohibiting what Allah allowed. Scripture supports it: "And gives his wealth, in spite of love for it" (2:177), and "And they give food, in spite of their love for it" (76:8).

### Four questions answered, and the answer that divided the room

Imam Ahmad records, through Ibn ʿAbbās, a delegation of Jews asking to be told things only a Prophet would know. The Prophet ﷺ invited their questions, but first took a pledge like the one Ya'qub took from his children: if they recognised the truth of his answers, they would follow him in Islam. They agreed.

The Prophet took their covenant that they will follow him if he answers these questions, and they agreed. He said:

> "I ask you by He Who sent down the Tawrah to Musa, do you not know that Isra'il once became very ill? When his illness was prolonged, he vowed to Allah that if He cures His illness, he would prohibit the best types of drink and food for himself. Was not the best food to him camel meat and the best drink camel milk?"

Affirmation followed, and the Messenger ﷺ called Allah to witness against them before continuing:

> "I ask you by Allah, other than Whom there is no deity (worthy of worship), Who sent down the Tawrah to Musa, do you not know that man's discharge is thick and white and woman's is yellow and thin? If any of these fluids becomes dominant, the offspring will take its sex and resemblance by Allah's leave. Hence, if the man's is more than the woman's, the child will be male, by Allah's leave. If the woman's discharge is more than the man's, then the child will be female, by Allah's leave."

A second affirmation brought a second call for Allah's witness, and then:

> "I ask you by He Who sent down the Tawrah to Musa, do you not know that the eyes of this unlettered Prophet sleep, but his heart does not sleep?"

A third affirmation brought a third witnessing. Then came the decisive request: 'Tell us now about your Wali among the angels, for this is when we either follow or shun you.' His answer named Jibril as his Wali, the one bringing revelation, and as the Wali of every Prophet Allah sent. Rejection followed at once: 'We then shun you. Had you a Wali other than Jibril, we would have followed you.' On that, Allah, the Exalted revealed, "Say: 'Whoever is an enemy to Jibril...'" (2:97).

### Abrogation inside their own law

The second objective is a refutation of any denial of abrogation, naskh. Start with Jacob's marriage: two sisters could be wives at the same time, then the Tawrah prohibited the practice. Earlier, Adam's sons could marry Adam's daughters, before that too was forbidden. Ibrahim's law allowed female servants as companions alongside a wife, as Hajar was taken while Sarah was married to him, the Tawrah later prohibited this. Food tells the same story. Noah on leaving the ark could eat all types of animals. Isra'il then forbade camel meat and milk for himself, his children imitated him, and the Tawrah later prohibited that food and added several more prohibitions. Every example sits inside the Tawrah, and every one is a Naskh, an abrogation. Let the Jews now consider what Allah legislated for ʿĪsā, and whether it falls in that category. Why do they not follow ʿĪsā in this regard? Instead they defied and rebelled against ʿĪsā and against the religion Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ with.

The Jews would ask on the same pattern why Islam differs from former revealed religions on the lawful and unlawful, such as camel and rabbit meat made illegal by their self-made laws while licit in Islam, and how a revealed religion could command prayer toward the Kaʿbah instead of al-Bayt al-Maqdis, Jerusalem, the direction of prayer in the teachings of all prophets until then. They refused to believe that God could reveal a religion in which the Kaʿbah was the direction for prayer.

### Before any command: a kindness, and the two schools of effort

In their original state, things receive no declaration of permission or prohibition from God. No divine ordinance, ḥadd, exists concerning them in that state, and this is liberality and kindness from the Real. The state lasts until a command or law arrives. God later eased precepts of religious obligation, aḥkām al-taklīf, for advanced disciples, ahl al-nihāya. They adopt what is easiest so they can perfect what comes to them from precepts of the hearts, aḥkām al-qulūb, since difficulties incumbent on their hearts are harder for them. Novices, ahl al-bidāya, receive difficulty in tasks and litanies, adopting the more onerous way so as to empty their hearts of thoughts. Whoever thinks otherwise is in error.

False claims are alluded to in "Whoever invents falsehood against God". People of false claims and errors absolve themselves and attribute false notions, hawājis, to God, but God is free of these. Incoming thoughts, khawāṬir, can be distinguished from false notions, hawājis, only by a rare servant.

### In short

- All food was lawful until Jacob, suffering sciatica, vowed away the camel meat he loved most, and the Torah cannot be produced to prove otherwise.
- Abrogation is proved from inside the Torah itself: Noah's universal permission, Jacob's vow, Adam's marriages, Hajar's companionship and two sisters all changed.
- The four questions were answered under covenant, and the refusals turned on one name: Jibril, the Wali of every prophet (2:97, 66:1).

94.text:
The lie is then named and closed: "Then whoever still fabricates lies about Allah, they will be the ˹true˺ wrongdoers". Proof has been made manifest. Anyone who continues inventing claims about Allah after the exposition, most of all a claim contradicted by his own Book, wrongs himself by transgressing truth into falsehood.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Then whoever still fabricates lies about Allah"**: whosoever shall invent a lie against Allah after that, after the evidence has been made clear, after the exposition in the Torah shows them to be liars. The evidence is that Jacob made certain foods unlawful for himself in a vow and that they were not made unlawful by Allah.

**"they will be the ˹true˺ wrongdoers"**: then it is these that are the wrongdoers, the evildoers who transgress the truth into falsehood, unbelievers who lie about Allah. They wrong themselves by turning away from the obvious truth.

### The lies named in full

Allah said "Then after that, whosoever shall invent a lie against Allah, then these it is that are the wrongdoers" (3:94) in reference to those who lie about Allah and claim that He made the Sabbath and the Tawrah eternal. They claim that Allah did not send another Prophet calling to Allah with the proofs and evidences, although evidence indicates that abrogation, as described, occurred before in the Tawrah. Such lies are now a matter of record rather than interpretation. The book they would not produce contained the prohibition's origin, and it was a man's vow after Abraham, not an eternal command from Adam.

### In short

- After the manifest proof that Jacob's vow came after Abraham, continued invention about Allah is evildoing.
- The lies include the claims that the Sabbath and Torah are eternal and that no further prophet would come.

95.text:
The passage ends by turning the hearer somewhere positive: "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah has declared the truth. So follow the Way of Abraham, the upright—who was not a polytheist.”" Allah has spoken the truth in what He conveyed and legislated in the Qur'an, and the religion of Ibrāhīm (Abraham) legislated there is the perfect way. No Prophet has brought a more complete, clear, plain and perfect way than he did.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah has declared the truth"**: Say, O Muhammad: God has spoken the truth in this matter just as He has in all that He has related. Allah speaketh truth when He said Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, and regarding what He stated concerning the lawful and the unlawful, about Jacob and everything He revealed and established in the sacred law.

**"So follow the Way of Abraham, the upright"**: therefore follow the creed of Abraham, the one which I follow, the religion of Ibrahim the Hanif. He abandoned all other ways of life for the path of surrendering in devotion to Allah, worshipping Him and following His sacred law, and he only worshipped Allah.

**"who was not a polytheist.”"**: and he was not of the Mushrikin, not an idolater who followed their religion, and he was not of the idolaters.

### The same command elsewhere

"Say: 'Truly, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a right religion, the religion of Ibrahim, the Hanif, and he was not of the idolaters'" (6:161). "Then, We have sent the revelation to you (saying): 'Follow the religion of Ibrahim, the Hanif, and he was not of the idolaters'" (16:123).

### Total abandonment as Abraham's creed

Abraham's creed, milla, is complete abandonment to God: al-khurūju ilā Allāh bi-l-kulliya, and surrender to His decree without holding back in any way, wa-l-taslīmu li-ḥukmihi min ghayri an tabqā baqiyya. To affirm anything other than God in accounting for what comes into being is idolatry, shirk.

### In short

- Allah has spoken the truth about Jacob, Abraham and the lawful and unlawful.
- Abraham's way is to be followed as the complete and perfect path of surrender (6:161, 16:123).
- His creed inwardly is total abandonment to God and surrender to His decree without reserve.

96.text:
The surah settles a contest of sanctuaries: "Surely the first House ˹of worship˺ established for humanity is the one at Bakkah—a blessed sanctuary and a guide for ˹all˺ people". Mujahid reports mutual boasting. Jerusalem's defenders prized its prophets' migrations and sacredness, Muslims answered that the Kaʿbah was better. Revelation gives Bakkah's House three distinctions: priority, blessing and guidance for everyone.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Surely the first House ˹of worship˺ established for humanity is the one at Bakkah"**: it was appointed for all people and their ritual life. Around it they perform Tawaf, beside it they pray, and within its area they remain in Iʿtikaf. Ibrahim Al-Khalil built it at Allah's command and invited people to Hajj there, although Jews and Christians who claim his religion do not make that pilgrimage. Its honour is not confined to one nation. An aura placed by Allah draws human hearts generally.

**"a blessed sanctuary"**: sanctified and full of blessing, the ground holds forgiveness and mercy.

**"and a guide for ˹all˺ people"**: guidance reaches Al-ʿAlamin, mankind and jinn. Every prophet, messenger, veracious one (siddiq) and believer takes it as Qiblah.

### First house in time, or first for worship?

One reading makes the Kaʿbah the world's first house of any kind, set apart for divine worship before residence existed elsewhere. Adam's prophethood and vicegerency make it plausible that he built God's House right after reaching earth, before his own dwelling. ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar, Mujahid, Qatadah and successor authorities therefore called it the world's first house. Another reading allows homes to precede it while preserving priority as the first building devoted exclusively to worship, that view is reported from ʿAli.

Al-Baihaqi's Dala'il al-Nubuwwah reports ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs: after Adam and Hawwa' arrived in the mortal world, Jibra'il conveyed a command to build Allah's House. Once they obeyed, Tawaf was prescribed for them, and they learned that they were the first people just as this was the first House appointed for people.

Abu Dharr's questions establish a second chronology:

> "I said, 'O Allah's Messenger! Which Masjid was the first to be built on the surface of the earth?' He said, 'Al-Masjid Al-Haram (in Makkah).' I said, 'Which was built next?' He replied 'Al-Masjid Al-Aqsa (in Jerusalem).' I said, 'What was the period of time between building the two?' He said, 'Forty years.' He added, 'Wherever (you may be, and) the prayer becomes due, perform the prayer there, for the whole earth was made a Masjid.'"

Imam Ahmad recorded this, and Al-Bukhari and Muslim collected it too. Angels reportedly built the House before Adam's creation, with the Aqsa following forty years later. Another report calls the first visible thing at creation a white foam over which the earth was unrolled, beneath the House's site.

The forty years can refer to Ibrahim's new edifice and Bayt al-Maqdis's initial construction forty years afterward. Sulayman's later Bayt al-Maqdis was also a rebuilding on Abrahamic foundations rather than a brand-new foundation. Reports thus need not conflict.

### Rebuilding on ancient foundations

Adam's structure is reported to have survived into Nuh's time and vanished in the Flood. Ibrahim rebuilt after its traces disappeared, on the same foundations. Successive collapses produced further rebuilding by Jurhum and then the Amalkites. Near the Prophet's era, Quraysh rebuilt it, and the Prophet ﷺ participated, helping place the Black Stone with his blessed hands.

Quraysh nonetheless altered the Abrahamic plan. They excluded the section known as Hatim. Two doors, entrance and rear exit, became one eastern door. They raised that door high above ground level, restricting entry to people they permitted.

The Prophet ﷺ told ʿA'ishah he wished to demolish the current structure and raise it exactly on Ibrahim's foundation, correcting Quraysh's arbitrary deviation. New Muslims' imperfect knowledge and potential misunderstanding made him leave it temporarily, and death came before implementation.

His nephew through ʿA'ishah, ʿAbdullah ibn Zubayr, heard the statement. As Makkah al-Mukarramah's ruler after the Khulafa al-Rashidin, he demolished and rebuilt it according to the Prophet's wish and Ibrahim's original foundation. His rule over Makkah al-Muʿazzamah was brief. Hajjaj ibn Yusuf invaded, ʿAbdullah was martyred, and Hajjaj, hostile to the martyr gaining fame from the feat, smeared him as wrong and claimed the Prophet had intended the Quraysh form to remain. The structure was demolished again and rebuilt in that earlier Jahiliyyah form.

Later rulers considered restoring the Prophet's stated preference. Imam Malik ibn Anas, master-jurist of that period, warned that repeated demolition and rebuilding would turn God's House into a plaything for rulers chasing fame. The ummah accepted his fatwa. Hajjaj's structure therefore remains, repaired over centuries as damage and dilapidation required.

Scripture itself points to older foundations. Ibrahim and Ismail were "raising up the foundations of the House" (2:127), implying that the Qawa'id were already present. God had also "settled for Ibrahim the site of the House" (22:26), suggesting a predetermined location. Reports add that an angel led Ibrahim to foundations buried under sand dunes.

### Why Bakkah?

Bakkah names Makkah. One derivation says it brings Buka', crying or weeping, upon tyrants and the arrogant, humbling them nearby. Another says crowds gather (do Buka') around it. It crushes the necks of tyrants (tabukku). Some explain Bakkah as Makkah al-Muʿazzamah by the familiar substitution of mīm for bā, others treat Bakkah simply as an alternative name.

Makkah carries many names: Bakkah, Al-Bayt Al-ʿAtiq, the Ancient House, Al-Bayt Al-Haram, the Sacred House, Al-Balad Al-Amin, the City of Safety, Al-Ma'mun, Security, Umm Rahm, Mother of Mercy, Umm Al-Qura, Mother of the Towns, Salah, and more.

### Blessing measured in usefulness

Barakah means growth and sustaining. Quantity can visibly multiply, but blessing can also make a limited quantity do what much more would ordinarily be required for. The second kind also counts as increase.

Outward blessing is conspicuous in a dry and barren desert. Makkah receives fruits, vegetables and necessities in every season. Residents alone do not exhaust them, visitors arrive from the whole world. Hundreds of thousands during Hajj can outnumber residents four or five to one and remain for months. Outside the season, thousands continuously enter and leave. Markets do not historically run out during the pilgrimage crowds. Sacrificial animals, at least one per pilgrim on average and sometimes more, remain available without special import arrangements. "Brought toward it are fruits of everything" (28:57) captures the phenomenon.

Inward blessing is too large to enumerate. Hajj and ʿUmra revolve around Baytullah. Prayer values also climb through the sacred mosques:

- 1 salah at home.
- 25 salahs in a local masjid.
- 500 salahs in a Jami', a large congregational mosque.
- 1,000 salahs in al-Masjid al-Aqsa.
- 50,000 salahs in the Prophet's Masjid.
- 100,000 salahs in al-Masjid al-Haram.

Ibn Majah and Tahawi are among this narration's reporters. Correct Hajj also cleanses a Muslim of past sins as if he had been born that day, pure and pristine. These blessings and its role as guidance belong to all worlds.

### In short

- Bakkah's House is the world's first House, or first exclusively for worship, and it stands blessed as guidance and Qiblah for all.
- Adam, Ibrahim, Jurhum, the Amalkites, Quraysh, Ibn Zubayr and Hajjaj built successively on ancient foundations (2:127, 22:26), giving Makkah's aura to all humanity.
- Barakah shows outwardly through provision for millions in a barren valley (28:57), and inwardly through prayer rewarded up to one hundred thousandfold in al-Masjid al-Haram.

97.text:
Inside the first House, meaning gathers: "In it are clear signs and the standing-place of Abraham. Whoever enters it should be safe. Pilgrimage to this House is an obligation by Allah upon whoever is able among the people. And whoever disbelieves, then surely Allah is not in need of ˹any of His˺ creation". Baytullah is distinguished by manifest signs, safety for entrants, and Hajj required from anyone able to reach it.

### Phrase by phrase

**"In it are clear signs and the standing-place of Abraham"**: manifest signs demonstrate that Ibrahim built the Kaʿbah and that Allah honoured and blessed it. Clear signs include the acts of worship performed in it and its landmarks. Alongside the Abraham standing place stand Ishmael's semi-circular white marble wall, Hatim, and the black stone.

**"Whoever enters it should be safe"**: entry brings security from violence. The Haram is a refuge for anyone in fear, and no harm comes to an entrant there.

**"Pilgrimage to this House is an obligation by Allah upon whoever is able among the people"**: Hajj to the House is a duty mankind owes Allah for those able to undertake the journey. Its verbal noun can be read hijj al-bayt or hajj al-bayt, "the intention to journey there". Ability defines the people addressed: anyone able to make his way there and perform the acts.

**"And whoever disbelieves, then surely Allah is not in need of ˹any of His˺ creation"**: whoever disbelieves in Allah, Muhammad, the Qur'an and the obligation of pilgrimage brings no loss to God. He stands Independent of all creatures, humans, jinn and angels, and needs neither their belief nor their devotions.

### The Maqam: footprints, movement and casing

When Kaʿbah walls rose, Ibrahim stood on the Maqam to build higher while Isma'il handed up stones. It originally stood beside the House. During his reign, ʿUmar bin Al-Khattab moved it farther east. Tawaf performers could then circle easily without disturbing worshippers praying beside the Maqam after finishing. Allah commands, "And take you (people) the Maqam (station) of Ibrahim as a place of prayer" (2:125).

Reports explain its sign quality. Al-ʿAwfi transmits Ibn ʿAbbās: "Such as the Maqam and Al-Mash'ar [Al-Haram]." Mujahid points to Ibrahim's feet impressions remaining on the Maqam. ʿUmar bin ʿAbdul-ʿAziz, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, As-Suddi, Muqatil bin Hayyan and others said similarly. The House has endured all this length of time and the constant passing of hands over it.

The stone reportedly possessed responsive movement. It raised itself with the construction level and descended when required. Footprints still mark it. An inert stone gaining sudden volition to respond functionally, or assuming wax-like plasticity beneath a perfect foot impression, signposts Allah's power and Baytullah's merit.

Its position migrated over time. From the door area, it was removed after the command in 2:125 for Tawaf convenience, then placed in front of Baytullah outside the mataf, the Tawaf area, close to Bi'r Zamzam. That well's original site is now marked with a black marble circle on Baytullah's floor with an Arabic legend inlaid. Later, the stone was secured in a small structure behind which the two post-tawaf rak'at were offered. Today, a strong metal-crystal casing encloses it, but the particular stone inside remains the Maqamu Ibrahim. Post-Tawaf salah of two rak'at behind or close to it is more merit-worthy. Yet Maqamu Ibrahim in its literal sense covers the entire al-Masjid al-Haram, so Muslim jurists allow the two rak'at anywhere within the Sacred Mosque.

### More signs: birds, protection, rain and disappearing pebbles

Reward for good deeds multiplies in the House, birds never fly over it, and people of Makkah have received protection from enemy attacks because of its blessings. Abrahah's elephant army, invading Makkah, was destroyed by birds.

Rainfall provides another reported sign: rain falling on one side of Baytullah seems to favour countries situated on that side with substantial rainfall. The Jamarat's pebbles provide a more testable one. Every pilgrim throws seven pebbles at each pillar for three days, with a couple million or more pilgrims every year. Without removal, the Jamarat would be buried under a mountain of pebbles. Yet after three days, only scattered pebbles are visible. According to the Prophet ﷺ, angels pick up the thrown pebbles, scattered ones belong to people whose Hajj was not accepted for some reason. Picking up pebbles lying near the Jamarat for throwing is forbidden because they belong to unaccepted pilgrimages.

Shaykh Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti, in al-Khasa'is al-Kubra, counts this among miracles of the Holy Prophet ﷺ that still live, stand and will continue until the Day of Judgment for everyone to see. The Holy Qur'an's unmatched presence is another: no force in the world can jointly match it, an inability that persisted in the Prophet's time and will persist to Judgment. Every Muslim in every period can challenge the whole world, "Then, produce a Surah like it" (10:38). Similarly, the statement about angels invisibly collecting accepted pebbles has stood the test of time for centuries. It is a continuing prophetic miracle and a major sign in the Kaʿbah.

### Safety declared from creation

Even Jahiliyyah felt the Haram's refuge. Al-Hasan Al-Basri describes a murderer wearing a piece of wool around his neck before entering. The murdered man's son could meet him inside and would make no move until he left the sanctuary. Scripture frames it universally: "Have they not seen that We have made (Makkah) a secure sanctuary, while men are being snatched away from all around them?" (29:67). "So let them worship (Allah) the Lord of this House (the Ka'bah). (He) Who has fed them against hunger, and has made them safe from fear" (106:3-4).

Hunting, driving game from its den to be hunted, cutting trees and picking grass are prohibited in the Haram. At the conquest, the Prophet ﷺ announced, as recorded in The Two Sahihs with wording from Muslim and attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās:

> "There is no more Hijrah (migration to Makkah), only Jihad and good intention. If you were mobilized, then march forth."

He also said:

> "Beware! Allah made this town (Makkah) a sanctuary when He created the heavens and earth, and it is sacred by Allah's decree until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in Makkah was not permitted for anyone before me, and it was made legal for me for only a few hours or so on that day. No doubt it is at this moment a sanctuary by Allah's decree until the Day of Resurrection. It is not allowed to uproot its thorny shrubs, hunt its game, pick up its lost objects, except by announcing it, or to uproot its trees."

Al-ʿAbbās intervened for lemongrass, used in their houses and graves. The exception came: "Except lemongrass."

Abu Shurayh Al-ʿAdawi spoke to ʿAmr bin Sa'id while troops were being sent toward Makkah against ʿAbdullah bin Az-Zubayr. The Two Sahihs recorded his plea. His ears had heard it, his heart memorised it, and his eyes saw the Prophet ﷺ speak after glorifying and praising Allah:

> 'Allah, not the people, made Makkah a sanctuary. Therefore, anybody who has belief in Allah and the Last Day, should neither shed blood in it nor cut down its trees. If anybody argues that fighting in it is permissible on the basis that Allah's Messenger fought in Makkah, say to him, "Allah allowed His Messenger and did not allow you." Allah allowed me only for a few hours on that day (of the conquest), and today its sanctity is as valid as it was before. So, those who are present, should inform those who are absent of this fact.'"

ʿAmr answered: "O Abu Shurayh! I know better than you in this respect, Makkah does not give protection to a sinner, a murderer or a thief."

Jabir bin ʿAbdullah heard a simpler prohibition from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "None of you is allowed to carry a weapon in Makkah." Muslim recorded it.

Affection had a voice as well. Abdullah bin ʿAdi bin Al-Hamra' Az-Zuhri heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say while standing at Al-Hazwarah in Makkah's marketplace:

> "(By Allah! You are the best of Allah's land and the most beloved land to Allah. Had it not been for the fact that I was driven out of you, I would not have left you.)"

Imam Ahmad collected this Hadith and this is his wording. At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also collected it. At-Tirmidhi said, "Hasan Sahih."

### Security under law and in human instinct

Legally, an entrant cannot be molested or killed there. A person who kills someone or commits another crime, then enters the sanctuary, should not be punished inside. He is compelled out first. Punishment follows departure. Divine law thus protects the entrant while he remains within.

A second security is factual. Divine creation planted awe and reverence for Baytullah in people's hearts. Wild, warring Jahiliyyah Arab tribes were ready to sacrifice their lives to uphold Baytullah's honour. Esteem for the Haram was so deep that a son could encounter his father's killer there, say nothing, and quietly move away despite a burning rage for revenge.

Only a few hours were ever excepted. Revelation at the conquest of Makkah allowed the Holy Prophet ﷺ alone to fight so Baytullah could be cleansed for an important objective of faith. His express announcement soon made the original prohibition of fighting permanently valid.

Hajjaj ibn Yusuf's later armed action against ʿAbdullah ibn Zubayr, with killings and terror, was a grave sin and a flagrant violation of law and the Kaʿbah's sanctity, hated by the entire community, and it does not dent the divine declaration. Hajjaj himself knew the action was unlawful and a serious crime, but political and administrative considerations overwhelmed him. The wider community has always held the Haram and Baytullah in highest esteem and has regarded fighting or quarrelling in sacred precincts as one of the ugliest sins. That esteem is Baytullah's universal and exclusive mark.

### Hajj: a duty once, for whoever can reach it

Hajj is obligatory by this verse, a fundamental pillar mentioned by many Hadiths and agreed upon by Muslims. Text and scholarly consensus limit the adult Muslim to one obligatory performance in a lifetime. Abu Hurayrah reported in Imam Ahmad that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ once delivered a speech saying:

> "O people! Hajj has been enjoined on you, therefore, perform Hajj."

A man asked, "Is it every year, O Allah's Messenger?" The Prophet ﷺ remained silent until the man repeated the question three times and He then said:

> "Had I said yes, it would have become an obligation and you would not have been able to fulfill it."

He said next:

> "Leave me as I leave you, those before you were destroyed because of their many questions and disputing with their Prophets. If I command you with something, perform it as much as you can. If I forbid something for you, then refrain from it."

Muslim recorded similarly.

Ability has multiple categories, personal physical ability and ability related to other things, elaborated in jurisprudence. Abu ʿIsa At-Tirmidhi records Ibn ʿUmar answering three questions. Who is the pilgrim? "He who has untidy hair and clothes." Which Hajj is better? "The noisy (with supplication to Allah) and bloody (with sacrifice)." What is the ability to undertake the journey? "Having provision and a means of transportation." Ibn Majah collected the narration. Al-Hakim narrated that Anas said that the Messenger of Allah was asked about Allah's statement "for those who are able to undertake the journey" [3:97]: "What does 'able to undertake the journey' mean?" The Prophet ﷺ answered, "Having sufficient provision and a means of transportation." Al-Hakim considered Anas's chain authentic by Muslim's guidelines, though the Two Sahihs did not collect the report. Ahmad also recorded Ibn ʿAbbas: whoever intends Hajj should rush to perform it. Abu Dawud collected that Hadith too.

"Means" means surplus resources beyond basic needs. They should cover travel to Baytullah and back, expenses during stay in the Holy Land, and family expenses until return, since that is a standing obligation on him. Physical handicaps that prevent going that far and completing Hajj's many requirements, inability to see, or to use hands and feet, negate ability. As women are not legally permitted to travel without a Mahram (marriage with whom is prohibited), they would be considered "able" to embark on their Hajj if they are travelling with a Mahram making his Hajj, whether the Mahram bears his own expenses or the woman pays for his expenses as well. Similarly, route security is part of "ability": acute danger to life and property means an absence of ability to perform Hajj.

Literally, Hajj means "to intend". What it means in terms of prescribed religious observance is already stated in the Holy Qur'an itself: the tawaf of the Kaʿbah, the stay in ʿArafat, and in Muzdalifah. Remaining details have been made clear by the Holy Prophet ﷺ through his words and deeds.

### Whoever disbelieves after capability

Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujahid and several others commented on this verse: "Whoever denies the necessity of Hajj becomes disbeliever, and Allah is far Richer than to need him." Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Isma'ili recorded that 'Umar bin Al-Khattab said: "Whoever can afford Hajj but did not perform it, there is no difference in his case if he dies while Jew or Christian." This has an authentic chain of narration leading to 'Umar.

Intentional rejection of Hajj's obligation is undoubtedly included. Such a person cannot be considered a Muslim. He is a disbeliever indeed, for the description "And if one disbelieves" fits him clearly and comprehensively. A different case is the believer who accepts the obligation, has means and ability, and still does not perform it. He is no less a denier of the Divine command in practice. In his case, "and if one disbelieves" applies by admonition and warning, since he acts like disbelievers who do not perform Hajj. Muslim jurists therefore treat the verse as a severe warning to capable non-performers: heedlessness makes them resemble disbelievers. Refuge with Allah is sought from such a fate.

### The House of stone, and the heart it draws

Start with visitors, not masonry. Bodily selves, nufūs, circumambulate the House, while hearts, qulūb, seek the Real. What joins servant to sanctuary is imaged as mud bound to stone: the servant is madara, a bit of mud, the House is ḥajara, a bit of stone, and rabaṭa al-madara bi-l-ḥajara (the mud is bonded to the stone) lets mud, madar, remain with stone, ḥajar, while the Eternal is magnified. Relics are stones, but their traces point backward to the people who stood there.

Response differs by heart. One stone can cool and delight, muthlij wa-mubhij, while another experience of the same stone stirs and arouses, munfij wa-muzʿij. Lovers awaken, muzʿij, and poor souls, fuqarāʾ, leap, munfij. Visit a House as a mazār, a place for loved ones, and traces, āthār, or news, akhbār, may be sought. Through separation, the innermost self returns wasted, kharāb. Through connection, approach and approval, ījāb, are won. Houses remain in pact with lovers who stop at them, even in silence. Bodily visitation finds kindness. Heart visitation finds unveiling. God calls it "My House" (2:125 and 22:26).

### In short

- In the House are manifest signs, among them the Maqam stone that rose with the walls and kept Ibrahim's footprints, moved east by ʿUmar and still prayed behind (2:125).
- Whoever enters is safe under a sanctity declared at creation, lifted only for hours at the conquest, so that killing, hunting, cutting and weapons are all barred.
- Hajj to the House is a duty once in a lifetime for whoever has provision, transport, bodily ability, a secure route and, for women, a Mahram, and denying its obligation is disbelief.

98.text:
The address returns to the People of the Book with a witness in the room: "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O People of the Book! Why do you deny the revelations of Allah, when Allah is a Witness to what you do?”" They had learned the truth about the Messenger from the previous Prophets, who brought glad tidings of his coming. Refusing him therefore happens before the One who watched them receive that knowledge.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O People of the Book! Why do you deny the revelations of Allah"**: why do you reject the Ayat of Allah, refuse the truth and reject what the Messenger ﷺ was sent with, Muhammad and the Qur'an? Why do you disbelieve in God’s verses, the Qur’ān, and reject the proof of the truth of your prophet-hood, including the proofs that came in the Torah and the Gospel?

**"when Allah is a Witness to what you do?”"**: Allah is Witness over what you do, of disbelief, by concealing the Truth and engaging in sins. He watches over everything you do, witnessing it, and will reward you accordingly. He is not unaware, and He will hold them responsible for their actions, on "The Day whereon neither wealth nor sons will avail" (26:88).

### What they already knew

Truth had reached them before refusal. Earlier Prophets and honourable Messengers had announced an unlettered Arab Hashimi Prophet from Makkah, master of Adam's children, Final Prophet and Messenger of the Lord of heavens and earth. Defiance therefore rejects a Messenger they were ordered to announce, not an unknown claimant. Allah witnesses their conduct and will hold them responsible.

### When truth puts a self-made religion at risk

When truth's call arrives pure, self-styled religion faces a threat to its interests. Its servants resist a new messenger with fallacious objections meant to turn hearers away. Basics receive little stress inside their system, hair-splitting over religion's relative aspects matters more, and virtue becomes full adherence to a man-made religious form. Rabbit meat may be shunned because saints did not consume it, alongside legalised illegal things. Facing al-Bayt al-Maqdis with compass precision can become paramount while daily activities remain unoriented toward God.

Sacrifice, not religious form, determines virtue. God's true servant offers love as his gift to his Lord, values no material thing above Him, accepts prestige loss for recognising truth, and spends wealth for God's cause. Cherished ambitions sacrificed at that price mark the virtuous God-worshipper.

Sacrifice, not religious form, determines virtue. God's true servant offers love as his gift to his Lord, values no material thing above Him, accepts prestige loss for recognising truth, and spends wealth for God's cause. Cherished ambitions sacrificed at that price mark the virtuous God-worshipper.

### Called by the law, barred by decree

One inward reading sees a pilgrimage paradox. The law calls the People of Scripture and makes pilgrimage obligatory for them, yet true reality, ḥaqīqa, and divine subjugation, qahr, bar them from it. They are summoned legally and by command, madʿuwūna sharʿan wa-amran, while being banished by decree and subjugation, maṬrūdūna ḥukman wa-qahran.

### In short

- Denial happens before Allah's witnessing eye, despite the glad tidings of the unlettered Prophet already conveyed by earlier prophets.
- He will hold them responsible on a Day when wealth and sons do not avail (26:88).
- The purity of the truth threatens self-made religion, whose virtue is sacrifice, not form.

99.text:
Refusal becomes obstruction: "Say, “O People of the Book! Why do you turn the believers away from the Way of Allah—striving to make it ˹appear˺ crooked, while you are witnesses ˹to its truth˺? And Allah is never unaware of what you do.”" They do not merely decline the path. They bar believers from it, call its straightness crooked, and do so while their own Book testifies that Islam is the upright religion pleasing to God.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, “O People of the Book! Why do you turn the believers away from the Way of Allah"**: why do you stop those who have believed from the path of Allah, bar believers causing them to turn away from God's way, His religion, by denying the truth of the Prophet and concealing His graces? Why do you stop people who have faith from the Religion of Allah, wanting to turn its people from guidance to misguidance?

**"striving to make it ˹appear˺ crooked"**: desiring to make it crooked, inclining away from the truth, wanting to twist it from the truth to falsehood. The word is the verbal noun meaning "made crooked."

**"while you are witnesses ˹to its truth˺?"**: while you yourselves are witnesses, while your own knowledge says Islam is the upright religion pleasing to God, as your Book states. Its truth confirms what your Scriptures contain.

**"And Allah is never unaware of what you do.”"**: God is not heedless of what you do, in the way of unbelief and mendacity. Allah is not oblivious to your disbelief: concealing the Truth and committing transgressions. Instead, He gives you respite until your appointed time and then requites you. They will be repaid accordingly.

### Whom they tried to turn

This verse was revealed about those who invited ʿAmmar [Ibn Yasir] and his fellow Muslims to join their religion: Judaism. The obstruction was aimed first at believers in Allah, Muhammad and the Qur'an, to drive them back from the Religion of Allah and His worship.

An inward question sharpens the absurdity. How can one who is barred himself bar another? Surely in this is a secret belonging to the divine Lordship.

### In short

- The People of the Book bar believers from Allah's way and call it crooked, though their Book witnesses Islam's uprightness.
- ʿAmmar and his fellow Muslims were among those invited back to Judaism.
- Allah is never unaware, and respite lasts only until the appointed time.

100.text:
The warning is redirected to the believers themselves: "O believers! If you were to yield to a group of those who were given the Scripture, they would turn you back from belief to disbelief". The danger is not argument. It is suggestion, memory and tribal pride, used by people who envy the favour given to the believers in the sending of the Messenger.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O believers! If you were to yield to a group of those who were given the Scripture"**: O you who believe! If you obey a group of those who were given the Scripture, Jews and Christians, in what they say and accept their opinion in what they claim. If you obey a party of those who have received the Scripture, the Torah.

**"they would turn you back from belief to disbelief"**: they would render you disbelievers after you have believed, make you disbelievers in Allah and Muhammad after your belief in Allah and the message of Muhammad. The return comes through their envy and their misguidance.

### The envy behind obedience

Allah warns His believing servants against obeying the People of the Book, who envy the believers for the favour that Allah gave them by sending His Messenger ﷺ. Similarly, Allah said: "Many of the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) wish that they could turn you away as disbelievers after you have believed, out of their own envy" (2:109).

### Shammas ibn Qays and the poems of war

A particular event stands behind the warning. Shammas ibn Qays, a Jew with chronic malice against Muslims, saw the Ansar tribes Aws and Khazraj sitting together amiably. Malevolence drove him to sow discord. He arranged for a man to remind both tribes of their long pre-Islamic wars and the self-congratulating poems each side had composed about tribal pride. Recitation should happen while they sat together.

Poems heated the gathering. Charges and counter-charges rose until a fresh war's place and time were nearly set. News reached the Holy Prophet ﷺ, who came and rebuked them: he was present amidst them, after Islam had united them in friendship, so was this sheer ignorance and a wish to revert to kufr?

Warning entered their hearts. They recognised a Satanic slip, embraced each other, wept and repented. These verses were revealed against that background. This event appears in Ruh al-Ma'ani as narrated by Ibn Ishaq, while others narrate it from Zaid ibn Aslam.

Another narration through Ayyub from Ikrimah, transmitted by al-Mu'ammil ibn Isma'il, pictures a Jew in a mixed assembly reciting one tribe's war poetry until rival claims, battle cries for Aws and Khazraj, and armed lines formed.

### Caution, taqwa, and the keeper within

Trial never leaves this world. Satan's temptations create a standing risk that belief will turn to unbelief, and death may arrive while the spirit of faith is absent and amends are almost impossible. A person must therefore become his own keeper.

Taqwa is religion's mainspring: an unshakeable sense, held until death, that every action is accountable to God. This is the true and straight path. Turning from that path usually rearranges religious priorities. Secondary matters get made fundamental and are stressed as though they deserved the place of God-fearing concern for the Hereafter. Different groups stress different secondary aspects, and such alterations breed differences, serious schisms and eventually sects. Taqwa keeps attention on the one God, without it, trivial matters come to the forefront, disunity follows, and disunity carries calamity in both worlds. Unity becomes natural only when all emphasis rests on taqwa.

Estrangement also spreads socially. Anyone who becomes part of the estranged circle or follows God's enemy into ruinous companionship will be cast down to the same level.

### In short

- Obeying an envious group of the People of the Book returns believers to disbelief (2:109).
- Shammas ibn Qays engineered the recital of pre-Islamic war poems until Aws and Khazraj nearly set a time and place for fresh war.
- The keeper against Satan's turning is taqwa, unshakeable accountability, which alone makes unity natural.

101.text:
The defence against that turning is named: "How can you disbelieve when Allah’s revelations are recited to you and His Messenger is in your midst? Whoever holds firmly to Allah is surely guided to the Straight Path". Disbelief is far from a community receiving revelation day and night, with the Messenger reciting and conveying it. The verse was revealed while swords were being drawn inside that very community.

### Phrase by phrase

**"How can you disbelieve when Allah’s revelations are recited to you and His Messenger is in your midst?"**: amazement and rebuke frame the question. How could you disbelieve in Allah after faith when the biggest reason for firm faith stands with you? Allah's verses are recited to you while Messenger Muhammad clarifies them.

**"Whoever holds firmly to Allah is surely guided to the Straight Path"**: whoever depends upon Allah, then he is indeed guided to the right path. He who holdeth fast to Allah, he who adheres to Allah's Religion and His Book, is directed along a clear, solid way, which is Islam, it is also said this means: he has become firm on this way. Whoever holds on firmly to the Book of Allah and His Messenger's way of life, Allah has guided them to the right path.

### Two tribes with swords, and a voice raised between them

The Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, stood between two armies, read this verse and raised his voice. Hearing stopped talk and produced listening. Once recitation ended, weapons dropped and embraces and crying followed.

Zayd ibn Aslam names the instigator as Shas ibn Qays, an elderly Jew formed in the pre-Islamic period, a great disbeliever with extreme hate and intense envy toward Muslims. Seeing Aws and Khazraj companions gathered in friendly reconciliation after former enmity infuriated him. "The people of Banu Qaylah have united in this land," he said.

Ibn 'Abbas places swords in the story: mention of the pre-Islamic feud led Aws and Khazraj to brandish weapons at each other. News reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he went to them, and revelation ran from this verse through "And hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate" (3:103). Another chain has talk turning to anger, arms taken and two groups marching toward each other, before revelation came down through "He did save you from it".

This verse was also revealed about Mu'adh [Ibn Jabal] and his companions.

### Amazement, covenants and the most amazing faith

"And what is the matter with you that you believe not in Allah! While the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord; and He has indeed taken your covenant, if you are real believers" (57:8). A Hadith states that one day, the Prophet said to his Companions, "Who among the faithful believers do you consider has the most amazing faith?" They said, "The angels." He said, "Why would they not believe, since they are with their Lord?" They mentioned the Prophets, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "Why would they not believe while the revelation is sent down to them?" They said, "Then, we are." He said, "Why would not you believe when I am among you?" They asked, "Who has the most amazing faith?" The Prophet said, "A people who will come after you and who will find only books that they will believe in."

Trust and reliance in Allah form the basis for right guidance, avoidance of wickedness, acquisition of truth and achievement of righteous aims.

Iʿtisam, holding firmly to Allah, means staying totally committed to iman. It denotes affirming His Being and Attributes, remaining staunchly faithful to His ordinances, and refusing to be lured into supporting any adversary. Such a person "is surely guided to the straight path", and being on that path is the key to all the good and benefit promised by Allah's Word.

### Holding fast, found rather than achieved

Disbelief's shade should not cross a heart lit by rising suns of deeper knowledge, ʿirfān. When day comes, night slips away. Holding fast is nevertheless received, not self-manufactured. Guidance from God in the beginning, bidāya, produces holding in the end, nihāya, holding does not create guidance, hidāya. Sincerity defines the true state: taking oneself to Him, persevering in flight toward Him and continually appealing for His help. Remove separation's covering from the innermost self and no atom seems to belong to, or come from, anything other than God. Those who hold fast are those held fast by Him. The leader of first and last said, "I seek refuge in You from You." Self-powered holding without effacement of strength and power lands in idolatry, shirk, while its owner remains unaware.

### In short

- Disbelief is amazing where Allah's verses, commands and prohibitions are recited and His Messenger is present (57:8).
- The Prophet read this verse standing between Aws and Khazraj until weapons dropped and enemies embraced, up to (3:103).
- Holding fast means affirming Allah's Being and Attributes without supporting any adversary, and inwardly it is found from God rather than achieved by the self.

102.text:
The remedy for discord starts with the individual: "O believers! Be mindful of Allah in the way He deserves, and do not die except in ˹a state of full˺ submission ˹to Him˺". Taqwa and unity are the two principles announced here and in the next verse. A life managed under responsibility before Allah, avoiding what is forbidden and undesirable as He deserves, is the only soil in which unity can hold.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O believers! Be mindful of Allah in the way He deserves"**: Have Taqwa of Allah as is His due. Taqwa in Arabic denotes avoidance and abstinence, translated as "fear" because what must be abstained from carries the danger of Divine retribution.

**"and do not die except in ˹a state of full˺ submission ˹to Him˺"**: die not except as true Muslims, professing His Oneness. Keep Islam intact while you are well and safe. Refuge is sought from dying on anything other than Islam.

### What "as is His due" demands

Ibn Abi Hatim recorded ʿAbdullah bin Mas'ud's comment:

> "(Have Taqwa of Allah as is His due,) 'That He is obeyed and not defied, remembered and not forgotten and appreciated and not unappreciated.'"

An authentic chain reaches ʿAbdullah bin Mas'ud. Al-Hakim collected the report in his Mustadrak from Ibn Mas'ud, relating it to the Prophet ﷺ, and said: "It is authentic according to the criteria of the Two Shaykhs [Al-Bukhari and Muslim], and they did not record it." Even so, it appears to be Ibn Mas'ud's own statement, and Allah knows best. Rabi', Qatadah and Hasan al-Basri give the same triad in Al-Bahr Al-Muhit: obey without disobeying, remember without forgetting, and be grateful without ingratitude. The report is also carried with a chain ascending to the Prophet ﷺ himself.

Different senses are added. Due fear can mean obeying Allah while dismissing all derogatory criticism, standing firm on justice even when justice hurts oneself, one's children or one's parents. Anas said the servant will not attain it until he keeps his tongue idle, others make protection of the tongue the gate to it. When people asked who was strong enough for such a task, the qualification came: "So fear God as much as you can" (64:16). Ibn 'Abbas and Tawus treat that as the explanation of "as is His due": do your best with all attention and energy to guard against evil, and the obligation stands fulfilled. Falling into something impermissible despite that best effort is not a failure of due taqwa.

### Three degrees of a single word

Taqwa is not one flat state. At its lowest degree, it is abstaining from Kufr and Shirk: disbelief in Allah and His Message, and assigning partners to His divinity. Every Muslim counts as Muttaqi in this sense, even if involved in sins, and the Qur'an often uses Muttaqin and Taqwa at this level.

The desired degree is higher: avoiding whatever Allah and His Messenger dislike. The merits and blessings promised for Taqwa in Qur'an and Hadith attach to this degree of abstinence.

The third degree is a station for prophets, their devoted deputies and men of Allah. It means standing guard over the heart against every onslaught unrelated to Allah, keeping it filled with His remembrance and the desire for His pleasure. That is not within everybody's grasp.

Because total obedience to Allah and His Messenger and total avoidance of disobedience to both are exactly what Taqwa means, Taqwa is in reality the whole of Islam. This is why the same verse can command both taqwa as His due and dying only as Muslims.

### Living determines dying

Death is not in human control, so the command needs explanation. The rule supplied is: "As you live, so shall you die; and as you die, so shall you be raised." The Most Generous Allah has decided that a person's settled state in life is the state of his death and resurrection. A determined person who lives by Islam's tenets to the best of his determination and ability will, God willing, die in Islam. Reports of people whose lifetime of good deeds is wasted by something awful later apply, in this reading, to those who lacked sincerity and steadfastness from the very beginning. And Allah knows best.

Two deathbed protections follow. Imam Ahmad recorded that Mujahid described people circling the Sacred House while Ibn 'Abbas sat with a bent-handled walking stick. Ibn 'Abbas said the Messenger of Allah recited this verse and then said:

> "(Verily, if a drop of Zaqqum (a tree in Hell) falls, it will spoil life for the people of earth. What about those whose food is only from Zaqqum)"

This was recorded by At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak. At-Tirmidhi said, "Hasan Sahih", Al-Hakim said it meets the conditions of the Two Sahihs, which did not record it.

Imam Ahmad recorded that Jabir heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say three nights before his death: "None of you should die except while having sincere trust in Allah, the Exalted and Most Honorable." Muslim also recorded it. The Two Sahihs record Abu Hurayrah's report of the Prophet's words: "Allah said, 'I am as My servant thinks of Me.'"

The verse's own occasion is placed in an Aws and Khazraj dispute where Tha'labah Ibn Ghanam and As'ad Ibn Zurarah boasted about their killings and raids on rivals in pre-Islamic days. The command tells believers to surrender sincerely, acknowledging that they worship Him and declare His divine Oneness.

### Godwariness addressed to two kinds of people

The forms of address sort the audience. "O people" pairs with "Be wary of your Lord". Common people hear that address. Their godwariness is based on seeing blessings, and they nurture the body for serving the Real. "O you who have faith" pairs with "Be wary of God". That address reaches the folk of caresses and generosity. Their godwariness is watchfulness of the Beneficent, and their aim is the spirit's repose in witnessing the Real.

So the wage-earners are told, "Be wary of your Lord", and the recognizers are told, "Be wary of God". Wage-earners seek joy and blessings, things other than Him. Recognizers seek the mystery of the Beneficent, God Himself. AḤmad ibn Khiẓrūya saw the Real in a dream and heard: "O AḤmad! Everyone is seeking something from Me, except Abū Yazīd. He is seeking Me." Other people wish for repose and comfort, but the recognizer wishes only to encounter Him empty, and on reaching union would disdain even the state of Paradise's dwellers.

Godwariness is also sorted into three kinds. Wariness of punishment, through patience against disobedience, belongs to the text "Be wary of the Fire that has..." (3:131). Godwariness of gratitude for blessings belongs to "Be wary of your Lord" (4:1). Godwariness at the vision of Unity, taking no account of reward or punishment, belongs to this verse. The first is the godwariness of the wrongdoers, the second of the moderate, and the third of the preceders.

### In short

- Taqwa as His due is obedience without defiance, remembrance without forgetting, and gratitude without ingratitude, measured at the edge of one's best effort (64:16).
- Its degrees climb from avoiding kufr and shirk, to avoiding everything Allah dislikes, to guarding the heart for His pleasure alone.
- Since states settle at death, sincerity from the beginning, protection of the tongue, and sincere trust in Allah are its safeguards.

103.text:
Discord is answered with a single grip: "And hold firmly to the rope of Allah and do not be divided. Remember Allah’s favour upon you when you were enemies, then He united your hearts, so you—by His grace—became brothers. And you were at the brink of a fiery pit and He saved you from it. This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to you, so that you may be ˹rightly˺ guided". The binding factor is named before division is forbidden, and then a people pulled back from a pit is reminded what division nearly cost.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And hold firmly to the rope of Allah"**: Hold fast, all of you together, to the Rope of Allah, to the Religion of Allah and His Book.

**"and do not be divided"**: be not divided among yourselves. Stick to the community of the believers and do not separate in religion. Avoid scattering once Islam has been submitted to.

**"Remember Allah’s favour upon you when you were enemies, then He united your hearts, so you—by His grace—became brothers"**: For Aws and Khazraj, favour takes concrete form: former enemies were joined through Islam, becoming religious brothers and companions.

**"And you were at the brink of a fiery pit and He saved you from it"**: Ye were upon the brink, the edge of an abyss of fire because of disbelief, He saved you by means of faith. Dying disbelieving would have completed the fall.

**"This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to you, so that you may be ˹rightly˺ guided"**: Thus Allah maketh clear His revelations, His commands, prohibitions and favours (unto you, that haply ye may be guided) from error. Just as He has made clear what has been mentioned, God makes clear to you His signs that you might be guided.

### Habl: a cord that is also a covenant

Abdullah ibn Masud narrated the Prophet's saying:

> The Book of Allah is the cord of Allah, extended from the heavens to the earth.

In Zayd ibn Arqam's narration, the words are: "The cord of Allah is the Qur'an." Habl in Arabic also means covenant. In an absolute sense, it covers everything that can serve as a connecting link. The metaphor suggests a link that establishes communion between believers and their Lord on one side, and brings all believers close together into one group on the other. Grip that strong rope while climbing, and the community remains protected against a fall, stable and impregnable in collective strength like a climber's body.

Rope can also mean Allah's covenant itself, as in the verse of humiliation: "(Indignity is put over them wherever they may be, except when under a covenant (of protection) from Allah, and from men;)" [3:112], said in reference to pledges and peace treaties.

Holding fast to the Book with total strength, all in unison, prevents Satan from dividing believers. Scattered forces are united, and a dead nation gets new life. Breaking away from it ruins national and collective life, and individual life fares no better. More clearly still: "Surely, those who believe and do good deeds, among them the All-Merciful Allah shall create (mutual) affection" (19:96).

### Three things loved, and the verdict on sects

Several hadiths require adhering to the Jama'ah, the congregation of believers, and prohibit division. Muslim recorded that Abi Hurairah said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

> "(It pleases Allah for you to acquire three qualities and displeases Him that you acquire three characteristics. It pleases Him that you worship Him Alone and not associate anything or anyone with Him in worship, that you hold on to the Rope of Allah altogether and do not divide, and that you advise whoever Allah appoints as your Leader. The three that displease Him are that you say, 'It was said,' and, 'So-and-so said,' asking many unnecessary questions and wasting money.)"

The Prophet ﷺ has also said that three things are liked for you by Allah, and three disliked. Liked are: worship of Allah alone without attributing partners to His divinity, holding on to the Book of Allah firmly and avoiding disunity, and goodwill for those in authority from among you. Displeasing Him are unnecessary argumentation, needless asking, and wastage of resources.

The positive comes first, then the negative is identified and forbidden: "Surely, this is the straight path, so, follow it. And do not follow (other) ways which will cause you to become separated from His way" (6:153). And the sectarian verdict: "Those who have made divisions in their religion and become sects, you have nothing to do with them" (6:159).

### Brotherhood after a pre-Islamic war

During Jahiliyyah, Aws and Khazraj lived at war, with great hatred, enmity and ill feelings, and long conflicts and battles. Islam changed those who embraced it into brothers who loved each other by Allah's grace, having good ties for Allah's sake and helping each other in righteousness and piety: "(He it is Who has supported you with His Help and with the believers. And He has united their hearts. If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have united their hearts, but Allah has united them)" (8:62-63).

Before Islam, disbelief left them at a pit's edge. Faith delivered them. The Messenger later reminded the Ansar of the bounty while dividing Hunayn's spoils: some disliked receiving less than others, although Allah had directed the distribution. He asked whether he had not found them misguided before Allah guided them through him, divided before Allah united them around him, and poor before Allah enriched them through him. Each question received the answer: "Indeed, Allah and His Messenger have granted us bounty." 

Both tribes were Arabs inhabiting Madinah. Continuous war, attacks and counter-attacks considerably weakened them until Islam ended hostilities and made them like brothers. Allegiance explains the change. A truth-denier is faithful only to himself. A believer gives allegiance solely to God. Many self- or group-allegiances naturally multiply strife and dissension, a society bowed only to one God is directed towards a single focal point. Bound by one cord, its members cease mutual clashes.

Centuries-deep enmities were erased when Allah made them brothers through Islam's benediction and the noble Prophet ﷺ. Life became worth living materially and spiritually, with exemplary friendship even enemies found awesome. No combined treasures of the world could purchase that brotherly unity. The verse also eliminates the mischief of those who tried to disunite Aws and Khazraj by reviving past feuds. Once in Islam, division is unthinkable.

### Why no human program can be the centre

A centre of attraction is required for unity. Peoples have tried race and tribe, as with Quraysh and Banu Tamim in Arabia, colour, black as one nation and white as another, geography or language, Indian against Arab, and ancestral custom, as with the Arya Samajists in India.

Human unity appeals normally ask everyone else to accept a self-made program. Other parties have programs of their own, so calls fragment instead of uniting. A few people can fuse temporarily around shared objectives, but once interests are served or frustrated, bickering and hostility replace unity. Sects within sects and parties within parties can make even two-person unity a myth.

Imposing one group's conception on humanity and expecting unanimous acceptance is against commonsense and justice, and is cheeky self-deception. A system from the Creator-Sustainer of all worlds, Rabb al-ʿAlamin, is different in principle. Rational human beings cannot deny it on principle, although identification is contested: Jews claim the Torah's system, Christians claim the Evangel's system, and even polytheist groups attribute their rites to god.

Qur'an makes the Book of Allah the centre instead. Muslims become a nation attached to Ḥablillah, disbelievers another nation, unattached to that strong cord. "(It is He who created you. So, some of you are infidels and some of you are believers)" (64:16). Geography, race, tribe and language are unchosen and uncontrollable. Black cannot become white, Qurayshi cannot become Tamimi, Indian cannot become Arab. Limited unities follow, never a platform for all humanity. A divinely revealed way of life can be elected freely from East or West, by black or white, in Arabic, English or any language, by any family, tribe or human group. Humanity can then gather concentrically around God-given guidance and tune material and spiritual deeds to one accepted way.

Muslims can be proud of that principle and confident when inviting others to join. Conspiracies hatched by Europeans for centuries to crush Muslim unity have divided claimants to Islam, race, language and nationalities have been accepted as dividing forces, severing Arabs from Non-Arabs and Indians from non-Indians. Qur'an instead proclaims those distinctions ill-founded and divisive, and unity based on them irrational and false. Muslims have no choice but to hold on to the cord of Allah, all of them, as a way of life. That produced honour before and would produce any future success.

First, Muslims live by Allah's prescribed system. Second, they hold fast to His cord all together. Past ascendance followed those instructions, and no reason prevents a future rise. Firm grip on the Qur'an also acts like a climber's strong rope, uniting scattered forces, reviving a dead nation and keeping individual and collective life from ruin when it is not broken away from.

### Differences that are mercy, and differences that divide

Not all differences are blameworthy. Blame begins where people stay away from the Qur'an and think by whims and wishes. A different path stays united around the Qur'an while accepting the Prophet's explanation and detail. From that centre, God-given natural ability and intellectual quality may generate subsidiary opinions. Companions, Successors and leading jurists differed in exactly this natural, unforbidden way, and such difference was called a "mercy" for the community.

Status changes the verdict. If subsidiary debates are invested with mainstream religion's status, and controversy, confrontation, insult and vilification follow, blame returns.

### Unity as obedience rewarded

Allah Almighty is the Master of hearts. Activating mutual love and consideration in the hearts of a people is purely a Divine blessing. One becomes deserving of Allah's blessings only through obedience to Him. With disobedience and sin, one cannot hope for this reward. It follows that for Muslims, if they desire a stable organization among them and unity, the only alternative open is to make obedience to Allah their lifestyle. This point is hinted at towards the end of the verse: "This is how Allah makes His signs clear to you, so that you may take the right path" (103). Obedience marks the Muttaqin, sustains the ummah, and keeps remembrance alive from the opening command onward.

### Holding fast without scattering

Clinging to the traces of the intermediary, āthār al-wāsiṭa (the noble one ʿazīz ﷺ), is what holding fast to His bond means. Confirming what is true and right, taḥaqquq, and remaining devoted, taʿalluq, to the Book and Sunna create the grip. "Hold fast to God's bond" addresses the elite, khawāṣṣ, "hold fast to God" (4:146 and 22:78) addresses the elect of the elect, khāṣṣ al-khāṣṣ.

Turning away from His auspicious occurrences, sawāniḥ, toward one's own choosing and devising, iḥtiyāl, thinking and reasoning, istidlāl, and ways of knowing and behaving, ashkāl, is dangerous. Seeking refuge in the shade of one's planning, tadbīr, and illumination from one's intellect and speculation, tafkīr, denies the shade of divine solicitude and leaves an unfortunate state.

"And do not scatter." Scattering or separation, tafriqa, is the most intense punishment, companion to shirk. Enmity arose when people remained with worldly concerns, turned toward narrow human nature and competed in lower-self stinginess. Deliverance from captivity to created things brought hearts together and drove afflictions from innermost selves. Their sought object became one, so even a thousand people in one pursuit would truly be one. Brotherhood came by grace as safeguarding, ʿiṣma. Aim and aspiration united, and worldly concerns of the lower self, with furtive stinginess and avarice, were annihilated. Before that, objects of desire, munākum, held them captive, bound by the shackles of worldly concerns and whims, hawākum.

### In short

- Hold fast together to Hablillah, the cord of Allah, the Qur'an and His covenant, and do not divide, since division and sectarianism are forbidden (3:112, 6:153, 6:159, 64:16).
- Aws and Khazraj were saved from the brink of the Fire into brotherhood no earthly spending could have purchased (8:62-63, 19:96).
- The only centre that can unite all humanity is the revealed way of life itself, held by the elite as devotion to Book and Sunna (4:146, 22:78), and differences inside it are mercy only while they stay subsidiary and civil.

104.text:
Collective correction is organised: "Let there be a group among you who call ˹others˺ to goodness, encourage what is good, and forbid what is evil—it is they who will be successful". After taqwa and holding to the cord, the community must care affectionately for one another's correction through daʿwah. A dedicated segment is therefore required, although the duty itself reaches every Muslim according to ability.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Let there be a group among you who call ˹others˺ to goodness"**: Let there arise out of you a group of people inviting to all that is good, Islam, in the manner Allah commanded. This group's primary objective is its call towards good. A dedicated mission is therefore required to call people to the Qur'an and the Sunnah through word and deed, whenever people incline away from good or indulge in evils, according to ability. Ad-Dahhak said, "They are a special group of the Companions and a special group of those after them, that is those who perform Jihad and the scholars."

**"encourage what is good, and forbid what is evil"**: Al-Ma'ruf is what Islam orders and Al-Munkar what Islam forbids. Literally "recognised", Maʿruf covers all good promoted by prophets in their ages and known as good. Literally "non-recognised" or "alien," Munkar covers evils and disorders recognised as impermissible by the Holy Prophet's declaration.

**"it is they who will be successful"**: And it is they who are the successful, saved from Allah's wrath and punishment, with complete success in this world and the Afterlife.

### A collective obligation, and an individual duty

Min in minkum can be partitive. The commanded function is then fard kifaya, a collective duty, because an ignorant person cannot perform it competently. Min can also be extra, yielding the sense that the community as a whole should become a calling community. Either way, a segment of the Ummah must actually carry the task, while each member remains responsible in proportion to ability.

Muslim records Abu Hurayrah's report:

> "(Whoever among you witnesses an evil, let him change it with his hand. If he is unable, then let him change it with his tongue. If he is unable, then let him change it with his heart, and this is the weakest faith.)"

Another narration removes anything beyond that lowest point: "(There is no faith beyond that, not even the weight of a mustard seed.)" Imam Ahmad records Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman's warning that a community will enjoin righteousness and forbid evil or face a punishment from Allah, after which supplication will not be accepted. At-Tirmidhi collected it and called it Hasan.

The mission also sits inside collective well-being. First comes self-correction through taqwa and holding Allah's cord, then comes correction of others through da'wah and positive propagation. The whole community is addressed elsewhere: "You are the best Ummah raised for mankind. You bid the Fair and forbid the Unfair" (3:110).
