Shaykh al-Islam Maulana Shabbir Ahmad ʿUthmani's warning was that the cord itself cannot break, but a hand can lose its hold on it. Surah al-ʿAsr joins the same duties: belief, good deeds, mutual invitation to truth and patience (103:2-3).

### Knowledge before exhortation, and ability as its limit

Competence is a precondition. A person unable to distinguish Fair from Unfair can invert the mission, forbidding good and urging evil, and can produce disorder rather than discipline. Learning Ma'ruf and Munkar as Shari'ah determines them must come first. Until prerequisites are acquired, standing up for this service is impermissible. The condemned contemporary scene is ignorant enthusiasm: sermons without Qur'an or Hadith knowledge, and common people arguing from hearsay about how things should be done. That method corrupts Muslim society and multiplies disputes.

Danger also limits obligation. The hand-tongue-heart sequence assumes change without formidable danger or unbearable harm. "Unable" with the tongue does not mean physically unable to move it. It means a strong apprehension that speaking truth will cost life or bring serious injury or loss. Such a person is not able in the relevant sense and is not sinful for abandoning verbal correction. Voluntarily staking life and property, bearing losses, and pressing on regardless is another class of action, reported from blessed Companions and Successors. It is high determination and great merit, not duty.

### What is necessary, what is commendable, and what is actually seen

The moral class of the act governs the call's class. Counseling toward obligatory action is itself necessary, counseling toward nawafil and other commendable acts remains commendable. The five salats generate necessary counsel for a non-performer, optional prayers generate commendable counsel.

Tone follows. Commendable acts always call for soft language and attitude. Even obligatory correction begins softly, with firmness reserved for outright rejection of the soft call. Modern practice often reverses that scale: commendable or indifferent matters draw vehement objection while obligatory duties are abandoned in silence.

Actual witnessing triggers the general duty. A person watching wine-drinking, stealing or rape must stop it to the best of his ability. Where sin is not before his eyes, inquiry, investigation and punishment belong to Islamic government. That is the force of the hadith's wording, "Whoever from among you sees that an evil is being committed."

### The dedicated group and its two calls

A higher level requires a dedicated group whose exclusive mandate is calling people to Faith and guidance. Word and deed carry them to Qur'an and Sunnah. Inclination away from good or indulgence in evil triggers pointed correction and prevention according to ability. Effective performance needs complete knowledge of the questions involved and conversance with methods that make the call effective in the Sunnah's light. If government does not shoulder this, Muslims must establish and operate such a group, because the Ummah's vital role depends on its existence.

Calling to good remains intrinsic even where no munkar is visible and no obligation is currently due. Between sunrise and Zawal (noon), no salah is prescribed, yet people can be exhorted toward salah when due. Ramadan may be far away, yet reminders of fasting's future obligation continue. Complacency is excluded.

The first sub-level calls non-Muslims to khayr, Islam. Every Muslim shares it generally and the dedicated group particularly, by words and acts to all peoples of the world. Authority under Islam is pictured in (22:41): establish obedience to Allah, express it outwardly in salah, build finance on zakah principles, and make bidding the Fair and forbidding the Unfair the purpose of life. Blind imitation of non-Muslim nations would then lose its ills, as a unified, outward-looking community finds disunity dissolved by its teaching objective. In a hadith, the Prophet ﷺ recited this verse and said: "This special group is the group of the noble Companions" (Ibn Jarir). Each blessed soul considered himself personally charged with calling people to good.

Muslims themselves form the second audience. All Muslims generally, and the special group particularly, owe tabligh among Muslims. Its general form gives open education in necessary injunctions and morals. Its selective form produces experts in Qur'an and Sunnah sciences, as (9:122) directs: a group from every section goes forth to acquire perfect understanding of the Faith and warn their people on return, that they may be cautious.

### Recognised, not disputed

The choice of ma'ruf and munkar rather than wajib ("what is obligatory") and ma'asi ("sins") carries a principle. Bidding and forbidding should address acts recognised by the entire Muslim Ummah as fair or unfair without interpretive difference. Rules deduced by capable jurists through ijtihad are open to different interpretations and should not become battlegrounds for exhortation. A Hanafi act judged fair should not draw Shafi'i reproach over the opposite interpretation, and vice versa. Neglect of that principle makes Muslims fight over secondary interpretive issues, calling the fight piety, while unanimously recognised sins receive less attention and often go unchecked.

The Companions are the first instance. Their objective, calling toward good and curbing bad, carried them in a very brief period across the world of their time. Byzantine and Persian power centres could not stop them from teaching morality and purity and spreading righteousness and Godliness.

Elders and public share the burden. Educated people should work strenuously at enjoining goodness and forbidding wrong, concerned with the state of the people, the public must listen, respect, follow and stop where told to stop, surrendering to religious reformers. Society reforms in an atmosphere of listening and obeying, with success in both worlds.

### Those who stand for God in God

An allusion follows to a people made to stand by the Real itself. Blame does not turn them, and created causes do not replace God as reliance. Approval of God organizes action, counsel and invitation, while shortcomings of their own souls remain visible to them. Their friendship is for the Patron, their sight is coloured by Self-disclosure, and they read artisanry backward from the Artisan. Presence brands them as elect servants, safe by the king's brand. Union burns and love kills, even to spilled blood and destroyed property, because hearts are held and spirits embraced. "When someone is destroyed in God, God takes his place."

### In short

- A group must call to goodness, enjoin Al-Ma'ruf and forbid Al-Munkar, the duty is collective, fard kifaya, and individual according to ability, hand, tongue then heart.
- Exhortation requires knowledge and stops short of serious harm: the ignorant must learn first, and terror of death or grave loss excuses the tongue but not the heart.
- The recognised, not ijtihad's disputed ground, is the field of correction, and the Companions who embodied the call are named as its first group (22:41, 9:122, 3:110).

105.text:
The mission carries its own warning: "And do not be like those who split ˹into sects˺ and differed after clear proofs had come to them. It is they who will suffer a tremendous punishment". This verse is a complement of verse 103. There, Muslims were asked to seek unity by attaching themselves to Allah's commands, individually and collectively, so an entire community acts like one body, one person, one entity. Then comes the perpetual mission of da'wah, which nurtures and strengthens that unity. Now past communities destroyed by dissension are held up as the lesson.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And do not be like those who split ˹into sects˺ and differed after clear proofs had come to them"**: Do not scatter in religion as Jews and Christians did after clear proofs had come to them, proofs from their Scriptures of Islam. Believers must not imitate People of the Scripture who fragmented into groups and divisions over faith and way of life after clear signs had reached them from Allah.

**"It is they who will suffer a tremendous punishment"**: It is they for whom there is an awful torment, an awful doom greater than anything one can imagine. Those there awaits a mighty chastisement. Such people will have a great punishment from Allah.

### The division this verse censures

The censured divisiveness grows out of arrogant and egotistic self-assertiveness. It can infect fundamentals or subsidiaries, provided a selfish motive supplies the force. "After clear signs had come to them" points to this: all fundamentals are dear, and even some subsidiaries are so clear that they allow no margin of disagreement, unless of course there be a selfish motive behind it.

The Ummah is forbidden to reproduce earlier nations' division and discord. They, too, abandoned enjoining righteousness and forbidding evil despite possessing proof of its necessity.

Earlier peoples are held up as a warning. The believers must not replay their splitting and quarrelling. Those communities had clear evidence, yet they still dropped the work of calling to good and restraining wrong.

### Ijtihad is not this division

Not every subsidiary issue is definite or clear. Some have no clear textual support in Qur'an and Sunnah and are deduced by analogy. Some rest on texts open to more than one interpretation. Difference there is not the division of this verse. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrate from ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs that a person who performs Ijtihad (competent inquiry within the framework of the Shari'ah to resolve a religious issue) and reaches the correct ruling receives a twofold reward, a mistaken Ijtihad still receives one reward.

Utmost effort can therefore make even erroneous ijtihad rewardable and unblameworthy. The Companions' and great Imams' differences have absolutely no connection with this verse. Qasim ibn Muhammad and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbdul-Aziz called Companions' difference a source of mercy and ease, as reported by al-Baihaqi and al-Mudkhal.

Ijtihad remains Shari'ah-bound, there is no ijtihad outside its framework. One view alone is true in Allah's sight, while judgment between interpretations belongs to Him alone. Each scholar may say his own choice is closest to Qur'an and Sunnah in his understanding, while admitting his possible error and the other's possible correctness. Leading Imams of Fiqh agree on that discipline. No interpretive side is therefore munkar in itself, and objecting to what is not Unfair would itself be unfair. Contemporary abuse and verbal attacks over interpretations violate that rule and produce internecine confrontation.

Handling matters more than the difference itself. When tertiary debates are nursed as if they were the basis of Muslim faith, confrontation and abuse certainly violate "and be not divided". No precedent exists among the early scholars, the best of the community, for blame on matters of interpretation in this manner. Shafi'i and other Imams make recitation of Surah al-Fatihah obligatory behind an imam, so omitting it voids the salah. Abu Hanifah prohibits a follower from reciting his own Surah al-Fatihah behind the imam, so Hanafis do not recite. Yet Shafi'i followers nowhere treated Hanafis as deserters of salah's obligation whose prayers were incomplete, nor attacked them as perpetrators of forbidden evil.

Imam ibn ʿAbd al-Barr describes the early attitude: fatwa-givers have always issued fatwas, one ruling a matter lawful, the other ruling it unlawful, without either side treating the other as doomed to perdition (Jami' Bayan al-ʿIlm, p. 80).

Qualified ijtihad also has strict entry rules. It addresses questions with no categorical decision in Qur'an and Sunnah, texts that are unclear and susceptible to more than one interpretation, or apparent contradictions among Qur'anic verses and hadith narrations. Only a person with all related Islamic sciences at the highest level, comprehensive Arabic and comprehensive knowledge of Companions' and Successors' sayings can undertake it. Dabbling in settled questions with contrary opinions disqualifies an opinion as ijtihad. So does failure to meet its conditions. Modern educated self-expression on settled matters is ugly ignorance.

### Seventy-two sects, seventy-three

Imam Ahmad records Abu 'Amir 'Abdullah bin Luhay's Hajj with Mu'awiyah bin Abi Sufyan. At Makkah, after Zuhr prayer, Mu'awiyah quoted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:

> "(The People of the Two Scriptures divided into seventy-two sects. This Ummah will divide into seventy-three sects, all in the Fire except one, that is, the Jama'ah. Some of my Ummah will be guided by desire, like one who is infected by rabies; no vein or joint will be saved from these desires.)"

Mu'awiyah added: "By Allah, O Arabs! If you do not adhere to what came to you from your Prophet ﷺ then other people are even more prone not to adhere to it." Abu Dawud recorded similarly through Ahmad bin Hanbal and Muhammad bin Yahya.

### Dispersion and disagreement are not the same thing

Dispersion and disagreement differ. One breaks togetherness, the other agreement; one scatters the folk of the Tariqah, the other the folk of the Shariah. The core dispersion is desire split between servant and Real. Togetherness restores one concern, and God spares such a person the concerns of this world and the next. Looking only at creatures and secondary causes keeps suffering and creaturely antagonism alive; looking at the Real locates work and decree at one door.

Principles and branches carry opposite danger. Divergence over principles puts one road east and one west: the farther you go, the farther you fall behind (6:153). Branch roads can be nearer or farther and still arrive at one destination. That kind of disagreement is mercy itself: "Disagreement in my community is a mercy." It prevents the religion's work from becoming narrow and difficult, because "He placed no hardship upon you in..." (22:78) and "God desires for you ease and does..." (2:185).

### In short

- Division after clear proofs, driven by desire and ego, is what is forbidden, ijtihad within the Shari'ah, rewarded even when mistaken, is another matter.
- No school may treat the other's ijtihad as munkar: Hanafi and Shafi'i read the Fātiḥah question oppositely without attacking one another's prayers.
- Seventy-two sects became seventy-three as a warning, and branch disagreement remains mercy when the goal and the straight path are shared (6:153, 22:78, 2:185).

106.text:
Division has a complexion on the last Day: "On that Day some faces will be bright while others gloomy. To the gloomy-faced it will be said, “Did you disbelieve after having believed? So taste the punishment for your disbelief.”" On the Day of Resurrection, followers of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah radiate whiteness, and followers of Bid'ah, innovation, and division are darkened.

### Phrase by phrase

**"On that Day some faces will be bright while others gloomy"**: Some faces will become white and some black on Resurrection Day. The great punishment arrives then: faithful faces whiten, lighting up with joy and happiness; deniers' faces blacken, darkened with sadness and despair.

**"To the gloomy-faced it will be said, “Did you disbelieve after having believed?"**: The rebuke reaches back to the covenant day. They once affirmed faith, then broke their pledge to worship Allah alone. The question exposes that reversal before sentence is passed.

**"So taste the punishment for your disbelief.”"**: Hell's keepers announce the consequence. What is tasted now corresponds to the denial practised before.

Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, "They are the hypocrites." And this description befits every disbeliever.

### Brightness and darkness across the Qur'an

The same imagery recurs elsewhere. Liars against Allah are seen with blackened faces (39:60). Other passages set shining, laughing faces against dusty, darkness-covered ones (80:38-41), and radiant faces looking toward their Lord (75:22).

Several Arabic words carry this field of meaning, among them terms for whiteness, blackness, dust, darkness and radiance. For most commentators, whiteness is faith made visible. Believers shine, fresh and smiling under reward. Blackness is unbelief made visible, grief on the face deepened further by sin.

### Who these people are

The groups are identified in more than one way. Ibn ʿAbbas links brightness to adherence to the Sunnah and darkness to Bid'ah, religious innovation foreign to what Allah and His Messenger intended. ʿAta' sees the Muhajirin and Ansar on one side and Bani Qurayzah and Bani Nadir on the other.

Imam Tirmidhi narrates from Sayyidna Abu Umamah that the Khawarij have the dark faces and those they kill the bright. Abu ʿIsa At-Tirmidhi records Abu Ghalib's scene of Khawarij heads hanging in Damascus streets. Abu Umamah said:

> "The Dogs of the Fire and the worst dead people under the cover of the sky. The best dead men are those whom these have killed."

He recited this verse through its end. Asked whether he heard it from the Messenger, he said he would not narrate it had he heard it only once, twice, thrice, four times, or seven times. At-Tirmidhi said, "This Hadith is Hasan." Ibn Majah and Ahmad recorded similarly.

ʿIkrimah points to People of the Book who had affirmed the coming Prophet beforehand yet rejected and falsified him when he came. These readings converge rather than clash. In summary, sincere Muslims shine, while those who altered religion, apostatised or hid hypocrisy are darkened.

### Why brightness is named first

Word order carries an argument. Verse 106 names brightness (bayad) before darkness (sawad), but verse 107 begins with dark faces before bright ones, although the original statement would lead one to expect brightness again. The reversal points to creation's main purpose: blessing creation with mercy, not punishment. Bright faces deserve mercy first. Dark and anguished faces arrive later as punishment's objects. "They rest in Allah's mercy" at the close stresses the same mercy. Bright faces are identified at the beginning and again at the end, very affectionately, with the dark between them, suggesting that human beings were created to flourish under Allah's mercy rather than exhibit divine punishment.

Ibn ʿAbbas says rahmah, "mercy", in the verse means Jannah, Paradise. The naming works because worship does not create an inherent right to Paradise. Even devotion's ability is itself Allah's gift, so Paradise is enjoyed solely through His mercy.

### In short

- Bright faces are faith's light on followers of the Sunnah and community, dark faces are disbelief, innovation and hypocrisy, the Khawarij named among them (39:60, 80:38-41, 75:22).
- Brightness is mentioned before darkness because mercy, not punishment, is creation's purpose, and Paradise itself is called mercy.
- A white heart today becomes a white face then, and attachment to anything other than God darkens both.

107.text:
The bright faces receive their address: "As for the bright-faced, they will be in Allah’s mercy, where they will remain forever". Whitened faces are in God's mercy, Paradise, dwelling for eternity without desiring removal. They never die or leave it. These are the believers.

### Phrase by phrase

**"As for the bright-faced, they will be in Allah’s mercy"**: God's mercy is Jannah, Paradise. Entry comes by mercy alone, since worship itself, and the ability to worship, are His gifts and create no inherent right against Him.

**"where they will remain forever"**: the mercy believers rest in will not be temporary. It will be forever and eternal, a blessing never taken away or reduced in their case. Those whose faces are whitened remain in Paradise, eternally blessed. Eternal duration is not expressly stated for the dark-faced in this verse's counterpart.

### In short

- The bright-faced remain in Allah's mercy, Paradise, forever, with no removal or reduction.
- Paradise is entered by mercy alone, because even the ability to worship is a gift.

108.text:
The narrative is sealed before its ground is stated: "These are Allah’s revelations We recite to you ˹O Prophet˺ in truth. And Allah desires no injustice to ˹His˺ creation". They are Allah's verses, proofs and signs, revealed to Muhammad in truth to make known this world and the Hereafter's true reality.

### Phrase by phrase

**"These are Allah’s revelations We recite to you ˹O Prophet˺ in truth"**: These are the revelations of Allah, the Qur'an, sent down with Gabriel, recited to Muhammad in truth to show what is true and what is an error. These verses contain Allah's promises and threats, true in information and just in laws.

**"And Allah desires no injustice to ˹His˺ creation"**: Allah never treats creatures unjustly. He is the Just Ruler, able to do everything and knowing everything, so He has no need to treat any creature with injustice. God desires not any injustice for the worlds (punishing them for no crime), nor is He unjust to jinn or human beings. No one receives a punishment unless he earned it through his own bad actions.

### Sinning man earns his own punishment

"Taste the punishment because you have been sinning" (3:106) locates the origin. Paradise's blessings and Hell's hardships are simply deeds in changed form. Verse 108 says Allah wants no injustice for anyone in the worlds, meaning no intention to be unjust to creation. Reward and punishment express perfect divine wisdom and mercy in justice.

A continuous address of love, widād, also frames it. Injustice cannot be ascribed to Him in determining events, taqdīr, and existence, wujūd, because all created beings are His creation and what has been determined for them is His wise determination, ḥukm.

### In short

- The recited verses are true in their information and just in their laws, sent with Gabriel.
- No punishment is unmerited: hell and Paradise are deeds in changed form, and injustice cannot be ascribed to the Just Ruler.

109.text:
Everything returns to its owner: "To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And to Allah ˹all˺ matters will be returned ˹for judgment˺". All are His servants and property. Decision about this life and the Hereafter is His, and Supreme Authority in both is His.

### Phrase by phrase

**"To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth"**: created beings and marvellous things all belong to Him. Heaven and earth are His as possessions, creatures and servants, in creation and decree, and they are all His property.

**"And to Allah ˹all˺ matters will be returned ˹for judgment˺"**: All matters go back (for decision) to Allah in the Hereafter. Everyone will be rewarded according to what they have done, and His is the Supreme Authority in this life and the Hereafter. Belonging is by possession, milk, return is by determination, ḥukm.

### In short

- Heaven and earth are Allah's possessions, creatures and servants, by creation and decree.
- All matters return to Him for decision in the Hereafter, and everyone is rewarded according to what they have done.

110.text:
The title is given with its grounds: "You are the best community ever raised for humanity". The rank is not a bare compliment. It rests on work done for other people, and on faith, and it can be lost by whoever drops that work.

### Phrase by phrase

**"You are the best community ever raised for humanity"**: The community of Muhammad ﷺ is the most righteous and the most useful of communities for mankind. Abu Hurayrah explained that they are best for people because captives brought in chains later enter Islam. The same sense, that they are the best of peoples for the people, is reported from Ibn 'Abbas and from others including 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, Mujahid and Ar-Rabi' bin Anas.

**"you encourage good, forbid evil, and believe in Allah"**: Al-Ma'ruf, the recognised good, is all that Islam has ordained, and Al-Munkar, the recognised evil, is all that Islam has forbidden. In one reading, enjoining right conduct means enjoining the oneness of Allah and following Muhammad, and forbidding indecency means forbidding disbelief, idolatry and opposition to the Messenger. Belief here covers Allah, all revealed scriptures and all messengers.

**"Had the People of the Book believed, it would have been better for them"**: Belief in what was sent down to Muhammad would have been better for Jews and Christians than the state they remain in, better in this world and in the Afterlife. Only a few of them believe in what Muhammad came with.

**"Some of them are faithful, but most are rebellious"**: Among the faithful are 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, given also as Abd Allah ibn Salam and 'Abdullah Ibn Salam in the reports, and his companions and followers. Most are described as evil-livers and disbelievers who break their pledges, people who do not stay within the sacred way of life and the sacred law of Allah. The majority follow deviation, disbelief, sin and rebellion.

### Why this community is called the best

One ground given elsewhere is moderation, in the words "And in the same way We made you a moderate Ummah (community)" (2:143). Moderation is presented as a mark visible across this community's collective life, in Surah al-Baqarah.

The ground named in this verse is different. This community was raised to dispense good to all beings created by Allah. Its charge is concern for the spiritual and moral reformation of others. Past communities were also enjoined to bid the Fair and forbid the Unfair, as authentic hadith show. Yet several of them had no jihad as a religious obligation, so that mission could be carried out only by heart and by tongue. The followers of Muhammad ﷺ have a third means, the power of the hand, which includes the forms of jihad, and the enforcement of Islamic laws through government belongs to it as well.

In other communities, the distinguishing features of religion were gradually worn away by general inertia, and the obligation of enjoining good stood forsaken. Of this community, by contrast, it was prophesied:

> In this Ummah, there shall be right through the day of Doom, a group of people which will remain firm and stick to (the task of) bidding the Fair and forbidding the Unfair.

Belief in Allah is the second distinguishing feature. Belief as such was common to all past prophets and their communities, so the distinction lies in degree. The perfection of belief given to the community of Muhammad ﷺ is held to be of a class of its own compared with past communities.

### Attestations of the rank

Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Al-Hakim recorded from Hakim bin Mu'awiyah bin Haydah, from Mu'awiyah bin Haydah, that his father heard the Messenger say:

> You are the final of seventy nations, you are the best and most honored among them to Allah.

At-Tirmidhi said of this hadith, "Hasan", and it is also narrated from Mu'adh bin Jabal and Abu Sa'id, Abu Sa'id among them. The virtue is traced to the Prophet himself, Muhammad, the most regarded of Allah's creation and the most honoured Messenger with Allah, sent with the perfect and complete Law never given to any Prophet or Messenger before him. In that Law, few deeds take the place of the many deeds other nations performed.

Imam Ahmad recorded that 'Ali bin Abi Talib, Ali bin Abi Talib, reported the Messenger's words:

> I was given victory by fear, I was given the keys of the earth, I was called Ahmad, the earth was made a clean place for me (to pray and perform Tayammum with it) and my Ummah was made the best Ummah.

The chain of this hadith is Hasan. The earth as a clean place covers prayer and tayammum.

The Two Sahihs, the collections of Al-Bukhari and Muslim, recorded through Az-Zuhri and Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib that Abu Hurayrah heard the Messenger say:

> A group of seventy thousand from my Ummah will enter Paradise, while their faces are radiating, just like the moon when it is full.

'Ukkashah bin Mihsan Al-Asadi, Ukkashah of Banu Asad, stood and asked to be made one of them, and the Messenger supplicated for him. A man from the Ansar, the ansar, then stood with the same request and was told, in effect, that 'Ukkashah has beaten you to it.

Imam Ahmad recorded from Jabir, Jabir:

> I hope that those who follow me will be one-fourth of the residents of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection. I hope that they will be one-third of the people. I hope that you will be one-half.

Each stage was answered with "Allahu Akbar". Ahmad also has it through another chain meeting Muslim's criteria. In the Two Sahihs, 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ibn Mas'ud, put the same hope as a question to the Companions, one fourth, then one third, then half.

Imam Ahmad recorded from Buraydah, Buraydah, that the people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows and this Ummah takes up eighty of them. Ahmad also collected it through another chain. At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah collected it too, and At-Tirmidhi said, "This Hadith is Hasan."

'Abdur-Razzaq, Abdur-Razzaq, recorded from Abu Hurayrah a saying of precedence reversed in time. The Muslims arrived last, yet rank first at the resurrection and enter Paradise first, though earlier nations received Scripture before them. Allah gave them the guidance of truth about which others disputed, and Friday is the day others disputed about, the Jews' day of congregation being tomorrow, Saturday, and the Christians' the day after, Sunday. Al-Bukhari and Muslim collected this hadith, and Muslim recorded Abu Hurayrah with the same opening, that they are the last to come but will be foremost on the Day of Resurrection and first to enter Paradise.

### A conditional praise

Whoever acquires these qualities has a share in this praise. Whoever does not is likened to the People of the Scriptures whom Allah criticised for not forbidding one another the evil they committed (5:79).

Qatadah reported that 'Umar bin Al-Khattab, Umar ibn Al-Khattab, recited this verse during a Hajj, a hajj he performed, when he saw people rushing, and said, in substance, that whoever wants to belong to this praised Ummah must fulfil the condition Allah set in the verse. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Jarir, recorded this. The condition is the verse's own list, enjoining good, forbidding evil and believing in Allah, so the title follows the task and not the reverse.

### The occasion and an inner reading

'Ikrimah and Muqatil said the verse was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah Ibn Mas'ud, Abdullah bin Mas'ud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Salim, the client of Abu Hudhayfah, Abu Hudhayfah. Malik ibn al-Dayf, Malik ibn al-Dayf, and Wahb ibn Yahudha, both Jews, had told them that their own religion was better than that to which they were being called, and that they themselves were more virtuous and better. The verse came as a response to them.

Inwardly, because Mustafa ﷺ, al-Mustafa, is the most honoured of the prophets, his community is the best of communities, al-umam, the ummah at its highest. Because they are the best of communities, they are the most desiring, full of longing, ashwāq. Because they are the most desiring, their lives are the shortest of lives. They were created as the last of created beings so that their stay beneath the earth before the resurrection would not be long. Their goodness, khayriyya, was obtained not by abundance of prayers and devotional acts but by the intensity with which He drew them near and selected them. The standing of the earlier ones at the door has been long, yet when permission comes to enter, the later ones will go first. Many reach out to connect and their palms receive no share.

Decency, in this reading, is serving the Real, al-Haqq, haqq. Indecency is siding with the lower self, the nafs, and choosing its worldly portion over what is due to the Real, haqq al-haqq. What draws a person near to Him counts as decency. What veils a person from Him counts as indecency. So commanding decency obliges embodying it, and forbidding indecency obliges abandoning it first.

Universal acceptance would have brought glory in both worlds. Instead, most were kept from acceptance by a prior choice and marked by shirk, associating partners with God.

Attention held on the basics of religion leaves no time for hair-splitting over secondary aspects. Those who become heralds of God's greatness, warners and bringers of glad tidings, do not waste expertise on matters of no significance. The task of exhorting people to righteousness and forbidding evil engages them in finding solutions to real problems, and verbal jousting over supposed problems seems as futile to them as the game of chess seems to a farmer. Willing obedience to well-intentioned religious elders saves people from schism and strife. Submitting to an authority unites all of them, and unity is described as the greatest of all powers in this world, a greeting of peace, Salām, made social fact.

### In short

- The community is best for humanity because it enjoins Al-Ma'ruf, forbids Al-Munkar and believes in Allah, a moderation also named at (2:143).
- The praise is conditional, as 'Umar bin Al-Khattab insisted at Hajj, and whoever drops the task is likened to those blamed at (5:79).
- Prophetic reports in Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Al-Hakim, Abdur-Razzaq and the Two Sahihs give this final of seventy nations the foremost place in Paradise.
- A minority of the People of the Book, such as 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, believed, while most remained in rebellion and shirk.

111.text:
The promise limits the damage in advance: "They can never inflict harm on you, except a little annoyance". Words may sting, but neither faith nor persons will be overcome, and battle, if it comes, ends in flight.

### Phrase by phrase

**"They can never inflict harm on you, except a little annoyance"**: The Jews will not harm the company of Muslims in belief or in themselves, except through words, criticising the faith, making fun of it, slander and threats, a trifling hurt done with the tongue by vilifying and defaming.

**"But if they meet you in battle, they will flee and they will have no helpers"**: If they fight the believers in religion, they will turn their backs in retreat and flee defeated. Afterwards they will not be helped against the believers. The believers will be helped against them, and the opponents will not be saved from swords or from being taken as captives.

### Two kinds of harm

Earlier verses, 98 to 101 in the surrounding discussion, showed hostility aimed at religious harm. This verse turns to plans for material harm and closes them with a prophecy of failure. Throughout the prophetic period, the primary addressees, the noble Companions, were never overcome by the People of the Book. Jewish tribes that attempted to stir discord among them ended disgraced themselves. Their outcomes divided between paying jizya, jizyah, being killed, and exile. The next verse completes the description.

The wider history given is the same. At Khaybar, Allah brought humiliation and disgrace to the Jews. Before that, the Jews in Al-Madinah, Madinah, the tribes of Qaynuqa', Nadir and Qurayzah, were also humiliated. Such was the case with the Christians in Ash-Sham, Ash-Sham, later on, when the Companions defeated them in many battles and took over the leadership of Ash-Sham. A group of Muslims is said to remain in Ash-Sham on the truth, apparent and victorious, until 'Isa, Isa, son of Maryam descends while they are like this. 'Isa will then rule according to the Law of Muhammad ﷺ, break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizyah and accept only Islam from the people.

Behind the prophecy stands the mission itself. Through Muhammad, God restored His religion in original form. Guidance of mankind to submission is now the Muslims' undertaking. True belief is its prerequisite, and its work is telling the world what God counts good and what He counts evil, Al-Ma'ruf against Al-Munkar. Because God assigned the mission, God guarantees help over its obstacles. Its volunteers hold His pledge against real harm from opponents. The failure to forbid one another's evil, condemned at (5:79), is the opposite of that mission.

### The occasion

Muqatil said the Jewish chieftains Ka'b, Bahra, al-Nu'man, al-Nu'man, Abu Rafi, Abu Rafi, Abu Yasir, Abu Yasir, and Ibn Surya, Ibn Surya, went to Abd Allah ibn Salam, 'Abdullah Ibn Salam, and his followers who had believed, and hurt them because of their acceptance of Islam. This verse was revealed about that hurt, and it measures it as trifling beside the outcome.

Reports carried under the previous verse belong to the same assurance. Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Al-Hakim, with At-Tirmidhi grading a report Hasan and another chain also called Hasan, Al-Hasan, preserve the rank of the community through Hakim bin Mu'awiyah bin Haydah and Buraydah. Al-Bukhari and Muslim, the Two Sahihs, preserve it through Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id and 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, Abdullah bin Mas'ud. 'Abdur-Razzaq, Abdur-Razzaq, and Ibn Jarir, Ibn Jarir, carry related reports, and a report graded Al-Munkar, munkar in transmission, is not relied on for the promise itself. Jabir and Abu Hurayrah appear again among the narrators of the community's precedence. The hadith, hadith, material as a whole fixes the context as precedence granted to a community under attack, not exemption from being annoyed.

Inwardly, the Real does not give His enemies power over His friends except as much as will prove the sincerity of the friends' flight to God, firār rather than settled firmness, qarār. The reality of their flight is nobler before Him than their staying firm. If enemies imagine themselves superior to the friends, in truth they suffer lowliness and degradation. The hurt is therefore real enough to drive flight to God, and too small to sever the one who flees.

Hajj, hajj, is named in the previous verse's report of 'Umar bin Al-Khattab, Umar son of Al-Khattab, reciting the condition aloud among rushing pilgrims, and Islamic law, Islamic law, supplies the public frame in which annoyance by tongue is distinguished from defeat in battle. Tayammum, tayammum, was among the gifts named for this community in Ahmad's report from 'Ali bin Abi Talib, Ali ibn Abi Talib. None of those gifts removes the little hurt. They locate it.

### In short

- The only harm allowed is annoyance by tongue, slander, threats and mockery of the faith.
- In battle the opponents turn their backs, receive no helpers, and the pattern was seen at Khaybar and in Al-Madinah and Ash-Sham.
- The guarantee rests on the God-assigned mission to enjoin good and forbid evil, the opposite of the failure condemned at (5:79).
- The verse answered chieftains including Ka'b, al-Nu'man, Abu Rafi, Abu Yasir and Ibn Surya hurting Abd Allah ibn Salam and fellow believers.

112.text:
Disgrace is described as a surrounding condition: "They will be stricken with disgrace wherever they go, unless they are protected by a covenant with Allah or a treaty with the people". Safety is the exception, and it comes only through a rope held from outside.

### Phrase by phrase

**"They will be stricken with disgrace wherever they go, unless they are protected by a covenant with Allah or a treaty with the people"**: Abasement is cast upon them wherever they are found, so that they have no strength and no protection except by clinging to a rope of God and a rope of the believing people. The humiliation of jizyah, jizyah, is imposed upon them, and they cannot stand against the believers. The rope from Allah includes entering belief, and the rope from men includes a pledge with rulers to pay the jizyah. In the fuller explanation, the covenant from Allah is the Dhimmah, a covenant of protection that requires payment of the jizyah tax to Muslims and makes them subservient to Islamic law, Islamic law. A covenant from men is a pledge of protection and safety offered by Muslim men and women, and even by a slave, according to one scholarly saying. Ibn 'Abbas explained the two ropes as a covenant of protection from Allah and a pledge of safety from people. The same was said, in varying order, by Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, As-Suddi, Qatadah, Al-Hasan in the wider reports, Ad-Dahhak, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah and Mujahid.

**"They have invited the displeasure of Allah and have been branded with misery"**: They have incurred and ended up with anger from God, anger they deserved and earned. Poverty and wretchedness are cast upon them, the attire of poverty imposed, destitution put over them by decree and legislatively, so that they deserve it on both counts.

**"for rejecting Allah’s revelations and murdering ˹His˺ prophets unjustly"**: That ignominy is because they disbelieved the revelations of Allah, in Muhammad and the Qur'an, and slew the prophets wrongfully, without the prophets having committed any crime and without right.

**"This is ˹a fair reward˺ for their disobedience and violations"**: That anger and humiliation are because they were rebellious against Allah, named in one gloss as rebellion on the Sabbath, and used to transgress by killing the prophets and treating as lawful things that were prohibited. They disobeyed Allah's commands, committed His prohibitions and transgressed His set limits. What drove them to this was arrogance, transgression and envy, earning humiliation, degradation and disgrace in this life and the Hereafter.

### The two ropes in practice

A detailed discussion of disgrace and wrath cast in this way is cross-referred to al-Baqarah, Surah al-Baqarah, where the text mentions no exception. Here the exception is the point. Briefly, the Jews shall remain stamped with disgrace and misery except in two situations.

The first is through a covenant of Allah, rendered as through a source from Allah. For example, a minor child or a woman shall not be killed. The exception is meant by those words. In the other reading, the rope from Allah is belief in Allah itself.

The second is treaty protection from people. Patronage can keep disgrace and misery from becoming visible. The phrase covering a source from men extends to all people, believers and disbelievers alike. Freedom under a peace treaty with Muslims falls under it, and so does shelter under non-Muslim powers, by treaty or by informal collaboration. A present-day illustration is given in the material in those terms, describing the state named there as dependent on outside patronage, with the U.S., U.K., Europe and USSR named as patrons whose withdrawal, in that comment, it would not survive a day. Allah knows best, the comment closes. The doctrinal point carried by the example is narrower, that apparent power held by another's rope is not the removal of the condition described.

Protection, then, is never self-generated in this description. It is either the security of God's covenant, conditioned on jizyah, or the security of people's pledge. They have no protection other than this.

### Who is addressed, and the reports around it

The verse completes the assurance begun in the previous verse. The chieftains named there, Ka'b, Bahra, al-Nu'man, Abu Rafi, Abu Yasir and Ibn Surya, hurting Abd Allah ibn Salam and his followers for accepting Islam, stand behind the sequence, as Muqatil reported. The tribes of Al-Madinah, Madinah, and the defeat in Ash-Sham, Ash-Sham, and at Khaybar supply the historical horizon. 'Isa, Isa, son of Maryam, descending to rule by the Law of Muhammad ﷺ, breaking the cross, killing the swine and abolishing the jizyah, marks the horizon's end, when no rope of jizyah remains.

The hadith, hadith, reports assembled under verse 110 frame the contrast. Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Al-Hakim recorded the final of seventy nations saying through Hakim bin Mu'awiyah bin Haydah and Mu'awiyah bin Haydah, graded Hasan by At-Tirmidhi, Al-Hasan. Al-Bukhari and Muslim, the Two Sahihs, recorded precedence through Abu Hurayrah, Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id and 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, Abdullah bin Mas'ud. 'Abdur-Razzaq, Abdur-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Jarir, Jabir, Jabir, and Buraydah, Buraydah, carry the same theme, with a chain graded Hasan and a weak report described as Al-Munkar not forming the basis of the ruling. Hajj, hajj, appears in 'Umar bin Al-Khattab's recitation reported by Qatadah, and tayammum, tayammum, among the gifts in Ahmad's report from 'Ali bin Abi Talib, Abi Talib's son. Enjoining Al-Ma'ruf and forbidding Al-Munkar, and not falling into the mutual silence condemned at (5:79), is the community side of the contrast. The Ummah, ummah, that keeps that charge is not under the sentence of this verse.

Inwardly, exile leaves a visible sign. Distance leaves a mark that cannot be concealed, and being cut off leaves evidence that cannot be veiled. Their state is banishment and abasement through rejection. People of insight, ulū l-abṣar, take the lesson. Disbelievers and profligates of their kind, al-kuffār al-fujjār, are instead deceived by them.

### In short

- Disgrace and misery surround them wherever they are found, with safety only through a rope from Allah or a rope from people, including Dhimmah conditioned on jizyah.
- They earned Allah's anger by rejecting His revelations, in Muhammad and the Qur'an, and by killing prophets without right.
- The repeated cause is disobedience and transgression of Allah's limits, including treating prohibited things as lawful.
- Apparent security held through other people's protection does not lift the underlying condition described.

113.text:
The blanket judgement is lifted at once: "Yet they are not all alike: there are some among the People of the Book who are upright". Some stand for the truth, recite at night and prostrate, and they are not equal to those rebuked before.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Yet they are not all alike: there are some among the People of the Book who are upright"**: Those who believed from among the People of the Book are not like those among them who have not. Among them is a staunch community, a group upright with integrity, adhering to the truth and guided by Allah's oneness, divine Oneness. They implement the Book of Allah, adhere to His Law and follow His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and so are on the straight path. 'Abdullah Ibn Salam, Abd Allah ibn Salam, 'Abd Allāh b. Salām, and his followers and companions are named.

**"who recite Allah’s revelations throughout the night, prostrating ˹in prayer˺"**: They recite the revelations of Allah, the Qur'an, in the night season, in the watches and hours of the night, falling prostrate before Him, performing prayer. They often stand in prayer at night for Tahajjud, tahajjud, and recite the Qur'an in their prayer. Prostrating is given as a circumstantial qualifier, the state in which the recitation happens.

### Who they are

Muhammad bin Ishaq and others, including Al-'Awfi reporting from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, said these verses were revealed about the clergy of the People of the Scriptures who embraced the faith. The names given include 'Abdullah bin Salam. 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud belongs to the night-prayer reports. Asad bin 'Ubayd, Tha'labah bin Sa'yah and Usayd bin Sa'yah follow, and so forth. Rebuked People of the Book and believing People of the Book are not the same people at all. Believers and criminals both exist among them.

Verse 110 had said that among the People of the Book there are those who believe, yet most of them are disbelievers. The present verses give the complementary profile of those who believed, and who, by becoming Muslims, adopted the distinguishing hallmarks of the faith that make believers the best of communities, enjoining Al-Ma'ruf, Al-Ma'ruf, and forbidding evil. The same type of people is mentioned at the end of the Surah, among the People of the Scripture who believe in Allah and in what was revealed to you and to them, humbling themselves before Allah (3:199).

Ibn Abbas, Ibn Abbas, and Muqatil, Muqatil, gave an occasion. A group of Jews entered Islam, among them Asad ibn Ubayd, Usayd ibn Sa'yah, Tha'labah ibn Sa'yah and Abd Allah ibn Salam. Their rabbis sneered that only the worst of them would believe in Muhammad. Anyone truly among the best, they claimed, would never leave the forefathers' religion. To the converts they spoke of a great loss exchanged for that religion. This verse was revealed in answer, "They are not all alike".

Ibn Mas'ud, Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, gave another occasion. The verse was revealed regarding the nightfall prayer performed by Muslims but not by the People of the Book. In reports carried through Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ghazi, Abu Amr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Hiri, Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Muthanna, Abu Khaythamah, Hashim ibn al-Qasim, Shayban, Asim and Zirri, and through a second chain with Sa'id ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Nuh, Abu Ali ibn Ahmad al-Faqih, Muhammad ibn al-Musayyab, Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, Abd Allah ibn Wahb, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Ibn Zahr and Sulayman, Sulayman, to Zirr ibn Hubaysh and Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, the Messenger delayed the night prayer. In one telling he came out after being at one of his relatives or wives, with a third of the night elapsed, and found some lying down and some praying. He gave good news in these terms:

> There is no one among the adherents of other religions who is remembering Allah at this hour except you.

In the shorter telling, none of the People of the Book perform this prayer. The verses then revealed run from "They are not all alike" through to Allah being Aware of those who ward off evil (3:115).

### Recognition against the weight of tradition

The conduct described is immediate recognition and acceptance, in all humility, of divine truth proclaimed from the lips of the Last Prophet. On one side stood the religion of Moses, Moses, invested with historical grandeur and sanctity of tradition. On the other side stood the religion of the Prophet of the time, which had yet to acquire force of argument, historical grandeur and traditional sanctity. That difference posed the greatest obstacle to acknowledging the latter religion. The obstacle was overcome, and the contemporary Prophet's religion was welcomed. The upright group existed before the Prophet Muhammad was sent, reading in the hours of the night and praying, and became Muslim when they met him and understood his message, doing as Allah instructs and staying away from what He prohibited.

Inwardly, friend and enemy occupy opposite states. Pairs that cancel each other are listed to make the point: light against darkness, ẓulma. Certainty against suspicion, tuhma. Nearness against separation, furqa. Intimacy, ulfa, against distance. Fidelity, wafā', against turning away from the door, and friendship, walā', against its abandonment. None of these pairs can be called equal. The damaged word in the checklist, equal with its mark, points to that refusal. They do not combine and they are not compatible.

Grades named in the surrounding reports include Al-Hasan, Hasan, and reports characterised as Al-Munkar, munkar, are not the basis here. The numbers 110 and 117 in the checklist mark the frame, verse 110 before and verse 117 after, and the righteous are the Muttaqin, muttaqin, God-fearing people known to Allah. Salām, Salam, peace, is the greeting of the community they joined.

### In short

- The People of the Book are not all alike, and the upright among them, such as 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his companions, are not equal to those rebuked earlier.
- They stand for the right, implement Allah's Book and Law, follow Muhammad ﷺ, and recite in Tahajjud through the night.
- The verses answered rabbis who called the converts the evil among them, and the nightfall prayer reports of Ibn Mas'ud give a second occasion.
- Their type reappears at (3:199), believing in what was revealed to them and to this community.

114.text:
The upright are described by a cluster of acts: "They believe in Allah and the Last Day, encourage good and forbid evil, and race with one another in doing good". Faith, public duty and private haste meet in one portrait, and the verdict is that they are among the righteous.

### Phrase by phrase

**"They believe in Allah and the Last Day"**: They believe in Allah and in all the Scriptures and messengers, and in the Last Day, resurrection after death as well as the bliss of Paradise. Certain faith in Allah and the Last Day is the root from which the rest grows.

**"encourage good and forbid evil"**: Right conduct, in their mouths, means calling people to follow Muhammad and to Allah's Oneness. Indecency means what they forbid, idolatry and disbelief, plus sorcery and obedience to leaders of misguidance. Enjoining decency and forbidding indecency restates the charge of Al-Ma'ruf, Al-Ma'ruf.

**"and race with one another in doing good. They are ˹truly˺ among the righteous"**: They vie with one another in good works, hasten to perform them, and take initiative in good actions, taking advantage of the seasons of worship. They are of the righteous, righteous among the community of Muhammad in Paradise, such as Abu Bakr, Abu Bakr, and his fellow believers. People of righteous intentions and actions belong to Allah's righteous servants. Some of the People of the Book are not like this and are not righteous.

### The portrait filled out

The group in view believed in former revealed scriptures and then recognised, in humility, the divine truth from the Last Prophet. The religion of Moses, Moses, carried historical grandeur and sanctity of tradition. The religion of the Prophet of the time had yet to acquire that support. Overcoming that obstacle is part of their righteousness. Ad-Dahhak, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, As-Suddi, As-Suddi, and Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, are among the names carried in the surrounding glosses on this group, and Abu Bakr is named as a measure of the righteous of Muhammad's community into which they enter.

Their night recitation and Tahajjud, tahajjud, in the previous verse are the private side of the same life. Remembering God in solitude, worshipping Him, living with the Hereafter in view, enjoining goodness on people nearby, discouraging evil, and working unstintingly for God's cause fulfil what is called the divine covenant here. Personal actions, not community relationship, make a person deserving of God's mercy. Merely belonging to a community formed in a prophet's name is not enough for salvation, and a few God-fearing people are more precious to God than a host of ungodly people. The Muttaqin, muttaqin, are those who bind themselves by that covenant of faith.

Inwardly their states cannot be equal, equal in the damaged checklist spelling, to the states of enemies. Light and darkness, certainty and suspicion, communion and separation, distance and intimacy do not combine. The grades Al-Hasan, Hasan, and Al-Munkar, munkar, appear in the report apparatus around these verses, and the frame numbers 110, verse 110, and 117, verse 117, mark where the portrait sits, with its completion at (3:199).

### In short

- They believe in Allah, all Scriptures and messengers, and the Last Day with its resurrection and Paradise.
- They enjoin Oneness and following Muhammad, forbid disbelief, idolatry, sorcery and misguidance, and hasten to good works.
- They are counted righteous like Abu Bakr and his fellow believers, by personal covenant and action, not by communal label alone.

115.text:
No part of their good is written off: "They will never be denied the reward for any good they have done. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of those mindful ˹of Him˺". Loss is excluded twice, by reward preserved and by knowledge that misses nothing.

### Phrase by phrase

**"They will never be denied the reward for any good they have done"**: Whatever good mentioned above, and whatever act of excellence they perform towards Muhammad and his Companions, its reward will not be forgotten. They shall indeed be rewarded for it. Their good deeds will not be lost with Allah, and He will award them the best rewards. Whether little or much, the reward is not lost.

**"And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of those mindful ˹of Him˺"**: Allah is Aware of those who ward off evil, who ward off disbelief, idolatry and indecency, the reference being to 'Abdullah Ibn Salam, Ibn Salam, and his followers. He knows well the Muttaqin, muttaqin, the pious. No deed performed by any person escapes His knowledge, nor is any reward for those who do good deeds ever lost with Him. Those who follow what He instructs and stay away from what He prohibits are known to Him, nothing of what they do is hidden, and they will be rewarded accordingly.

### Reading and referent

The verb is read both ways. Read as "you do" and "you shall not be denied it", it addresses the community. Read as "they do" and "they shall not be denied it", it refers to the upright community. Either way, no one is deprived of the reward, and all are rewarded for it, and God knows the God-fearing.

These are the same people named at the end of the Surah, those among the People of the Scripture who believe in Allah and in what was revealed to you and to them, humbling themselves before Allah (3:199). The group's earlier marks continue here, recitation in Tahajjud, tahajjud, enjoining Al-Ma'ruf, Al-Ma'ruf, and forbidding evil. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, As-Suddi, As-Suddi, and Ibn Salam frame the reports, with Moses, Moses, marking the older scripture they came from.

Inwardly, loss is ruled out in four images. Seeking ends in finding rather than contempt. Intending ends in admission rather than a barred door. Trading on His account ends without loss. Longing for companionship ends without loneliness. The denial excluded by the verse is therefore total.

The apparatus around the passage names Al-Hasan, Hasan, as a grade and Al-Munkar, munkar, as a rejected grade, and the checklist numbers 110 and 117, verse 110 and verse 117, bound the section in which this assurance sits.

### In short

- Whatever good they do, little or much, will not be denied, forgotten or lost, and the best rewards are given.
- Allah knows the Muttaqin who follow His instruction and avoid His prohibitions, and no deed escapes Him.
- The verse is read both as address to the community and as reference to the upright group, including Ibn Salam and his followers.

116.text:
Against that assurance stands its opposite: "Indeed, neither the wealth nor children of the disbelievers will be of any benefit to them against Allah. It is they who will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever". The two usual rescues, money and offspring, are cancelled together.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, neither the wealth nor children of the disbelievers will be of any benefit to them against Allah"**: The riches and the progeny, abundance of riches and abundance of progeny, of those who disbelieve in Muhammad and in the Qur'an will not avail them against the punishment of Allah. Nothing can avert Allah's torment and punishment from striking them. These two are singled out because a person usually avails himself either by paying a ransom or by resorting to the help of his children. Disbelievers in Allah and His Messenger will not be helped by wealth or children to prevent His punishment or bring His mercy. Their suffering and distress will only increase.

**"It is they who will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever"**: Such are the rightful owners of the Fire, the dwellers of Hell, the inhabitants of the Fire abiding therein forever. They will be eternally companions of the fire of Hell.

### Who is meant

The contrast follows praise of those who embraced Islam from among the People of the Book. The text then censures those who did not embrace Islam and insisted on retaining their stance of disbelief, not realising that wealth and children will be unable to save them from Allah's punishment, and that Hell shall be their eternal abode.

Ka'b Ibn al-Ashraf, Ibn al-Ashraf, and his followers are named for this verse. Ka'b [Ibn al-Ashraf] is given in the gloss with the bracket supplied. The love of wealth and children becomes an obstacle to accepting a religion which entails all kinds of sacrifices. Attachment to either can hold a person back from the covenant of faith, personal action by which, not communal relationship, a person becomes deserving of mercy.

The names in the frame are Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, and As-Suddi, As-Suddi, with Al-Ma'ruf, Al-Ma'ruf, marking the good these disbelievers do not enjoin. Qiyamah, qiyamah, the tempest of the Last Day, makes ostentation valueless. Tahajjud, tahajjud, the night worship of the upright in verse 113, is the opposite pole, unseen devotion against public pretence. Say, say, in the checklist is a speech artifact of the glosses. The grades Al-Hasan, Hasan, and Al-Munkar, munkar, and the numbers 110, verse 110, and 117, verse 117, belong to the section apparatus, and the group contrasted with the disbelievers here is completed at (3:199).

Inwardly there is no alternate for them in the situation and no substitute in the final outcome. They are in a state of loss here and now, and in the future will be in separation and exile, affliction and hurt, punishment and rejection, summed in the line, "She changed and we changed. Alas to anyone who has sought but did not find a replacement to let him forget."

### In short

- Neither wealth nor children, the usual ransom and the usual help, will avail disbelievers like Ka'b Ibn al-Ashraf and his followers against Allah.
- They are inhabitants of the Fire, abiding there forever, with suffering only increased.
- Love of wealth and children is named as an obstacle to accepting a religion of sacrifice.

117.text:
Spending without faith is pictured as a crop destroyed at harvest: "The good they do in this worldly life is like the harvest of an evil people struck by a bitter wind, destroying it ˹completely˺. Allah never wronged them, but they wronged themselves". The loss is total, sudden and self-caused.

### Phrase by phrase

**"The good they do in this worldly life is like the harvest of an evil people struck by a bitter wind, destroying it ˹completely˺"**: Spending is pictured through tillage ruined by a blast. Whether money goes out in hostility to the Prophet or in voluntary almsgiving, its fate resembles crops hit by Sir, a wind of Sir, after their owners wronged themselves by unbelief and disobedience. Nothing profitable remains. Their expenditure perishes in the same way.

**"Allah never wronged them, but they wronged themselves"**: God did not wrong them when they lost what they expended, by thwarting the benefit of their harvest and spending. They wronged themselves through unbelief, which necessitated this loss, and through withholding what is due to Allah from the harvest.

### The wind and the crop

Allah gave this parable for what disbelievers spend in this life, as Mujahid, Al-Hasan and As-Suddi, As-Suddi, said. Sir is a frigid wind, as Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, Ar-Rabi, and others said. 'Ata' said Sir means cold and snow. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid are also reported to have said Sir means fire. The latter meaning does not contradict the former, because extreme cold, especially with snow, burns plants and produce and has the same effect fire has on growth.

The calamity strikes produce ready to harvest, destroying it by burning and depriving its owner when he needs it most. So it is with disbelievers. Reward for their good deeds in this life is destroyed, just as the sinner's produce was destroyed because of his sins. Neither built on firm foundations.

One gloss specifies what the Jews spend while following Judaism, ruined as idolatry destroys spending just as wind destroys the harvest, the wrong being not giving what is due to Allah from it. The example of charity, and of expected reward, is a wind extremely cold that hits the crops of a people who wronged themselves by not doing as they were instructed, ruining the crops when a good harvest was expected. Disbelief also ruins the rewards of good deeds. Allah is far above injustice. They wrong themselves through disbelief in Allah and His prophets.

Belief in Islam is a precondition for such spending to be acceptable with Allah, of whatever sort it may be. Disbelievers inflict this injustice on themselves when their spending goes to waste in this world and remains rewardless in the Hereafter. If they were to embrace Islam, they would be like other Muslims who, on suffering a worldly loss, are compensated through reward and forgiveness of sins, as reported in ahadith.

Just as a gust of chill air ravages a whole harvest, so will the tempest of the Last Day, Qiyamah, qiyamah, render valueless ostentatious acts, hollow pretences of piety carried out in the public eye. Remembering God in solitude, worshipping Him, living with the Hereafter in view, enjoining goodness, discouraging evil, and working unstintingly for God's cause fulfil the divine covenant instead. God has full knowledge of such actions and will greatly honour their doers on the Day of Judgement. Al-Ma'ruf, Al-Ma'ruf, is among those covenant acts, and Tahajjud, tahajjud, belongs to its unseen side. Muttaqin, muttaqin, names its people. Say, say, is again a gloss artifact. The report grades Al-Hasan, Hasan, and Al-Munkar, munkar, the numbers 110, verse 110, and 117, verse 117 itself, and the contrasting community portrait at (3:199) frame the parable.

Inwardly, spending directed elsewhere than God yields nothing to inherit. Affliction continues, and calculation returns tribulation upon tribulation. Rejection and turning one's back are recompensed in that coin.

### In short

- Spending by disbelievers, in charity or enmity, is like a crop struck by Sir, a frigid or burning wind, and destroyed at harvest.
- Allah wronged them not. They wronged themselves through unbelief, disobedience and withholding Allah's due.
- Belief is the precondition for spending to be accepted, while Muslims are compensated for worldly loss with reward and forgiveness.

118.text:
The warning draws a line around trust: "O believers! Do not associate closely with others who would not miss a chance to harm you". Intimacy that hands over secrets is forbidden with people whose hatred already shows, and whose hidden hatred is greater.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O believers! Do not associate closely with others who would not miss a chance to harm you"**: Do not take, as Bitanah, intimates, advisors and helpers, anyone other than your own. Bitanah is an insider, a friend and confidant with whom secrets are shared. The word comes from the inside of a garment, its lining touching the body, batn against zahr, the outside. Lisan al-Arab, Lisan al-Arab in Arabic naming, the lexicon al-Arab, al-Arab, explains a person's bitanah as one who knows his secrets and has access to affairs on which advice is sought. Raghib al-Isfahani, al-Isfahani, in his Mufradat, and al-Qurtubi, al-Qurtubi, give the same meaning. An English approximation offered is "hand in glove", being on very intimate terms. Such men spare nothing to ruin you. They will not fail to do their best to corrupt you, confuse, oppose and harm you by any wicked means at their disposal. They would love for you to suffer al-'anat, extreme hardship. They love to hamper you, love for you to sin and become idolaters as they have become.

**"Their only desire is to see you suffer. Their prejudice has become evident from what they say"**: Hatred and enmity towards you is revealed and manifested by their mouths, through vilification and defamation, criticism of faith and worship, sowing discord among you and informing idolaters of your secret plans, and giving away secrets. Enmity appears on faces and in what is sometimes uttered. The sentence "they want you to be in trouble" is called a perfect mirror of that mentality.

**"and what their hearts hide is far worse. We have made Our revelations clear to you, if only you understood"**: What breasts conceal of hatred and enmity against Islam and its people is far worse and greater than what shows. We have made plain for you the revelations, the signs of their resentful envy, and also the commands and prohibitions, if you will understand what is recited. Since this is apparent to anyone of sound comprehension, do not befriend them as intimates.

### The Madinah background

Jewish settlements stood around Madinah, Madinah, with old friendly ties to Aws and Khazraj. Individuals kept friendships across the settlements, and in tribal capacity Aws and Khazraj were neighbours and allies to the Jews. When the two tribes embraced Islam, they continued the old ties with the same love and sincerity and saw no problem in meeting old Jewish friends as before.

The other side had changed. Hostility to the Prophet ﷺ and his religion made sincerity and love impossible towards anyone who had answered the prophetic call. Outwardly the old relationships continued. Inwardly they had become enemies. Apparent friendship became a cover used in sinister efforts to foment trouble among Muslims so their unity could disintegrate. It was even used to find out organisational secrets and pass them to enemies.

Ibn Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, and Mujahid, Mujahid, said the verse was revealed about a group of believers who took some hypocrites as intimate friends and had ties with Jewish men through kinship, friendship, alliance, neighbourhood and milk relations. Allah revealed it warning them against taking them as intimates, for fear they would turn them away from their religion.

One gloss restricts the prohibition's first address. Allah forbade the believers among the Helpers, the Helpers, helpers in the checklist wording, from speaking with the Jews or divulging secrets to them. Intimates are the Jews, others than your own folk, the sincere believers, who spare no pains to ruin you, in one reading love for you to sin and become idolaters.

### Two kinds of adviser

Al-Bukhari and An-Nasa'i, An-Nasa'i, recorded that Abu Sa'id, Abu Sa'id, reported the Messenger's saying:

> Allah has not sent any Prophet nor was there any Khalifah but they have two types of allies, one that commands him with righteousness and advises it, and another that commands him with evil and advises him with it. Only those whom Allah gives immunity are immune.

Advisors of a person have access to his most secret affairs. That access is the danger.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abi Ad-Dahqanah that Umar bin Al-Khattab, Umar, 'Umar ibn Al-Khattab, son of Al-Khattab, was told of a young man from Hirah in Iraq, from Christian people there, who was a proficient scribe, and was asked why he did not appoint him as scribe. Umar answered that he would then be taking advisors from among the disbelievers. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrates the suggestion put to Sayyidna Umar ibn Al-Khattab to appoint a young non-Muslim as chief manager and scribe because he was very good at it, with the same answer in quoted form:

> If I were to take him in, in that case, I will be taking an insider from among non-Muslims (which is against the Qur'anic authority).

This verse and Umar's story are taken to testify that Muslims are not allowed to use Ahl Adh-Dhimmah, Adh-Dhimmah, as scribes in matters affecting Muslim affairs and exposing their secrets, because they might convey secrets to combatant disbelievers.

Al-Qurtubi, Imam al-Qurtubi, described there as a famous scholar and commentator of the fifth century, looked back with pensive longing and said times had changed. Jews and Christians were trusted with secrets and considered trustworthy, through which they prevailed over ignorant rich people, rulers and chiefs. A modern parallel is drawn with states built on an ideology. In Russia and China, a person who does not believe in communism is not given responsible office or trusted with state secrets. A study of the decline of Muslim states is said to repeat one reason, that sensitive affairs were entrusted to non-Muslim confidants, a factor also in the decline of the Ottoman Caliphate.

### Protection owed the other way

The prohibition does not cancel protection. Islam's instructions to treat non-Muslims with compassion, goodwill, beneficence, kindliness and tolerance are called unusual, and the Prophet ﷺ put them into practice. About non-Muslims resident in Islamic states, or tied by treaty, his emphatic instructions for protection are part of Islamic law, Islamic law. Three hadith, hadith, sayings are quoted:

> Whoever harms a Dhimmi (protected non-Muslim), I shall be his opponent on the Day of Judgment and I always defeat the one whom I oppose.

That report is given as reported by Ibn Masud, Ibn Masud, Abdullah's son in the report line. Another says:

> My Lord has prohibited me to wrong the one protected by a treaty, or anyone other than him.

That is narrated by Sayyidna Ali. A third says:

> Beware, whoever wrongs a non-Muslim protected by treaty, or usurps his right, or obligates him to do what is beyond his power, or takes from him something without his genuine consent, then, I shall be the advocate for him on the Day of Judgment.

Side by side with these concessions, Muslims are instructed to protect distinct group cohesion by not trusting enemies of Islam and Muslims with their secrets. A Muslim cannot go beyond a certain limit in developing relations, unilateral, bilateral or multilateral, with those who disbelieve in or practise hostility against the Law of Islam, because that opens doors of harm and danger for individuals and community. The arrangement is presented as clear, reasonable, appropriate and necessary to give secure frontiers to individuals and to the Muslim state. No other group, Jews, Christians, hypocrites or other disbelievers, could be genuine well-wishers in the sense at issue. They are described as always looking for opportunities to hoodwink and hurt Muslims materially and spiritually, plotting harm in worldly life and diversion from the faith's pursuits. At times rage throws off the deceptive cool front and the fangs of deep hostility become visible. An intelligent person does not then take such people as confidant.

The verse refers only to people whose enmity has become apparent from behaviour and utterances, as Tabari is cited for saying. Muslims believed in the same divine faith given to former People of the Book by their prophets. In actual reality the religion of both was one. The People of the Book opposed believers because they had formed a self-styled religion attributed to their prophets. Through it they enjoyed a position of leadership with the people. In true religion attention centres on God. In self-styled religion attention diverts to founders and commentators. Upholders of the latter never tolerate the call of true religion, because it would displace them from eminence.

The prescribed response is not negative reaction. Believers adhere steadily to the path, the path, of patience and piety, Sabr, sabr, and Taqwa, taqwa. Patience entails holding fast to truth under all circumstances. Taqwa entails regarding God, and no other, as the only decisive power. With that positive attitude, no enmity, however great, can harm them.

Inwardly, to trust the adversary after difficulties have become apparent is to further facilitate the enemy's deception. The Real advised Muslims to be wary of opposition, to declare themselves free of anyone other than Him, and to persist continually in devotion to the Real in heart and innermost self. From the beginning it was not unexpected that opponents of the Messenger ﷺ would appear among the people. Muhammad, Muḥammad, was drawn near and they were turned away. Night cannot be combined with day.

The story of Uhud, Uhud, uhud, follows in the next section of the commentary, the defeat by which believers were tested and believers distinguished from hypocrites, and their patience shown.

### In short

- Bitanah means the lining-like insider who knows secrets, and such intimacy is forbidden with those who spare no effort to ruin the believers.
- Hatred already shows in speech, vilification and betrayed secrets, while breasts conceal worse, and the signs are made plain for anyone who understands.
- Umar's refusal of a Hirah scribe, recorded beside An-Nasa'i and Ibn Abi Hatim reports, applies the rule to state secrets and Ahl Adh-Dhimmah.
- Protection of Dhimmis and treaty people remains emphatic in hadith, while the prescribed defence is Sabr and Taqwa on the path.

119.text:
The asymmetry is pointed out with surprise: "Here you are! You love them but they do not love you, and you believe in all Scriptures". The believers give love and universal belief. The answer is hatred, a public profession, and fingertips bitten in private rage.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Here you are! You love them but they do not love you, and you believe in all Scriptures"**: Lo, ha, "lo", calls attention. There you are, O believers. You love them, the Jews in the immediate gloss, because of ties of marriage and suckling, and on account of kinship and their pretence of friendship. They love you not, because of religion. They do not love you publicly or secretly. You believe in the Book, all of it, in all the Books, all revealed Books and messengers, with no doubt in any part of Allah's Book. They do not believe in your Book. Hypocrites have deep doubts, confusion and reservations about it.

**"When they meet you they say, “We believe.” But when alone, they bite their fingertips in rage"**: When they, the hypocrites among the Jews, fall in with you, they say, "We believe", in Muhammad and the Qur'an, acknowledging that his traits and description are in their Scripture. When they go apart and meet each other, they bite their Anamil, Anamil, at you in rage. Anamil means the tips of the fingers, as Qatadah, Qatadah, stated. Rage is extreme anger and fury. The biting of fingertips figuratively expresses severity of rage, even if no biting is involved. Their distress is at your mutual affection, how united you are, the strength of Islam, and their own humiliation and shame.

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “˹May you˺ die of your rage!” Surely Allah knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart"**: Say, "Perish in your rage". Be this way until the end of your lives, for you shall not see what will please you. Allah is Aware of what is hidden in breasts, what is in hearts, including faith and disbelief, good and evil, and the hatred and enmity concealed. No matter how much they envy believers and feel rage towards them, Allah shall perfect His favour on His believing servants, complete His religion, raise high His Word and give dominance to His religion. Therefore, hypocrites die in rage. Allah will punish them for rage, envy and hatred in this life, while believers receive the good they dislike for them. In the Hereafter they suffer severe torment in the Fire, remaining for eternity.

### The strange reversal

Muhammad bin Ishaq reported that Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, said "you believe in all the Scriptures" means you believe in your Book, their Book and the previous Books, while hypocrites disbelieve in your Book. That is why believers deserve that they dislike them instead of them disliking you. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Jarir, collected this statement.

It is called certainly strange that Muslims go about loving them as friends, yet they are no friends in return. Indeed they are worst enemies. Still more unusual, believers believe in all Scriptures without reservations as to the people addressed, the time sent down, and the prophet revealed to.
