The others do not accept your Book and your Prophet ﷺ. Their belief in their own Books is not correct either. Expected affection would run the other way. They should have been affectionate towards you, and you the ones to give them a cold shoulder. What happens is just the reverse.

The hypocrite pattern is exact pretence. With believers they pretend to be believers and kind. In every respect they conceal the opposite. To contemporary Jews or Christians the verse is applied in the short gloss, eight words in that block.

Two types of ally stand behind the warning. Al-Bukhari and An-Nasa'i, An-Nasa'i, recorded from Abu Sa'id, Abu Sa'id, that every Prophet and every Khalifah has allies commanding righteousness and allies commanding evil, and only those Allah gives immunity are immune. Umar, Umar son of Al-Khattab, Al-Khattab, refused a proficient Hirah scribe lest he take advisors from disbelievers. Ahl Adh-Dhimmah, Adh-Dhimmah, are protected in rights, yet not made keepers of Muslim secrets. Helpers, helpers, in the Helper sense belong to Madinah, and the Uhud, Uhud, uhud, context follows, where pretence and loyalty were separated.

Faithful hearts explain the believers' side inwardly. They had limpid hearts and generous natures and did not keep tenderness and mercy back from the estranged. They wanted good for them, attached hearts to their submission, wanted their salvation, and did not hold back God's mercy from acquaintances or strangers. A saying kept crossing their minds, "Bring the sweetmeat, for it is the heart's beloved, suited for both the elect and the common." This is the tenderness Muhammad, MuḤammad and Muḥammad, showed to the estranged, saying:

> O God, guide my people, for they do not know.

Unbelievers had no limpidness in hearts or loyalty in natures. They never wanted good for people of faith, nor loved them. They grieved at good reaching them and became happy at bad, a pattern stated in (3:120) in the words "If something beautiful touches you, it vexes" them. Everyone does what is fitting for him, for "The pot pours what is inside it." Faith is generous and lovingly kind, fitting generosity and chivalry. Unbelief is base and ill-wanting, fitting baseness and unseemliness. The person of faith calls God's creatures to salvation and deliverance. The unbeliever calls them to the Fire and captivity. The summons "O my people! What is it with" me, calling you to deliverance while you call me to the Fire, is cited at (40:41).

### In short

- Believers love them for kinship, marriage and suckling ties and pretended friendship, while they return no love because of religion.
- Believers accept all Books and messengers without doubt, while the others reject the believers' Book, so the expected affection is reversed.
- In company they say "We believe", alone they bite their Anamil in rage at unity and strength, and are told to perish in that rage.
- Allah knows what breasts conceal, will perfect His favour to believers, and reserves severe eternal torment for concealed hatred.

120.text:
The final diagnosis makes their reaction predictable: "When you ˹believers˺ are touched with good, they grieve; but when you are afflicted with evil, they rejoice". Against that fixed enmity one remedy is prescribed, patience and God-consciousness, with a guarantee that plotting will not harm at all.

### Phrase by phrase

**"When you ˹believers˺ are touched with good, they grieve; but when you are afflicted with evil, they rejoice"**: If a good befalls you, a favour such as victory or booty, a lucky chance of conquest and booty, fertility, support, increase in numbers, wealth or children, it grieves them and is evil unto them. Jews and hypocrites do not like it, and worry and sadness overcome them. If evil overtakes you, disaster of drought, killing and defeat, decrease in wealth or children, or an enemy's victory, they rejoice at it and are happy. The conditional is semantically connected across the parenthetical reminder, and the meaning pressed is that enmity is endless, so why befriend them. Avoid them.

**"if you are patient and mindful ˹of Allah˺, their schemes will not harm you in the least"**: If you remain patient and have Taqwa, taqwa, if you persevere in the face of their harm and keep from evil, transgressing against Allah, and if you endure their harm and fear God by not befriending them, their cunning, guile, enmity and deeds will not hurt you at all. Readings are given as lā yadirkum or lā yadurrukum. Allah directs believers to safety from the wickedness of evil people and the plots of sinners by reverting to patience, fear of Allah and trust in Him. Patient with Allah's commands and decree, and mindful of not earning Allah's anger, they are untouched by tricks and attempts to hurt.

**"Surely Allah is Fully Aware of what they do"**: Allah surrounds and encompasses all that they do, of contravention, enmity and plotting. He has knowledge of it and will requite them for it, and will make them fail. A reading ya'malūn, what they do, and a reading ta'malūn, what you do, are both noted. Allah encompasses the enemies while believers have no power or strength except from Him. Whatever Allah wills occurs. Whatever He does not will does not occur. Nothing happens in His Kingdom except by His decision and decrees. Whoever relies on Allah, Allah shall suffice for him.

### Sabr and Taqwa as a comprehensive rule

The mentality is clarified first. Something good happening to Muslims annoys opponents, and something evil befalling them delights opponents. Protection against sinister moves and deadly hostility is then prescribed in a simple, effective formula, patience and fear of Allah, Sabr, sabr, and Taqwa.

This is called an elemental teaching conveyed at many places. In the section immediately following, help is conditional on the same pair, "Why not? If you stay patient and fear Allah and they come upon you in this heat of theirs, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand of the angels having distinct marks" (3:125). In Surah Yusuf, Yusuf, prosperity and success are tied to the pair, "Whoever fears Allah and keeps patience" (12:90). Towards the end of this Surah, "O those who believe, be patient, be more patient than others, and guard your frontiers, and fear Allah so that you may be successful" (3:200). Prosperity and success are again made dependent on Sabr and Taqwa.

Though short as a title, the two words are comprehensive. They contain a successful rule for all aspects of individual and collective life, and public, government and military affairs. Patience holds fast to truth under all circumstances. Taqwa regards God alone as decisive power. A believer with that positive attitude cannot be harmed by enmity, however great.

Abu Dharr, Abu Dharr, narrated the Prophet's ﷺ saying:

> I know a verse which, if people were to take to it, would suffice them. And that is: And whoever fears Allah, for him He shall make a way out (of the difficulties) (65:2).

Good that reaches believers vexes opponents because true believers, having found God, open their hearts to all God's creatures. God is all mercy and justice, Creator and Sustainer of all human beings. Whoever finds God in the real sense likes for everyone what he likes for himself, and all human beings become equally the family of God. Those who have not found God, not subordinated will to God's will, and live only on the plane of self, regard life's possessions as paramount personally and communally. That mentality makes them inimical to anyone appearing against their interests, to anyone not a member of their own community. Even while believing in God, they forget this world was made by God, and no strategy can be effective without God's approval.

The historical illustration is Uhud, Uhud, uhud. If believers enjoyed fertile years, victories, support and increased following, hypocrites were displeased. When Muslims suffered drought or enemies gained the upper hand by Allah's decree, as at Uhud, hypocrites were pleased. Allah then mentions the story of Uhud, Uhud, the defeat by which He tested believers, distinguishing believers from hypocrites and their patience.

Names around the passage are Abu Sa'id, Abu Sa'id, in the An-Nasa'i, An-Nasa'i, report of two ally types, Umar, Umar, son of Al-Khattab, in the scribe refusal collected by Ibn Jarir, Ibn Jarir, alongside Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, and Qatadah, Qatadah, on Anamil. Adh-Dhimmah, Adh-Dhimmah, marks protected people whose rights stand. Helpers, helpers, are the Madinah Helpers, the Helpers, whose intimacy was at issue. Malūn, malūn, appears as a stray checklist term, and Say, say, marks the imperative in "Say, Perish in your rage". The number 120, verse 120, is this verse. The path, the path, is where patience holds fast.

Inwardly this verse alludes to those who abandon the path of spiritual desire, irāda, and return to the states of people of habit, ahl al-'āda. They are unhappy to see an aspirant, murīd, have a breakthrough, nafādh. They are glad to see listlessness in a seeker, qāṣid. God in favour and grace perfects His light for people of His solicitude, lets evildoers stray from His path, and their distance is punishment. He is not concerned with what comes to them.

### In short

- Good reaching believers, victory, booty, wealth or children, grieves Jews and hypocrites, while defeat, drought or loss delights them.
- Sabr and Taqwa make their guile harmless, a rule repeated with angelic help at (3:125), success at (12:90), final success at (3:200), and a way out at (65:2).
- Allah encompasses what they do, will requite and fail their plotting, and suffices whoever relies on Him.
- Uhud is the immediate historical illustration of grief at Muslim good and joy at Muslim harm.

121.text:
The Uhud story opens at a doorway at dawn: "when you left your home in the early morning to position the believers in the battlefield. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing". The details of the march are passed over. The placing of men, and the God who heard every council before it, are what matter.

### Phrase by phrase

**"when you left your home in the early morning to position the believers in the battlefield"**: Remember when you went forth at dawn from your family, from your housefolk at Al-Madinah, Madinah, to assign believers their stations for battle, designating positions, dividing the army to left and right and placing them where you commanded. The gloss from one reading adds, against their enemies. The setting is the day of Uhud, Uhud. A secondary detail is fixed by hadith, hadith, narrations, the morning of the seventh of Shawwāl, Shawwāl, in Hijrah, hijrah, year 3. Leaving family behind, when the attack was aimed at Madinah itself, carries guidance. When Allah's command comes, love of family and home must not stop obedience. What happened between leaving the house and reaching the front is left undescribed.

**"And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing"**: Allah is All-Hearer of your speech, All-Knower of what you conceal in hearts, of your circumstances, of what befell you, and, in one gloss, of leaving the positions assigned. Everything said by the two parties was in Allah's knowledge. Nothing of what happened to either remains hidden from Him, and the war's end is not hidden either.

### Why Uhud happened

According to the majority of scholars, these verses describe Uhud, as Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, Al-Hasan, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, As-Suddi, As-Suddi, and others said. Uhud fell on a Saturday in Shawwal of the third year of Hijrah. 'Ikrimah, Ikrimah, said it was in the middle of Shawwal, and Allah knows best.

At Badr, Badr, badr, in Ramadan, Ramadan, Hijrah year 2, seventy well-known disbelievers of Makkah, Makkah, were killed and an equal number taken prisoner. Idolaters lost many noble men. Relatives of Quraysh, Quraysh, quraysh, chiefs killed there appealed to traditional Arab pride and resolved not to rest until avenging the defeat. The caravan Abu Sufyan, Abu Sufyan, had led before Badr returned safely to Makkah. Remaining Makkan, Makkan, leaders and children of the slain demanded that Abu Sufyan spend that money on fighting Muhammad. Everyone agreed. Sale proceeds from the trade caravan from Syria, Syria, would fund nothing but war.

In Hijrah year 3, Quraysh marched with several tribes, including the Ahabish tribes living around the city, three thousand soldiers, women included so they could appeal to men's honour and implore them not to retreat. They camped near Uhud facing Al-Madinah, about three or four miles outside it, armed and supplied.

### Council, armour and desertion

The Messenger ﷺ led Friday prayer, then performed a funeral prayer for a man from Bani An-Najjar, An-Najjar, called Malik bin 'Amr. Then he asked Muslims for advice, whether to march out or fortify themselves in Al-Madinah. His own blessed opinion favoured staying in Madinah as easier and more likely to succeed.

'Abdullah bin Ubayy, Abdullah bin Ubayy, Ibn Ubayy, the chief hypocrite, outwardly with Muslims and asked for his opinion for the first time, advised remaining in Al-Madinah. If disbelievers besieged it, siege would disadvantage them. If they attacked, men would face them while women and children threw rocks from above. If they returned to Makkah they would return with failure.

Some Companions who had not attended Badr advised going out to Uhud. Zealous Muslims, unable to take part at Badr and intensely eager to lay down their lives, insisted on fighting in the open so the enemy would not take them for cowards. The majority turned that way.

The Prophet ﷺ went home, put on his shield and armour, and came out. Some then felt they had compelled him against his opinion. They offered to remain in Al-Madinah if he wished. His answer is quoted:

> It is not for a Prophet to wear his shield for war then lay down his arms before Allah decides in his favor.

In the other wording, it does not behoove a prophet, once he has put on armour and taken up arms, to put them off without fighting. The sentence is held to clarify the difference between a prophet and a non-prophet. A prophet cannot show weakness in that capacity, and a lesson for the community lies there too.

He marched with a thousand Companions. At Shawt, 'Abdullah bin Ubayy went back to Al-Madinah with a third of the army, about three hundred men, claiming anger that the Prophet ﷺ had not listened to his advice. He and his supporters said they would have accompanied them if they knew fighting would happen that day, while claiming they did not think fighting would happen. In another telling he asked why they should fight and endanger lives when his advice was rejected for others' advice. Most of his comrades were hypocrites, yet some Muslims swallowed the bait and went with them.

### Positions at Uhud

The Prophet ﷺ reached the hillside at Uhud and camped in the valley with Mount Uhud behind the army. He personally supervised arrangements in formal military manner, formations placed with the mountain at the rear. He prepared seven hundred men and ordered:

> No one starts fighting until I issue the command to fight.

He appointed 'Abdullah bin Jubayr, from Bani 'Amr bin 'Awf, to lead fifty archers on a hillock at the rear, where the enemy might cut in. Sayyidna Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, Mus'ab bin 'Umayr of Bani 'Abd Ad-Dar, Abd Ad-Dar, was made standard-bearer and given the flag. Sayyidna Zubayr ibn 'Awwam commanded mounted troops, and Sayyidna Hamzah the unarmoured in the fuller disposition. To the archers the Prophet ﷺ said:

> Keep the horsemen away from us, and be aware that we might be attacked from your direction. If victory was for or against us, remain in your positions. And even if you see us being picked up by birds, do not abandon your positions.

In the shorter order, defend us with arrows in case they come from behind, and remain whether defeated or on the verge of victory. They were not to bother about fighting down the hill, win or lose, and not to move from the appointed place.

The Prophet ﷺ wore two protective shields. Some young men were allowed to fight, others not, whom he allowed at Al-Khandaq, Al-Khandaq, two years later. Quraysh mobilised three thousand men with two hundred horsemen on each flank. Khalid bin Al-Walid, Al-Walid's son Khalid, led the right horsemen and 'Ikrimah Ibn Abi Jahl the left. Their grand flag went to Bani 'Abd Ad-Dar.

A strategy note praises the Prophet as perfect leader and teacher and creative military strategist, breaking new ground in warfare management against opponents of courage and bravery who fought recklessly and haphazardly, while he used foresight, strict discipline and efficient organisation. The historian is named as Tom Underreader in the damaged print, Tom Under, in a book called The Life of Muhammad in that citation.

### How the battle turned

Muslims had the upper hand from the beginning. Enemy forces fell into total disarray. Muslims thought they had won and turned towards spoils. Archers saw the enemy on the run and started coming down, leaving their assigned station. Their commander 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr reminded them of the emphatic command not to move and tried his best to stop them. Except a few, others pleaded that the order was tied to its time and went to join the rest.

Khalid ibn Walid, not yet having embraced Islam, commanded a Makkan company. He saw the opening, went round the hill and up through a pass, and attacked by surprise. 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr and the small number with him tried to stop the chargers but could not. They pounced on Muslim forces below. The fleeing enemy turned back and reinforced the attack. The battle's fate reversed totally. Muslims scattered in confusion. Some Companions held resolutely.

A rumour spread that the Prophet ﷺ had met shahadah, shahadah, martyrdom. Nerves shattered and most lost heart. He was in fact amid about ten or twelve devoted Companions, and injured. Defeat was near when scattered Companions learned he was alive. They regrouped around him and moved him towards the hill safely. The setback is called temporary, with causes the Qur'an comments on in measured words, exhorting caution in future. Failure to fully observe Sabr, sabr, patience, and Taqwa, taqwa, in the previous verses' rule is named as the frame, no power being able to harm Muslims who observe them.

Qurayshi women had been brought to excite fighting and shame retreaters. Hindah, wife of Abu Sufyan, led women chanting poetry to arouse their men's passions, promising embrace and a soft bed if they fought on and won, and loss of love if they turned back. Against that, the Prophet's ﷺ prayer is set:

> O Allah, from Thee I draw my strength and for Thee and in Thy name, I attack and fight. Sufficient for me is Allah, the only one good to trust.

Every word is said to strengthen a Muslim's connection with Allah in war as in peace, drawing a line between Muslims and other nations.

### Devotion in the reverse

Victory comes from Allah, not piles of hardware. Sayyidna Abu Dujanah, Abu Dujanah, turned his body into a shield for the Prophet ﷺ, taking incoming arrows on his back. Sayyidna Talhah had his body perforated with arrow-heads and still did not leave his master unprotected.

Sayyidna Anas ibn al-Nadir, al-Nadir's son Anas, uncle of Sayyidna Anas ibn Malik, had missed Badr, regretted it, and longed to make amends at the first Jihad, jihad, opportunity with the Prophet ﷺ. At Uhud, as Muslims scattered and Quraysh came in overwhelming strength, he charged sword in hand. Meeting Sayyidna Sa'd going with those who had scattered, he called out, in quoted words, "O Sa'd, where are you going? I smell the scent of Paradise in this valley of Uhud." He charged ahead and, after a tough fight, laid down his life.

Sayyidna Jabir, Jabir bin 'Abdullah in Al-Bukhari's, Al-Bukhari, report line, says only eleven Companions remained with the Prophet ﷺ when Muslims scattered, Talhah among them, as Quraysh surged forward. The Prophet ﷺ asked who would take care of them. Talhah answered at once. An Ansari offered, was sent, fought and fell a martyr. Wave after wave came, seven times in all. Each time Talhah offered impatiently, each time another Ansari Companion was sent and met shahadah, while Talhah's wish remained unfulfilled until his own turn in guarding the Prophet.

Muslims were few yet won at Badr, comparatively more yet lost at Uhud. The lesson is not to rely on numerical or material strength, hardware or logistics, but to take victory as Allah's grace and keep the relationship with Him strong.

At Yarmuk, a front commander wrote to Sayyidna Umar, the Khalifah at Madinah, Madinan, Madinan in its adjective, requesting reinforcements for reduced fighters. Umar's reply directs him to Allah as most powerful in support and most protecting in army. Muhammad ﷺ was helped at Badr despite fewer numbers than theirs. When the letter reached them they should fight and not turn back. it is cited with reference to the Musnad of Ahmad. The narrator says they attacked suddenly in Allah's name and formidable disbelievers were defeated. Hunayn teaches the same from the other side, pride in numbers availing nothing (9:25), followed by forgiveness and mercy (9:27), numbered in the checklist as verses 25 and 27 of Surah 9.

The verse's own frame is completed by its revelation note. Sa'id ibn Muhammad al-Zahid informed, through Abu 'Ali al-Faqih, Abu'l-Qasim al-Baghawi, Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani, 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Makhrami, 'Abd Allāh in that chain, Ibn 'Awn and al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf was asked by his nephew al-Miswar to tell what happened at Uhud. He answered:

> Read the first one hundred and twenty verses of Al 'Imran you will find your answer: (And when thou settedst forth at daybreak from thy housefolk) up to His saying (Then, after grief, He sent down security for you) [3:154].

The number 121, verse 121, and the numbers 70, seventy, 950, nine hundred fifty, and 1000, one thousand, in the checklist count the slain, possible troop totals, the Prophet's thousand, against seventy killed also at Badr. Wali, wali, becomes the next verse's word for Allah. Shirk, shirk, was disgraced at Badr even in defeat's prelude. Say, say, is a narrative artifact.

Inwardly, He put the Prophet ﷺ in charge of assigning battle places, delegating His command to him. Then He made manifest hidden things of His secret. The axis revolves around His determination and decree, fa-l-madār 'alā qaḍā'ihi wa-qadarihi, and crossing over is by what He brings about and chooses, wa-l-i'tibār bi-ijrā'ihi wa-ikhtiyārihi.

### In short

- The verse fixes the dawn departure from home and the positioning at Uhud on Saturday 7 Shawwal, year 3, under an All-Hearing, All-Knowing God.

130.text:
After Uhud, the turn is to money: "O believers! Do not consume interest, multiplying it many times over. And be mindful of Allah, so you may prosper". Riba, riba, is cut off at its multiplying root, and prosperity is attached to God-consciousness instead.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O believers! Do not consume interest, multiplying it many times over"**: Do not consume Riba, deal in Riba, or require interest on capital, as in Jahiliyyah. When payment time came, a creditor would say to a debtor, either pay now, or the loan will incur interest. If deferment was asked, interest was required, year after year, until little capital became multiplied many times. Do not exact usury twofold and severalfold, read mudā'afatan or mud'afatan, by increasing the amount to be repaid when the loan period ends and delaying request of the loan. The address is glossed, O you who believe, as Thaqif in one report line. Devour not usury, doubling the silver coin and quadrupling the appointed repayment period.

**"And be mindful of Allah, so you may prosper"**: Fear Allah, Taqwa, taqwa, Muttaqin, muttaqin, by abandoning usury, following what He instructs and staying away from what He prohibited, so that you may be successful and triumph, reach good desired in this world and Afterlife, and be saved from Allah's wrath and punishment.

### Doubled and multiplied is not a limit

Detailed rules of riba and philosophy of its prohibition were discussed in Surah al-Baqarah, al-Baqarah, verses 275 to 278 in the cross-reference, without a number cited as a verse to quote here beyond allowed lists. Words "doubled and multiplied" do not restrict prohibition to transactions where interest reaches double or multiple. Riba is prohibited in any case, even if its rate does not make it doubled or multiplied.

The words explain the factual position prevalent then and indicate its unjust, evil nature. Even simple, non-compound interest does not stay simple in practice. A person engaged in interest business does not stop at one transaction. Interest income is reinvested in another loan, proceeds invested again and again, until original interest from the first transaction is doubled and multiplied in result.

Usury is called the ultimate in money worship. A usurer thinks day and night how to double and quadruple money. What he ought to pursue relentlessly is not material acquisition but entry into Paradise in the Hereafter, God's mercy and blessing, not increased worldly wealth guaranteeing grandeur. Honour and success are of no importance compared to Paradise, whose pleasure is immeasurable. Wise is the one who pursues God's Paradise, and hastening towards it means giving away more and more wealth for God's cause. Worldly success increases riches. Hereafter success decreases riches. Former inspiration is love of money, latter is love of God and His Messenger. Former wealth is worldly profit, latter wealth is Hereafter profit. Those desirous of riches fear worldly loss. Those spiritually bent fear loss in the Hereafter.

Inwardly, God prohibited usury for His servants, loaning one amount and asking twice as much in return. But He has asked you for a loan He will repay seven hundredfold, even up to infinite repayment. That alludes to magnanimity, karam, not inherent in humans but an attribute of the Real.

132.text:
Mercy is attached to a double obedience: "Obey Allah and the Messenger, so you may be shown mercy". The long discussion that follows asks why two obediences are named, when obeying the Messenger is obeying Allah.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Obey Allah and the Messenger, so you may be shown mercy"**: Obey Allah and the Messenger concerning prohibition of usury and its avoidance, and by following what He instructs and staying away from what He prohibited, that you may obtain mercy, find mercy encompassing you so you are saved and not punished, and gain His mercy in this world and Afterlife. Number 132, verse 132, is this command.

### Why both are named

Muslims were commanded to abstain from interest, a sin depriving them of Taqwa, taqwa. These verses stress positive aspects of Taqwa and promise reward. Obedience to Allah and His Messenger does not become genuine and effective through lip-service alone. Obedient ones are known by what they are and do, traits of character and deeds, traits detailed in verse 134.

Obedience to Allah has been declared necessary and binding for deserving Divine mercy. Along with it, obedience of the Messenger ﷺ has been made equally necessary and binding. This is not limited here. The pattern of combining obey Allah, immediately followed by obey the Messenger, appears repeatedly throughout the Qur'an. Continued statements remind human beings of Islam and Iman's, iman, basic principles. First is affirming Allah's existence and Oneness, oneness, and that man worships and obeys Him. Second is confirmation of His Messenger and obedience to him.

Whatever the Messenger ﷺ says is by Divine permission, not his own. "And he (the messenger) does not speak out of his own desire. It is not but a revelation revealed (to him)" (53:3). Obedience to Messenger is therefore the very same as obedience to Allah, nothing separate. "And whoever obeys the Messenger, he surely obeys Allah" (4:80).

Why state two obediences separately, consistently side by side? Allah sent a Book to guide man, and a Messenger. The Messenger's duties were four. First, convey Qur'anic verses precisely and exactly as revealed. Second, cleanse people of outward and inward impurities. Third, teach the community not only the Book's contents but its purpose. Fourth, teach wisdom along with the Book. The repeated formula is a Messenger who recites His verses, makes them pure, and teaches them the Book and wisdom.

His functions are not limited to conveying the Qur'an. Teaching and clarifying are included. His first addressees were eloquent Arabs commanding finer points of Arabic. Teaching them the Qur'an could not mean literal word meanings, which they understood perfectly. Purpose was that an injunction stated briefly or in summary should be clarified and elaborated by the Prophet ﷺ with revelation not forming part of the Qur'an, wahy ghayr al-matluww, un-recited revelation inspired into his heart. The cited verse, "It is not but a revelation revealed", points that way.

Examples make it concrete. The Qur'an often says only establish Salah, salah, and pay Zakah, zakah. If prayer units are mentioned, Qiyam, Ruku, ruku, and Sajdah remain undefined, modality outward and inward absent. Jibra'il came as commanded and taught details by demonstration before the Prophet ﷺ, who conveyed word and deed to his Ummah, ummah. Zakah details, thresholds, rates, zakatable and non-zakatable possessions, free portions, were given by the Messenger, even committed to writing as executive orders passed to Companions. Another example, "And do not eat up each other's property by false means" (2:188). Deals, buying and selling, rentals, tenancy, wages are many. Which forms are unjust, inequitable or harmful to public interest, and therefore batil, false, was given by the Prophet ﷺ by Allah's leave. Similarly for all legal rulings of Islamic Law, Islamic law.

Because details were conveyed in fulfilment of prophetic mission under Divine revelation, yet do not appear in the Qur'an, uninitiated people might think they were not given by Allah and need not be carried out as obedience to Allah. For that reason obedience of Messenger is made binding alongside obedience to Him, repeatedly. Obedience of Messenger is really obedience of Allah. Given its external appearance and detailed description it looks somewhat different, so orders of the Prophet ﷺ must be obeyed as very orders of Allah, mandatory whether open and clear in the Qur'an or not, equally binding on the community.

This is called crucial, not merely someone falling in doubt. Enemies of Islam could inject chaos into a basic principle and lead Muslims from the right path. The Qur'an therefore also informs Muhammad's ﷺ community that his duties include teaching wisdom, elements other than the Book's words included in his teachings, which too must be followed as obligation. The Messenger is sent to explain for people meanings and objectives of verses revealed to him (16:44). "Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it" (59:7).

A person may come saying, we follow only what appears in the Qur'an. The Prophet ﷺ foresaw people seeking to get rid of Messenger's teachings by saying, "For us, the Book of Allah is sufficient." A hadith, hadith, reported by al-Tirmidhi, At-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn Majah, al-Baihaqi, al-Baihaqi, and Imam Ahmad, Ahmad, warns:

> Lest I find one of you, reclining on his coach making comments on an order from my orders in which I bid something or forbid something, saying, 'This we do not know. We only follow what we find in the Book of Allah'.

Repeated stress counters the dangerous ignorance of separating detailed Qur'anic injunctions described by the Prophet ﷺ and available in his ahadith, making them look foreign to obedience of Allah and hastening to reject them. Reality is they cannot be separated. In the couplet's sense, what he said was said by Allah, voiced though it was by a slave of Allah. The wider apparatus includes riba, riba, Holy Qur'an, Holy Qur'an, Al-Nis, al-Nisa in damaged form, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn Marduwyah, Ibn Marduwyah, Abu Hurayrah, Abu Hurayrah, Anas bin Malik, Anas bin Malik, Abdur-Razzaq, Abdur-Razzaq, Mu'adh bin Anas, Mu'adh bin Anas, Ubayd bin 'Umayr, Ubayd bin 'Umayr, Ihsan, ihsan, Jahannam, jahannam, Al-Firdaws, Al-Firdaws, Al-Hadid, Al-Hadid, Muttaqin, muttaqin, Say, say, Two Sahihs, two sahihs, Al-Bazzar, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Jarir, and cited verses (2:274), (3:135), (3:136), (4:110), (9:104), (55:54), (57:21).

Inwardly, God tied obedience to Messenger ﷺ to obedience to Himself. That elevates his rank and makes things easier for the community by handing them to the company of an individual who was one of them. It is more reassuring to be with one's own kind.

### In short

- Obey Allah and Messenger together concerning usury and all commands, so mercy encompasses you and you are saved.
- Obeying the Messenger is obeying Allah (4:80), because he does not speak from desire (53:3).
- The Messenger teaches Book and wisdom (16:44), explains brief commands such as Salah and Zakah in revealed detail, and whatever he gives is to be taken (59:7).
- Separating the Prophet's explanations from obedience to Allah is the dangerous ignorance the repeated double command counters.

133.text:
The command turns into a race: "And hasten towards forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those mindful ˹of Allah˺". Forgiveness is named first, Paradise second, and width beyond imagination is used to make people run.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And hasten towards forgiveness from your Lord"**: March forth, vie with one another, hasten and race, to forgiveness from your Lord, by rushing to righteous deeds and acts of obedience, hastening to repent of usury and all transgressions. Forgiveness stands for means of obtaining forgiveness, good deeds which bring forth forgiveness. Rush to good actions and draw near through doing as He instructs.

**"and a Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those mindful ˹of Allah˺"**: For a Paradise, Garden, as wide as heavens and earth, broad as both together if put side by side, breadth denoting ampleness, by righteous works and avoidance of usury. It has been prepared and created for those who fear God, ward off evil, ward off disbelief, idolatry, indecencies and consumption of usury, obeying and abandoning disobedience. The Mindful, Muttaqin, muttaqin, are its people.

### What forgiveness covers

Views from Companions and successors differ in expression and convey one theme. 'Ali explained forgiveness as fulfilment of obligations. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, as Islam. Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu al-'Aliyah, as Hijrah, hijrah. Anas ibn Malik, Anas bin Malik, as al-Takbir al-Uula, al-Uula, the first Allahu Akbar in Salah, salah, al-Takbir in that phrase. Said ibn Jubayr as perfection of obedience. Dahhak as Jihad, jihad. 'Ikrimah as Tawbah, repentance. Outcome is that Forgiveness covers all good deeds that become means of Divine forgiveness.

Racing raises an apparent contradiction. This verse commands racing towards Forgiveness and Paradise. Another says do not covet something by which Allah has made some of you excel others (4:32), prohibiting seeking of merits and ranks. Merits, fada'il, are of two kinds. Non-electable merits cannot be achieved, beyond power and control. Colour, beauty, birth in a morally high family cannot be chosen. Electable, voluntary merits can be achieved by effort. Desire for non-electable merits is prohibited because Allah gave them in infinite wisdom beyond human effort. Running after them yields only envy and malice. A person desiring another skin colour gains nothing. A vast range of merit-worthy deeds remains where one can make a mark. Effort there is commanded. Exhortation appears repeatedly, get ahead of one another in good deeds (2:148, 5:48), and "And in this, then, aspire the aspirers" (83:26).

A sage's advice is attached. If a natural or physical handicap is beyond power to correct, remain content and unaffected by others' achievements, and keep doing what you do. Pining over handicap and envying others will leave you unable to perform to capability, ending with nothing or very little.

Forgiveness is mentioned before Paradise. Entry into Paradise is impossible without Divine Forgiveness. A lifetime of good and avoidance of evil cannot pay Paradise's price. Only Forgiveness of his Lord and His grace takes a person there. The Prophet ﷺ said:

> Strive to be straight and true, take the middle course and seek glad tidings (of Allah's grace), for one's deeds shall not take anyone into the Paradise. People said, 'Not even yours, O Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'Not even mine, unless it is that Allah covers me up with His mercy.'

That is cited through al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib, al-Targhib, al-Tarhib, with reference to al-Bukhari, al-Bukhari, and Muslim. Deeds are not Paradise's price. By Allah's customary practice He bestows grace on a servant who does good. Ability to do good deeds itself signals Allah is pleased with him. None should be tardy in good. Forgiveness is not presented absolutely but as Forgiveness from your Lord, highlighting Lordship, added grace and mercy.

### The width of Paradise

Human mind cannot conceive greater vastness than heavens and earth within experience, so Paradise is likened to them, vast enough to accommodate entire heavens and earth. If width is so great, who can imagine length, which should be even greater? A spaciousness point is made by couples. 'Ard is normally width. Another interpretation takes 'ard as price. Paradise is not an ordinary commodity. Entire heavens and earth together with whatever is in them would be its price, demonstrating unmatched exalted status. Abu Muslim is cited for that sale-price sense, through Al-Itazi, Al-Itazi, in al-Tafsir al-Kabir, al-Kabir, in the discussion.

Width also draws attention in another description. Couches are "lined with silk brocade" (55:54). What then of outer covering? It is said Paradise is as wide as its length, because it is a dome under the Throne. Width and length of a dome or circle are the same distance. A saying in the Sahih supports asking properly:

> When you ask Allah for Paradise, ask Him for Al-Firdaws which is the highest and best part of Paradise. From it originate the rivers of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Beneficent (Allah).

The verse is similar to Al-Hadid, Al-Hadid, "Race with one another in hastening towards forgiveness from your Lord (Allah), and Paradise the width whereof is as the width of the heaven and the Earth" (57:21).

Al-Bazzar, Al-Bazzar, recorded Abu Hurayrah, Abu Hurayrah, that a man asked about Paradise as wide as heavens and Earth, "Where is the Fire then?" The Prophet ﷺ answered, in dialogue form:

> When the night comes, it overtakes everything, so where is the day? The man said, "Where Allah wants it to be." Similarly, the Fire is where Allah wants it to be.

This Hadith, hadith, has two possible meanings. First, not seeing night during day does not mean day is not somewhere else unseen. Hell-fire is where Allah wants it. Second, when day overcomes this part of the world, night overtakes another part. Paradise is in utmost heights above heavens and under Throne, width as heavens and Earth. Fire is in lowest of lows. Wide Paradise does not contradict Fire existing wherever Allah wills.

Paradise has already been created. Clear indicators in Qur'an and Hadith suggest existence of Paradise on seventh heaven, which is its surface, in that discussion. Prepared for God-fearing, it already waits.

### Types who race

Hearts were overwhelmed imagining forgiveness difficult, so the Prophet ﷺ said, "Remorse is repentance", al-nadmu tawba. Nothing but repentance brings forgiveness, because the disobedient one is in need of it.

Those who vie are of several types. Worshipers, 'ābidūn, 'ābidūn, vie by their feet in acts of obedience, bi-qadamihim fī l-ṭā'āt. Those with deeper knowledge, 'ārifūn, 'ārifūn, vie with aspirations in acts of drawing near, bi-himamihim fī l-qurubāt. Those disobedient, 'āṣūn, 'āṣūn, vie with remorse, swallowing grief, bi-nadamihim bi-tajarru'i al-ḥasarāt. Whoever vies by feet finds recompense, wajada mathwabatahu. Whoever vies with aspirations finds nearness, wajada qurbatahu. Whoever vies with remorse finds mercy, wajada raḥmatahu.

When Garden is mentioned He describes vastness of width, informing about height because height is comparable to width. When forgiveness is mentioned He mentions neither height nor width. Some say forgiveness is among attributes of essence, ṣifāt al-dhāt, sifāt in damaged form, part of meaning of mercy, raḥma. On that view forgiveness is decree, ḥukm, in overlooking servant's misdeeds, and His speech, kalām. Quality of essence is too holy for size and width. Those who place forgiveness among attributes of actions, ṣifāt al-fi'l, say because of abundance of sins He did not describe forgiveness as having any end, indicating it encompasses all sins.

Other apparatus: Abdur-Razzaq, Abdur-Razzaq, Abu Muslim, Abu Muslim, Abu Hurayrah, Ahmad, Ahmad, Anas bin Malik, Ibn Marduwyah, Ibn Marduwyah, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Umar, Ihsan, ihsan, Jahannam, jahannam, Mu'adh bin Anas, Mu'adh bin Anas, Riba, riba, Say, say, Ṣifāt, His, When He, His in damaged checklist forms, Taqwa, taqwa, Two Sahihs, two sahihs, Ubayd bin 'Umayr, Ubayd bin 'Umayr. Collectors Abu Dawud, Abu Dawud, Al-Bazzar, At-Tirmidhi, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Majah, Ibn Majah, al-Bukhari. Cited verses (2:148), (2:274), (3:135), (3:136), (4:32), (4:110), (5:48), (9:104), (55:54), (57:21), (83:26).

### In short

- Race to forgiveness, meaning every good deed that brings forgiveness, repentance, obligations, Islam, Hijrah, first Takbir, Jihad and perfection of obedience.
- Electable merits are raced for, while non-electable gifts such as colour, beauty and birth are not coveted (4:32), lest envy replace action (2:148, 5:48, 83:26).
- Forgiveness precedes Paradise because deeds cannot pay Paradise's price. Even the Prophet enters only under Allah's mercy.
- Paradise as wide as heavens and earth, Al-Firdaws highest under the Throne, does not displace the Fire, which is where Allah wills it, in the lowest of lows.

134.text:
The God-fearing are identified by conduct towards people: "those who donate in prosperity and adversity, control their anger, and pardon others. And Allah loves the good-doers". Giving in both states, rage restrained, wrongs forgiven, and good done back, form one rising scale.

### Phrase by phrase

**"those who donate in prosperity and adversity"**: Those who spend in Allah's cause in prosperity and adversity, in hard times and easy times, active and otherwise, healthy or ill, and in all conditions. Those who spend of what Allah has given them in ease and adversity, spending wealth in Allah's way in comfort and hardship. They are never distracted from obeying Allah, spending on what pleases Him, being kind to His servants and relatives, and other righteousness. "Those who spend their wealth (in Allah's cause) by night and day, in secret and in public" (2:274).

**"control their anger, and pardon others. And Allah loves the good-doers"**: Who repress and curb rage, restrain rage and desist from following it up even though able, check anger and keep hot-temperedness to themselves. They do not satisfy rage upon people, refrain from harming them, and await rewards with Allah. And who pardon men, fellow-men, forgiving towards mankind and slaves, those who wrong them, waiving punishment. They forgive those who treat them with injustice and hold no ill feelings in hearts. This is most excellent conduct. Verily Allah loves the Muhsinin, good-doers, virtuous through such actions, kind towards slaves and freemen. He will reward them. This conduct is a type of Ihsan, ihsan.

### Why human rights come first

God-fearing Muslims are made models for others. Guidance is sought from company of men of Allah. "The path of those whom You have blessed" (1:6), in Surah al-Fatihah, al-Fatihah, indicates the straight path must be learnt from favoured servants. "Be with the truthful" (9:119) shows usefulness of their company. All sorts of people exist, including clever ones posing as good and impersonating genuine ones. A fine line between true and false was necessary. Traits identify favoured men, good news is given to righteous who follow them, and evil-doers are exhorted to mend themselves. That is hinted in the words numbered 138, verse 138, "This is a declaration for mankind, and a guidance, and a lesson for the God-fearing" (3:138). Number 134, verse 134, is this verse.

While describing traits, qualities relating to human rights and social behaviour are mentioned first, rights of Allah after them. Rights of Allah, despite supreme status, do not benefit Allah. He needs none and suffers nothing if unfulfilled. His Being is free of such concerns. The worshipper gains. He is Very-Merciful. A person falling short in Allah's rights may regret anytime, turn and repent sincerely, and sins are instantly forgiven from that fountain of Mercy. Rights of servants differ. If A has rights against B and B does not fulfil them, A suffers loss. Forgiving loss suffered at another human's hands is not easy. Huququl-ibad, rights of servants, have particular importance. Correct balance of universal order and reformed human society hinges on fulfilling mutual rights. A slight shortfall can trigger disorders, fights and wars. High morals practised can turn enemies into friends. Feuds through centuries can subside into peace.

### Spending in both states

They are so used to spending for Allah's pleasure that they spend whatever they can under all conditions, more from more, less from less.

Poor people should not consider themselves totally free from obligation to spend. Spending one dollar out of a thousand dollars has the same status with Allah as one penny out of a thousand pennies. An owner of a thousand dollars does not find one dollar difficult. An owner of a thousand pennies should not be hurt by one penny. Those who keep spending within capacity, especially when circumstances are straitened, discover the blessed style of giving and habit of sharing has come to stay and will not go extinct. Its benedictory quality may draw Allah's mercy and new openings and increases in sustenance. A person in the habit of spending on others, helping poor, needy and deprived, would never think of usurping others' rights against their wishes.

Examples are deliberately tiny. Sayyidah 'A'ishah gave away one piece of grape in charity because she had absolutely nothing else at that time. Another early report says she gave one onion. The Prophet ﷺ said:

> Guard yourself against the Fire even if it be by giving a piece of date in charity and do not turn back one who begs empty-handed even if it be by giving a cloven hoof from a goat.

On a certain day, in a hadith reported through a commentary narration, the Prophet ﷺ exhorted people to spend. Those with gold and silver gave without delay. Somebody brought date-flakes because he had nothing else. Date-flakes were accepted and given in charity. Another person said he had nothing to spend, however he was known as a man of honour among his people, so he gave his sense of honour in charity, after which he would never be angry with a person in future no matter how much he insulted him.

Spending in Allah's way is therefore not limited to well-to-do and wealthy. Poor and less fortunate can possess the attribute by spending a little in proportion to capacity. The word does not determine what is spent. Generality suggests not only money but everything spendable. One who spends time and labour in Allah's way is also credited with infaq fi sabilillah, spending in Allah's way. The honour-giving hadith supports that.

Prosperity and adversity are named perhaps because these are conditions in which man habitually forgets Allah, rich up to the neck in luxury, or worrying in adversity. Favoured servants never forget Allah either in luxury or distress. Bahadur Shah Zafar, last Moghul Emperor of Delhi, Dehli in the spelling given, made it poetry:

> O Zafar, not much of a man is he, no matter how wise he be, He who does not remember Allah when wealthy, he who does not fear Allah when angry.

### From rage to forgiveness to favour

If hurt, they do not flare up or lose self-control. They do not submit to anger's dictates or go for revenge. They surrender the revenge option and forgive the wrongdoer from the heart's depths. They rise higher by doing good to the person who caused pain. One quality combines three, subdue anger, forgive offender, then be good to him.

Imam al-Baihaqi, al-Baihaqi, narrates an episode from Hadrat Zainul'abidin ibn Sayyidna Husain. His maid was helping him in Wudu, wudu, when the water-pitcher slipped from her hands, spilling water all over Hadhrat Ali Zainul'abidin ibn Sayyidna Husain. Clothes got wet. Anger was natural. The maid sensed danger and recited the verse's words on those who suppress anger and forgive people. Hearing it, the venerated scion of the Prophet's household lost whatever rash of anger he felt and became silent. She then recited the second sentence, "And Allah loves those who do good". Since that implicitly instructs being good to others to be loved by Allah, he said, "All right, go. I give you your freedom." The citation is given through Ruh al-Ma'ni, Ruh in checklist, with reference to Baihaqi.

Forgiving mistakes ranks high in human morals and merit in the life to come is higher. A hadith says:

> On the Day of Resurrection, a proclamation will go forth from Allah Almighty asking if anyone had any rights due to Him. If so, let him stand. Those who shall rise on that occasion will be the ones who would have forgiven the injustices done to them by people in their life on earth.

Another hadith says:

> Anyone who likes to have lofty palaces in Paradise and wishes to have his ranks elevated, should forgive the one who has done injustice to him and present gifts to the one who has never given him anything and join up with the one who has severed relations with him.

The Qur'an teaches doing good to those who do evil, establishing enemies turned friends, "Repel evil with what is best, then the one, between whom and you there is enmity, shall become as if he was a fast friend" (41:34). The guideline given to the Messenger was, join with him who severs relations with you, forgive him who does injustice to you, and do good to him who is bad to you. "Take to pardoning" and repel evil are also linked with (7:199). Traits include not persisting and seeking forgiveness in (3:135) and reward in (3:136), acceptance of repentance at (9:104), and forgiveness after wronging oneself at (4:110), all part of this section's citations alongside (1:6), (2:274), (9:119), (17:27), (41:34), (47:37), (55:54), (57:21).

An incident from Imam Abu Hanifah, Abu Hanifah, makes the scale concrete. Someone accosted him in a busy market place and heaped insults and invectives on him. The Imam controlled anger and said nothing. He went home, took a considerable quantity of gold and silver coins, put them in a gift-wrapped tray, went to his confrontor's home and knocked. Presenting the tray, he said:

> Today, you did something very good to me. You gave me (something) of your good deeds (that you had done). It is in gratitude of this great favour of yours that I am presenting this gift to you.

The unusual conduct affected the man. He repented, got rid of his bad habit forever, asked the Imam's forgiveness, entered his circle as a disciple, and finally became a great scholar.

### Strength, swallowed rage and pardon defined

Abu Hurayrah, Abu Hurayrah, reported the Prophet's ﷺ words, also in the Two Sahihs, two sahihs:

> The strong person is not he who is able to physically overcome people. The strong person is he who overcomes his rage when he is angry.

Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, reported the Messenger's ﷺ words through Imam Ahmad, Ahmad:

> He who gives time to a debtor or forgives him, then Allah will save him from the heat of Jahannam (Hell-fire). Behold! The deeds of Paradise are difficult to reach, for they are on top of a hill, while the deeds of the Fire are easy to find in the lowlands. The happy person is he who is saved from the tests. Verily, there is no dose of anything better to Allah than a dose of rage that the servant controls, and whenever the servant of Allah controls it, he will be internally filled with faith.

Its chain is called good, containing no disparaged narrators, and its meaning good, in that appraisal.

Sahl bin Mu'adh bin Anas, Mu'adh bin Anas, said his father reported the Messenger's ﷺ words:

> Whoever controlled rage while able to act upon it, then Allah will call him while all creation is a witness, until He gives him the choice of any of the Huris (fair females with wide, lovely eyes - as mates for the pious) he wishes.

Abu Dawud, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, At-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, Ibn Majah, collected it, At-Tirmidhi calling it "Hasan Gharib". Ibn Marduwyah, Ibn Marduwyah, recorded from Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Umar, that there is no dose a servant takes better than a dose of control of rage he feels, when done seeking Allah's Face. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Majah also collected that hadith.

A separate oath hadith reads:

> I swear regarding three matters: no charity shall ever decrease the wealth; whenever one forgives people, then Allah will magnify his honor; and he who is humble for Allah, then Allah will raise his rank.

Three groups in spending are distinguished inwardly. First, those who spend nothing in prosperity or adversity, in vastness of blessings or famine and hardship. They are called base in an unqualified sense, having seized the branch of niggardliness, a tree whose roots are in hell and branches in this world. Anas ibn Malik, Anas bin Malik in the other spelling, reported from God's Messenger:

> Openhandedness is a tree in the Garden whose branches are in this world; when someone latches on to one of its branches, it will lead him to the Garden. And niggardliness is a tree in the Fire whose branches are in this world; when someone latches on to one of its branches, it will lead him to the Fire.

Second are those who spend in vastness of blessings but not in narrowness and hardship. Most of God's creatures among world folk are in this station, lacking confidence for open-handedness, always fearing poverty. To them alludes, "If He asks you for them, then" they are pressed (47:37). Third are those who spend in both states. Such a person may be impudent and impure, not knowing whence he takes or where he gives, not thinking of outcome, numbered among brothers of Satan, "Surely the squanderers are the brothers of" Satan (17:27). Or he is confident in God's sufficiency and assignment of daily provision.

The latter has recognised Mustafa's, MuṣṬafā, report that the holy spirit, Ruh, ruh, breathed into his mind that no one will die until provision is complete. So be wary of God and go lightly in seeking. Never let tardiness of provision make you seek God's bounty through disobedience, for what is with God is reached only by obeying Him. Every man has provision coming inescapably. Approved, it is blessed and expanded. Not approved, it is not blessed nor expanded. Provision seeks a man as his moment of death seeks him. Such a person relies on God's treasury, keeps his heart straight, spends all he has and holds nothing back, bringing it to hand from its place under Shariah, shariah, and spending it in its place in conformity with Shariah. The Lord praises his spending. They do not become angry at anyone, place all sins on themselves, consider themselves subjected and dominated over by people, tolerate suffering or welcome it with patience and forbearance, bearing witness God knows and sees. They do not hoard anything from God and prefer Him over everything.

Pardon has two meanings. One is to efface, as Arabs say winds pardoned tracks. The other is surplus, as God says "Take to pardoning" (7:199), take surplus of their property. Those who pardon people pass over and efface people's sins, not limiting themselves to that. They caress them and bestow from surplus they own. That is beautiful-doers' attribute, and God is their Friend. Beautiful doing in interacting with Real is "to worship God as if you see Him." In interacting with people, it is being good toward someone bad toward you, and acting worthily toward someone who does not act worthily toward you. God commanded take to pardoning, take excellent and beautiful character traits, pardon those who wrong you, join those who cut off from you, act with beauty toward those who act with ugliness toward you.

Remaining apparatus includes the Path, the path, in (1:6), Abdur-Razzaq, Abdur-Razzaq, Al-Firdaws, Al-Firdaws, Al-Hadid, Al-Hadid, Jahannam, jahannam, Al-Kabir, al-Kabir, Mālik, Mālik, al-Razi in the report citation damaged as al-Razi, Muttaqin, muttaqin, Taqwa, taqwa, Say, say, Riba, riba, and collectors Al-Bazzar, Al-Bazzar.

### In short

- The God-fearing spend in ease and hardship, by night and day (2:274), in health and illness, more from more and less from less, even a grape, an onion or a date piece.
- They repress anger though able to act, pardon wrongdoers without ill feeling, and rise to doing good to the one who hurt them.
- Strength is mastering rage when angry, and a swallowed dose of rage fills the servant with faith and saves from Jahannam.
- Human rights come first in the traits, because losses between people are hard to forgive, and high morals turn enemies into fast friends (41:34, 7:199).

135.text:
The last trait concerns failure itself: "those who, upon committing an evil deed or wronging themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness and do not knowingly persist in sin". The God-fearing are not sinless. They remember, regret, ask, and stop.

### Phrase by phrase

**"those who, upon committing an evil deed or wronging themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness"**: Those who, when they have committed Fahishah, an immoral sin, an indecency, a despicable sin such as adultery, or wronged themselves with evil, with less than that such as a kiss, remember Allah, remember His threat of punishment and warning to wrongdoers and promise to the Mindful, and ask forgiveness for their sins. If they were to commit a major sin, or wrong themselves by a lesser sin, they remember Allah. They ask their Lord for forgiveness regretting what they did, asking Allah not to take them to account, and pray forgiveness.

**"and do not knowingly persist in sin—and who forgives sins except Allah"**: And who, that is none, shall forgive sins but God? None except Allah forgives sins. Allah alone can forgive. They do not persist in what wrong they have done, while they know, persevere, knowing that what they did was sinful, that they have done wrong and Allah forgives all disobedience. They have desisted from it, do not continue in disobedience, repent from error, return to Allah before death, do not insist on error, and if they err again they repent from it. "Whoever repents, then Allah will forgive him", Mujahid and 'Abdullah bin 'Ubayd bin 'Umayr, Ubayd bin 'Umayr, commented on "while they know". "Know they not that Allah accepts repentance from His servants" (9:104). "And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but afterwards seeks Allah's forgiveness, he will find Allah Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful" (4:110).

### Two occasions of a kiss and a stare

'Ata' reported that Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, said this was revealed about Nabhan, seller of dates. A beautiful woman came to buy dates from him. He hugged and kissed her, then regretted his action. He went to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned what he did. This verse was then revealed.
