### Earlier words of the same law

In Surat Al-Baqarah, Al-Baqarah, "Or think you that you will enter Paradise without such (trials) as came to those who passed away before you? They were afflicted with severe poverty and ailments and were so shaken" (2:214). "Alif Lam Mim. Do people think that they will be left alone because they say: 'We believe,' and will not be tested?" (29:1,2) in the citation form given. Ways before you at (3:137) supplies the nations. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, reads Allah may know in the previous verse as finding out who would be patient while fighting enemies. Muttaqin, muttaqin, have been described by spending, anger-control, pardoning and repentance. Say, say, Two Sahihs, two sahihs, and the path, the path, frame the demand.

When an individual resolves to follow God's path he is confronted with problems and difficulties created by others. Sometimes problems produce uncertainty. Sometimes they make him think of expediency. Sometimes they arouse negative feelings. Sometimes he is tempted to embrace a version of God's religion with great public appeal. Herein lies present world's test. Reaction shows whether he is false or true in acceptance of faith. If actions correspond to verbal claim, he is true. If not, false.

Becoming God's witness is journey's final destination. Imagine a servant who comes forward as preacher of truth. He fully practises what he preaches. People may regard him insignificant, and he does not mind. He faces difficulties and is not discouraged. He perseveres sending out truth's call. He is neither disheartened nor given to negative thinking. Even when he pays price with life and property his stand is not shaken. This test is momentous. Passing it is how God selects him as witness in divine court. Continuing to convey divine message despite adverse situations proves he is convinced of the message's truth. It also shows message he conveys is not trivial but extremely serious.

Status of witness in God's court, whose evidence decides eternal fate, is not strength of verbal claims. Patience exercised and struggle for God's cause prove genuineness. Difficulties stand in paths of personal faith and public witnessing alike.

Wish-thinking is exposed inwardly. The wish of those who think they can arrive at a greatly esteemed place without enduring hardships casts them into abyss of destruction. Those who recognise value of the place sought have exertion of pains made easy. "Time is not generous with its pleasures for those who are reluctant to throw off restraints." Their speaker said, "When youth is on the lookout for the lightning of meanings, al-ma'ānī, the least valuable use of time is the pleasantry of sleep."

### In short

- Paradise is not entered untested, before Allah outwardly knows who struggled in Jihad and who were patient against the enemy.
- Former peoples were afflicted with poverty, ailments and shaking (2:214), and saying "We believe" does not leave people untested (29:1).
- Reaction under problems created by others proves true or false acceptance, and passing the test makes a servant God's witness.

143.text:
The wish is now confronted with its fulfilment: "You certainly wished ˹for the opportunity˺ for martyrdom before encountering it, now you have seen it with your own eyes". Longing said, "Would that we had a day like Badr". Uhud gave the day, and the seeing exposed retreat.

### Phrase by phrase

**"You certainly wished ˹for the opportunity˺ for martyrdom before encountering it, now you have seen it with your own eyes"**: You did indeed wish for death, longing for death in war, tamannawna with one of two tā' letters omitted from original tatamannawna, before you met it in the field, on Uhud, Uhud, uhud, day. You wished to meet disbelievers so you could gain martyrdom for Allah's sake, like brothers on Badr, Badr, badr, day, before you saw severity and ways of death. You were longing when you said, "Would that we had a day like the Day of Badr in order to attain what its martyrs attained." Now you have seen it, the cause of it, war, looking on with eyes open and contemplating conditions, seen fighting and war on Uhud day, seen swords of unbelievers, ran away from them and did not remain unshaken with your Prophet. So why did you retreat? Before today you wished you could meet enemy and were eager to fight them. What you wished has occurred, so fight them and be patient.

### Death seen, not death imagined

Now you have seen it is explained as death seen when swords appeared, blades sharpened, spears crisscrossed and men stood in lines for battle. This part contains a figure of speech mentioning imagining what can be felt but not seen. Death is not an object of sight in itself. Its causes and conditions are seen with eyes. In the shortest gloss, you have seen what you wished for with your own eyes on Uhud day, severity included.

In the Two Sahihs, two sahihs, the Messenger ﷺ said:

> Do not wish to encounter the enemy, and ask Allah for your well-being. However, if you do encounter them, then observe patience and know that Paradise is under the shade of swords.

The wish examined here is therefore not condemned as simple love of martyrdom. It is measured by endurance after encounter. Longing before meeting and patience after meeting are together the proof demanded in the previous verse. Trials before you at (2:214), ways before you at (3:137), testing at (29:1), Al-Baqarah, Al-Baqarah, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, Jihad, jihad, Muttaqin, muttaqin, Say, say, and the path, the path, complete the frame.

Reaction under created difficulties shows true or false acceptance. A person may feel uncertainty, expediency, negative feelings, or attraction to a publicly appealing version of religion. Continuing to convey and practise truth, insignificant in people's eyes, undiscouraged, unshaken even at price of life and property, proves conviction that the message is serious. God selects such a one as witness.

Pangs of longing come after being patient in enduring difficulties, in the inward line. "When tears flow down cheeks, the one who is crying is distinguished from the one who is only pretending." Seeing separates pretended longing from real longing as tears separate pretended grief from real grief.

### In short

- Believers longed for death and a day like Badr before meeting it, and at Uhud saw war, swords and death's causes with their own eyes.
- The rebuke is retreat after fulfilment of the wish, not the wish itself, and the command is to fight and be patient now it has come.
- Do not wish to encounter the enemy, but if encountered, observe patience, for Paradise is under swords' shade.

144.text:
The rumour is answered by a definition: "Muḥammad is no more than a messenger; other messengers have gone before him. If he were to die or to be killed, would you regress into disbelief?" A messenger can die. The God he delivered cannot, and gratitude is staying firm either way.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Muḥammad is no more than a messenger; other messengers have gone before him"**: Muhammad is no more than, only, a Messenger. Indeed Messengers have passed away before him, like whom other messengers passed away. He is to deliver Allah's Message and may be killed in the process, just as happened to many Prophets before. Muhammad, MuḤammad, is only a Messenger like messengers of Allah before him, who died or were killed. He was not a worshipped being, so if he were to die, turning back to previous religion does not follow.

**"If he were to die or to be killed, would you regress into disbelief? Those who do so will not harm Allah whatsoever. And Allah will reward those who are grateful"**: If he dies or is killed, will you then turn back on your heels, return to your old religion and unbelief, Kufr, kufr. The last statement is the locus of an interrogative of denial. He who turns back on his heels, returns to old religion, not the least harm will he do to Allah, does no hurt to Allah in any way, but harms himself, exposing himself to loss in this world and Afterlife. Allah, Strong and Victorious in that gloss, is unharmed. Allah will reward and give reward to the grateful, thankful, believers for faith and Jihad, jihad, those who obeyed Allah, defended His religion and followed His Messenger ﷺ whether alive or dead, thankful for His graces by staying firm, firm in faith and struggling for His sake.

### The rumour at Uhud

When Muslims suffered defeat at Uhud, Uhud, uhud, and some were killed, Shaytan shouted, "Muhammad has been killed." Ibn Qami'ah went back to idolators claiming, "I have killed Muhammad." Some Muslims believed the rumour and thought Messenger ﷺ had been killed, claiming this could happen, for Allah narrated that this occurred to many Prophets before. Therefore resolve was weakened and they did not actively participate in battle. Allah sent down this statement.

Ibn Abi Najih said his father said a man from the Muhajirin passed by an Ansari man who was bleeding during Uhud and said, "O fellow! Did you know that Muhammad was killed?" The Ansari man said:

> Even if Muhammad was killed, he has indeed conveyed the Message. Therefore, defend your religion.

This story was collected by Al-Hafiz, Al-Hafiz, Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi, Al-Bayhaqi, in Dala'il An-Nubuwwah, An-Nubuwwah.

When they said to the Messenger ﷺ, "O Prophet of Allah! We heard that you were killed, this is why we ran from the enemy," this revelation is the setting named in one gloss. With regard to being routed when it was rumoured the Prophet had been killed, and hypocrites had said to believers, "If he has been killed go back to your previous religion," this was revealed.

### A principle settled through love

Four to five sections of this Surah are devoted to Uhud's victory and defeat sequence and guidance beneath it. The frightening warning to noble Companions over some indiscretion settles a principle. Islam gives great importance to unique respect and love for the Prophet ﷺ, made integral to Faith, slightest deviation equated with straight kufr. At the same time Muslims must not fall prey to the disease that afflicted Nazarenes and Christians. They exaggerated respect and love due to Sayyidna Isa, Isa, isa, taking it to extremes, invested him with partnership in divinity, and started to worship him.

When rumour of the Prophet's ﷺ passing came during temporary setback, agony seized Companions as a direct natural reaction. Only one with knowledge of their supreme love could guess that distress. These blessed souls staked everything, money, property, children and very lives, for mentor and Messenger's sake, considering sacrifices most desirable achievement of mortal life and proving it by deeds. Imagine devotees hearing that pivot of struggle and symbol of hopes had passed, battle in full cry, defeat looming after initial victory, Muslims losing ground.

Natural outcome was a large group retreating in confusion. Retreat was fleeting confusion, without indication of turning away from Islam. Allah intended to mould Companions of His Messenger, pious and angelic, into role models for the whole world. An ordinary mistake by them was therefore considered very serious. They were addressed on retreating as if they had deserted the fold of Islam. With that wrath, warning was given that obligations of Faith, Worship and Jihad are for Allah who is Living and Eternal. Even if news of martyrdom were true, it would have come when appointed. Losing heart and abandoning Faith's dictates did not behave those in their position.

Muslims are warned Messenger ﷺ will leave mortal world one day or another, but they must hold Faith firmly after him in same measure as during his blessed times. Injury at Uhud and news of passing were a concealed divine arrangement through which all that could happen to Companions after him was revealed during his lifetime. Any slip could be corrected in the Prophet's ﷺ words, ensuring ardent lovers do not lose coolness under exacting conditions, especially when his actual passing takes place.

Real servants of God are those whose religiosity is not based on a human personality. God requires religiosity attaching servants with hearts and souls to the one God. A believer follows Islam for truth of its principles rather than support of some human individual. Entering Islam in that way, he finds it such a blessing that spirit overflows with gratitude to God. He regards Hereafter, not this world, as all in all. Life becomes transient. He discerns universe as a divine workshop, every happening at God's will, God both Giver and Taker.

### Abu Bakr recites it at the real death

That preparation bore fruit later. Even greatest Companions were overwhelmed with severest emotional shock at his actual passing. Sayyidna Abu Bakr, Abu Bakr, used authority of Qur'anic verses such as these to explain the situation, and all accepted truth and controlled emotions.

Collections named Sahih, Musnad and Sunan gathered various chains stating Abu Bakr recited this verse when Messenger ﷺ died. Al-Bukhari, Al-Bukhari, recorded that 'A'ishah said Abu Bakr came riding his horse from his dwelling in As-Sunh, As-Sunh. He dismounted, entered Masjid, and did not speak to anyone until he came to her room and went directly to the Prophet, covered with a marked blanket. Abu Bakr uncovered his face, knelt and kissed him, then wept and proclaimed:

> My father and my mother be sacrificed for you! Allah will not combine two deaths on you. You have died the death, which was written for you.

Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, narrated Abu Bakr then came out while Umar, Umar, 'Umar, was addressing people. Abu Bakr told him to sit down, but Umar refused. People attended to Abu Bakr and left Umar. Abu Bakr said:

> To proceed; whoever among you worshipped Muhammad, then Muhammad is dead, but whoever worshipped Allah, Allah is alive and will never die.

He then recited Allah's statement, "Muhammad is no more than a Messenger and indeed Messengers have passed away before him", through whoever turns back not harming Allah and Allah rewarding the grateful. The narrator added, by Allah, it was as if people never knew Allah had revealed this verse before until Abu Bakr recited it, and whoever heard it started reciting it. Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib said Umar said, "By Allah! When I heard Abu Bakr recite this Ayah, my feet could not hold me, and I fell to the ground."

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Abi, Ibn Abi, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Zayd, Ibn Zayd, Ata' Al-Khurasani, Ata' Al-Khurasani, Habib bin Suhban, Habib bin Suhban, Al-Amawi, Al-Amawi, As-Suhayli, As-Suhayli, As-Sunh, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Jarir, Al-Hasan, Hasan, the Path, the path, and the grade apparatus belong to the next verses in this shared block. Abu Bakr evidence is singled out inwardly. As much as Muhammad is praised and chosen among all men and caressed by God of world's folk, pole of world, lamp of heaven and earth, chieftain and full moon of universe, emulated by creatures, paragon of engendered beings and Seal of Prophets, despite all this he is mortal man. Death is fitting for him and annihilation applies to him. As many prophets as there have been, all went. The Real did not disappear, nor was God harmed. Real remained after all, God their keeper in perfection of exaltedness.

By allusion, folk of realisation are addressed. Perfection of Our exaltedness is free of need for that which was not, then came to be. No link exists between lordhood and contingent beings. Unity does not call for an existence-giver, Being does not need a strengthener. A sound report has God say:

> O My servants! If the first of you and the last of you, the men of you and jinn of you, the living of you and the dead of you, had the heart of the most godwary man among you, that would add nothing to My kingdom. O My servants! If the first of you and the last of you, the men of you and jinn of you, the living of you and the dead of you, had the heart of the most depraved man among you, that would take nothing away from My kingdom.

This verse provides evidence for Abu Bakr's eminence. When Mustafa, MuṣṬafā, was taken from this house of decrees and steed of death sent for his prophethood's shining face, in attribute of exaltedness Divine Presence snatched that shining face away from steed of death and took him into embrace of Unity.

### In short

- Muhammad is only a Messenger like dead or killed messengers before him, not a worshipped being whose death ends religion.
- Turning back harms only the turner, while Allah rewards the grateful who obey and defend His religion alive or dead.
- The Uhud rumour, Shaytan's shout and Ibn Qami'ah's claim, weakened resolve and drew this correction, answered on the field by a bleeding Ansari.
- Abu Bakr's recitation of it at the Prophet's actual death, from As-Sunh, settled Umar and the people, fulfilling Uhud's preparation.

145.text:
Death is removed from human negotiation: "No soul can ever die without Allah’s Will at the destined time. Those who desire worldly gain, We will let them have it, and those who desire heavenly reward, We will grant it to them". Retreat does not lengthen life, advance does not shorten it, and desire decides the share.

### Phrase by phrase

**"No soul can ever die without Allah’s Will at the destined time"**: No person can ever die except by Allah's leave, will and decree, and at an appointed term. It is not for any soul to die save by God's leave. A prescribed term, kitāban here a verbal noun, God has prescribed this term, a term fixed in time, neither brought forward nor deferred. Soul dies when time Allah has written comes to an end, set time arrived, life neither longer nor shorter. No one dies except by Allah's decision after finishing the term Allah destined. "And no aged man is granted a length of life nor is a part cut off from his life, but it is in a Book" (35:11). "He it is Who has created you from clay, and then has decreed a (stated) term (for you to die). And there is with Him another determined term (for you to be resurrected)" (6:2). A man's lifespan and sustenance are both registered at an appointed term, none shall take place before due time.

**"Those who desire worldly gain, We will let them have it, and those who desire heavenly reward, We will grant it to them. And Allah will reward those who are grateful"**: Whoever desires a reward in the world, benefit of worldly life with his works and Jihad, jihad, We shall give him of it, from worldly life what he desires, what Allah decides and decrees. Whoever works for this life only earns what Allah decides he will earn, and will not have a share in Hereafter. Whoever desires reward in Hereafter, benefit of Hereafter with works and jihad, We shall give him thereof, of its reward and what he desires, also, along with what He decides for him in this life. "Whosoever desires (by his deeds) the reward of the Hereafter, We give him increase in his reward, and whosoever desires the reward of this world (by his deeds), We give him thereof (what is decreed for him), and he has no portion in the Hereafter" (42:20). "Whoever desires the quick-passing (transitory enjoyment of this world), We readily grant him what We will for whom We like. Then, afterwards, We have appointed for him Hell; he will burn therein disgraced and despised. And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it, with the necessary effort due for it while he is a believer, then such are the ones whose striving shall be appreciated" (17:18-19). We shall reward the grateful, thankful, believers for faith and jihad. We shall award them with Our favour and mercy in this life and Hereafter, according to degree of appreciation of Allah and good deeds.

### Courage from a fixed term

This verse encourages cowards to participate in battle. Doing so or avoiding battle neither decreases nor increases life term. So why did you retreat in defeat? Defeat does not ward off death, nor standing one's ground sever life.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that Habib bin Suhban, Habib bin Suhban, said a Muslim man, Hujr bin 'Adi, said in a battle, "What prevents you from crossing this river (the Euphrates) to the enemy?" He recited in substance, no person can die except by Allah's leave and at appointed term. He crossed the river riding his horse, and Muslims followed him. When enemy saw them, they started shouting, "Diwan", Persian for crazy, and ran away.

Death of every human being lies written. Fixed is date, day and time. Death cannot come before, nor can one live after. Getting scared about a certain death means nothing. Steadfastness under calamities follows.

The case of archers is then hinted. Guards posted on the rear hill saw fellow Muslims collecting spoils after initial victory. Some thought victory left no need to stay at post. Why not also take part in collection? They moved away from where they were ordered to be. End of the verse, seeking return in world and return in Hereafter, comments on that choice.

Collection of spoils in its real sense is not unabashed pursuit of material condemned by Islamic Law, Islamic law. Collecting spoils, depositing in safe custody, and spending where it must be spent is part of Jihad, an act of worship. Companions in this mission never did it for sheer material gain. They would be entitled to due share in spoils even without actively participating in collection, as guaranteed under Islamic Law. Blessed Companions cannot be said to abandon duty under temptation of worldly gain. But minor mistakes by major people draw attention. Ordinary deviation is taken seriously and admonished, to take morals to highest level. Their act was identified as seeking return in this world so that tiniest speck of worldly temptation fails to find way into hearts. Granted at most some minor connection with desire for worldly gain, equally granted that possibility had not influenced hearts.

Names framing the block are Abu Bakr, Abu Bakr, Al-Amawi, Al-Amawi, Ata' Al-Khurasani, Ata' Al-Khurasani, Al-Hafiz, Al-Hafiz, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Abi, Ibn Abi, Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Zayd, Ibn Zayd, Isa in the previous verse, An-Nubuwwah, An-Nubuwwah, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, As-Suhayli, As-Suhayli, As-Sunh, As-Sunh, the Path, the path, Uhud, Uhud, Umar, Umar. Collectors Al-Bayhaqi, Al-Bayhaqi, Al-Bukhari, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Jarir. Grade Al-Hasan, Hasan. 'Āqiba, 'āqiba, end, belongs inwardly below. Say, say.

Breaths have a set duration for which there is no increase or decrease. Righteous have what comes in end, 'āqiba. Others have heedlessness, ghafla. Reward of Hereafter is first forgiveness, ghufrān, then gardens, jinān, then beatitude, riḍwān. Requital for thankfulness is thankfulness.

A believer whose religiosity attaches him to God, not a personality, regards Hereafter as all in all. He knows death may come at any point. He is able to discern universe as divine workshop where each happening takes place at God's will and God is both Giver and Taker.

### In short

- No Soul dies except by Allah's leave at a prescribed term, fixed in a Book (35:11, 6:2), neither advanced nor deferred.
- Fixed death encourages battle, as Hujr bin 'Adi crossing the Euphrates showed, since retreat wards off nothing and standing severs nothing.
- Worldly desirers receive only what is decreed and no Hereafter portion (42:20, 17:18-19), while Hereafter desirers receive its reward and grateful are rewarded in both worlds.

146.text:
Earlier prophets' followers supply the model Uhud lacked: "how many devotees fought along with their prophets and never faltered despite whatever ˹losses˺ they suffered in the cause of Allah, nor did they weaken or give in! Allah loves those who persevere". Death and wounds did not make them lose heart, weaken, or surrender.

### Phrase by phrase

**"how many devotees fought along with their prophets and never faltered despite whatever ˹losses˺ they suffered in the cause of Allah, nor did they weaken or give in! Allah loves those who persevere"**: Many a Prophet fought, and along with him many Ribbiyyun, devoted men. Many prophets fought with many groups of followers against scores of unbelievers. They never lost heart and quailed not for what befell them in Allah's way, in terms of death and injury. Nor did they weaken, lack strength to fight enemies, become feeble in face of enemy, or degrade and humble themselves, abase themselves before enemy or surrender and give in to enemy. As you did when it was said Prophet ﷺ had been killed, in the direct rebuke form. Allah loves the patient, steadfast, in fighting enemy alongside their Prophet, patient during trials, meaning He will reward them. Allah loves those patient with hardship and misfortune for His sake.

### Who are the Ribbiyyun, and what befell them

It was said this means many Prophets and their companions were killed in earlier times, view chosen by Ibn Jarir, Ibn Jarir. It was also said many Prophets witnessed companions' death before their eyes. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Ishaq, mentioned another explanation in his Sirah. Many a Prophet was killed, and he had many companions whose resolve did not weaken after their Prophet died. They did not become feeble before enemy. What they suffered in Jihad, jihad, in Allah's cause and for religion did not make them lose heart. This is patience, "and Allah loves the patient." As-Suhayli, As-Suhayli, agreed with this explanation and defended it vigorously. This view is supported by "And along with him many Ribbiyyun" following. In his book about battles, Al-Amawi, Al-Amawi, mentioned only this explanation.

A variant reading matters. How many a prophet has been killed, qutila, a variant has qātala, has fought. The subject of verb, person governing it, and with him, ma'ahu, has predicate subject following. Thousands manifold fought, but fainted not, did not shrink facing what afflicted them in God's way, wounds and slaying of prophets and companions. They neither weakened facing struggle nor humbled themselves nor succumbed to enemy.

Sufyan Ath-Thawri reported Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Mas'ud, said many Ribbiyyun means thousands. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id bin Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi' and 'Ata' Al-Khurasani, Ata' Al-Khurasani, said Ribbiyyun means large bands. 'Abdur-Razzaq narrated Ma'mmar said Al-Hasan, al-Basri in the checklist as al-Basri, said it means many scholars. He also said patient and pious scholars.

Word explanation deepens it. Ribbiyun derives from Rabb like Rabbani, meaning of the Rabb or Lord, rendered men of Allah. Use of vowel i in place of a is irregular in that citation. Some take Ribbiyun as many groups, derived from Ribbah, group. Who is meant is reported from Abdullah ibn Abbas and Hasan al-Basri as ulama, religious scholars, and fuqaha, jurisconsults. Istakanu derives from istakanah and means to be subdued, rendered weak and immobile. Wahanu derives from wahn and means to lose heart under suffering, or wilt under pressure.

Qatadah and Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, said nor did they weaken means after their Prophet was killed. Nor degrade themselves is by reverting from true guidance and religion. Rather they fought on the path, the path, Allah's Prophet fought on until they met Allah. Ibn 'Abbas said nor degrade themselves means nor became humiliated, while As-Suddi and Ibn Zayd, Ibn Zayd, said they did not give in to enemy.

Examples set by men of Allah from earlier communities are cited for present addressees to emulate, after admonition for shortcomings at Uhud, Uhud. They were not cowardly about fighting because of death and wounds received for Allah's sake. They did not weaken fighting enemy or surrender, but were patient and firm.

Apparatus terms include Abu Bakr, Abu Bakr, Habib bin Suhban, Habib bin Suhban, Al-Hafiz, Al-Hafiz, Ibn Abi, Ibn Abi, An-Nubuwwah, An-Nubuwwah, Hadith, hadith, in the saying that without Allah's grace no guidance, Zakah, zakah, or Salah, salah, would be possible, Ruh, ruh, Say, say, As-Sunh, As-Sunh, Umar, Umar, Collectors Al-Bayhaqi, Al-Bayhaqi, Al-Bukhari, Al-Bukhari, grade Al-Hasan, Hasan, and cited verses (6:2), (17:18-19), (35:11), (42:20).

Those who followed course in fidelity, stood fast regarding purity, did not withdraw from path, demanded realisation of themselves, reproaching themselves by restriction and scrutiny, found love of Real as legacy for patience. Real was what came after for them at end of affair, since they did not swerve from required effort or protection of pact, and submitted themselves utterly abandoning present world. Every one was constant and abiding holding to pact, staying true to condition of service and love. Status is earned only when believer passed tests, eyes set on God even when apparent supports crumbled, life at risk not depressing him, not retreating seeing destruction of worldly position. Remaining united at crucial moments, adhering strictly and patiently to truth, make believers deserving of divine succour.

### In short

- Many prophets fought, or were killed, with thousands, large bands, or patient pious scholars, the Ribbiyyun, beside them.
- They did not lose heart at death and wounds in Allah's way, did not weaken after prophets were killed, and did not surrender or revert.
- Allah loves the patient and steadfast during trials, and that endurance after a prophet's death is the model for Uhud.

147.text:
Their speech under trial is given whole: "And all they said was, “Our Lord! Forgive our sins and excesses, make our steps firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”" Steadfast fighters pray first against themselves, then for firm feet, then for victory.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And all they said was, “Our Lord! Forgive our sins and excesses, make our steps firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”"**: They said nothing but, "Our Lord! Forgive us our sins and our transgressions and wasted efforts and excesses, overstepping bounds in our affairs. Establish our feet firmly, make our foothold sure in war. And give us victory over the disbelieving folk." Their cry, believers' cry after killing of their prophet in one gloss, was only that they said, "O our Lord! Forgive us for our sins", sins other than enormities, "and wasted efforts" by committing grave sins, enormities. Make firm our feet with strength for struggle, help us against unbelieving folk. Patient people asked Allah to forgive disobedience and overstepping limits in what they did, make feet firm when they meet enemy, and help them against those who disbelieved in Him.

### Prayer before pride

After citing men of Allah fighting along with previous prophets undeterred against heavy odds, another quality is named. In spite of sacrificing conduct they kept praying to forgive past sins, condone shortcomings that may have crept in during present Jihad, jihad, efforts, enable them to remain steadfast, and make them prevail over enemies. This statement they kept repeating.

A true Muslim who knows things as they are is not proud of a good deed accomplished. No matter how great the accomplishment or exacting the struggle, he does not pat himself on back. Very accomplishment is direct outcome of Allah's grace and mercy. No good deed can issue forth without it. A hadith, hadith, says:

> Had it not been for the grace and mercy of Allah, we would have not received guidance in the straight path, nor we would have been able to pay zakah and perform salah.

Zakah, zakah, and Salah, salah, are named there. Seeking forgiveness is necessary under all conditions. Ability to perform a good deed does not put exact performance within one's control, in accordance with demands of supreme magnificence of One holding reins of Creation and Command. Hard trying still falls short, especially in doing things as Allah's due and right. Seeking forgiveness is therefore necessary during very course of such a deed.

Continuity cannot be predicted. Who can say for sure he will be given ability to continue a good deed in future as now? All is Taufiq, God-given ability to perform good. Repent over shortcomings in present, and pray Allah makes us steadfast and persistent in future. For a true Muslim this prayer should become second nature. ### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, Allah fulfilled His promise to you when you ˹initially˺ swept them away by His Will"**: Allah did indeed fulfil, made good and has been true to, His promise to you of victory over enemies on Uhud, Uhud, uhud, day, in beginning of the day, when you were killing and routing them, engaging them in battle, slaying enemies, by His permission, leave, command and help, for He allowed you to do that against them. You slew them by His will until a response is implied, when you lost heart He denied you His assistance.

Ibn Jurayj said Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, said Fashiltum means lost courage. And fell to disputing and quarrelling about the order and question of war. And disobeyed such as mistake made by archers, disobeyed Prophet by leaving positions, his command to remain at foot of mountain for arrow attack. Some said let us depart, for comrades have been given victory. Others said we should not disobey Prophet's command. You disobeyed his command and abandoned station in search of booty, after He showed you what you love and long for, victory over disbelievers and assistance and booty.

**"Some of you were after worldly gain while others desired a heavenly reward. He denied you victory over them as a test, yet He has pardoned you. And Allah is Gracious to the believers"**: Among you, some of archers, desired this world with Jihad, jihad, and fighting, abandoning station for booty, those who left positions to obtain gains of war. Some desired Hereafter with jihad and fighting, holding to station until slain, such as Abd Allāh, 'Abdullah bin Jubayr, Abdullah bin Jubayr, Ibn Jubayr, and companions who stayed at positions obeying Messenger's command until killed. Then He made you flee from them, turned you away, thumma sarafakum, supplement to implied response raddakum bi'l-hazīma, He turned you back in defeat, made them triumph and gave them power over you, that He might test and try you, make manifest sincere from otherwise, make clear believers patient with trials from those who abandoned positions and became weak. But surely He forgave you, He has pardoned you what you have done, did not exterminate you. Allah is Most Gracious, Lord of Kindness and Bounteous, to believers, in not exterminating archers, guiding them to faith, forgiving disobedience and rewarding difficulties. He forgave error because, and Allah knows best, idolators were many and well supplied, while Muslims had few men and few supplies.

### The archers' dispute and the duel of slogans

Al-Bukhari, Al-Bukhari, recorded Al-Bara, Al-Bara', said we met idolators that day and Prophet ﷺ appointed 'Abdullah bin Jubayr commander of archers. He instructed them to retain position. Only Al-Bukhari collected this Hadith, hadith, using this chain. That note belongs to the battle report as a whole.

Abu Sufyan, Abu Sufyan, then shouted questions about who was present, Muhammad, son of Abu Quhafah, Abu Quhafah, Abu Bakr, and son of Al-Khattab, Al-Khattab. Twice the Prophet ﷺ ordered silence. >
> Allah is Higher and more Sublime.
>
> We have the (idol) Al-'Uzza, Al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza.

>

They uncovered our back lines to disbelievers' horsemen, who took chance and attacked from behind. Then a person shouted, "Muhammad has been killed." We pulled back, and disbelievers followed us, after we had killed those who carried their flag, and none dared come close to flag, until then. Disbelievers' flag was left on ground until 'Amrah bint 'Alqamah Al-Harithiyyah, Al-Harithiyyah, picked it up and gave it to Quraysh, quraysh, who held it.

### Did the Companions tilt towards the material?

Noble Companions made an error of judgement. Graces beside warning need notice. By saying so He may test you, temporary setback is cleared from being punishment. It was to test them. Then comes proclamation, of course We have forgiven you.

Those split in two groups, some sought mundane while others sought Hereafter. What identifies seekers of mundane is intention to collect spoils equated with seeking mundane. If they had held assigned post and not taken part in collection, would due share have been lesser? Did participation entitle larger share? Law of Spoils as proved by Qur'an and Hadith is common knowledge. They as first observers knew beyond doubt due share was subject to being no more or less. Share would remain same whether helping collection or remaining on guard. Action cannot be classed as unqualified pursuit of material. It is participation in what mujahidin are supposed to do. Given human nature, thought of spoils entering hearts is not totally unimaginable. Allah likes to see hearts of Messenger's Companions clean and untouched even by remotest idea of tilt towards material possession. Very idea of going to possess things of dunya has been equated with seeking of mundane, explaining divine distaste.

Tilt in this verse's gloss was already treated in verse 145. They would have been entitled to share whether or not collecting. Collecting, depositing and spending spoils is itself part of Jihad. At most a minor speck of worldly desire is targeted, to take morals to highest level. High station of noble Companions is therefore maintained alongside clear proclamation of forgiveness.

### Anas bin An-Nadr

Al-Bukhari recorded Anas bin Malik said his uncle Anas bin An-Nadr was absent from Badr. He said he was absent from first battle Prophet ﷺ fought against pagans. By Allah, if Allah gives him a chance to fight along with Messenger, Allah will see how bravely he will fight. On Uhud day when Muslims turned backs and fled, he said, "O Allah! I apologize to You for what these (meaning Muslims) have done, and I denounce what these pagans have done." Then he advanced lifting sword. Sa'd bin Mu'adh met him. He said to him, "O Sa'd bin Mu'adh! Where are you! Paradise! I am smelling its aroma coming from before (Mount) Uhud". He went forth, fought, was killed. We found more than eighty stab wounds, sword blows or arrow holes on his body, mutilated so badly none except his sister could recognise him, only by fingers or a mole. Muslim, in Two Sahihs, Two Sahihs, also collected similar narration from Thabit from Anas.

Inwardly, a person's worth is his desire, and want is his leader. One wants this world, another afterworld, another the Patron. Wanting this world is trickery and delusion, wanting afterworld is occupation with wage-earners' work, wanting Patron is celebration and joy. Seeker of this world is wounded by fantasy, seeker of afterworld attached to palaces and houris, seeker of Patron in ocean of Solitariness, inundated by light. Dhu'l-Nūn the Egyptian said:

> O God, if I have any share of this world, I have given it to strangers. If I have anything stored up for the afterworld, I give it to the faithful. In this world, remembering You is enough for me, and in the afterworld seeing You is enough for me.

This world and afterworld are two commodities, vision is hard cash given. Broker of this world is Iblis. He offers wares at auction in bazaar of abandonment and adorns them for people. God says reporting from him, "I shall surely adorn for them what is in the earth" (15:39). Iblis's buyer is unbeliever. Price is abandoning religion and sheer associationism. Mustafa is broker of Paradise, offers at auction of solicitude in bazaar of afterworld. Buyer is God and sellers are faithful. Price is formula "There is no god but God." The Prophet said, "The price of the Garden is There is no god but God."

Pir of Tariqah said, I see a group distracted from Him by this world, a group distracted from Him by that world, and a group distracted from both worlds by Him. They wait to see when breeze of felicity will blow from side of proximity and sun of union will shine from mansion of solicitude. They weep with selflessness's tongue and say in hope, "O generous one! How can someone who yearns for You put up with life? He who hopes for you has a breast full of blood at hands of Your friendship!" "Without You, O ease of my spirit, how can I live? If You are not by my side, how can I be happy?"

### In short

- Allah fulfilled His promise by His leave at Uhud's start, then courage failed, archers disputed the order and disobeyed after victory was shown.
- Some archers desired this world and left for booty, while 'Abdullah bin Jubayr and companions desired Hereafter and held position until slain.
- He denied victory as a test to manifest sincere from otherwise, yet proclaimed pardon, Gracious to believers.
- The archers' due share would not have increased by collecting, so the rebuke targets even a remote tilt to dunya in hearts Allah keeps clean.

153.text:
The flight itself is put before their eyes: "when you were running far away ˹in panic˺—not looking at anyone—while the Messenger was calling to you from behind! So Allah rewarded your disobedience with distress upon distress". Grief is made into a teacher, so that later grief loses its power.

### Phrase by phrase

**"when you were running far away ˹in panic˺—not looking at anyone—while the Messenger was calling to you from behind!"**: And remember when you, Tus'iduna, ran away dreadfully, ascending and fleeing in distance, without even casting a side glance at anyone, not turning around and not stopping for anyone, paid no heed to anyone and did not wait for him. Al-Hasan and Qatadah, Qatadah, said Tus'iduna means go up the mountain. You did not glance at anyone else due to shock, fear and fright. And the Messenger was in your rear calling you back, calling you to fight, behind you saying, between you and idolaters, "I am Allah's Messenger, stop and fight!", "Come to me, servants of God this way, servants of God!", "Come to me, O servants of Allah! Come to me, O servants of Allah!" For you left him behind while he was calling you to stop fleeing from enemy and return and fight. Allah made disbelievers leave you after you went up mount escaping enemy.

**"So Allah rewarded your disobedience with distress upon distress. Now, do not grieve over the victory you were denied or the injury you suffered. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do"**: There did Allah give you one distress after another, grief over grief, ghamman bi-ghamm, by way of requital. He rewarded, He requited, you with grief through defeat for grief. Bā' bi in bi-ghamm is said to mean 'alā, for, because of grief you caused Prophet when you disobeyed his command, grief doubled in addition to grief of booty forfeited. So that, li-kaylā connected either to 'afā, He has pardoned, or athābakum, He rewarded you, lā of kay-lā thus extra, you might not grieve for what escaped you of booty, neither for what befell you of being slain and defeat. To teach you not to grieve for that which had escaped you, booty and triumph over enemy, nor for what struck you, injury and fatalities. Allah is Well-Aware, Informed and All-Aware, of all that you do, in Jihad, jihad, as well as in defeat, of everything you do and everything in hearts. All praise is due to Him and thanks, no deity worthy of worship except Him, Most High and Most Honored.

### Where they ran, and why they did not hear

As-Suddi, As-Suddi, said when disbelievers attacked Muslim lines at Uhud and defeated them, some Muslims ran away to Al-Madinah, Al-Madinah, while some went up Mount Uhud, Uhud, uhud, to a rock and stood on it. Messenger ﷺ kept heralding, "Come to me, O servants of Allah!" Allah mentioned Muslims went up Mount, and Prophet ﷺ called them to come back.

Exit from battlefield and inability to return even when called by Prophet in person, consequent grief afflicting him because of conduct, and later Companions feeling sorry for sorrow they brought on master, are the sequence described. According to hadith, hadith, narrations, when Sayyidna Ka'b ibn Malik called out to them Muslims heard his call and reassembled.

Ruh al-Ma'ani's author, named through al-Ma'ani, al-Ma'ani, in this block, resolves this by saying first call came from Messenger himself, could not be heard by Companions, and they kept going as they were. That was time Sayyidna Ka'b ibn Malik called. Everybody heard him and reassembled.

Another explanation given in a named commentary there, through Ashraf Thanavi's name in the block's wording, says real reason was confusion from news that Prophet ﷺ had fallen as martyr. When he called, there was obviously no refutation of news with the call. Even if voice reached retreating Companions, possibility remains it was not recognized. Finally Ka'b ibn Malik's call included refutation, mentioning Messenger ﷺ was alive. On hearing, everybody sighed in relief and reassembled. Displeasure of Allah and sorrow of Messenger can be explained by saying if they had stayed unagitated and firm they could have recognized calling voice.

### Who stayed with the Messenger

Al-Bukhari recorded Qays bin Abi Hazim, Abi Hazim, said, "I saw Talhah's hand, it was paralyzed, because he shielded the Prophet ﷺ with it", meaning on Uhud day. It is recorded in Two Sahihs, Two Sahihs, that Abu 'Uthman An-Nahdi, An-Nahdi, Abu 'Uthman, said, "On that day (Uhud) during which the Prophet ﷺ fought, only Talhah bin 'Ubaydullah and Sa'd remained with the Prophet."

Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib, Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib, Al-Musayyib, said he heard Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas, Abi Waqqas, say, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me arrows from his quiver on the day of Uhud and said, 'Shoot, may I sacrifice my father and mother for you.'" Al-Bukhari also collected this Hadith.

Two Sahihs recorded Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas say on Uhud day he saw two men wearing white clothes, one to right of Prophet ﷺ and one to left, defending Prophet fiercely. He had never seen those men before or after that day, meaning angels Jibril, jibril, and Mika'il, mikail.

### Ubayy bin Khalaf

Abu Al-Aswad said 'Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, said Ubayy bin Khalaf, Ubayy, of Bani Jumah swore in Makkah, makkah, that he would kill Messenger ﷺ. When Messenger was told of vow, he said, "Rather, I shall kill him, Allah willing." On Uhud day Ubayy came wearing iron shields and proclaiming, "May I not be saved, if Muhammad is saved." He headed towards Messenger intending to kill him, but Mus'ab bin 'Umayr, from Bani Abd Ad-Dar, Abd Ad-Dar, intercepted him and shielded Prophet with his body, and Mus'ab bin 'Umayr was killed. Messenger ﷺ saw Ubayy's neck exposed between shields and helmet, stabbed him with spear, and Ubayy fell from his horse. No blood spilled from wound. His people carried him away while he was moaning like an ox. They said, "Why are you so anxious, it is only a flesh wound". Ubayy mentioned Prophet's vow, "Rather, I shall kill Ubayy", then commented, "By He in Whose Hand is my soul! If what hit me hits the people of Dhul-Majaz (a popular pre-Islamic marketplace), they would all have perished." He died and went to Fire, "So, away with the dwellers of the blazing Fire!" (67:11). This was collected by Musa bin 'Uqbah from Az-Zuhri, Az-Zuhri, from Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib.

### The injured face

It is recorded in Two Sahih that when asked about injuries Messenger ﷺ sustained at Uhud, Sahl bin Sa'd, Sahl bin Sa'd, said face of Allah's Messenger ﷺ was injured, front tooth broken and helmet smashed on his head. Therefore Fatimah, daughter of Allah's Messenger, washed off blood while 'Ali was pouring water on her hand. When Fatimah saw bleeding increased more by water, she took a mat, burnt it, and placed ashes in Prophet's ﷺ wound and blood stopped oozing out.

### Two griefs, in several orders

He gave you grief over grief. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, said first grief was because of defeat, especially when rumoured Muhammad ﷺ was killed. Second grief was when idolators went up mount and Messenger ﷺ said, "O Allah! It is not for them to rise above us."

'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf, Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf, said first distress was because of defeat, second because rumour Muhammad ﷺ was killed, which to them was worse than defeat. Ibn Marduwyah, Ibn Marduwyah, recorded both. Mujahid and Qatadah said first distress was hearing Muhammad ﷺ was killed, second suffering casualties and injury. It has been reported Qatadah and Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, Ar-Rabi bin Anas, Ar-Rabi', Ar-Rabi, said it was opposite order. As-Suddi said first distress was victory and booty missed, second enemy rising above them on mount. In addition to grief wrought by Khalid Ibn al-Walid, Ibn al-Walid, He also inflicted grief of death and defeat in another gloss. First because of victory and gains lost, then rumour Prophet had been killed, later knew Prophet had not been killed, gives a third sequence.

Verse forms part of several previous verses, first verse here mentioning sorrows, second antidote, third reiterating form of defeat was no punishment, test to separate true sincere Muslims from hypocrites. Finally repeated proclamation mistake has been forgiven.

Remaining names, reordered, include Ibn Zayd, Jabir bin 'Abdullah, Jabir bin 'Abdullah, Ibn al-Ashraf through Ka'b, Al-Bara, ansar, Ansar, badr, Abu Bakr, Abu Quhafah, Al-Khattab, kufr, Al-Madinah, Muhammad bin Ishaq, An-Nadr, say, shirk, uhud, Al-'Uzza, Az-Zubayr bin Al-'Awwam, Al-Bukhari, Al-Hasan, Hasan, Ruh, ruh.

A period of slackening, fatra, is pictured inwardly. Calls reach a person from inside and outside, rocks in streets and bricks in walls seeming to cry, "do not do it O servant of God!" Set on a crooked course, layy, settled in error, ghayy, he will not admit what he knows fits his state better. Loyalty to his first aim would have checked the gallop. Instead come panting breaths, anfās mutaṣā'ida, and sorrow after sorrow, ḥasarāt mutawātira, estrangement bequeathed upon estrangement. Long distress at last is relieved by beautiful kindness. Gracious affection draws him near, captivity's narrowness opens into pardon's spaciousness. Some then stand still by God for God, negated from station and honour, no longer waiting to be welcomed.

### In short

- You fled up the mountain, to Al-Madinah and to a rock, glancing at no one, while Messenger called from behind, "Come to me, servants of Allah!"
- First calls went unheard or unrecognised in martyrdom rumour confusion, and Ka'b ibn Malik's call that the Prophet lived reassembled them.
- Allah requited disobedience with grief upon grief, defeat, rumour, casualties, missed booty and enemy above them, in orders the reports arrange differently.
- The aim was to teach you not to grieve over escaped booty or befallen injury, and Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

154.text:
After the grief, sleep itself becomes a sign: "Then after distress, He sent down serenity in the form of drowsiness overcoming some of you, while others were disturbed by evil thoughts about Allah—the thoughts of ˹pre-Islamic˺ ignorance". One party slept under swords. The other stayed awake with suspicion, asking who really commanded the affair.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Then after distress, He sent down serenity in the form of drowsiness overcoming some of you"**: Then after distress, grief, He sent down security, amanatan, for you, upon you. Slumber, nu'āsan, drowsiness, substitutes for security. Overcoming, yaghshā or taghshā, a party of you, namely believers. They would become dizzy under shields, swords falling from hands. Slumber overtook people of faith, certainty, firmness and reliance on Allah, certain Allah shall give victory to His Messenger ﷺ and fulfil his objective. Those with sincerity and certitude slept. Tranquillity and slumber overcame them while carrying weapons and feeling distress and grief. In this case slumber is a favour carrying calmness and safety. "(Remember) when He covered you with a slumber as a security from Him" at Badr (8:11), in Surat Al-Anfal, Al-Anfal. Peace and security came after pain and distress. A group trusting Allah's promise became overcome by sleep because of peace and serenity in hearts.

**"while others were disturbed by evil thoughts about Allah—the thoughts of ˹pre-Islamic˺ ignorance. They ask, “Do we have a say in the matter?” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “All matters are destined by Allah.”"**: Another party, whose own souls distressed them, caused them grief so their only wish was deliverance regardless of Prophet and Companions, unable to fall asleep. These were hypocrites. They only thought about themselves, most cowardly people and least likely to support truth, anxious on own account, overcome with anxiousness about themselves, worried about own safety, upset and scared, not overcome by slumber due to worry, fright and fear. They thought wrongly of Allah, that He would not come to help of Messenger and Companions, would not help His Prophet or support servants, thought of ignorance, as they thought in time of ignorance before Islam, who did not understand Allah's reality. They are liars, people of doubts and evil thoughts about Allah, Exalted and Most Honoured. "Nay, but you thought that the Messenger and believers would never return" is the pattern cited at (48:12). This group thought idolators achieved ultimate victory when forces took upper hand, and Islam and its people would perish. That is typical of people of doubt and hesitation in hardship. They said, "Have we any part in the affair?", hal read interrogative as negative mā, we have no part in assistance promised, any part in triumph and domination, any say in whether they went out to fight, due to ignorance of Allah, saying if they had they would not have done so. Say, O Muhammad, "Indeed the affair belongs wholly to Allah", "The affair belongs entirely", decree is His, He does what He wills. Kullahu read accusative for emphasis, or kulluhu nominative as subject of a new sentence. Triumph and domination are in Allah's Hand. Everything that happens is up to Allah. He decreed they would go out to fight.

**"They conceal in their hearts what they do not reveal to you. They say ˹to themselves˺, “If we had any say in the matter, none of us would have come to die here.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Even if you were to remain in your homes, those among you who were destined to be killed would have met the same fate.” Through this, Allah tests what is within you and purifies what is in your hearts. And Allah knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart"**: They hide within themselves what they dare not and do not reveal, disclose and manifest, to you, for fear they would be killed, although they tried to conceal this thought from Messenger ﷺ. Saying, yaqūlūna, explicates preceding statement. "Had we had any part in affair, choice been ours, we would not have set out and thus been slain. But we were forced to set out." Say, "Even if you had remained, had been, in your homes in Medina, those for whom death was decreed, whom God appointed that they be slain, would certainly have gone forth, sallied forth, to place of their death, places where they were to lie, battleground where they were to fall, and would have been slain. Staying put at home would not have saved them, for God's decree will be inevitably." This is Allah's appointed destiny and decision that will certainly come to pass, no escaping it. All this was in order Allah might test and try what is in your breasts, hearts, of sincerity or hypocrisy, intentions and motives, so He tests you with whatever befell you, distinguishing good from evil and deeds and statements of believers from hypocrites. And to purify, prove and bring to fore, that which was in your hearts, sins, faith and hypocrisy. He did what He did at Uhud, Uhud, uhud, for that. Allah is All-Knower and Aware of what is in breasts, what hearts conceal, people's hearts of good and evil, hearts of hypocrites, and it is also said hearts of archers. Nothing can be hidden from Him. He tries people only to make matters manifest for them. Allah knows what is in hearts of people, nothing hidden.

### Swords falling from sleeping hands

Al-Bukhari, Al-Bukhari, recorded Anas said Abu Talhah, Abu Talhah, said:

> I was among those who were overcome by slumber during the battle of Uhud. My sword fell from my hand several times and I would pick it up, then it would fall and I would pick it up again.

Al-Bukhari collected this Hadith, hadith, in stories of battles without chain, and in book of Tafsir with chain. At-Tirmidhi, At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i and Al-Hakim, Al-Hakim, recorded from Anas that Abu Talhah said, "On the day of Uhud, I raised my head and looked around and found that everyone's head was nodding from slumber." That is At-Tirmidhi's wording, who said "Hasan Sahih". An-Nasa'i also recorded this Hadith from Anas, Abu Talhah among those overcome by slumber.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Ishaq, recorded 'Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr said Az-Zubayr, Az-Zubayr, said:

> I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when fear intensified and Allah sent sleep to us (during the battle of Uhud). At that time, every man among us (except the hypocrites) was nodding off. By Allah! As if in a dream, I heard the words of Mu'attib bin Qushayr, 'If we had anything to do with the affair, none of us would have been killed here.'

He memorized these words, which Allah mentioned later. He hid within himself what he dare not reveal. Ibn Abi Hatim collected this Hadith. Mu'attib Ibn Qushayr, the hypocrite, and his fellows are referred to as not overcome by sleep, anxious on own account.

### A test, not a punishment

Noble Companions, as verse 154, number 154, shows, were actually tested through sufferings at Uhud. This was no punishment. Objective was to make true and sincere Muslims distinct from hypocrites. Mode was a test of inner qualities.

Eloquent expression "He awarded you sorrow" is suggestive of punishment. It is resolved by saying outward form was no doubt punishment, but real purpose was affectionate correction, similar to a well-meaning reprimand from father to son or teacher to student. In common usage this can be called punishment of some sort, but in reality it is training and correction, very different from pure legal punishment.

Most important thing for a believer in life's trials is to remain calm and composed, so he may draw up plans with full concentration. Composure and concentration derive from complete trust in God. Even on most earth-shaking occasions, when people find it impossible to sleep, believers are able to revitalize themselves with soothing effect of sleep. At Uhud, despite severest conditions, they were able to sleep, in this reading a good night's sleep. Rested and refreshed, they then pursued enemy forces to Hamra al-Asad, some eight miles from Madinah, Madinah. Severely wounded and defeated, they would not have been able to take further action had calm not descended. Hot pursuit awed enemy, who turned and retreated to Makkah, Makkah. Those who have not made God guardian and protector in the full sense inevitably fear for own lives. Bereft of concern for religion, they are engrossed in own selves. Such people are never blessed with composure through divine succour.

Something more worthy is what Allah has done in their case despite mistakes. Grief was physically changed into tranquillity through drowsiness. They were told suffering was no punishment, it was a test. Then clearly worded proclamation of forgiveness came. These had appeared earlier, yet reaffirmed here. There is wisdom behind repetition. First time, the purpose was to comfort noble Companions themselves. Here is refutation of what hypocrites said to Muslims. They chided them for not acting on advice, as result of which they suffered hardships.

Other names and terms include Abdur-Rahman, Abdur-Rahman, Abi Bilta'ah in Hatib's case, Abu Talhah, Ahmad, Ahmad, Al-Anfal, al-'Aqidatul in al-'Aqidatul Wasitiyah, badr, Badr, al-Ghani, al-Ghani in 'Uthman al-Ghani, Ibn Abi, Ibn Humam, Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn Taymiyyah, al-Jama, al-Jama'ah, Jihad, jihad, al-Ma'ani, al-Ma'ani, al-Musamarah, al-Musamarah in Sharh al-Musamarah, an-Nasfiyah, an-Nasfiyah in al-'Aqa'id an-Nasfiyah, Ruh, ruh, Salaf, Salaf, Say, say, Sunnah, sunnah, Uthman, Uthman, Wajib, wajib, Zajjaj, Zajjaj.

Inwardly, people for whom a period of slackening, fatra, occurs are alluded to. Calls of Real come within and without, rocks in streets and bricks in walls seeming to cry out "do not do it O servant of God!" Resolved on crooked way, layy, settled in error, ghayy, he refuses to acknowledge what he knows would be more fitting. Staying with his original aim would let him rein himself in. He instead gets gasping breaths, anfās mutaṣā'ida, and continuous sorrows, ḥasarāt mutawātira, Real bequeathing one lonely estrangement after another. Eventually after long distress Real will relieve him with beautiful kindness, draw him near with gracious affection, deliver him from captivity's narrowness to pardon's spaciousness. Many will reach place of most respected and become still by God for God, negated from station and honour, standing without waiting to be brought near or looking to be welcomed.

### In short

- After grief Allah sent security as slumber on people of faith, Abu Talhah's sword falling and rising, every head nodding except hypocrites.
- Hypocrites, thinking wrongly of Allah as in ignorance and at (48:12), said "Have we any part in the affair?" and hid "none of us would have been killed here".
- The answer is that the affair belongs wholly to Allah, and those decreed slain would have gone out to their death-places even from homes in Medina.
- Uhud was a test to distinguish sincerity from hypocrisy and purify hearts, an affectionate correction rather than pure punishment, and Allah knows breasts.

155.text:
Those who fled are explained and pardoned in the same sentence: "Indeed, those ˹believers˺ who fled on the day when the two armies met were made to slip by Satan because of their misdeeds. But Allah has pardoned them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing". Flight is traced, not excused, and pardon is proclaimed over it.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, those ˹believers˺ who fled on the day when the two armies met were made to slip by Satan because of their misdeeds"**: Those of you who turned back and turned away from battle on day the two hosts, Muslim host and disbelievers' host, hosts of Muhammad and Abu Sufyan, Abu Sufyan, met and encountered each other at Uhud, Uhud, uhud. Shaytan, Satan, alone only caused them to err, made them slip with evil insinuations, enticed them to believe Muhammad was killed, through some, because of some, of what they had earned. Because of some of their previous errors and sins, namely when they disobeyed Prophet's command, because of leaving their positions. Except twelve men in one count of those who did not turn away. Reward of a good deed includes being directed to another good deed following it. Retribution of sin includes committing another sin following it. One sin drags in yet another sin, like one good deed pulls in another. Deeds, good and bad, have magnetic pull. A good deed makes other good deeds easy, heart desiring good and righteous. A sin clears way for other sins, heart desiring sinful. Ready reward of a good deed is another good deed a person is enabled to accomplish. Ready punishment of an evil deed is another evil deed whose way first has cleared. As explained in hadith, hadith, sin makes heart dark and when heart goes dark Satan prevails, in a citation from a work on wayfaring there.

**"But Allah has pardoned them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing"**: But Allah indeed has forgiven them, God pardoned them, has forgiven them since He did not exterminate them, will not take them to account, out of favour and mercy. He forgives sins, pardons and exonerates creatures, forgives those who repented among them. Surely Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Forgiving to believers and those who repent to Him, Most Forbearing, Clement, Forbearing hastening not against disobedient with punishment, not quick to punish.

### Why past sin could make them slip

Last part of verse 154, so Allah may test, indicates cause of hardships was wise divine arrangement. Verse 155 following seems to suggest some past mistake of theirs is cause of Satanic effect. Particular past mistake was the obvious reason that gave Satan incentive to make them slip once again, an effort in which Satan incidentally succeeded. Behind slip and outcome were wise arrangements made by Creator. Those are covered under expression so Allah may test.

A report from Zajjaj, Zajjaj, says Satan made them recall some of their sins, in presence of which they hesitated to appear before their Lord. So they moved away from Jihad, jihad, hoping to fight later on following personal correction, and thus meet Allah as martyrs in Jihad. In a separate gloss, offence is leaving positions. Some Salaf, Salaf, said the same consequence pattern in words already given, reward and retribution drawing their like.

State alluded to inwardly is those whose spiritual desire, irāda, has become meagre, intentions, niyyāt, weak. Whims, hawā, control them and listlessness, fatra, rules them. Face to face with others' counsel, call of desires and whispers of satans, they put trust in false speech. They have preferred whims over piety and stayed back. But they do not find happiness in what they have chosen.

### Uthman's flight and the prohibition of reproach

Those who fled are specified in one gloss as 'Uthman Ibn 'Affan, Ibn 'Affan, 'Uthman, Uthman, and his fellow believers, on day two hosts met. Satan enticed them to believe Muhammad was killed and thus fled to a place about six parasangs, farasikh, from scene. They were six people in all in that gloss, because of leaving positions. Allah hath forgiven them since He did not exterminate them. Allah is Forgiving of those who repented among them, Clement for He did not hasten punishment.

Imam Ahmad, Ahmad, recorded Shaqiq said 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf met Al-Walid bin 'Uqbah. Al-Walid said to him, "Why did you desert 'Uthman, Leader of the Faithful?" 'Abdur-Rahman, Abdur-Rahman, said, "Tell him that I did not run away during Uhud, remain behind during Badr, Badr, badr, nor abandon the Sunnah, sunnah, of 'Umar." Al-Walid told 'Uthman what 'Abdur-Rahman said. 'Uthman replied:

> As for his statement, 'I did not run away during Uhud,' how can he blame me for an error that Allah has already forgiven. Allah said, (Those of you who turned back on the day the two hosts met, Shaytan only caused them to err because of some of what they had earned. But Allah, indeed, has forgiven them). As for his statement that I remained behind from participating in Badr, I was nursing Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until she passed away. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me a share in the booty of Badr, and whoever gets a share in the booty from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will have participated in battle. As for his statement that I abandoned the Sunnah of 'Umar, neither I nor he are able to endure it. Go and convey this answer to him.

Most of fifty Companions commanded to guard a hill-top strategic point, with clear instruction not to leave duty-post no matter what happened at battle front underneath, moved away. Reason was erroneous independent judgment. They thought side had won the battle. Order to guard post, according to their view, had been carried out. They thought they could go down and join rest of Muslims. In reality action was clear contravention of definite instructions. This mistake motivated leaving battlefield, as reported from Zajjaj, Moreover retreat took place while Messenger was unmoved from front line and calling them back. Viewed without personalities and circumstances, action would be classed as very serious breach of military conduct. Of many blames imputed to various Companions under the genre of Mushajarat, mutual quarrels and armed confrontations between noble Companions after the Prophet ﷺ, this would be rated most serious.

But what Allah has done in their case is more worthy of consideration. Grief was physically changed into tranquillity through drowsiness. Suffering was no punishment, it was a matter of test. Clearly worded proclamation of forgiveness came, here reaffirmed. At first purpose was to comfort Companions themselves. Incidentally here is refutation of what hypocrites said to Muslims. They chided them for not acting on their advice, as result of which they suffered hardships.

In short, these verses make it clear Companions of Messenger hold unique position of affection in His sight despite serious mistakes. Not only pardoned and forgiven, they have been blessed with much more, made special recipients of grace and mercy. This comes from Allah Himself through authentic words of Holy Qur'an.

A similar case in hadith relates Sayyidna Hatib ibn Abi Bilta'ah, Abi Bilta'ah. He wrote a letter to mushrikin of Makkah, Makkah, passing on information about Muslims living in Madinah, Madinah. Prophet ﷺ was told through revelation, letter was intercepted. Companions were angry. Sayyidna Umar asked permission to behead that hypocrite. Prophet ﷺ knew Hatib was no hypocrite. He was a true sincere Muslim who made a mistake inadvertently. He forgave him and declared he was one of people, veterans, of Badr, and perhaps Allah has enforced general pardon for all participants of Badr. This narration appears in all authentic books of ahadith in that comment.

This affirmation anchors the position of the followers of Sunnah, sunnah, and Jama'ah, al-Jama'ah, ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah. Companions are not placed beyond sin. Sin did happen from them, and can. What the community may not do is fasten evil or defect on them in a derogatory way. God and His Messenger met serious slips with forgiveness and the station of "and may they be pleased with Allah". After that, a claim to speak derogatorily about any of them has no standing.

Sayyidna Abdullah ibn Umar on hearing somebody satirize Sayyidna Uthman al-Ghani, al-Ghani, and some noble Companions by saying they had run away from battlefield, reference being this incidence at Uhud, said, "Nobody has the right to criticize that which Allah has expressly proclaimed to have been forgiven", citing Sahih al-Bukhari, Al-Bukhari. Therefore all doctrinal source-books of ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah unanimously agree it is Wajib, wajib, necessary to honour position of noble Companions and abstain from criticising, mocking or speaking ill of them. In al-'Aqa'id an-Nasfiyah, an-Nasfiyah, it is necessary that one should not talk about Companions except in a good manner. In Sharh al-Musamarah, al-Musamarah, Ibn Humam, Ibn Humam, has said belief of followers of Sunnah is that all Companions were purified and remembered with praise. In Sharh Muwaqif it is obligatory to honour Companions, all of them, and avoiding satire or criticism against them is equally mandatory. Hafiz Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn Taymiyyah, in al-'Aqidatul Wasitiyah, al-'Aqidatul, says:

> It is a cardinal belief of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah that Muslims must refrain from accusing or criticizing any Companion of the Holy Prophet ﷺ in the matter of disagreements or armed conflicts which may have come up among them. There is a reason for this. Most of the narrations imputing drawbacks in them which have crept into history are a pack of lies planted by enemies. They simply have no truth in them. Then, there are others in which the reality has been reversed by additions and alterations. Even if, there was some truth about something, that has to be taken as the independent judgment of the Companions in which they have no choice. Going a step further, we can assume a situation where they may not be helpless but be capable of using their choice, then, what works there is the Divine Law that is, good deeds make up for the bad ones. And it is more than obvious that nobody can claim equality with them in the matter of good deeds. The good they did cannot be matched by the good done by anybody else. Similarly, nobody else can be more deserving of the mercy and forgiveness of Allah Almighty as compared to them. Therefore, nobody has the right to sit on judgment against them and call their deeds to account and in that process, criticise or speak ill of them.

On the historical side, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy counselled defence of Madinah within walls instead of boldly coming out. Prophet, at instance of sincere Muslims, went out, posting men strategically. Battle began well, turned to near defeat due to disobedience of fifty archers guarding a pass. Seeing imminent victory, they abandoned posts, attracted by prospects of booty. When victory turned to defeat, hypocrites who had deserted even before battle, on pretext counsel was not accepted, began saying had their words been heeded calamity could have been averted. Death is decreed by God and comes regardless of circumstances. No precaution can save one from death. Happenings, whatever their apparent reason, are wrought by God so true believers may turn in repentance and become worthy of further blessings, and to reveal truth about those who are not true servants.

When fifty archers at Mount Uhud pass saw Muslims had won, a large number insisted on going in pursuit of booty. Abdullah ibn Jubayr and a few others pointed out it was against Prophet's orders. They deserted posts, leaving behind eleven men. Satan made inroads using dissension already evident among them. However, when they admitted error, they were forgiven. After initial setback God's succour came. Almighty struck terror into enemies' hearts resulting in retreat, although they were just a few miles from Madinah. Had God's succour not come, nothing could stop them forcing entry into Madinah and uprooting nascent tree of Islam.

Other names and terms include Abu Talhah, Abu Talhah, At-Tirmidhi, At-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim, Al-Hakim, Al-Anfal, Al-Anfal, Az-Zubayr, Az-Zubayr, Ibn Abi, Ibn Abi, Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Ishaq, Al-Ma'ani, al-Ma'ani, Ruh, ruh, Say, say. Verse 154 is number 154, while citations outside this verse sit at (8:11) and (48:12).

### In short

- Those who turned back when the two hosts met were made to slip by Satan because of some of what they earned, disobedience to the Prophet's order and past sins darkening hearts.
- One sin draws another as one good deed draws another, yet Allah proclaimed pardon and is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing, not hastening punishment.
- 'Uthman's answer to reproach rests on this pardon, and Companions whom Allah forgave must not be criticised derogatorily, honouring them being Wajib.

156.text:
A counterfactual is forbidden as a creed: "O believers! Do not be like the unfaithful who say about their brothers who travel throughout the land or engage in battle, “If they had stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed.” Allah makes such thinking a cause of agony in their hearts". The sentence looks like love. Its fruit is regret, because it puts death in the wrong hands.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O believers! Do not be like the unfaithful who say about their brothers who travel throughout the land or engage in battle, “If they had stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed.”"**: Be not like those who disbelieve, hypocrites disbelieving in secret, who do not have faith in destiny and Allah's decree. Do not say as they say of their brothers, regarding their affair, relatives and dead brethren, when they travel through the earth, journey in the land for trading, earning a living and otherwise, then die, or go out to fight, are on raiding campaigns, ghuzzan, plural of ghāzin, participating in battles with Companions of Muhammad and with their Prophet in a fighting expedition, and are then slain. "If they had stayed with us", here with us in our area, in Medina, Madinah, in Madinah the city, and not gone or not fought, "they would not have died", on their journey, while travelling, "or been killed", during fighting expedition, in battle. Had they abandoned these trips, they would not have met their demise, in their false creed.

**"Allah makes such thinking a cause of agony in their hearts. It is Allah who gives life and causes death. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do"**: So that, so God may make that, make that doubt and saying of theirs as conclusion of their affair, anguish, grief, regret and a cause of regret in their hearts. Allah creates this evil thought in their hearts so sadness and grief they feel for their loss would increase. Their regret is increased by the belief itself. Life and death are elsewhere. On a journey God may grant life, in settlement He may decree death. The decision is His alone. Leave and decree govern every living and dying, every increase or decrease of a lifespan. Staying behind cannot block what He has decreed. Going out cannot pull it nearer. And Allah is All-Seer, Sees and is All-Seeing of what you do, what you say. Read ta'malūna, you do, or ya'malūna, they do. He will requite you for it. His knowledge and vision encompass all creation, none of their affairs escapes Him, none of what you do is hidden from Him, and you will be rewarded according to what you do.

### The hypocrites behind the saying

'Abdullah Ibn Ubayy, Ibn Ubayy, and his followers who returned to Medina are named, disbelieved in secret. O ye who believe, in Muhammad and Qur'an, be not in war as those who disbelieved in secret, said of their brethren, the hypocrites, who went abroad in land with Companions of Muhammad or were fighting in the field with their Prophet. If they had been here with us in Medina they would not have died on journey or been killed during fighting expedition. That Allah may make it, doubt, anguish and grief in their hearts.

Saying of hypocrites in verse 156 is extension of what was cited in verse 154, number 154, earlier, "If we had any say in the matter, we would have not been killed here." Number 156, verse 156 is this verse. Since there were chances sincere Muslims may be affected by such doubt-creating devices used by hypocrites, Muslims were asked to remain unconcerned with such sayings and doings and adhere to belief span of life and time of death are ordained by Allah alone.

All that happens in world is by God's will. Everything takes place under veil of cause and effect. Incidents appear to have cause behind them but actually occur at God's will. Man's faith is tested through apparent causes, making it difficult to see hidden hand of God in all things. Non-believer is lost in trying to understand causes and effects, while believer penetrates veil to discover actual reality. One who claims to be a believer yet regards life and death, success and failure as results of human strategies is not true to his claim. When a non-believer suffers a setback he grieves over it, thinking had he adopted this or that course he could have been saved. When a believer confronts same situation he resigns himself to it by accepting God's will. With conviction everything happens by God's will, all other human causes appear insignificant and not worthy of further consideration.

Whoever makes a habit of worrying about what is past and planning for his future and each new moment, least of his punishment will be constriction of heart through disconcerting worries. Quality of life disappears from his heart because of forgetfulness and his saying "if only such and such" or "maybe such and such". Result of this kind of thinking is estrangement and grief, constriction of heart and separation.

Malūna, malūna in damaged spelling for malūna, a checklist artifact around cursed or blamed ones in neighbouring verses, and Say, say, belong to shared apparatus, while brethren, land travel and battle in this verse are its own.

### In short
