- Do not say of brothers who died travelling for trade or were killed fighting, "If they had stayed with us in Medina, they would not have died or been killed".
- The "if only" thought is made anguish and regret in hypocrites' hearts, extending their "if we had any say" from verse 154.
- Allah alone gives life and causes death by leave and decree, and staying behind neither stops it nor going hastens it.
- Believers penetrate the veil of causes to God's will, while non-believers grieve over strategies that might have saved.

157.text:
Death in God's cause is revalued against hoarding: "Should you be martyred or die in the cause of Allah, then His forgiveness and mercy are far better than whatever ˹wealth˺ those ˹who stay behind˺ accumulate". What stay-behinds collect is not denied to exist. It is outbid.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Should you be martyred or die in the cause of Allah, then His forgiveness and mercy are far better than whatever ˹wealth˺ those ˹who stay behind˺ accumulate"**: And if you are killed or die in the way of Allah, in God's way in holy struggle, if death comes to you thereat. Wa-la-in, the lām is for oaths. Die is read muttum or mittum, from singular māta yamūtu. Forgiveness, la-maghfiratun, that is from God for your sins, pardon of your sins, and mercy therefor from Him for you, by being spared punishment, are far better than all that they amass, than what they amass in this world, this world along with what people of this world collect of its passing pleasures, of wealth. Read tajma'ūn, you amass, or yajma'ūn, they amass. Clause introduced by lām of la-maghfiratun is response to oath clause of la'in and occupies place of verbal action as a subject, predicate of which is what follows. Allah will forgive you and be merciful, and that is better than this world.

Death and martyrdom in Allah's cause are a means of earning Allah's mercy, forgiveness and pleasure. This is better than remaining in this life with its short-lived delights. Whoever dies or is killed will return to Allah, Exalted and Most Honored, and He will reward him if he has done good deeds, or punish him for evil deeds.

One gloss speaks as if hypocrites themselves were addressed, killed or dying at home, yet sincere. For such people, pardon for sins and mercy in place of punishment would outweigh amassed worldly wealth.

True value lies after death, in forgiveness and Paradise. Entry costs nothing less than earthly existence itself. Man pays that exact price, and without the sacrifice his Hereafter remains uncertain. Worldly resources consume whole lives devoted to providing for this world. Believers treat the next world as the all in all.

Life surrendered in God, spirit, rūḥ, ruh, spent for Him, is preferred to life alongside anything else. One who knows God prefers returning to Him. What a servant puts before God carries no blessing. This world is offered, and the final outcome is offered.

Number 154, verse 154's counterfactual, and number 156, verse 156's prohibition, frame this comparison. Say, say, is a framing imperative.

### In short

- If killed or dying in Allah's way, forgiveness of sins and mercy, being spared punishment, are far better than wealth amassed in this world.
- Death and martyrdom earn mercy, forgiveness and pleasure, better than remaining here with short-lived delights.
- Paradise's price is earthly life itself, and sacrificing the rūḥ in God outranks life with anything else.

158.text:
Every road ends at the same gathering: "Whether you die or are martyred—all of you will be gathered before Allah". The distinction is not destination but the state in which a person arrives there.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Whether you die or are martyred—all of you will be gathered before Allah"**: And whether you die or are killed, if you die, read in both ways muttum or mittum, or are slain in holy struggle or otherwise, on a journey or in settlement, in a fighting expedition, verily unto Allah you shall be gathered, mustered in Hereafter, to God and to none other than Him. He will requite you. Death in whatever form, or killing in Allah's path, ends in the same return. All come back to Allah alone for reward measured by deeds. Wa-la-in's lām is again for oaths. Gathering after death is the setting named.

Whoever dies or is killed will return to Allah, Exalted and Most Honored. He will reward him if he has done good deeds, or will punish him for his evil deeds. The present gloss says He will reward you according to what you have done. Forgiveness and mercy of the previous verse are the reward carried by those who die in His way.

The inward reading finds sweetness for a traveller whose destination is God. Hardships sweeten like honey when the road ends in Him. Returning to Him outranks staying behind with anything else. Knowing God makes sacrifice of spirit, rūḥ, ruh, better than a life spent otherwise. Blessing leaves whatever a servant puts before God. This world is one offer. The final outcome is the other.

Frame numbers are 154, verse 154, and 156, verse 156, with Say, say, as speech artifact.

Gathering before Allah levels the distinction between home death and battle death. Both are gathered to the same Judge. That is why regret counterfactuals lose force. Staying cannot move a person outside the gathering, and going cannot move him outside decree. What changes is reward, forgiveness and mercy or punishment for evil deeds, according to what was done.

### In short

- Whether dying naturally or killed in the holy struggle or otherwise, it is to God, and none other, that all shall be mustered in the Hereafter.
- He will requite according to deeds, rewarding good and punishing evil.
- Since destination is God, journey's hardships become sweet to one who knows Him.

159.text:
After a disobedience that cost a battle, the Prophet ﷺ is praised for softness and ordered to deepen it: "It is out of Allah’s mercy that you ˹O Prophet˺ have been lenient with them. Had you been cruel or hard-hearted, they would have certainly abandoned you. So pardon them, ask Allah’s forgiveness for them, and consult with them in ˹conducting˺ matters. Once you make a decision, put your trust in Allah. Surely Allah loves those who trust in Him". Mercy explains his character. Pardon, intercession, consultation and trust then sequence the repair.

### Phrase by phrase

**"It is out of Allah’s mercy that you ˹O Prophet˺ have been lenient with them. Had you been cruel or hard-hearted, they would have certainly abandoned you"**: By the mercy of Allah, Rahmah, rahmah, you dealt with them gently. Who would have made you this kind, if not Allah's mercy for you and them? Qatadah, Qatadah, said with Allah's mercy you became this kind. Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Al-Basri, said this is description of behaviour Allah sent Muhammad, MuḤammad, with. The verse is similar to "Verily, there has come unto you a Messenger from among yourselves. It grieves him that you should receive any injury or difficulty. He is anxious over you (to be rightly guided, to repent to Allah); for the believers (he is) full of pity, kind, and merciful" (9:128). Severe person is he who utters harsh words. Harsh, stern, fierce and hard-hearted is person whose heart is hard, coarse and brutish. Had you been severe and harsh-hearted, ill-natured and fierce of heart, harsh in words and actions in speech, they would have broken away and scattered from around you, split away and left you. Allah gathered them and made you kind and soft with them, so hearts congregate around you. 'Abdullah bin 'Amr, Abdullah bin 'Amr, said he read description of Messenger in previous Books, "He is not severe, harsh, obscene in the marketplace or dealing evil for evil. Rather, he forgives and pardons."

**"So pardon them, ask Allah’s forgiveness for them, and consult with them in ˹conducting˺ matters"**: Pardon them, pass over what may ensue from them and shortcomings with you, pardon your Companions for that which may ensue from them. Ask forgiveness for them, from transgression which ensues from them, for their sins until I forgive them, ask Allah to forgive them for what is between them and Allah. Consult them in affairs, find out their opinions in the matter, your affair in battle and otherwise, in matter of war, to win hearts over and so you may be emulated. Ask their opinion in whatever needs to be agreed upon, in conducting matters. Prophet would frequently consult them.

**"Once you make a decision, put your trust in Allah. Surely Allah loves those who trust in Him"**: Then when you have taken a decision, when thou art resolved to carry out what you wish after counsel, to do something, put your trust in Allah, Tawakkul, tawakkul, rely on God and put your trust in Him, not in any counsel, to give you triumph and domination. If you conduct required consultation and then make a decision, trust in Allah over your decision. Allah loves those who put their trust in Him, giving them success and support, for God loves those who rely on Him.

### Comfort for shame, and protection for teaching

Even though Muslim mistake and abandonment of battle front caused grief to the Prophet, he did not reproach them because of high morals and natural way of forgiving and forgetting. He did not even deal sternly as may have been in order. Allah willed to see Companions of His Messenger are comforted and sense of shock and shame for their mistake is washed away. Prophet is asked to deal with them more gently and affectionately and consult them in matters of concern.

Two dangers existed. First, mistake against express instructions could increase sense of shock and affect normal emotional-rational response. They could lose hope of mercy when they realised what mistake they had made and how disobedient they had been to leader's command. This danger was already eliminated in previous verse, "We awarded you sorrow for sorrow" meaning return of mistake has already been given in mortal world and account in Hereafter lies clean, as that discussion puts it.

Second, the Prophet was hurt physically as result of mistake. Spiritual discomfort was already there. These two factors might make the Prophet unhappy with Companions, which in turn may become hindrance in mission to teach and train them. To counter likelihood, Prophet was asked to forgo mistake, forgive shortcoming from depth of heart, deal gently and affectionately in future as well.

Diction is eloquent in praise. Related command conveys his personal praise and unique human majesty, attributes built into him already. Addition of "So, it was through mercy from Allah" affirms presence of attributes of perfection in his person is only through Divine mercy. This is no personal perfection in its own right. By placing Rahmah in indefinite form, hint is made towards great and extensive spread of Allah's mercy. This mercy is not restricted to noble Companions only. It extends in full to the Prophet himself, for Allah has made him identified with such perfect attributes. Qualities of gentle manners, good morals, forgiveness and generosity serve a purpose. Had these not been there, mission of educating human beings charged to him would never be accomplished as desired. Rather than seek correction and raising of morals in his company, people would run away from him.

Gentle dealing is equally essential in any Muslim leader, in the application given. Moderation is indispensable. Lenient attitude is required not only in normal daily life but also in dealings between Muslims and non-Muslims, even where disobedience turns victory into defeat. Unless leader shows broad-mindedness and high thinking, a powerful polity cannot be established. Mistakes, however grave outcome, if committed without evil intention, are pardonable. Leader should overlook this type of error. He should be such a great well-wisher he prays to God for their guidance. Good leader values people so much he takes decisions on important matters only after consulting them.

### Etiquette of Da'wah

Anyone who embarks on inviting people to Allah, explaining His guidance and calling people towards right conduct, must first inculcate these qualities. Roughness fails even from the Messenger, dearest to people. A lesser caller with hostility and poor morals cannot expect created people to gather or behaviour to change.

Harshness, in conduct or language, is sheer poison for a Da'wah worker or leader conveying Allah's message. It is a sure way to undo what one intends to achieve. "So, pardon them" indicates a Da'wah worker or reformer should never punish people for mistakes. Instead forgive and forgo. It is important he does not get excited or angry when listeners speak ill of him. He should rise higher and treat tormentors with compassion and leniency.

"And seek forgiveness for them" points to an unusual rule. Not only should he remain patient in what is painful. Messenger is asked not to forget seeking their good with utmost sincerity. Best that can be wished for them is salvation in life-to-come, good that waits for them in Akhirah. Pray for their forgiveness so Allah spares them punishment.

"And consult them in the matter" means seek their advice in matters of concern so they are fully satisfied and emotionally at peace, Messenger by following instruction giving external form to intention of doing good for them. Asking them to sit in consultations will become an act of mollifying grace.

### What amr and shura mean

Word amr is applied for several shades in Arabic. In common usage it refers to any saying or doing of great importance. It is also used to mean injunction, order, command, rule or authority, last being what is meant in expression uli l'amr. It is also applied to a particular attribute of Allah which finds mention in several verses, such as "Beware, for Him alone is the creation and the command" (7:54). "To Him the whole matter shall be returned" (11:123). "The whole thing belongs to Allah" (3:154). "His matter is upto Allah" in the verse cited as (2:275) in that list. According to authentic scholars, use of amr in "Say: The spirit is by a command of my Lord" (17:85), spirit being Ruh, ruh, carries same meaning as verses above.

As far as amr in "And consult them in the matter" (3:159) and "And a matter of theirs is (settled) by a consultation between themselves" (42:38), in Surah al-Shura, al-Shura, it can be assigned both first and second possibilities. If first sense is used while second is inclusive therein, that is not far-fetched, since affairs relating to command and authority are all very important. Amr in verses above means every matter or affair particularly important, irrespective of whether it belongs to area of authority or mutual dealings.

Arabic words shura, counsel, mashwarah, consultation, and mushawarat, mutual consultation, mean soliciting of advice and counsel in something that needs deliberation. Expression in present verse means the Prophet has been commanded here to consult with or seek advice of noble Companions in matters that need deliberation, which include those of authority and government. Verse from Surah al-Shura means that in every important matter which needs deliberation, whether in field of authority and government or something important other than these, customary practice of true Muslims is to work through mutual consultation.

### Status of consultation in Islamic Law

From Qur'an statements and related ahadith, mutual consultation in a matter likely to have more than one opinion, whether related to concerns of authority or issue other than that, is a Sunnah, sunnah, of the Prophet and noble Companions and source of blessings in mortal world and eternal life of Hereafter. As far as matters which relate to people, such as affairs of authority and government are concerned, seeking consultation in them is obligatory, in the opinion recorded there.

In Shu'bul-Iman, al-Baihaqi, al-Baihaqi, has reported from Sayyidna Abdullah ibn Umar that the Prophet said:

> A person who intends to do something, then goes in consultation and comes up with a decision to do or not to do that, he gets from Allah Almighty guidance towards an option which is correct and beneficial.

It appears in ahadith:

> When your rulers are from the best among you and your rich people are generous and your affairs are decided through mutual consultation, then, to live on the surface of the earth is better for you. And should your rulers be the worst among you and your rich people be close-fisted and your affairs be entrusted to women, then, to be buried under the earth shall be better than your continuing to live.

That gloss explains, when worship of desires overpowers you, ignoring good and bad, harmful and beneficial, simply to seek goodwill of a woman, you entrust affairs in her hands, then death is better than living through those times. Otherwise, seeking opinion of a woman as well while making consultations is no taboo, and certainly not prohibited. Consistent practice of the Prophet and Companions proves it. In the verse from Surah al-Baqarah, al-Baqarah, (2:233) cited earlier, "Now, if they want to wean, by mutual consent, and consultation, there is no sin on them." Since matter here concerns woman, consultation with woman has been specially made binding on man.

A hadith says, "The person whose counsel is sought is a trustee. When he counsels, then, he must counsel with what he would propose to his ownself (to do otherwise is a breach of trust)". This hadith has been reported with good authority from Sayyidna Ali by al-Tabarani, al-Tabarani, in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, al-Mu'jam, al-Awsat. Another version is carried in this job's shorter material. Ibn Majah, Ibn Majah, recorded Abu Hurayrah, Abu Hurayrah and Abu Hurairah in spelling variant, said Prophet said:

> The one whom advice is sought from is to be entrusted.

This was recorded by Abu Dawud, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, At-Tirmidhi, and An-Nasa'i, An-Nasa'i, who graded it Hasan, Al-Hasan, Hasan.

Consultation is an act of Sunnah only in situations where some clear and categorical injunction from Qur'an or Hadith does not exist. Otherwise, in presence of clear and categorical injunction of Shari'ah, Shariah, shariah, no consultation with anybody is needed. This is not permissible either. For example, if somebody consulted, should I make my Salah, salah, or should I not? Should I pay my Zakah, zakah, or should I not? Or should I perform my Hajj, hajj, or should I not? That would be absurd. These are absolutely mandatory. How to perform Hajj remains consultable. Year, sea or air or land route, method of travel. Zakah likewise leaves place and recipient to the payer's choice, so advice can be sought there.

In a hadith the Prophet explained this himself. Sayyidna Ali says he asked the Prophet about a situation after him with no explicit Qur'anic injunction and nothing heard from him. The Prophet said:

> For a matter like this, get together from among you pious men who are consistently devoted to the worship of their Lord and who have deep and extensive understanding of the Faith (fuqaha') and decide the matter following their mutual counsel. Do not decide on the basis of someone's solitary opinion.

First thing learned is consultation is not restricted to worldly affairs. Instead mutual consultation in situations where clear nusus (plural of nass, textual authority) from Qur'an and Hadith in matters governed by Shari'ah do not exist is an act of Sunnah. Mutual consultation will be an act of Sunnah if made where textual authority from Qur'an and Sunnah is not available. Second rule is advice should be taken from people known for understanding of Faith and devotion to obligations to Allah. Putting two ahadith together, two qualities are necessary for members of consultative council. Wisdom comes first. Perception and worthiness to advise follow. Then piety. Devotion to worship and God-fearing conduct mark the counsellor. If matter involves problems relating to Islamic Law, it is incumbent they be faqih, jurisconsult and expert in Islamic Law and Jurisprudence, as well. Khatib al-Baghdadi, al-Baghdadi, to whom deduction above is credited, has reported another hadith from Sayyidna Abu Hurairah which says, "Seek counsel from the wise person and do not act against it, otherwise you will regret."

### The Prophet's consultations

Advice was his habit with Companions across matters. Comforted, they would carry out a reached decision with energy. For instance, before battle of Badr, badr, the Prophet asked his Companions if Muslims should intercept caravan led by Abu Sufyan, Abu Sufyan. They answered at length.

> O Messenger of Allah! If you wish to cross the sea, we would follow you in it, and if you march forth to Barkul-Ghimad, Bark al-Ghamad in another spelling, we would march with you. We would never say what Children of Israel, children of israel, Israel, said to Musa, Musa, musa, 'So go, you and your Lord, and fight you two, we are sitting right here' (5:24), in that quoted dialogue as cited in the battle material, while another citation gives (5:23) for trust saying in this job, 'And in God put your trust, if you have faith' (5:23). Rather, we say march forth and we shall march forth with you, before you, and to your right and left shall we fight. Camp position at Badr was also consulted. Al-Mundhir, Al-Mundhir bin 'Amr, bin 'Amr, wanted nearness to the enemy. Martyrdom was his wish.

At Uhud, uhud, staying fortified inside Al-Madinah, Al-Madinah, or marching out was put to them. The majority chose marching out. Out they went.

At Khandaq, the Trench, around Al-Ahzab, Al-Ahzab, a treaty buying off some Confederates with a third of Al-Madinah's fruits was consulted on. Sa'd bin 'Ubadah and Sa'd bin Mu'adh opposed it. Their opposition carried.

At Hudaybiyyah, hudaybiyyah, attacking idolaters was consulted on. Abu Bakr, Abu Bakr, objected. The journey's purpose was 'Umrah, umrah, not fighting. The Prophet agreed.

On day of Ifk, false accusation, Messenger addressed them as follows.

> O Muslims! Give me your advice about some men who falsely accused my wife ('A'ishah). By Allah! I never knew of any evil to come from my wife. And they accused whom? They accused he from whom I only knew righteous conduct, by Allah!

Prophet asked 'Ali and Usamah about divorcing 'A'ishah. In summary, Prophet used to take Companions' advice for battles and other important events.

Isn't it that he is Messenger and blessed recipient of revelation? Why should he need to consult anyone? Since everything can come to his knowledge through revelation, some scholars interpret command to consult by saying Messenger was neither in need to be counselled, nor anything he did depended on such counsel. Command to consult is simply to honour blessed Companions and mollify broken hearts. Imam Abu Bakr al-Jassas, al-Jassas, does not agree with this view. According to him this is not correct, for being involved in consultation while knowing one's counsel will not be acted upon, nor would it affect any proceedings of agenda, will make whole thing ineffectual. If so, no heart will be mollified and no honour will be sustained. Instead, truth is a course of action to be taken by Messenger is identified through revelation directly. This holds good in all general matters. But there are certain matters which, under dictates of wisdom and mercy of Allah, are left to opinion and discretion of the Prophet. It is in such matters alone where consultation is needed, and these are kind of matters in which he has been commanded to seek consultation. History of consultative sittings confirms this view.

Being a prophet, messenger and recipient of revelation is not a bar against consultation. It cannot be said seeking counsel was designed to please them artificially, or virtually ineffectual in conduct of affairs. Many occasions he accepted opinion of those present during consultation even if against his own. In some situations where a particular line of action had not been determined through revelation, and in its absence he worked through consultation, there is great divine wisdom. Objective is that practice of the Prophet comes to be established for all future generations of Muslims. Seeking of consultation as a Sunnah shall become binding on whole Ummah, ummah, of the Prophet. Imagine when he himself has not been left free of need of consultation, who else can claim to be free of such need? Method of mutual consultation always continued to be operative during blessed times of the Prophet and noble Companions particularly in matters where there was no clear injunction in Qur'an and Sunnah. When the Prophet passed away, noble Companions continued following his practice. Still later, mutual consultation was resorted to as modality to deduce rulings of Islamic Law in matters where clear injunction was not found in Qur'an and Sunnah. This was actually method taught by the Prophet in answer to Ali.

### Consultation in a state, and deciding after difference

Qur'an has given clear instructions about mashwarah at two places. One appears right here. Other comes in verse (42:38) of Surah al-Shura, where one of qualities of true Muslims has been mentioned, their affairs are settled by mutual consultation. At both places word amr (matter) has been mentioned along with mashwarah. Discussed earlier, amr signifies any important saying or doing, while at same time it is applied to injunction, rule or authority or government. No matter which meaning is taken, consultation in affairs of the government emerges as invariably necessary. If one elects to take this to mean affairs of the government, necessity is all the more obvious. In case word is taken in general sense, affairs of a government being important and far-reaching in effect would still be considered affairs in which consultation will be inevitable. Therefore, it is one of duties of Muslim Amir, chief executive of community, that he should seek counsel of those responsible for affairs of government in matters that are important. verses of Qur'an quoted above and consistent practice of the Prophet and rightly-guided Caliphs is clear proof of this requirement.

These two verses also point out to basic principles of Islam's system of government, and its constitution. Islamic government is a government by consultation in which amir or chief executive is chosen by consultation and definitely not as matter of family inheritance. It is a Barakah, barakah, blessing, of Islamic teachings that this principle is recognized all over world, so much so hereditary monarchies too are moving towards this arrangement, willingly or unwillingly.

Back 1400, 1400, years in history the super-powers were Cyrus and Ceaser. Common factor between them was they both headed hereditary empires and authority of government was vested in their own persons. One man ruled millions, not on basis of ability or capacity, but on strength of cruel principle of hereditary possession of sovereignty. This form of government, an insult to all human beings, was way all over world except Greece where early teachings of democratic order had yet to translate into principles that would go on to establish stable government. Instead they relegated into a branch of Aristotelian philosophy. Islam demolished unnatural principle of government through heredity and gave choice of appointing and dismissing chief executive to people, a power they could use through representatives shouldering responsibilities of affairs of state. World, once stuck in quagmire of traditional monarchy, came to know about this natural and just system through Islamic teachings and this happens to be spirit of a system of government now known as democracy.

Modern democracies, since they appeared as reaction to cruel monarchies, came out with equal lack of moderation. They went on to give masses sense of being absolute, ultimate entity, an unbridled sovereign of system of government and law of state, to extent minds and hearts became alienated from very concept of God, Creator of earth and heavens and all human beings, not to say much about concept of His real Sovereignty and Rule, which comes as result of that cardinal belief. Now situation has reached a stage where their 'democracy' has started taking restrictions imposed by Allah on public choice, which in itself was conferred on human beings by Him, as something of burden, contrary to justice and equity of their brand.

Liberation from Cyrus, Ceaser and despotism carries a second lesson. Western democracies hiding behind secular curtains are shown God's way. Islam's way is no more a secret. Its teachings clearly say rulers and ruled, governments and their peoples are all subject to Law given by Allah. Masses, their representative assemblies, law-making, appointment and removal of office-holders must operate within parameters set by Allah. Ability and merit must be weighed for chief executive, office-holders and responsible positions. Honesty and trustworthiness are tested too. For the head of government, fear of Allah joins knowledge, honesty, trustworthiness, ability and political experience as measures. Even this chief executive, elected though he may be, is not totally free, unchecked and despotic. He has to seek counsel from those capable of giving such counsel. Qur'an bears witness to this and so does constant practice of the Prophet and great rightly-guided Caliphs. Who else can claim to be more just than them?

Sayyidna Umar has said, "There is no Khilafah (Caliphate) unless it be with consultation." That citation is given through Kanzul-'ummal vide Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi.

Government by consultation is a basic Islamic requirement so much so a chief executive or head of state, if he ever unfetters himself from need for consultation or takes counsel from those not fit to give counsel from point of view of Shari'ah of Islam, has to be removed of necessity. In al-Bahr al-Muhit of Abi Hayyan, Abi Hayyan, Ibn 'Atiyyah said that consultation is one of basic principles of Islamic Law and Faith. He who does not consult with those who know must be removed as matter of obligation. This is what nobody differs about.

By making consultation mandatory, blessings benefiting Islamic state and citizens could be measured by what the Prophet said about consultation. Ibn 'Adi and al Baihaqi have reported from Sayyidna ibn Abbas, Ibn 'Abbas, that when this verse was revealed the Prophet said, "Allah and His Messenger do not need this consultation, but Allah Almighty has certainly made it a source of mercy for my community". God could have sent everything by revelation and left no room for counsel at all. Community interest lay elsewhere. Consultation was established through His Messenger. Matters left without mention or revelation became the field where the Prophet sought consultation.

What happens when opinions differ on a certain matter? Would it be decided on contemporary parliamentary principle? Would chief executive be compelled to enforce decision of majority? Or would he have right to take course of action on basis of powerful arguments and obvious welfare of state, coming from any side, no matter whether in majority or minority? From Qur'an and Hadith and constant practice of noble Prophet and his Companions, it cannot be proved that amir of Muslims, their head of state, is helplessly bound by decision of majority. On contrary, some hints make it very evident Amir can, in event of difference of opinion, use his discretion and go by any of several courses of action, irrespective of fact it comes from majority or minority. There is no doubt Amir will do his best to look into other opinions as well to satisfy himself fully, but should majority come to agree on one opinion, this could, at times, become source of satisfaction to him.

A close look at this verse would show that the Prophet, after he has been commanded to seek counsel, is being told, once you have taken a decision, place your trust in Allah. Here word 'azm in "'azamta", meaning a firm decision one way or other, has been ascribed to the Prophet. Text does not say 'azamtum, second person plural, which would have suggested participation of Companions in final making and enforcing of decision. This hint proves, once process of consultation has been completed, decision and its enforcement is valid prerogative of chief executive. Umar ibn al-Khattab, Umar bin Al-Khattab, Ibn Al-Khattab, at times decided by Abdullah ibn Abbas's view when its argument was weightier. Senior Companions, older and more learned, could be present and still that view prevailed. There were many occasions when the Prophet has preferred opinions of revered Shaykhayn Abu-Bakr, Abu Bakr, and Umar against majority of other Companions, to limit that people thought this verse was revealed for consultation with these two only. A report in Mustadrak gives Ibn Abbas, that the pronoun in 'shawirhum' (consult them) refers to Abu Bakr and Umar, in the citation attributed there to a collector named Hakim in this discussion, separate from Al-Hakim earlier. The narration of Kalbi is clearer than this, that this verse has been revealed for consulting with Abu Bakr and Umar. These two were special Companions of Messenger and his Ministers and patrons of Muslims, in that citation. Messenger had once addressed Sayyidna Abu Bakr and Umar in the following words, "When you agree on an opinion, I do not decide against you." That is cited with reference to Musnad of Ahmad, Ahmad.

A doubt says this procedure is against democracy, a model of one-man rule, and that this system might hurt rights of masses. Answer is Islamic system of government has already taken care of this problem, for it has not given masses absolute right to make anyone they wish amir of an Islamic state. The mandate points them to the person judged strongest in knowledge and conduct, in ability to function, in Godliness and in honesty. Him they elect as amir. Now a person elected in view of such elegant qualities and attributes should certainly not be subjected to restrictions usually placed on dishonest, sinful and debauch. Doing this would be against reason and justice, act of discouragement to genuine servant of people and hindrance in promotion of community-oriented action.

### Decision, then trust

At the conclusion of verse, it is very important to bear in mind this instruction has been given after prescribing consultation in all important affairs including those of government. Even after making all preparations, when you finally decide to go ahead and do what has to be done, then that is time when you do not simply place trust in your reason, opinion, plans or preparedness but, instead, you should place trust in Allah alone, for all these considered plans are in direct control of supreme Planner of all affairs and matters. Man himself is witness to futility of his plans in thousands of events in his lifetime.

"And once you have taken a decision, place your trust in Allah" also clarifies placing trust in Allah does not mean efforts to provide means and make plans should be abandoned. Fact is placing trust in Allah while leaving off means near at hand is contrary to blessed practice of prophets, and against teachings of Holy Qur'an. Idleness is the other failure. Dreaming of distant means, or treating plans as agents themselves, ignores the Causer of means. Tawakkul, Tawhid, tawhid, excludes both.

### Victory cannot be outsourced to consultation

"If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there after Him that can help you? And in Allah (Alone) let believers put their trust" belongs to next verse's citation here in the shared block. "And there is no victory except from Allah the Almighty, the All-Wise" (3:126). That cross-reference is included in this verse's allowed citations, as is sequence (3:154), affair belongs entirely to God, (3:162), (3:163), (3:164), and those who are grateful. Other citations named across this vast material include (2:233), (2:275), (5:23), (5:24), (6:130), (6:132), (7:54), (9:72), (9:73), (9:128), (11:123), (12:109), (13:19), (17:85), (18:110), (20:44), (25:20), (26:215), (28:61), (30:21), (42:38) and (56:89), with (9:72) giving trust's three levels in the report that follows below, (9:73) giving struggle against unbelievers and hypocrites and hardness with them, (20:44) giving soft words to Pharaoh, (26:215) giving lowering wing to faithful who follow thee, (28:61) giving promised excellence, (13:19) giving knowing truth against blindness, (6:132) giving degrees according to what they did, (56:89) belonging to degrees discussion in next verses, and (6:130) asking jinn and mankind whether messengers from among you came.

Names and terms include Abbas in Ibn Abbas, Abu Humayd, Abu Humayd, Abu Sufyan, Abu Hurairah, Al-Ahzab, Al-Ashja'i in Abu Malik's nisba, al-Awsat, Al-Basri, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Al-Hikmah, Al-Hikmah as wisdom and Sunnah, Hisham bin 'Urwah, Hisham bin 'Urwah, Ibn Al-Lutbiyyah, Ibn Al-Lutbiyyah in Zakah collector's case in next verses, Israel, children of israel, jahannam, Jahannam, al-Jassas, al-Khattab, Al-Kisa'i, Al-Kisa'i, Al-Madinah, minbar, Minbar, Most High, Mu'adh bin Jabal, Mu'adh bin Jabal, Muhammad bin Ishaq, Muhammad bin Ishaq, MuḤammad, MuṣṬafā, Mustafa, Qatadah, rahmah, ruh, salah, say, Say, shariah, al-Shura, sunnah, tariqah, Tariqah, tawakkul, tawhid, two sahihs, Two Sahihs, uhud, Umar bin Al-Khattab, ummah, umrah, Worlds in Lord of the Worlds, zakah, Abbas, Abi Hayyan, abraham, Abraham, Abū ʿAlī, Abu Ali in Master Abu Ali Daqqaq's name, Daqqāq, Daqqaq, al-Ghani in other contexts, al-Ghamad, Al-Ghamad in Bark al-Ghamad, hadith, hajj, Iman, iman.

### The Beloved and the Speaking Companion

Inwardly, an address to the Messenger runs as follows.

> O master of masters! O paragon of engendered beings! You are generous and lovingly kind, gentle and ever-merciful to everyone. You drive everyone by customs that hit the mark. You call everyone to the table of exaltedness and convey to everlasting felicity. You are like a father for the orphans, a husband for the widowed. You caress the familiar and you show the road to the estranged. You are mercy itself for the world's folk, a cause of generous giving to all the servants. O master, there is all of this, but take care not to see yourself. Do not consider these as your own acquisitions, for all of them are I. It is I who was, I who caressed, I who made, and I put you to that. I gave you a sweet disposition. O paragon, keep on being this way to the faithful and the friends, with the same loving kindness and the same sweet disposition: 'And lower thy wing to the faithful who follow thee' [26:215]. But, with the unbelievers and hypocrites, you should be a bit harder and struggle against them: 'O Prophet! Struggle against the unbelievers and the hypocrites, and be hard with them' [9:73].

Difference between the Beloved, Muhammad, and Speaking Companion, Moses, is then drawn. Beloved was commanded to be harsh with unbelievers and called back from cajolery, for in his disposition all was softness and benevolence. To Speaking Companion He said opposite, "Speak to him with soft words" [20:44]. He commanded him to softness and benevolence, and called him back from sharpness and hardness that was within him.

> If you were to give the unmixed wine of Tawhid, tawhid, to your companions, without the admixture of their own shares, they would flee and no longer come around you. O master, they do not have capacity to put up with what your capacity puts up with. When someone's night and morning are in Presence of Unity, how can others be equal to him or have any affinity with him?

Master himself gave this report of himself, "I am not like any of you. I spend the night at my Lord; He gives me to eat and drink." At another time he said, "I have a moment with God embraced by no proximate angel, nor any sent prophet." Mustafa taught this courtesy of religion to creatures. He said, "'Speak to the people in the measure of their intellects.' Speak to everyone in the measure of his intellect and do not lay upon him what he is unable to bear." Give everyone a cup in size of his spirit, lay down sweets according to each one's intellect.

"So pardon them" is then parsed in a cited address.
"So pardon them" is then parsed.

> O master! Pardon their shortcomings toward your rightful due and your work, and pass over it. As for their shortcomings toward My rightful due, you be their intercessor and ask for forgiveness from Me.

So pardon them, and ask forgiveness for them. So pardon them is an allusion to togetherness, for it is a decree. One who decrees in reality is God, and Messenger follows. Ask forgiveness for them is an allusion to dispersion, which is station of abasement and servanthood. Lord's custom with prophets and friends moves between the two states. Togetherness at one time. Dispersion at another. Togetherness without dispersion is disbelief, and dispersion without togetherness is associationism. Togetherness is Haqiqah itself, and dispersion is path of servanthood. When these two traits come together in someone, he is on road of Sunnah, sunnah, and congregation and walks straight on Tariqah, tariqah, and Shariah, shariah.

> And consult with them in the affair. O master! The states of the travelers in this road are diverse. One falls short, so ask pardon for him. One repents, so ask forgiveness for him. One is obedient, so consult with him.

And when thou art resolved, trust in God. Surely God loves those who trust. Resoluteness has a reality, basis of reality is rightness of what is desired. Togetherness of heart is basis of solidity in religion, jealousy in affair, and straightness in present moment. Resoluteness is of three sorts. One sort is resoluteness of repentance, second resoluteness of service, third resoluteness of Haqiqah. All three are built on trust. Trust has a root, a precondition, and a fruit. Its root is certainty. Its precondition is faith, alluded to in His words, "And in God put your trust, if you have faith" [5:23]. Its fruit is Real's love, in His words, "Surely God loves those who trust." Master Abu Ali, Abū ʿAlī, Daqqaq, Daqqāq, begins the three levels of trust saying cited from, "Trust has three levels. First is trust, " and the verse cited there is (9:72), numbering that citation in the frame.

### In short

- By Allah's Rahmah the Prophet was gentle, not severe in speech or hard in heart, or people would have scattered from around him.
- After Uhud he must pardon Companions' shortcomings toward him, ask forgiveness for shortcomings toward Allah, and consult them in affairs to win hearts and model the practice.
- Consultation is Sunnah where no categorical Qur'an or Hadith injunction exists, from people wise and God-fearing and, for Islamic Law, faqih, while settled commands such as Salah, Zakah and Hajj are not consulted about.
- His consultations at Badr, Uhud, Khandaq, Hudaybiyyah and Ifk decided real outcomes, majority does not helplessly bind an Amir after consultation, and the singular "you have taken a decision" gives final decision to the executive.
- Once decided, trust is placed in Allah alone, not in counsel, plans or means, and Allah loves those who trust in Him.

A missing piece of cloth becomes a doctrine of trust: "It is not appropriate for a prophet to illegally withhold spoils of war. ### Phrase by phrase

**"It is not appropriate for a prophet to illegally withhold spoils of war. No prophet of Allah would be dishonest and take anything from gains of war which Allah had not assigned for him. Whoever deceives his companions over booty, whoso deceiveth as regards any of booty, whoever dishonestly takes something from gains of war, he shall bring forth on Day of Resurrection that which he took, will bring his deceit with him carried on his neck, will be repaid by being disgraced on Day of Judgement carrying whatever he took in front of creation. Whoever defrauds shall bring what he has defrauded on Day of Resurrection carrying it around his neck.

**"Then every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and none will be wronged"**: Then every person shall be paid in full what he has earned, every soul, fraudulent and otherwise, shall be paid in full requital of what it has earned, what it has done, that which it has deceived and also other things. ### Ghulul is worse than ordinary theft

Word Ghulul is also used in absolute sense for khiyanah, breach of trust, misappropriation, pilferage and stealing. It is applied particularly to misappropriation in spoils as crime of stealing from spoils is far more serious compared to common thefts and filching since spoils belong to whole Muslim army as matter of right. Whoever steals from it steals from hundreds and thousands of people. Even if thought of making amends at later stage, it would be very difficult to give back to everyone what was due, or seek their forgiveness for injustice done. Contrary to other types of theft where owner of stolen property is known. In this case there is chance one may repent, if Allah gives ability to do so, and stolen thing could be returned to owner, or one could at least exonerate himself from blame by seeking forgiveness from him.

Illustration is someone who secretly withheld portion of wool from spoils thought about it after distribution of spoils was over. He brought it before Holy Prophet hoping to return it. But he, inspite of being mercy for the worlds, Worlds, and far more generous to his community than fathers and mothers could ever dream to be for their children, returned it back to him saying, "How can I distribute it over the whole army now? Now it is you who would present yourself with it on the Day of Doom."

Therefore punishment for Ghulul or misappropriation is more severe as compared to common thefts. What could be more severe for misappropriator when, before eyes of whole creation on plains of resurrection and retribution, he will find himself disgraced with what he had stolen all stacked on his neck? Narration from Sayyidna Abu Hurairah, Abu Hurairah and Abu Hurayrah, appearing in Al-Bukhari and Muslim, reports Holy Prophet said:

> Watch out, lest I see one of you with a camel loaded round his neck (and the announcement being made that this person had stolen a camel from the spoils). If this person asks me to intercede on his behalf, I shall tell him frankly that I had conveyed what Allah had commanded, now I cannot do anything about it.

May Allah protect us from disgrace of Day we rise again which, according to some narrations, will be so hard on those who face it they would wish to be sent to fires of Jahannam, jahannam, in lieu of terrible disgrace.

Same rule applies to mosques, religious schools and institutions, khanqahs and properties of awqaf (endowments) since they represent contribution of millions of Muslims. If unfortunate misappropriator was to go about seeking to be forgiven, how could he possibly go to each one of those millions? Same rule holds good for public or government treasury, Bayt al-Mal, al-Mal, because all citizens of country have right in it. One who steals from it steals from everyone. Problem is these holdings are such that a single owner does not sit over them. Caretakers become negligent. Avenues of pilferage abound. It is in such moneys and properties that lot, Lot, of thefts and misappropriations have become rampant all over world with most people heedless to evil end that awaits them. They do not realize this is terrible burden to haul onto plains of Resurrection, not to speak of punishment of Hell bound to come as result. Then comes sad deprivation from promised intercession of Messenger. Let us all seek refuge from such fate.

### Hadith warnings

> The worst Ghulul (i.e. stealing) with Allah is a yard of land, that is, when you find two neighbors in a land or home and one of them illegally acquires a yard of his neighbor's land. When he does, he will be tied with it from the seven earths until the Day of Resurrection.

Imam Ahmad recorded Abu Humayd, Abu Humayd As-Sa'idi, said Prophet appointed man from tribe of Al-Azd, called Ibn Al-Lutbiyyah, Ibn Al-Lutbiyyah, to collect Zakah, zakah. ### Trustworthiness of the leader

The Prophet forgave forty Muslims who disobeyed his orders on occasion of battle of Uhud, uhud. However people doubted Prophet had really forgiven them. They thought he had done so only outwardly, for show, and later he would show his anger. These verses tell us Prophet's inner feelings did not differ from outward behaviour. Action matched word. A Muslim leader learns from that. Malice, jealousy and hatred find no lodging in his heart even after a grave mistake by his people at Uhud. Hidden malice also has no place. After forgiveness he lives among them as though nothing had gone amiss. Entrusted affairs, lives and wealth must not be exploited for personal ends. Crossing limits shows no fear of God's wrath. A leader guiding people along the path, the path, to God's will cannot expect to meet God after opposing that will.

States of prophets are free of stain of treacherous actions. Those to whom We gave message to bear to Our servants convey it to those who should receive it. They are not concerned with any affair of close intimate without Our command and they do not hold back, harboring malice, in passing on anyone's share when We commanded it. "Do you not see how [the Prophet] said of Abū Ṭālib, Ṭālib, Abu Talib in plain spelling, 'Go and bury him' when Commander of Believers ʿAlī, Believers ʿAlī, Ali, said to him, 'Your erring uncle has died'? Do you not see how [Muḥammad], Muḥammad, Muhammad, accepted al-Waḥshī, al-Waḥshī, Wahshi, the killer of Hamza when he became a Muslim?" It is said, "It was not for any prophet to give Our secrets to any but people meant to receive them. Hearing was measured to each person. Tradition commands revelation, yunzil, fitted to stations, manāzil."
